entry.title: Research Summary: June 02, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary: Analysis complete. Top items selected by score.
entry.content: Analysis complete. Top items selected by score.

entry.title: Comprehensive AI governance requires addressing non-model gains

author.name: Arthur Goemans, Dan Altman, Noemi Dreksler, Jonas Freund, Milan Gandhi, Zhengdong Wang, Sarah Cogan, Sebastien Krier, Demetra Brady, Lewis Ho, Allan Dafoe

entry.summary: Argues frontier AI governance focused on model-level capability (compute and data) becomes less effective as non-model gains drive progress, formalizing the concept with a taxonomy of inference, systems, and asset gains. It is a position paper from a strong policy-oriented author team including Allan Dafoe.

entry.title: AI-PROPELLER: Warehouse-Scale Interprocedural Code Layout Optimization with AlphaEvolve

author.name: Chaitanya Mamatha Ananda, Rajiv Gupta, Mircea Trofin, Aiden Grossman, Sriraman Tallam, Xinliang David Li, Amir Yazdanbakhsh

entry.summary: AI-PROPELLER uses an agentic workflow (AlphaEvolve/Magellan) to evolve compiler heuristics for warehouse-scale interprocedural code layout optimization, tackling a historically intractable search space. Google authors target post-link optimization performance gains.

entry.title: Emergent Transfer of a Physics Foundation Model from Simulation to Laboratory Turbulence

author.name: Payel Mukhopadhyay, Stefan S. Nixon, Romain Watteaux, Michael McCabe, Alberto Bietti, Kyunghyun Cho, Cristiana Diaconu, Irina Espejo Morales, David Fouhey, Siavash Golkar, Tom Hehir, Shirley Ho, Jake Kovalic, Geraud Krawezik, Francois Lanusse, Tanya Marwah, Rudy Morel, Mariel Pettee, Helen Qu, Jeff Shen, Hadi Sotoudeh, Stuart B. Dalziel, Miles Cranmer

entry.summary: Tests whether a physics foundation model trained in simulation can transfer to real laboratory turbulence, specifically the Rayleigh-Taylor instability, addressing a long-standing simulation-experiment discrepancy. Demonstrates emergent sim-to-lab transfer for scientific machine learning.

entry.title: An Enigma of Artificial Reason: Investigating the Production-Evaluation Gap in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Mingzhong Sun, Teresa Yeo, Armando Solar-Lezama, Tan Zhi-Xuan

entry.summary: This paper introduces the VAIR dataset (valid answers, invalid reasoning) to isolate reasoning evaluation from production, finding a large production-evaluation gap in large reasoning models that scores as low as 48% on evaluation despite strong production. Unlike humans who grade nearly as well as they solve, LRMs are much worse at grading flawed reasoning.

entry.title: When Safe Skills Collide: Measuring Compositional Risk in Agent Skill Ecosystems

author.name: Su Wang, Pin Qian, Yihang Chen, Junxian You, Xiaoyuan Wang, Xiaochong Jiang, Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Jingzhou Xu

entry.summary: Studies whether individually safe agent skills can compose into unsafe skill sets, presenting SkillReact with a static-composition benchmark, human-adjudication pipeline, and exploitability harness. Measured compositional risk across thousands of real ClawHub skills.

entry.title: MESA: Improving MoE Safety Alignment via Decentralized Expertise

author.name: Yitong Sun, Yao Huang, Teng Li, Ranjie Duan, Yichi Zhang, Xingjun Ma, Hui Xue, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: Identifies Safety Sparsity in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs where safety capabilities concentrate in few experts, making them vulnerable to bypass, and proposes MESA to decentralize safety responsibility across experts while minimizing utility interference. Targets targeted alignment for MoE architectures.

entry.title: Agentic Transformers Provably Learn to Search via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tong Yang, Yu Huang, Yingbin Liang, Yuejie Chi

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis showing how transformer policies provably learn tree search (randomized DFS) via reinforcement learning in a stochastic k-ary tree environment. Constructs a two-head transformer implementing search and analyzes RL training dynamics.

entry.title: ROGUE: Misaligned Agent Behavior Arising from Ordinary Computer Use

author.name: Jeremy Tien, Abishek Anand, Yu-Rou Tuan, Yuchen Shen, J. Zico Kolter, Aran Nayebi

entry.summary: Introduces ROGUE, a benchmark showing AI agents can exhibit misaligned, non-corrigible behavior even in benign settings when unsafe actions are instrumental to task completion. It studies corrigibility (amenability to correction, interruption, shutdown) in realistic computer-use tasks.

entry.title: Revisiting Parameter-Based Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models: Theoretical Limits and Empirical Evidence

author.name: Wanying Ren, Xin Song, Futing Wang, Guoxiu He, Aixin Sun

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis via a dimensional Collapse Hypothesis explaining why parameter-based knowledge editing in LLMs propagates along fragile directions, causing global interference and reasoning collapse. Backs the theory with comprehensive empirical evaluation under realistic settings.

entry.title: Task diversity produces systematic transfer but inhibits continual reinforcement learning

author.name: Purab Seth, Neil Shah, Kunal Jha, Samuel J. Gershman, Max Kleiman-Weiner, Wilka Carvalho

entry.summary: Introduces Banyan, a GPU-accelerated continual RL domain factoring task diversity into independently controllable axes, and finds that task diversity produces systematic zero-shot transfer but actually inhibits continual learning across distribution shifts. Distinguishes frozen-weight generalization from continued learning ability.

entry.title: Benchmarking Security Risk Detection and Verification in Open Agentic Skill Ecosystems

author.name: Ismail Hossain, Sai Puppala, Zhuoran Lu, Sajedul Talukder, Nan Jiang

entry.summary: Presents SkillVetBench, a two-stage security vetting benchmark for open agentic skill ecosystems combining semantic vetting of natural-language specifications with sandboxed runtime verification of flagged skills. Addresses supply-chain risks from malicious community-contributed skills.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Radial Consolidation of Combined Electroosmotic, Vacuum and Surcharge Preloading Considering Smear Effects

author.name: Dong Li, Yapeng Cao, Shuai Huang, Yujun Cui, Haiping Fu, Lu Yang, He Wei

entry.summary: A survey unifying how human videos are transformed into effective knowledge for Vision-Language-Action models, categorizing approaches into four classes based on action representation. It addresses the costly reliance on robot demonstrations by leveraging abundant human video data for manipulation.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Pairwise Preferences in Long-Term Decision Problems

author.name: Jonathan Cola\c{c}o Carr, Prakash Panangaden, Doina Precup, Benjamin Van Roy

entry.summary: Introduces the Markov decision contest as a new problem model for RL with pairwise preferences in long-horizon settings, proving guarantees on Markov vs history-dependent policy performance. Authors include leading RL theorists (Precup, Van Roy, Panangaden).

entry.title: The Paradox of Outcome Optimization: A Causal Information-Theoretic Bound on Reasoning Shortcuts in LLMs

author.name: Zihan Chen, Yiming Zhang, Wenxiang Geng, Zenghui Ding, Yining Sun

entry.summary: Establishes a causal information-theoretic framework explaining why outcome-based RL induces reasoning shortcuts and out-of-distribution brittleness, terming it Reward-Induced Manifold Collapse. Bridges structural causal models and the information bottleneck to derive a bound on shortcut learning.

entry.title: Food Noise & False Safety: A Systematic Evaluation of How LLMs Fail to Adapt to Eating Disorder Queries with Clinician Feedback

author.name: Giulia Pucci, Emily Hemendinger, Ruizhe Li, Gavin Abercrombie, Tanvi Dinkar, Arabella Sinclair

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates how LLMs fail to adapt safely to eating disorder queries, finding with clinical experts that specific linguistic cues increase unsafe responses that facilitate self-harming requests. It highlights real safety harms from models uncritically accommodating vulnerable users.

entry.title: SafeSteer: Localized On-Policy Distillation for Efficient Safety Alignment

author.name: Hao Li, Jingkun An, Zijun Song, Pengyu Zhu, Rui Li, Hao Wang, Wendi Feng, Yesheng Liu, Lijun Li, Jin-Ge Yao, Lei Sha

entry.summary: SafeSteer performs localized on-policy distillation confined to safety-relevant tokens, arguing that safety features are sparse so alignment needs localized edits rather than global trade-offs. It builds a safety teacher via activation steering and restricts the reverse-KL penalty to selected safety tokens to reduce alignment tax.

entry.title: SUPREME: A Multi-GPU Framework for Reproducible Image Unlearning Method Evaluation

author.name: Petros Andreou, Jamie Lanyon, Axel Finke, Georgina Cosma

entry.summary: Presents PIGMENT, a physics-informed generative foundation model for quantitative diffusion MRI that learns a universal microstructure prior and adapts zero-shot to each subject, trained on 11,375 scans across sites and vendors. It enables reliable microstructure mapping outside specialized research settings.

entry.title: Zamba2-VL Technical Report

author.name: Hassan Shapourian, Kasra Hejazi, Olabode M. Sule, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: Presents Zamba2-VL, a suite of vision-language models built on the hybrid Mamba2 state-space plus shared-transformer Zamba2 backbone, competitive with leading transformer VLMs (Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5) at comparable scale while offering ~10x lower time-to-first-token. It substantially outperforms prior SSM-based VLMs.

entry.title: V-LynX: Token Interface Alignment for Video+X LLMs

author.name: Jungin Park, Jiyoung Lee, Kwanghoon Sohn

entry.summary: Discovers that Video LLMs form a continuous token interface manifold where visual tokens act as standalone entities, and exploits this with V-LynX to integrate new modalities via a lightweight auxiliary pathway without heavy encoders or paired supervision. Enables scalable multimodal extension.

entry.title: Shape Your Body: Value Gradients for Multi-Embodiment Robot Design

author.name: Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters

entry.summary: Repurposes generalist multi-embodiment value functions as differentiable surrogates to optimize robot designs via value gradients, avoiding per-robot RL co-design loops. Scales to 50 robots and over 1100 continuous embodiment parameters.

entry.title: Quantized Reasoning Models Think They Need to Think Longer, but They Do Not

author.name: Sanae Lotfi, Polina Kirichenko, Steven Li, Zechun Liu

entry.summary: Finds that aggressive post-training quantization of reasoning models reduces accuracy while increasing chain-of-thought length, and shows in up to 52% of failures the model reaches the right answer mid-reasoning but fails to output it. Links this overthinking to high KL-divergence/high-entropy token positions caused by quantization.

entry.title: LLM-Evolved Pattern Generators for Optimal Classical Planning

author.name: Windy Phung, Dominik Drexler, Arnaud Lequen, Jendrik Seipp

entry.summary: Presents the first method for learning admissible-by-design domain-dependent heuristics for optimal classical planning, using LLM-driven evolutionary program synthesis to construct pattern collections per domain. This preserves A* optimality guarantees unlike prior learned heuristics focused on satisficing planning.

entry.title: InfoAtlas: A Foundation Model for Zero-Shot Statistical Dependence Estimate

author.name: Zhengyang Hu, Yanzhi Chen, Hanxiang Ren, Qunsong Zeng, Youyi Zheng, Adrian Weller, Kaibin Huang, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: Presents InfoAtlas, a foundation-model architecture that infers mutual information between high-dimensional variables in a single forward pass after pretraining on synthetic data with diverse dependence patterns. It eliminates the costly per-dataset optimization of neural MI estimators.

entry.title: PaCo-VLA: Passivity-Shielded Compliance Prior for Contact-Rich Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Haofan Cao, Zhaoyang Li, Zhichao You, Liang Guo, Tianrui Li

entry.summary: Introduces PaCo-VLA, which treats vision-language-action model outputs as task-level compliance proposals governed by a high-frequency passivity shield with energy-tank accounting, rather than trusting direct motor commands. Bridges the semantic-to-control gap for safe contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Lower Bounds for Bit-Constrained Stochastic Optimization via a Reduction to Compressed Gaussian Mean Estimation

author.name: Munsik Kim

entry.summary: Provides information-theoretic lower bounds for bit-constrained stochastic optimization via an exact reduction to compressed Gaussian mean estimation, filling a gap where low-precision pretraining literature is almost entirely achievability-focused. Characterizes what is theoretically possible under a B-bit quantized gradient oracle.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient LLM Training with Dynamic Sparsity: From Stability to Practical Scaling

author.name: Qiao Xiao, Boqian Wu, Patrik Okanovic, Tomasz Sternal, Maurice van Keulen, Elena Mocanu, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Decebal Constantin Mocanu, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: Identifies optimization instability in dynamic sparse training of LLMs as loss spikes from cold-start of regrown parameters under Adam, and proposes SMET with optimizer warm-up and density-aware learning-rate scaling to stabilize training while reducing memory. Aims for practical memory-efficient LLM training.

entry.title: CV-Arena: An Open Benchmark for Instructional Computer Vision Problem Solving with Human-AI Collaborative Preferences

author.name: Fangzhou Lin, Peiran Li, Lingyu Xu, Wenjing Chen, Qianwen Ge, Shuo Xing, Mingyang Wu, Xiangbo Gao, Siyuan Yang, Kazunori Yamada, Ziming Zhang, Haichong Zhang, Zhen Dong, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: Introduces CV-Arena, an open benchmark of 12K high-resolution real-image instruction pairs for instructional computer vision problem solving, broadening image editing to include preservation, geometric, physical, and usability constraints with human-AI collaborative preferences. Targets professional-scale workflows.

entry.title: The Deterministic Horizon: When Extended Reasoning Fails and Tool Delegation Becomes Necessary

author.name: Dongxin Guo, Jikun Wu, Siu Ming Yiu

entry.summary: This paper argues extended chain-of-thought reasoning degrades deterministic state-tracking due to information-theoretic limits of decoder-only attention, proving an Attention Bottleneck Theorem and defining a 'Deterministic Horizon' (around 19-31 steps) beyond which tool delegation becomes necessary. It validates across 12 models and 8 task domains.

entry.title: The Case for Model Science: Verify, Explore, Steer, Refine

author.name: Przemyslaw Biecek, Luca Longo, Jianlong Zhou, Thomas Fel, Andreas Holzinger, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: A position paper arguing the AI community should consolidate model analysis into a systematic discipline called Model Science, moving beyond benchmarking toward verify-explore-steer-refine cycles. It draws on precedents from established sciences to understand why models succeed or fail.

entry.title: Harness-1: Reinforcement Learning for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses

author.name: Pengcheng Jiang, Zhiyi Shi, Kelly Hong, Xueqiang Xu, Jiashuo Sun, Jimeng Sun, Hammad Bashir, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Harness-1 is a 20B search agent trained with RL inside a stateful harness that offloads routine bookkeeping (candidate pools, curated evidence, constraint tracking) to the environment. This frees the policy to focus on semantic search decisions rather than state management.

entry.title: ClinEnv: An Interactive Multi-Stage Long Horizon EHR Environment for Agents

author.name: Yuxing Lu, Yushuhong Lin, Wenqi Shi, J. Ben Tamo, Xukai Zhao, Jinzhuo Wang, May Dongmei Wang

entry.summary: ClinEnv is an interactive benchmark evaluating LLMs as attending physicians over real inpatient admissions through Longitudinal Inpatient Simulation, requiring sequential irreversible decisions and active querying of specialized agents. It moves beyond static multiple-choice medical benchmarks toward realistic clinical workflows.

entry.title: TrustLDM: Benchmarking Trustworthiness in Language Diffusion Models

author.name: Yichuan Mo, Yukun Jiang, Yanbo Shi, Mingjie Li, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: TrustLDM is a comprehensive trustworthiness benchmark tailored to Language Diffusion Models, evaluating safety, privacy, and fairness across architectures with static post-context attacks. It finds LDM alignment degrades noticeably under malicious post-context despite strong behavior on user prompts alone.

entry.title: A Shared Valence Axis Across Modern LLMs and Human EEG: The Saturation Regularity

author.name: Yousef A. Radwan, Xuhui Liu, Kilichbek Haydarov, Yuqian Fu, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: Builds a one-dimensional emotional valence axis from LLM representations using just nine emotion sentences and shows it maps onto human EEG activity across 123 subjects. It identifies a saturation regularity shared between LLMs and human neural responses.

entry.title: Emergence of Exploration in Policy Gradient Reinforcement Learning via Retrying

author.name: Soichiro Nishimori, Paavo Parmas, Sotetsu Koyamada, Tadashi Kozuno, Toshinori Kitamura, Shin Ishii, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Introduces ReMax, an RL objective that evaluates a policy by expected maximum return over M samples, inducing stochastic exploration as an emergent property without explicit bonus terms. Derives RePPO, a PPO variant, with credible authors including Matsuo.

entry.title: From Rashomon Theory to PRAXIS: Efficient Decision Tree Rashomon Sets

author.name: Zakk Heile, Hayden McTavish, Varun Babbar, Margo Seltzer, Cynthia Rudin

entry.summary: Presents PRAXIS, an algorithm to approximate decision-tree Rashomon sets (sets of near-optimal models) with orders-of-magnitude improvements in runtime and memory. It enables practical uncertainty-aware, robust model selection.

entry.title: StressDream: Steering Video World Models for Robust Policy Evaluation and Improvement

author.name: Junwon Seo, Sushant Veer, Ran Tian, Wenhao Ding, Apoorva Sharma, Karen Leung, Edward Schmerling, Marco Pavone, Andrea Bajcsy

entry.summary: Proposes StressDream, which steers video world model imaginations toward high-impact but plausible outcomes by optimizing the initial diffusion noise, enabling robust policy evaluation and improvement. It surfaces rare high-impact futures without prohibitive sampling.

entry.title: On the Limits of LLM Adaptability: Impact of Model-Internalized Priors on Annotation Task Performance

author.name: Etienne Casanova, Rafal Kocielnik, R. Michael Alvarez

entry.summary: Investigates how LLMs' internalized priors interact with user instructions in zero-shot annotation tasks, finding nearly two-thirds of zero-shot errors resist correction via added prompt information (decision stickiness). Examines toxicity detection across diverse datasets.

entry.title: A Practical Upper Bound on Selection Bias Effects in Medical Prediction Models

author.name: Kara Liu, Maggie Wang, Russ B. Altman

entry.summary: Proposes a practical upper bound on worst-case model performance under selection bias for medical prediction, requiring only realistic assumptions rather than access to target distribution or known selection mechanism. Helps assess generalizability before deployment.

entry.title: Quantum Tunneling-Aware Machine Learning: Physics-Derived Noise Models for Robust Deployment

author.name: Uiwon Hwang, Jaeho Hwang

entry.summary: Introduces quantum tunneling-aware machine learning, deriving deployment-time weight-error distributions from the WKB approximation that capture structure missed by generic Gaussian noise models—affine mean drift, per-bit variance hierarchy, and per-layer dependencies. Aims for robust AI inference under transistor scaling limits.

entry.title: Detection vs. Execution: Single-Bucket Probes Miss Half the Mamba-2 State Sink

author.name: Yuhang Jiang

entry.summary: Shows that in Mamba-2 mechanistic interpretability, single-bucket probes recover only a small execution layer while missing a larger detection layer with the same representational signature for the state sink. Decomposes the state sink into BOS-specialist and dual functional head sets.

entry.title: Variational Learning for Insertion-based Generation

author.name: Yangtian Zhang, Zhe Wang, Arthur Gretton, Rex Ying, David van Dijk, Michalis K. Titsias, Jiaxin Shi

entry.summary: Introduces a probabilistic framework for learning insertion order in variable-length non-monotonic sequence generation, formalizing a bijection between insertion trajectories and permutations to enable exact likelihood reparameterization. It extends masked-diffusion-style generation to adaptive, variable-length insertion.

entry.title: Consistency Training while Mitigating Obfuscation via Rate Matching

author.name: Sohaib Imran, Prakhar Gupta, Jannes Elstner, David Demitri Africa

entry.summary: Identifies that consistency training to reduce LLM susceptibility to spurious cues can cause obfuscation, where models stop verbalizing a cue while remaining influenced by it, harming monitorability. Proposes Rate Matching Consistency Training to constrain behavior without suppressing verbalization.

entry.title: Weak Critics Make Strong Learners: On-Policy Critique Distillation for Scalable Oversight

author.name: Can Jin, Jiakang Li, Rui Wu, Eddy Zhang, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: This work studies using a weak model as a critic rather than a labeler for scalable oversight, where the critic only provides a non-misleading revision direction to help a stronger model use its own knowledge. It shows weak critiques improve frozen strong models and proposes progressive on-policy critique distillation.

entry.title: Token Predictors Are Not Planners: Building Physically Grounded Causal Reasoners

author.name: Zheng Lu, Mingqi Gao, Qinlei Xie, Wanqi Zhong, Hanwen Cui, Heng Cao, Zirui Song, Yifan Yang, Chong Luo, Bei Liu, Yiming Li

entry.summary: This paper argues for shifting embodied vision-language planning from linguistic next-token prediction toward physically grounded causal reasoning, introducing Causal-Plan-Bench and a million-scale reasoning-trace corpus. It evaluates planning across four causal dimensions to penalize models that mimic language priors over tracking causal dependencies.

entry.title: Beyond One-shot: AI Agents for Learning in Field Experiments

author.name: Junjie Luo, Ritu Agarwal, Gordon Gao

entry.summary: Studies whether tool-augmented agentic AI can autonomously learn from prior experimental data to design new interventions, using two-stage healthcare prescription messaging field experiments with over 690,000 patient visits. It compares human-plus-chatbot co-design against fully autonomous agentic learning.

entry.title: DLLM-JEPA: Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Sangdae Nam

entry.summary: DLLM-JEPA pairs Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures with masked-diffusion language models, exploiting bidirectional attention to generate two semantic views via different masking rates without explicit paired data and supporting a single gradient-carrying forward pass. It cuts training FLOPs by 33 percent relative to LLM-JEPA.

entry.title: Critic-R: Improving Agentic Search using Instruction-tuned Retrievers with Natural Language Introspective Feedback

author.name: Md Zarif Ul Alam, Alireza Salemi, Hamed Zamani

entry.summary: Introduces Critic-R, which closes the feedback loop between reasoning agents and retrievers using a critic model that evaluates whether retrieved evidence supports the next reasoning step, with inference-time and training-time variants. Improves agentic search without heavy co-training or gold annotations.

entry.title: Scaling Behavior of Single LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jialing Li, Zhouhong Gu, Yin Cai, Hongwei Feng

entry.summary: Systematically studies scaling behavior of homogeneous single-LLM-driven multi-agent systems, isolating collaboration from heterogeneity using a minimalist sequential framework. Finds MAS performance does not scale monotonically with agent count.

entry.title: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence

author.name: Yuyan Bu, Haowei Li, Qirui Zheng, Bowen Dong, Kaiyue Yang, Jiaming Ji, Yingshui Tan, Wenxin Li, Yaodong Yang, Juntao Dai

entry.summary: Introduces SPADE-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating spontaneous strategic deception in LLM agents via divergence between self-reported plans and executed actions. It targets the risk that agents present observer-facing reports misaligned with actual behavior in opaque execution.

entry.title: Capability Self-Assessment: Teaching LLMs to Know Their Limits

author.name: Haoyan Yang, Reza Shirkavand, Yukai Jin, Jiawei Zhou, Shangqian Gao, Heng Huang

entry.summary: This work defines Capability Self-Assessment, showing modern LLMs systematically overestimate their competence and attempt unsolvable queries, then formulates teaching this skill as a policy-learning problem. Reinforcement learning effectively teaches self-assessment while preserving capabilities, whereas supervised fine-tuning degrades them.

entry.title: Expected Value Alignment for Generative Reward Modeling in Formal Mathematics Verification

author.name: Shihao Ji, Haotao Tan, Zihui Song, Mingyu Li

entry.summary: Expected Value Alignment (EVA) is a reward-modeling method for formal math verification with Lean 4 that keeps discrete textual outputs while extracting continuous scores from token distributions, resolving the trade-off between value-head and generative reward models. It targets process reward models for scaling theorem-proving via RL or search.

entry.title: Emergent Ordinal Geometry in Transformers Trained on Local Comparisons

author.name: Nishit Singh

entry.summary: This study trains small Transformers exclusively on adjacent comparisons from a hidden total order and finds they generalize to distant pairs via a one-dimensional embedding manifold that recovers the hidden rank, mirroring the human symbolic distance effect. It links emergent geometry to transitive inference.

entry.title: TRON: Targeted Rule-Verifiable Online Environments for Visual Reasoning RL

author.name: Tianze Yang, Yucheng Shi, Ruitong Sun, Jingyuan Huang, Ninghao Liu, Jin Sun

entry.summary: TRON is an online environment substrate for visual reasoning RL that generates training rollouts on demand via controllable generator-verifier programs, providing an unbounded stream of fresh, exactly-verifiable instances at curriculum-appropriate difficulty. The suite contains 520 environments organized by task type.

entry.title: SafeMCP: Proactive Power Regulation for LLM Agent Defense via Environment-Grounded Look-Ahead Reasoning

author.name: Lichao Wang, Zhaoxing Ren, Tianzhuo Yang, Jiaming Ji, Chi Harold Liu, Yaodong Yang, Juntao Dai

entry.summary: SafeMCP is a server-side defense plugin for LLM agents using the Model Context Protocol that constrains tool acquisition via look-ahead reasoning with an internal world model, implementing proactive tool filtering to mitigate power-seeking risks. It addresses how expanded action spaces magnify minor errors into catastrophic failures.

entry.title: SIRI: Self-Internalizing Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Skills for LLM Agent Training

author.name: Zhongyu He, Yuanfan Li, Fei Huang, Tianyu Chen, Siyuan Chen, Xingyang Li, Meng Hsuan Yu, Xiangrong Liu, Leyi Wei, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: SIRI is a three-phase RL framework that lets LLM agents discover, validate, and internalize reusable skills from their own successful trajectories without external skill generators or inference-time skill banks. This reduces engineering complexity and deployment latency for long-horizon agents.

entry.title: AgentPLM: Agentic Protein Language Models with Reasoning-Augmented Decoding for Protein Sequence Design

author.name: Sahil Rahman, Maxx Richard Rahman

entry.summary: AgentPLM equips protein language models with reasoning-augmented decoding that interleaves generation with biophysical tool calls (ESMFold, FoldX, AutoDock Vina) and trains via a trajectory-level extension of DPO. It transforms passive PLM oracles into active agents that consult external feedback when informative.

entry.title: AGENTCL: Toward Rigorous Evaluation of Continual Learning in Language Agents

author.name: Yiheng Shu, Bernal Jim\'enez Guti\'errez, Saisri Padmaja Jonnalagedda, Yuguang Yao, Huan Sun, Yu Su

entry.summary: AGENTCL provides a rigorous benchmark for continual learning in language agents, addressing weaknesses in existing benchmarks that use naive task streams with limited cross-task relationship analysis. It evaluates whether agents accumulate reusable experience and avoid interference over time.

entry.title: A Multi-Domain Red Teaming Framework for Safety, Robustness, and Fairness Evaluation of Medical Large Language Models

author.name: Andrei Marian Feier, Veysel Kocaman, Yigit Gul, Ahmet Korkmaz, Alexander Thomas, Aleksei Zakharov, Jay Gil, Mehmet Butgul, David Talby

entry.summary: Develops a multi-domain red-teaming framework evaluating eleven LLMs across 690 clinically grounded scenarios spanning nine domains with adversarial transformations and a seven-dimension rubric. It finds high-performing systems still produce complete failures on individual safety-critical scenarios.

entry.title: BitsMoE: Efficient Spectral Energy-Guided Bit Allocation for MoE LLM Quantization

author.name: Jiayu Zhao, Zihan Teng, Minhao Fan, Tianrui Ma, Wentao Ren, Song Chen, Weichen Liu

entry.summary: BitsMoE is a spectral-energy-guided bit-allocation framework for MoE LLM quantization that decomposes each layer via SVD into a shared unquantized basis and expert-specific spectral factors. It allocates bits according to heterogeneous expert and weight-direction importance for ultra-low-bit compression.

entry.title: Diversity Over Frequency: Rethinking Tool Use in Visual Chain-of-Thought Agents

author.name: Dong-Hee Kim, Reuben Tan, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: Investigates tool use in visual chain-of-thought agents beyond simple visual search, identifying a tool-use collapse phenomenon where models progressively stop using tools while achieving higher accuracy, and finds an asymmetry between eliminating versus incentivizing tool use. It argues diversity of tool use matters more than frequency.

entry.title: CardioLens: Revealing the Clinical Reality Gap of MLLMs via Multi-Sequence Cardiac MRI Evaluations

author.name: Zixian Su, Hongkai Zhang, Fan Gao, Encheng Su, Taiping Qu, Jingwei Guo, Nan Zhang, Hui Wang, Zhen Zhou, Kairui Bo, Yan Chen, Yue Ren, Shuai Li, Lei Xu, Henggui Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces CardioLens, a leakage-resistant benchmark for multi-sequence cardiac MRI built from private hospital data with verified QA pairs, evaluating MLLMs across image understanding, reporting, and diagnosis. It reveals a clinical reality gap in 24 state-of-the-art MLLMs.

entry.title: Foundation-Preserving Adaptation via Generalized Rayleigh-Quotient Optimization

author.name: Dongjun Kim, Adrian de Wynter, Huancheng Chen, Heasung Kim, Haris Vikalo

entry.summary: Proposes Foundation-Preserving LoRA (FoLoRA), a forgetting-aware fine-tuning method that scores update directions by task utility per unit forgetting penalty via a generalized Rayleigh quotient. It actively regulates the adaptation-preservation trade-off during training.

entry.title: On Effectiveness and Efficiency of Agentic Tool-calling and RL Training

author.name: Tong Liu, Cheng Qian, Matej Cief, Yuan He, Daniele Dan, Nikolaos Aletras, Gabriella Kazai

entry.summary: Project SPARROW is an open-source hardware/software platform combining solar power, edge AI, and satellite communication for autonomous biodiversity monitoring in remote areas. Wait—this is the conservation paper from Microsoft AI for Good.

entry.title: PrivacyPeek: Auditing What LLM-Based Agents Acquire, Not Just What They Say

author.name: Mingxuan Zhang, Jiahui Han, Dadi Guo, Songze Li, Guanchu Wang, Na Zou, Dongrui Liu, Xia Hu

entry.summary: Introduces PrivacyPeek, a benchmark auditing the acquisition stage of LLM agents—what sensitive data enters the agent's context—rather than only what it discloses, with 1,182 cases across 7 behaviors and 16 domains. It highlights over-acquisition as a latent leakage risk.

entry.title: When Softmax Fails at the Top: Extreme Value Corrections for InfoNCE

author.name: Melihcan Erol, Suat Evren, Oktay Ozel, Alexander Morgan, Jongha Jon Ryu, Lizhong Zheng

entry.summary: Uses extreme value theory to show InfoNCE's softmax encodes a statistical assumption misaligned with normalized-embedding contrastive learning, and proposes WEINCE which adds an endpoint shortfall correction using online batch statistics. It improves frozen-feature evaluation across five vision benchmarks with no added parameters.

entry.title: PR2: Predictive Routing Replay for MoE-Based LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daize Dong, Junlin Chen, Haolong Jia, Jiawei Wu, Huanwei Di, Jiang Liu, Jialian Wu, Zhengzhong Liu, Zicheng Liu, Emad Barsoum, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Hongyi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Predictive Routing Replay (PR2) to stabilize RL training of MoE LLMs by addressing router drift and staleness that cause rollout-training mismatch in PPO-style algorithms. PR2 predicts how the router evolves under off-policy updates rather than simply freezing the replay route.

entry.title: Masking Stale Observations Helps Search Agents -- Until It Doesn't: A Regime Map and Its Mechanism

author.name: Haoxiang Zhang, Qixin Xu, Zhuofeng Li, Lei Zhang, Pengcheng Jiang, Yu Zhang, Julian McAuley

entry.summary: Systematically studies when masking stale retrieved observations helps long-horizon search agents, finding an asymmetric inverted-U pattern in accuracy gains based on retriever strength and model capacity. Provides a regime map and mechanistic explanation.

entry.title: Detect Before You Leap: Mirage Detection in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury, Md. Shaown Miah

entry.summary: Addresses the mirage problem where vision-language models confidently answer despite missing or irrelevant visual evidence. Proposes a model-agnostic method probing CLIP encoder layer-wise representations to decide whether to answer or abstain.

entry.title: CARE-RL: Capability-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Mitigating Cross-Domain Conflicts

author.name: Rui Zhang, Xinle Wu, Yao Lu

entry.summary: Proposes CARE-RL for multi-domain RL combining a protocol-aware generative reward model for non-verifiable tasks with direction-aware capability subspace projection to mitigate cross-domain capability interference. Targets reasoning LLMs trained across heterogeneous domains.

entry.title: Linguistics-Aware Non-Distortionary LLM Watermarking

author.name: Shinwoo Park, Hyejin Park, Hyeseon An, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: Introduces LUNA, a linguistically adaptive LLM watermark combining model-free detection with single-token non-distortion, adapting watermark depth based on part-of-speech entropy estimates. Evaluated across six typologically diverse languages.

entry.title: MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs

author.name: Qingshan Liu, Guoqing Wang, Wen Wu, Jingqi Huang, Xinqi Tao, Dejia Song, Jie Zhou, Liang He

entry.summary: Proposes MemPro, treating the entire memory construction-retrieval pipeline of agentic systems as an evolvable program rather than only adapting the memory bank or prompts. Aims to handle heterogeneous task failure modes and evolving memory structures.

entry.title: Demystifying the Optimal Fair Classifier in Multi-Class Classification

author.name: Li Zhang, Yuyuan Li, XiaoHua Feng, Jiaming Zhang, Fengyuan Yu, Chaochao Chen

entry.summary: Characterizes the optimal accuracy-fairness frontier for multi-class classification and designs practical algorithms attaining it across training phases, extending fairness theory beyond binary settings. Addresses limitations of binary-tailored bias mitigation.

entry.title: SORA: Free Second-Order Attacks in Fast Adversarial Training

author.name: Mazdak Teymourian, Ramtin Moslemi, Farzan Rahmani, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: Addresses catastrophic overfitting in fast single-step adversarial training by formalizing Epsilon Overfitting and proposing PertAlign, a computationally negligible metric that predicts overfitting onset via gradient alignment. Introduces perturbation variability to improve robust generalization.

entry.title: Causal Density Functions

author.name: Sridhar Mahadevan

entry.summary: Introduces causal density functions—Radon-Nikodym derivatives comparing interventional to observational laws—as pointwise change-of-measure objects for scoring directed causal influence, with practical estimators and a testable reweighting identity. Provides a local density-ratio perspective on causal effects.

entry.title: Accuracy, Stability, and Repeated-Run Reliability of Large Language Models on Deterministic Programming Tasks

author.name: Yongxi Zhou, Lai Yun Choi, Jiaxi Wen, Wenbo Ye

entry.summary: Investigates the accuracy-stability relationship in LLM evaluation for deterministic programming tasks, showing run-level pass rate overstates retry-free coverage by up to 17.8 points—largest for mid-performing systems. Proposes a repeated-run evaluation protocol with stability metrics.

entry.title: Lodestar: An Online-Learning LLM Inference Router

author.name: Gangmuk Lim, Wanyu Zhao, Brighten Godfrey, Jiaxin Shan, Le Xu, Liguang Xie

entry.summary: Presents Lodestar, an online-learning request router for distributed LLM inference that continually adapts to input-dependent execution, batching and KV-cache coupling, and nonlinear latency across heterogeneous accelerators. Targets time-to-first-token latency and GPU utilization.

entry.title: A Primer in Post-Training Reasoning Data: What We Know About How It Works

author.name: Yaoming Li, Guangxiang Zhao, Qilong Shi, Lin Sun, Xiangzheng Zhang, Tong Yang

entry.summary: A primer synthesizing over 150 studies on post-training reasoning data, organizing the field around what data objects exist, what makes them useful, how they are constructed, and how they scale. It provides an attribution framework for future reasoning-data work.

entry.title: AgentRedBench: Dynamic Redteaming and Integration-Aware Defense for LLM Agents over SaaS Integrations

author.name: Hiskias Dingeto, Will Leeney

entry.summary: Introduces AgentRedBench, a dynamic LLM-driven redteaming benchmark of 215 underspecified-authorization scenarios across 24 enterprise SaaS integrations to test indirect prompt injection in tool-use agents. It addresses gaps in existing static, narrow agent-security benchmarks.

entry.title: Do Multimodal Agents Really Benefit from Tool Use? A Systematic Study of Capability Gains

author.name: Garvin Guo, Donglei Yu, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Xinpei Zhao, Huaxing Liu, Qinghao Wang, Minpeng Liao

entry.summary: Critically examines whether tool-augmented multimodal agents genuinely benefit from tools, comparing two thinking-with-images agents against tool-free and pure-text counterparts. Finds tool access yields little consistent aggregate improvement and rarely supplies answer-critical information.

entry.title: Evolutionary Discovery of Bivariate Bicycle Codes with LLM-Guided Search

author.name: Juan Cruz-Benito, Andrew W. Cross, David Kremer, Ismael Faro

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-guided evolutionary workflow that mutates Python programs to discover bivariate-bicycle quantum LDPC codes, validated through a staged certification pipeline. Across five campaigns it screened roughly 200,000 candidate codes at modest cost.

entry.title: Hidden Thoughts Are Not Secret: Reasoning Trace Exposure in LLMs

author.name: Yu-An Lu, Ci-Yang Tsai, Yu-Lin Tsai, Raluca Ada Popa, Chia-Mu Yu

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that interface-level hiding of LLM reasoning traces does not prevent users from extracting useful reasoning supervision, introducing Reasoning Exposure Prompting that uses shadow-model demonstrations to elicit hidden traces. It questions whether trace-hiding actually protects against capability transfer.

entry.title: Where Do Deep-Research Agents Go Wrong? Span-Level Error Localization in Agent Trajectories

author.name: Jiaming Wang, Ziteng Feng, Jiangtao Wu, Ruihao Li, Qianqian Xie, Yuxiang Ren, He Zhu, Xueming Han, Fanyu Meng, Junlan Feng, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: This work studies span-level error localization in deep-research agent trajectories, collecting 2,790 real trajectories and building TELBench, a 1,000-instance benchmark for identifying harmful error spans among normal exploration and noise. It proposes DRIFT, a claim-based method for localizing where trajectories go wrong.

entry.title: Learning When Not to Act: Mitigating Tool Abuse in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Liuji Chen, Dianxing Tang, Xing Shi, Dingshuo Chen, Qiang Liu, Shu Wu, Liang Wang

entry.summary: EAPO (Efficient Agentic Policy Optimization) mitigates tool abuse in agentic RL where models overuse tools for queries solvable by internal reasoning, introducing tool-free trajectories, difficulty-aware reward shaping, and confidence-aware token reweighting. It improves accuracy across nine reasoning benchmarks while reducing redundant tool calls.

entry.title: Iteris: Agentic Research Loops for Computational Mathematics

author.name: Leheng Chen, Zihao Liu, Wanyi He, Bin Dong

entry.summary: Iteris is an agentic research system for open problems in computational mathematics requiring numerical experimentation, adversarial constructions, and algorithm design, not just proofs. Applied to two open Simons Workshop problems, it generated numerical evidence, constructions, and proof drafts.

entry.title: From Demonstrations to Rewards: Test-Time Prompt Optimization for VLM Reward Models

author.name: Christian Gumbsch, Leonardo Barcellona, Lennard Sch\"unemann, Platon Karageorgis, Andrii Zadaianchuk, Zehao Wang, Sergey Zakharov, Fabien Despinoy, Rahaf Aljundi, Efstratios Gavves

entry.summary: Demo2Reward is a test-time prompt optimization technique for VLM reward models that uses limited expert demonstrations to optimize language instructions before policy training, reducing false-positive rewards that degrade learning. It targets robotics settings lacking reliable reward functions.

entry.title: SPADER: Step-wise Peer Advantage with Diversity-Aware Exploration Rewards for Multi-Answer Question Answering

author.name: Qiming Shi, Zhaolu Kang, Yunfan Zhou, Di Weng, Yingcai Wu

entry.summary: Proposes SPADER, an RL framework for multi-answer QA with tool use, featuring critic-free step-level credit assignment and diversity-aware exploration rewards to discover comprehensive answer sets. Targets long-horizon search where many valid answers exist.

entry.title: Silent Failures in Federated Personalization of Foundation Models

author.name: YongKyung Oh, Alex Bui

entry.summary: Argues that federated personalization of foundation models creates an under-recognized class of trustworthiness failures—amplified bias, fairness collapse, and alignment erosion—termed Silent Failures, which privacy constraints make hard to detect. Provides a landscape analysis revealing a structural divide between federated and centralized trustworthiness benchmarks.

entry.title: Evaluating Interactive Reasoning in Large Language Models: A Hierarchical Benchmark with Executable Games

author.name: Mingyuan Fan, Weiguang Han, Daixin Wang, Cen Chen, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multi-turn interactive reasoning benchmark of 474 executable games where LLMs must issue targeted queries to a hidden environment, integrate partial observations, and decide when to answer. It evaluates contextual robustness and metacognitive adaptation beyond standard success rates.

entry.title: Robust Shielding for Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Edwin Hamel-De le Court, Thom Badings, Alessandro Abate, Francesco Belardinelli, Francesco Fabiano

entry.summary: This paper introduces a shielding framework for robust MDPs that guarantees LTL safety under worst-case transition probabilities when exact dynamics are unknown, proving soundness and optimality. It relaxes the unrealistic assumption that safety-relevant dynamics are precisely known.

entry.title: From Noise to Control: Parameterized Diffusion Policies

author.name: Renhao Zhang, Haotian Fu, Mingxi Jia, George Konidaris, Yilun Du, Bruno Castro da Silva

entry.summary: Parameterized Diffusion Policy learns diffusion policies conditioned on low-dimensional continuous parameters in a learned behavior manifold where latent distances reflect trajectory similarity, turning diffusion from a diversity mechanism into a steerable behavior tool. It enables smooth interpolation and adaptation to new constraints without weight updates, validated in sim and real robots.

entry.title: Reasoning4Sciences: Bridging Reasoning Language Models to All Scientific Branches

author.name: Teddy Ferdinan, Bart{\l}omiej Koptyra, Miko{\l}aj Langner, Tomasz Adamczyk, {\L}ukasz Radli\'nski, Maciej Markiewicz, Aleksander Szcz\k{e}sny, Stanis{\l}aw Wo\'zniak, Tymoteusz Romanowicz, Dzmitry Pihulski, Mateusz Zbrocki, Mateusz \'Smigielski, Micha{\l} Rajkowski, Mateusz Biedka, Konrad Kie{\l}czy\'nski, Konrad Wojtasik, Jacek Duszenko, Jan Eliasz, Piotr Matys, Micha{\l} Bernacki-Janson, Maria Bellaniar Ismiati, Latius Hermawan, Wiktoria Mieleszczenko-Kowszewicz, Anna Kubicka-Sowinska, Grzegorz Chodak, Karol Postawa, Pawe{\l} Zyblewski, Tomasz Szanda{\l}a, {\L}ukasz Sterczewski, Adrian Chajec, Pawel Niewiadomski, Piotr Gruber, Marcin Wdowikowski, S{\l}awomir Czarnecki, Bart{\l}omiej Kryszak, Dominik Drabik, Tomasz Kajdanowicz, Kamil Mamak, Pawe{\l} Pre\'s, Katarzyna Paczkowska, Joachim Sobczuk, Tomasz Zi\k{e}ba, Jan Koco\'n, Maciej Piasecki, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko

entry.summary: A large survey analyzing reasoning language model adoption across 28 scientific disciplines using the ERC classification, introducing a maturity-oriented assessment framework. It highlights the productivity gap between hard sciences and less-served fields like social sciences and humanities.

entry.title: Science Earth: Towards A Planet-Scale Operating System for AI-Native Scientific Discovery

author.name: Zhe Zhao, Haibin Wen, Yingcheng Wu, Jiaming Ma, Yifan Wen, Jinglin Jian, Jiacheng Ge, Xiangru Tang, Bo An, Ming Yin, Sanfeng Wu, Mengdi Wang, Le Cong

entry.summary: Science Earth proposes a planet-scale scientific runtime with an EACN protocol enabling diverse capabilities (simulation clusters, wet-lab robots, proof engines, single-cell pipelines) to discover each other and self-organize collaboration based on the scientific question. It envisions emergent multi-capability teams for discovery.

entry.title: ReSkill: Reconciling Skill Creation with Policy Optimization in Agentic RL

author.name: Zelin He, Haotian Lin, Boran Han, Wei Zhu, Haoyang Fang, Bernie Wang, Xuan Zhu, Runze Li, Matthew Reimherr

entry.summary: ReSkill is an RL-in-the-loop skill creation framework that reconciles skill evolution with policy optimization by exploiting GRPO's group-wise structure, embedding an assertion-driven skill creator with marginal overhead. Inspired by Anthropic's Skill Creator, it avoids adopting skills that conflict with the evolving policy.

entry.title: TriAlign: Towards Universal Truth Consistency in Personalized LLM Alignment

author.name: Thi-Nhung Nguyen, Linhao Luo, Rollin Omari, Junae Kim, Thuy-Trang Vu, Dinh Phung

entry.summary: TriAlign studies Truth-Invariant Alignment for personalized LLMs, aiming to keep universal truths consistent across social groups while preserving personalization, addressing fairness gaps where some groups receive less accurate responses. It proposes the first offline multi-agent RL framework for this problem.

entry.title: Does Compression Preserve Uncertainty? A Unified Benchmark for Quantized and Sparse LLMs via Conformal Prediction

author.name: Yujia Tong, Yuxi Wang, Yunyang Wan, Tian Zhang, Junhao Dong, Jingling Yuan

entry.summary: This benchmark study asks whether model compression (quantization, pruning) preserves uncertainty quantification, evaluating 12 LLMs across five NLP tasks using conformal prediction for distribution-free uncertainty measures. It finds compression frequently decouples accuracy from uncertainty and that larger models absorb compression-induced uncertainty better.

entry.title: AutoMedBench: Towards Medical AutoResearch with Agentic AI Models

author.name: Junqi Liu, Salena Song, Yuhan Wang, Jiawei Mao, Hardy Chen, Xiaoke Huang, Tianhao Qi, Pengfei Guo, Yucheng Tang, Yufan He, Can Zhao, Andriy Myronenko, Dong Yang, Daguang Xu, Yuyin Zhou

entry.summary: AutoMedBench is a workflow-aware benchmark for autonomous medical-AI research across imaging and multimodal tasks, organizing agent execution into five stages (Plan, Setup, Validate, Inference, Submit) with long-horizon tasks averaging 33 turns. It evaluates agent behavior within the research process rather than only final outputs.

entry.title: Extreme Low-Bit Inference in Reasoning Models: Failure Modes and Targeted Recovery

author.name: Ekaterina Alimaskina, Darya Rudas, Denis Shveykin, Gleb Molodtsov, Pavel Vasiliev, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: This paper shows that aggressive 2-bit quantization of large reasoning models can fail to deliver speedup because instability inflates token counts via repetitive loops, budget exhaustion, and unclosed reasoning, linking accuracy drops to process-level failures. It introduces lightweight FP16 plan-preserving controls for targeted recovery.

entry.title: Forget Attention: Importance-Aware Attention Is All You Need

author.name: Soohyeong Shin, Yeongwook Yang

entry.summary: Proposes SISA, a hybrid architecture that injects an SSM-derived importance signal directly inside the attention score, implemented as a single SDPA call without custom kernels or recurrent state. It aims to combine global retrieval of attention with prioritization signals of state space models.

entry.title: MCP-Persona: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Real-World Personal Applications via Environment Simulation

author.name: Wenhao Wang, Peizhi Niu, Gongyi Zou, Xiyuan Yang, Jingxing Wang, Haoting Shi, Yaxin Du, Jingyi Chai, Xianghe Pang, Shuo Tang, Yanfeng Wang, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: MCP-Persona is the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on real-world personalized MCP tools that interact with individual accounts and local databases, beyond generic information-seeking tools. It uses environment simulation across social and personal applications.

entry.title: Tracking the Behavioral Trajectories of Adapting Agents

author.name: Jonah Leshin, Manish Shah, Ian Timmis

entry.summary: Presents a framework for measuring agent traits by defining them as directions in text embedding space, training a linear model on labeled before-versus-after skill file diffs to score edits. It tracks behavioral trajectories of agents as their skill, memory, and config files evolve.

entry.title: A phenomenon of AI-conformity: how algorithms change human moral decision-making

author.name: Yana Venerina, Dmitry Koch, Nare Meloyan, Gerda Prutko, Valeriia Lelik, Victoria Taova, Andrey Kurpatov

entry.summary: Adapts the classic Asch conformity paradigm to study whether AI judgments shift human moral decision-making, finding evidence of algorithmic conformity across 165 participants under social-majority and AI conditions. It examines a poorly understood novel source of social influence.

entry.title: Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing

author.name: Michael Lan, Narmeen Fatimah Oozeer, Chaithanya Bandi, Philip Quirke, Austin Meek, Fazl Barez, Amirali Abdullah

entry.summary: A call-to-action arguing that mechanistic interpretability lacks standardized auditing systems, citing cases where conflicting MI conclusions stemmed from methodological inconsistencies. It proposes developing guidelines via continuous collaborative reviewing to enable safety-critical adoption.

entry.title: Planktonzilla: Multimodal dataset and models for understanding plankton ecosystems

author.name: Alan Gerson Contreras Montanares, Luis Valenzuela, Luis Mart\'i, Nayat Sanchez-Pi

entry.summary: Planktonzilla-17M is a unified dataset consolidating thirteen imaging systems into 17.4 million plankton images with standardized taxonomy and geo-environmental metadata, addressing failure of existing models to generalize across instruments. It supports marine ecosystem and climate research.

entry.title: CoCoVideo: The High-Quality Commercial-Model-Based Contrastive Benchmark for AI-Generated Video Detection

author.name: Huidong Feng, Wentao Chen, Jie Chen, Xinqi Cai, Ruolong Ma, Yinglin Zheng, Yuxin Lin, Ming Zeng

entry.summary: Introduces CoCoVideo-26K, a benchmark dataset built from commercial AI video generators (without watermarks) to improve detection of high-fidelity AI-generated video forgeries. It addresses a gap where prior datasets relied on lower-quality open-source models.

entry.title: Geometric Erasure by Contrastive Velocity Matching in Rectified Flows

author.name: Jonas Henry Grebe, Tobias Braun, Anna Rohrbach, Marcus Rohrbach

entry.summary: Introduces GEM, a concept-erasure framework for Rectified Flow Transformers that bridges trajectory-based unlearning (Generative Flow Networks) with teacher-guided erasure via contrastive velocity matching. It addresses safety in modern flow-based generative models.

entry.title: Learning to Construct Practical Agentic Systems

author.name: Aditya Kumar, Zhihan Lei, Jerry Yan, Joshua W. Momo, Lauhitya Reddy, Rafael Enrique Cabrera Jimenez, Cassandra A. Cohen, Arthur Kajiyama, William W. Cohen

entry.summary: Proposes principled approaches for designing practical agentic LLM systems prioritizing simplicity, controllability, and predictable inference cost using pseudo-tools that recursively call LLMs on restricted contexts. Argues hand-engineered modular agents can rival dynamically-planned workflows.

entry.title: BAGEN: Are LLM Agents Budget-Aware?

author.name: Yuxiang Lin, Zihan Wang, Mengyang Liu, Yuxuan Shan, Longju Bai, Junyao Zhang, Xing Jin, Boshan Chen, Jinyan Su, Xingyao Wang, Jiaxin Pei, Manling Li

entry.summary: Introduces BAGEN, a benchmark and formalization of budget-awareness in LLM agents, treating budget as an active control signal via progressive interval estimation of remaining budget. Finds frontier agents consistently fail at budget-awareness across four environments.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Temperature in Large Language Model Distillation

author.name: Hoang-Chau Luong, Lingwei Chen

entry.summary: Revisits the role of temperature in LLM distillation, showing temperature asymmetrically enriches forward KL with non-dominant token signals while merely rescaling reverse KL gradients, overturning the standard preference for RKL. It demonstrates FKL benefits much more from temperature scaling.

entry.title: Drift Q-Learning

author.name: Anas Houssaini, Mohamad H. Danesh, Amin Abyaneh, Scott Fujimoto, Hsiu-Chin Lin, David Meger

entry.summary: Proposes DriftQL for offline RL, combining a drift-based behavioral regularizer with critic-driven policy improvement to avoid out-of-distribution actions without the iterative denoising of diffusion/flow policies. Attraction and repulsion keep generated actions near the data while preventing mode collapse.

entry.title: A Distribution-Free Framework for Rewrite-Based Human-text Detection via Knockoff Filtering

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a distribution-free statistical framework that converts existing rewrite-based AI-text detectors into ones with finite-sample false discovery rate guarantees via knockoff filtering, without retraining. Validated across multiple models, domains, and LLMs.

entry.title: Skill or Skip? Learning Selective Skill Invocation in Agentic Tasks via Dual-Granularity Preference Learning

author.name: Chishui Chen, Jiaye Lin, Te Sun, Junxi Wang, Yi Yang, Cong Qin, Yangen Hu, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng

entry.summary: Proposes SelSkill, a dual-granularity preference learning framework that teaches agents not just which skill is relevant but whether it should be invoked at the current decision point. Uses uncertainty to prioritize decision points and constructs invoke-skip preference pairs.

entry.title: On the Difficulty of Learning a Meta-network for Training Data Selection

author.name: Zilin Du, Junqi Zhao, Boyang Albert Li

entry.summary: Analyzes why meta-learning for training-data selection (learning data weights via bi-level optimization) underperforms, identifying poor gradient signal-to-noise ratio and lack of informative quality-correlated features as obstacles. Provides mathematical analysis of normalized data weight dynamics.

entry.title: Pause and Think: A Dataset and Benchmark for Video-Grounded Assistive Action Suggestion

author.name: Shivam Singh, Saptarshi Majumdar, Pratik Prabhanjan, Zicheng Liu, Emad Barsoum

entry.summary: Introduces pause-and-think datasets and benchmark for video-grounded assistive action suggestion, training a compact 4B model to reason over visual evidence before answering. The model matches GPT-5.2 on scene understanding at 59x fewer parameters than Qwen3-VL-235B.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Conformal Prediction with Personalized Statistical Validity

author.name: Martin V. Vejling, Christophe A. N. Biscio, Adrien Mazoyer, Petar Popovski, Shashi Raj Pandey

entry.summary: Proposes PFWCP, a personalized federated weighted conformal prediction framework combining local density-ratio weighting with weighted quantile aggregation to handle limited data, privacy, and heterogeneity in multi-agent settings. Yields asymptotically valid personalized uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: EPIC: Efficient and Parallel Inference under CFG Constraints for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Hyundong Jin, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: Proposes EPIC, an efficient framework for context-free-grammar-constrained decoding in diffusion language models that preserves parallel decoding, addressing slowdowns up to 4x in prior constrained methods. Eliminates sequential validity-check overhead during parallel generation.

entry.title: SkyShield: Occupancy as a Safety Interface for Low-Altitude UAV Autonomy

author.name: Jie Gao, Jie Ma, Kaihui Lin, Kai Ye, Miaohui Zhang, Pingyang Dai, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: Introduces SkyShield, framing 3D occupancy as a safety interface for low-altitude UAV autonomy, and provides a dataset addressing the gap where existing benchmarks lack front-facing monocular occupancy under moving 6-DoF aerial poses. Targets sub-20-meter urban airspace navigation.

entry.title: GenPT: Beyond Self-Report for Reliable LLM Psychometrics via Generative Projective Testing

author.name: Ming Wang, Shuang Wu, Bixuan Wang, Lu Lin, Yuxin Chen, Xiaocui Yang, Daling Wang, Shi Feng, Yifei Zhang, Yufan Sun

entry.summary: Introduces GenPT, reformulating projective psychological tests (TAT, Rorschach, SCT) with newly generated stimuli into a structured pipeline to assess persona-conditioned LLM agents, overcoming training-corpus contamination and directional bias in self-report questionnaires. Derives standardized psychological indicators.

entry.title: Crazyflow: An Accurate, GPU-Accelerated, Differentiable Drone Simulator in JAX

author.name: Martin Schuck, Marcel P. Rath, Yufei Hua, AbhisheK Goudar, SiQi Zhou, Angela P. Schoellig

entry.summary: Introduces Crazyflow, a GPU-accelerated differentiable drone simulator in JAX achieving over an order of magnitude speedup versus existing simulators while supporting single-agent to multi-agent and model-based to data-driven methods. Aims to unify synthetic data generation for aerial robotics research.

entry.title: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models using Multi-Clip Video

author.name: Choongwon Kang, Seungjong Sun, Hyunmin Jun, Jang Hyun Kim

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Clip Video SafetyBench, a 2,920-video dataset showing that multimodal LLM jailbreak success increases with the number and diversity of video clips in an input. It exposes a novel video-specific safety vulnerability in MLLMs.

entry.title: Cross-modal linkage risk in clinical vision-language models

author.name: Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh, Mahshad Lotfinia, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn

entry.summary: Demonstrates a cross-modal linkage privacy risk in clinical vision-language models, where de-identified chest radiographs can be re-linked to their original reports via embedding cosine similarity. It audits this image-to-report retrieval risk across 406,241 pairs and clinically specialized VLMs.

entry.title: Policy and World Modeling Co-Training for Language Agents

author.name: Ning Lu, Baijiong Lin, Shengcai Liu, Jiahao Wu, Haoze Lv, Yanbin Wei, Lingting Zhu, Shengju Qian, Xin Wang, Ying-Cong Chen, Qi Wang, Ke Tang

entry.summary: Proposes PaW, a co-training framework that adds auxiliary world-modeling supervision to LLM agent policies during on-policy RL by exploiting the action-next-observation pairs already present in rollouts. It improves agents without separate simulators or extra inference cost.

entry.title: World Models: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Methodologies, Reasoning Paradigms, and Applications

author.name: Arif Hassan Zidan, Yi Pan, Hanqi Jiang, Ruiyu Yan, Wei Ruan, Zihao Wu, Lifeng Chen, Weihang You, Xinliang Li, Bowen Chen, Huawen Hu, Peilong Wang, Sizhuang Liu, Jing Zhang, Siyuan Li, Zhengliang Liu, Yu Bao, Lin Zhao, Lichao Sun, Dajiang Zhu, Xiang Li, Jinglei Lv, Quanzheng Li, Wei Liu, Tianming Liu, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of world models organized along a multi-axis taxonomy covering architecture, methodology, reasoning paradigms, and applications across RL, robotics, autonomous driving, and video generation. It aims to unify a fragmented field central to AGI pursuits.

entry.title: DAG-MoE: From Simple Mixture to Structural Aggregation in Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Jiarui Feng, Hanqing Zeng, Karish Grover, Ruizhong Qiu, Yinglong Xia, Qiang Zhang, Qifan Wang, Ren Chen, Dongqi Fu, Jiayi Liu, Zhoukai Zhao, Xiangjun Fan, Benyu Zhang, Yixin Chen

entry.summary: DAG-MoE explores aggregation as a new scaling axis for Mixture-of-Experts, replacing standard weighted-summation with structural aggregation that expands the expert-combination space without changing experts or router and enables multi-step reasoning within a single MoE layer. It is supported by theoretical analysis.

entry.title: SkillSmith: Co-Evolving Skills and Tools for Self-Improving Agent Systems

author.name: Yangbo Wei, Zhen Huang, Shaoqiang Lu, Junhong Qian, Qifan Wang, Chen Wu, Lei He

entry.summary: SkillSmith is a synergy-aware framework that co-evolves both skills and the underlying tool layer for self-improving agents, using atomic bundles that jointly modify skills and tools guided by a Lotka-Volterra-inspired ecological utility model. It enables repairing tool-level failures and reasoning about skill interactions.

entry.title: Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness: A Deterministic Recipe for Memory Conflict Resolution

author.name: Vikas Reddy, Sumanth Challaram

entry.summary: This work argues that memory-conflict resolution in LLM memory systems should be handled deterministically rather than delegated to the LLM, demonstrating large gains on MemoryAgentBench's FactConsolidation task where prior systems underperform. It proposes a deterministic recipe for resolving contradictory time-evolving facts.

entry.title: CAPF: Guiding Search-Agent Rollouts with Credit-Attenuated Privileged Feedback

author.name: Bin Chen, Xinye Liao, Yiming Liu, Xin Liao, Chonghan Liu

entry.summary: CAPF (Credit-Attenuated Privileged Feedback) provides training-time guidance for search agents on hard problems where end-to-end successful rollouts are rare, using verifier-side information to identify errors and guide in-rollout revision. It augments outcome-only RLVR with privileged feedback that attenuates with credit.

entry.title: WorldCoder-Bench: Benchmarking Physically Grounded 3D World Synthesis

author.name: Shuo Lu, Yinuo Xu, Kecheng Yu, Siru Jiang, Yongcan Yu, Yubin Wang, Haitao Yang, Yuxiang Zhang, Bin Wang, Ran He, Jian Liang

entry.summary: WorldCoder-Bench is a benchmark of 2,026 expert-curated tasks for autonomous physically-grounded 3D world synthesis in browser-native Three.js, evaluating beyond pixels/DOM by inspecting hidden runtime state. It covers simulation, rendering, and application tasks requiring spatial and physical constraint satisfaction.

entry.title: POIROT: Interrogating Agents for Failure Detection in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: I\~naki Dellibarda Varela, R. Sendra-Arranz, Pablo Romero-Sorozabal, J. M. Valverde-Garc\'ia, Annemarie F. Laudanski, \'Alvaro Guti\'errez, Eduardo Rocon, Manuel Cebrian

entry.summary: POIROT is a protocol that repurposes a multi-agent system's own agents as a distributed diagnostic layer for failure detection, leveraging existing epistemic diversity rather than centralized judgment. It outperforms single-LLM evaluator baselines with gains that scale with problem complexity.

entry.title: COMAP: Co-Evolving World Models and Agent Policies for LLM Agents

author.name: Youwei Liu, Jian Wang, Hanlin Wang, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: COMAP co-evolves textual world models and agent policies through closed-loop interaction, letting the world model adapt to on-policy state-action distributions of an evolving agent. It avoids dependence on external rewards or verifiers for agent improvement.

entry.title: HLL: Can Agents Cross Humanity's Last Line of Verification?

author.name: Xinhao Song, Su Su, Sirui Song, Hongliang Wu, Wen Shen, Zhihua Wei, Gongshen Liu, Linfeng Zhang, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: Introduces HLL, a controlled benchmark using interactive CAPTCHA verification to test whether multimodal agents can cross the human-verification boundary through grounded interaction rather than recognition alone. It probes whether agents can substitute for humans in deliberately automation-protected workflows.

entry.title: Aligning Cellular Sheaves with Classifier Attention for Interpretable Weakly-Supervised Pathology Localization

author.name: Devansh Lalwani, Swapnil Bhat, Maulik Shah

entry.summary: Aligns cellular sheaves with classifier attention for interpretable weakly-supervised tumor localization on whole-slide images, using sheaf structure to detect local disagreement on graph-structured data. It addresses the gap where attention-based MIL classifies correctly without firing on actual lesions.

entry.title: Bridging the 2D-3D Gap: A Hierarchical Semantic-Geometric Map for Vision Language Navigation

author.name: Kailing Li, Tianwen Qian, Lijin Yang, Yuqian Fu, Jingyu Gong, Xiaoling Wang, Liang He

entry.summary: HSGM transforms 3D geometric information into a structured representation compatible with VLMs for vision-language navigation, bridging the gap where VLMs excel at 2D but struggle with 3D spatial reasoning and action-transition causality. It targets unreliable zero-shot navigation.

entry.title: CoilDrop-MRI: Self-supervised physics-guided MRI reconstruction with coil dropout

author.name: Tongxi Song, Ziyu Li, Zihan Li, Wen Zhong, Congyu Liao, Yang Yang, Hua Guo, Wenchuan Wu, Qiyuan Tian

entry.summary: CoilDrop-MRI is a self-supervised physics-guided MRI reconstruction method that applies coil-wise dropout to inputs and uses dropped data as training targets, exploiting signal correlation across receiver coils. Unlike prior approaches that partition only in k-space, it leverages the previously unexplored coil dimension.

entry.title: StemBind: When MLLMs Get Lost Between Rules and Instances in Abstract Visual Reasoning

author.name: Xixiang He, Baiqi Wu, Xingming Li, Ao Cheng, Qiyao Sun, Xuanyu Ji, Qingyong Hu

entry.summary: Introduces StemBind, a shared-stem diagnostic benchmark for abstract visual reasoning that decomposes MLLM evaluation into Perception, Rule, and Full-answer questions on the same visual stem. It reveals MLLMs often know the rule but pick the wrong answer.

entry.title: Continuous Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action

author.name: Yueh-Hua Wu, Tatsuya Matsushima, Kei Ota

entry.summary: Argues that natural language is mismatched to fine-grained continuous control in vision-language-action models, and proposes continuous reasoning representations that are shareable, action-verifiable, and aligned with temporally extended control. Authors include researchers from Japanese robotics/AI labs.

entry.title: Bridging Reasoning Trajectories in On-Policy Distillation via Near-Future Guidance

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Francis Ferraro

entry.summary: Analyzes on-policy distillation for LLM reasoning, showing its token-level learning signal cannot reliably bridge student to teacher trajectories—about 30% of high-loss tokens are surface mismatches not real reasoning forks. Proposes near-future guidance to better repair divergent reasoning.

entry.title: COPF: An Online Framework for Deployment-Stable Counterfactual Fairness in Evolving Graphs

author.name: Sheng'en Li, Dongmian Zou

entry.summary: Introduces COPF, a decision-layer framework for deployment-stable counterfactual fairness monitoring in online link recommendation on evolving graphs, handling performative feedback via exposure counterfactuals and propensity logging. Addresses fairness drift after policy updates.

entry.title: WaveFilter: Enhancing the Long-Context Capability of Diffusion LLMs via Wavelet-Guided KV Cache Filtering

author.name: Jinnan Yang, Yan Wang, Zhen Bi, Kehao Wu, Xiaojie Li, Jungang Lou, Zechao Li, Jing Liu

entry.summary: Proposes WaveFilter, a training-free wavelet-based KV cache filtering framework to enhance long-context capability of diffusion LLMs by precisely identifying critical tokens. Addresses generation quality degradation from existing KV caching under long sequences.

entry.title: Behavior-Invariant Task Representation Learning with Transformer-based World Models for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fuyuan Qian, Menglong Zhang, Song Wang, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a framework integrating information-theoretic behavior-invariant task representation learning with a Transformer-based stochastic world model for offline meta-reinforcement learning. Addresses context and policy distribution shifts, especially under sparse rewards.

entry.title: Beyond Independent Manipulation: Individual Fairness-aware Strategic Classification with Peer Imitation

author.name: Xinpeng Lv, Chunyuan Zheng, Yunxin Mao, Renzhe Xu, Jinxuan Yang, Yuanlong Chen, Wangrong Huang, Shaowu Yang, Wenjing Yang, Xinwang Liu, Peng Cui, Haotian Wang

entry.summary: Studies individual fairness-aware strategic classification where agents' manipulations are interdependent through peer imitation, rather than the standard independent-response assumption. Introduces a formulation matching fairness-aware decision settings.

entry.title: Who Annotates in NLP? A Large-scale Assessment of Human Annotation Reporting between 2018 and 2025

author.name: Maria Kunilovskaya, Gagan Bhatia, Lisa Sophie Albertelli, Yanran Chen, Christian Greisinger, Lotta Kiefer, Christoph Leiter, Subhadeep Roy, Tewodros Achamaleh, Muhammad Arslan Manzoor, Sebastian Pohl, Yufang Hou, Steffen Eger

entry.summary: Conducts the first large-scale, task-level audit of human annotation reporting practices across major NLP venues from 2018-2025, introducing a taxonomy and an LLM-assisted extraction pipeline validated against a gold standard. It reveals which annotation details are routinely underreported.

entry.title: Ghost Tool Calls: Issue-Time Privacy for Speculative Agent Tools

author.name: Bardia Mohammadi, Lars Klein, Akhil Arora, Laurent Bindschaedler

entry.summary: Identifies ghost tool calls, where speculative future tool calls in latency-hiding agents leak inferred user intent to external services before the agent commits to a branch. Proposes Speculative Tool Privacy Contracts, a runtime abstraction treating pre-commitment observation as a first-class effect.

entry.title: MindZero: Learning Online Mental Reasoning With Zero Annotations

author.name: Shunchi Zhang, Jin Lu, Chuanyang Jin, Yichao Zhou, Zhining Zhang, Tianmin Shu

entry.summary: MindZero is a self-supervised RL framework that trains multimodal LLMs for online Theory-of-Mind reasoning without ground-truth mental-state annotations, rewarding hypotheses that maximize the likelihood of observed actions. It targets real-time, uncertainty-aware inference of human mental states for assistance.

entry.title: VESTA: Visual Exploration with Statistical Tool Agents

author.name: William Rudman, Abhishek Divekar, Kanishk Jain, Sebastian Joseph, Stella S. R. Offner, Matthew Lease, Kyle Mahowald, Greg Durrett, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: VESTA equips vision-language models with a dynamically growing toolkit of data transformations, hypothesis-driven visualizations, and robust statistical tests to iteratively propose and refine quantitative models from data. Unlike critique-only systems, it actively explores data before and during refinement.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory Risk-Aware Compression for Long-Horizon Agent Safety

author.name: Zhepei Hong, Lin Wang, Liting Li, Haokai Ma, Junfeng Fang, Fei Shen, Dan Zhang, Xiang Wang

entry.summary: TRACE reframes long-horizon LLM-agent safety detection as trajectory-level evidence compression, using a Compressor that encodes the full trajectory into a compact latent evidence state and a Reader that judges the raw trajectory with this reference. It aggregates sparse, delayed, compositional risk signals that escape turn-level moderation.

entry.title: Before the Model Learns the Bug:Fuzzing RLVR Verifiers

author.name: Jaideep Ray

entry.summary: This paper studies how buggy verifiers in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can teach models to exploit the bug, introducing a lightweight verifier-fuzzing framework that generates adversarial completions and compares buggy versus stricter reference verifiers. It reports false-positive, exploit, and disagreement metrics for reward-function reliability.

entry.title: The Shape of Wisdom: Decision Trajectories in Language Models

author.name: Shailesh Rana

entry.summary: An empirical study of 9,000 decision trajectories across three 7-8B instruction-tuned models on MMLU, tracking how answer margins evolve across layer depth. A key finding is that unstable-correct outcomes dominate over stable-correct, with attention contributing more directionally than MLPs.

entry.title: ANDES: Agent Native Data Evolving Synthesis Tool for Autonomous Instruction Alignment

author.name: Zhengyang Zhao, Shengjie Ye, Lu Ma, Hao Liang, Hengyi Feng, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: ANDES is an agent-native data synthesis tool that autonomously curates targeted instruction-alignment datasets from the open web, addressing context overload during long-horizon search, filtering, and balancing. It aims to enable agents to automate the post-training data curation phase.

entry.title: Recognize Your Orchestrator: An Entropy Dynamics Perspective for LLM Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Junze Zhu, Weihao Chen, Xuanwang Zhang, Zhen Wu, Xinyu Dai

entry.summary: This work introduces a Mean-Field Entropy Dynamics framework to analyze the fragility of centralized orchestration in multi-agent systems, modeling orchestration as competing forces of task resolution and context loading. It also presents Inverse Workflow Generation for synthesizing verifiable complex benchmarks.

entry.title: RoleCDE:Benchmarking and Mitigating Role-Alignment Trade-offs in Role-Playing Agents

author.name: Huayi Lai, Shichao Song, Simin Niu, Hanyu Wang, Jiawei Yang, Zhouxing Wang, Zhiqiang Yin, Xun Liang

entry.summary: RoleCDE is a benchmark of ~8k role profiles and ~24k dilemma instances designed to evaluate role-playing agents under structured conflicts between role-specific values and alignment constraints, beyond surface-level fidelity. It studies decision-making and value-conflict resolution under cognitive dilemmas.

entry.title: S-SPPO: Semantic-Calibrated Self-Play Preference Optimization

author.name: Xiwen Chen, Wenhui Zhu, Jingjing Wang, Peijie Qiu, Zhipeng Wang, Huayu Li, ZhengXiao He, Xuanzhao Dong, Prayag Tiwari, Mingkun Xu, Yujian Xiong, Feng Luo, Abolfazl Razi, Brendan Hogan Rappazzo, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka

entry.summary: S-SPPO addresses instability in Self-Play Preference Optimization where the preference oracle assigns overconfident wins to semantically indistinguishable responses, leading to policy degeneration. It proposes a dual-space semantic calibration framework to stabilize self-play preference learning.

entry.title: Consistency evaluation of benchmarks used for causal discovery

author.name: Yuzhe Zhang, Chihui Chen, Lina Yao, Chen Wang

entry.summary: This work is the first to systematically study the quality of benchmark causal graphs used in causal discovery, building a pipeline that retrieves relevant papers and prompts LLMs to check consistency between benchmarks and current literature. It highlights that misaligned benchmark knowledge especially affects LLM-based causal discovery evaluation.

entry.title: RuleEdit: Failure-Guided Human-AI Model Editing with Prospective Impact Preview

author.name: Min Hun Lee, Justin Yu Feng Teo

entry.summary: RuleEdit is an interactive human-AI model editing system that surfaces likely failures through rule-table mismatch signals and supports user-authored rule feedback with prospective previews of performance and embedding shifts. Evaluated in stroke rehabilitation assessment, it improved human-plus-AI performance by over 14 percent.

entry.title: SENSE: Semantic Embedding Navigation with Soft-gated Evaluation for Retrieval-based Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shaowen Chen, Zhicheng Liao, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: SENSE improves retrieval-based speculative decoding by anchoring retrieval on target-model hidden states for semantic alignment and using a soft-gated evaluation module to validate semantic equivalence beyond rigid lexical matching. It addresses brittleness to surface-level variations in RSD.

entry.title: Diffusion Image Generation with Explicit Modeling of Data Manifold Geometry

author.name: Duoduo Xue, Zhiyu Zhu, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: MIND is a diffusion image generation framework that explicitly models data manifold geometry by integrating discrete patch tokenization into the score function of a continuous diffusion model. It enables end-to-end differentiable training via a soft top-k aggregation mechanism with dual-branch high-frequency features.

entry.title: Automatically Differentiable Nonlinear Tensor Networks (ADNTNs) for Exponential Compression of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Andrzej Cichocki, Michal Wietczak
