entry.summary: Introduces Automatically Differentiable Nonlinear Tensor Networks (ADNTNs) as structured weight generators using hierarchical tensor cores with nonlinear activations for extreme neural network compression. Extends low-rank adaptation and tensor factorization using TTN, aTTN, and MERA architectures.

entry.title: BudgetDraft: Acceptance-Aware Multi-View Training for Sparse-KV Speculative Decoding

author.name: Liang He, Jingbo Wen, Qishi Zhan, Yixiong Chen, Kangning Cui, Qizhen Lan, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes BudgetDraft, a multi-view sparse-KV training method for speculative decoding that exposes the drafter to multiple KV budgets during training to maintain acceptance rates at mid-to-long context lengths. It addresses sparse/full cache mismatch under fixed memory budgets.

entry.title: DataShield: Safety-degrading Data Filtering for LLM Benign Instruction Fine-Tuning

author.name: Junbo Zhang, Qianli Zhou, Xinyang Deng, Wen Jiang, Jie Pan, Jinbiao Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes DataShield, an efficient method to identify safety-degrading samples within benign fine-tuning datasets by quantifying each sample's contribution to model compliance behavior via a compliance vector. It addresses safety erosion from benign fine-tuning.

entry.title: Real2SAM2Real: Generative 3D Caches as Complementary Context for Video Diffusion

author.name: Jiayi Wu, Haoming Cai, Cornelia Fermuller, Christopher Metzler, Yiannis Aloimonos

entry.summary: Proposes Real2SAM2Real, which uses 3D lifting models (e.g., SAM3D) to extract an explicitly editable 3D cache as a geometric scaffold for video diffusion models, improving camera/scene control. The holistic 3D volume prior reduces structural collapse during complex motion and occlusion.

entry.title: LLMs Need Encoders for Semantic IDs Too

author.name: Xiangyi Chen, Zelun Wang, Xinyi Li, Yi-Ping Hsu, Jaewon Yang, Jiajing Xu

entry.summary: Argues that Semantic IDs in generative recommendation are a distinct modality requiring dedicated encoders, like vision encoders for images, and proposes PrefixMem, a lightweight prefix n-gram memory encoder providing prefix-conditioned representations. It avoids relying on the LLM to learn context-dependent SID meanings from scratch.

entry.title: Improving Visual Representation Alignment Generation with GRPO

author.name: Shentong Mo, Sukmin Yun

entry.summary: Proposes VRPO, using GRPO-style reinforcement learning to adaptively optimize representation alignment in diffusion transformers, replacing static cosine or contrastive alignment objectives. Aims to dynamically balance representation consistency and generation quality.

entry.title: DASH: Dual-Branch Score Distillation for Guidance-Calibrated Compact Diffusion Models

author.name: Abdullah Al Shafi, Kazi Saeed Alam, Sk Imran Hossain, Engelbert Mephu Nguifo

entry.summary: Introduces DASH, a dual-branch distillation framework for compact class-conditional diffusion models that independently supervises both score branches to fix the underdetermined classifier-free guidance gap left by output-level distillation. Prevents degenerate solutions where guidance becomes ineffective.

entry.title: Certificates without Electrons? Theory and Evidence on Impacts from AI-Driven Power Demand

author.name: Dana Golden, Aruna Balasubramanian, Niranjan Balasubramanian

entry.summary: Develops a game-theoretic model of how data center carbon-neutrality instruments (RECs, PPAs, behind-the-meter colocation) interact with grid reliability, identifying a timing wedge between consumption and credited renewable generation that degrades reliability and increases emissions. Relevant to AI-driven power demand growth.

entry.title: SkillPager: Query-Adaptive Intra-Skill Navigation via Semantic Node Retrieval

author.name: Zicai Cui, Zihan Guo, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SkillPager, a two-stage framework that parses skill documents into typed semantic nodes offline and uses maximal marginal relevance for query-conditioned node selection online, achieving near-full-document sufficiency while cutting prompt tokens by 47%. Addresses token waste in skill-based LLM agents.

entry.title: From Cues to Horizons: Dynamic Risk Horizon Profiling for Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Xinyi Ning, Zilin Bian, Dachuan Zuo, Semiha Ergan, Kaan Ozbay

entry.summary: Proposes a risk horizon profiling module with a continuous learnable potential field for risk-aware vehicle trajectory prediction, incorporating future risk evolution and uncertainty rather than treating past risk as a secondary signal. Adaptively identifies relevant surrounding agents.

entry.title: How Hard Can It Be? Hardness-Aware Multi-Objective Unlearning

author.name: Jiangwei Chen, Xinyuan Niu, Rachael Hwee Ling Sim, Zhengyuan Liu, Nancy F. Chen, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low

entry.summary: Proposes a hardness-aware, theoretically grounded constrained-optimization approach to machine unlearning that quantifies the difficulty of jointly improving forget quality and retain utility via similarity measures. It offers per-data guarantees rather than aggregate loss weighting.

entry.title: SeClaw: Spec-Driven Security Task Synthesis for Evaluating Autonomous Agents

author.name: Hao Cheng, Changtao Miao, Tianle Song, Yin Wu, He Liu, Erjia Xiao, Junchi Chen, Xiaoyu Shi, Yichi Wang, Jing Yang, Taowen Wang, Jinhao Duan, Mengshu Sun, Peiyan Dong, Xuan Shen, Yang Cao, Renjing Xu, Kaidi Xu, Jindong Gu, Bo Zhang, Jize Zhang, Chenhao Lin, Philip Torr, Chao Shen

entry.summary: Introduces SeClaw, a framework combining specification-driven security task synthesis with execution-based evaluation for autonomous LLM agents in stateful environments. It enables scalable, controllable construction of security scenarios beyond manually curated tasks.

entry.title: AutoForest: Automatically Generating Forest Plots from Biomedical Studies with End-to-End Evidence Extraction and Synthesis

author.name: Massimiliano Pronesti, Angelo Miculescu, Mohsin Kapdi, Paul Flanagan, Ois\'in Redmond, Joao Bettencourt-Silva, Gurdeep Mannu, Spiros Denaxas, Rui Bebiano Da Providencia E Costa, Anya Belz, Yufang Hou

entry.summary: Introduces AutoForest, an end-to-end system automating the full pipeline from raw biomedical documents to synthesized forest plots, including evidence extraction, intervention definition, harmonization, and meta-analytic computation. It is the first to automate the complete systematic-review forest-plot workflow.

entry.title: Initialization is Half the Battle: Generating Diverse Images from a Guidance Potential Posterior

author.name: Xiang Li, Dianbo Liu, Kenji Kawaguchi

entry.summary: Identifies that standard Gaussian initialization causes generative model trajectories to collapse into dominant modes, and proposes DivIn, which samples initial noise from a guidance-potential posterior via Langevin dynamics to enhance diversity. It addresses mode collapse at the initialization stage rather than during generation.

entry.title: Mitigating Perceptual Judgment Bias in Multimodal LLM-as-a-Judge via Perceptual Perturbation and Reward Modeling

author.name: Seojeong Park, Jiho Choi, Junyong Kang, Seonho Lee, Jaeyo Shin, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: Identifies Perceptual Judgment Bias in multimodal LLM-as-a-judge evaluators, where they reward plausible text narratives over perceptually correct answers when visual and textual cues conflict. Introduces a perceptually perturbed counterfactual dataset and reward modeling to mitigate it.

entry.title: Adaptive Order Policies for Masked Diffusion

author.name: Jama Hussein Mohamud, Mohsin Hasan, Mirco Ravanelli, Yoshua Bengio

entry.summary: Proposes learning the unmasking order in masked diffusion models via a lightweight policy network with a reweighted loss that prefers positions where the denoiser is likely correct. It improves over random or heuristic unmasking orders for discrete sequence generation.

entry.title: Adversarially Robust Control of Conditional Value-at-Risk via Rockafellar-Uryasev Conformal Inference

author.name: Catherine Chen, Jingyan Shen, Zhun Deng, Lihua Lei

entry.summary: Presents an online, distribution-free framework for controlling Conditional Value-at-Risk in non-stationary and adversarial environments, combining conformal tail-risk control, online learning, and the Rockafellar-Uryasev CVaR variational representation. It provides adversarial regret guarantees for nonlinear tail-risk control.

entry.title: How Much Orthogonalization Does Muon Need?

author.name: Hua Huang

entry.summary: Investigates how much orthogonalization the Muon optimizer actually requires, using a relaxed cubic Newton-Schulz schedule with fewer matrix multiplications to probe the relationship between polar accuracy, spectral shaping, and training quality. It suggests Muon may need less precise orthogonalization than assumed.

entry.title: CAST: Non-Privileged Clipped Asymmetric Self-Teaching with Advantage Flipping for GRPO

author.name: Yang Li, Gongle Xue, Yijia Guo, Yuheng Yuan, Liwen Hu, Lei Ma

entry.summary: CAST improves GRPO-based RL for LLM reasoning by combining clipped asymmetric self-teaching with advantage flipping to address vanishing group-relative advantages when all sampled trajectories are uniformly correct or incorrect. It uses dense token-level guidance aligned with trajectory correctness via diagnostics on on-policy self-distillation noise.

entry.title: SDR: Set-Distance Rewards for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Halil Ibrahim Gulluk, Max Van Puyvelde, Wim Van Criekinge, Olivier Gevaert

entry.summary: SDR proposes set-to-set distance rewards for RL post-training of vision-language models in radiology report generation, treating reports as unordered sets of findings embedded by a frozen sentence transformer rather than causal reasoning chains. This yields continuous, permutation-invariant rewards better suited to clinical reports.

entry.title: ForeSci: Evaluating LLM Agents for Forward-Looking AI Research Judgment

author.name: Qiuyu Tian, Zequn Liu, Yingce Xia, Haojie Yin, Youyong Kong

entry.summary: ForeSci is a temporally controlled benchmark of 500 tasks across four AI domains for evaluating whether LLM agents can make forward-looking research judgments from pre-cutoff evidence, with post-cutoff papers hidden and used only for validation. It tests decisions like which bottleneck to attack or direction to pursue.

entry.title: Latent Reward Steering: An Adaptive Inference-Time Framework that Implicitly Promotes Cognitive Behaviors in Reasoning LLMs

author.name: Jiakang Li, Guanyu Zhu, Can Jin, Chenxi Huang, Dexu Yu, Ronghao Chen, Yang Zhou, Hongwu Peng, Xuanqi Lan, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Youhua Li

entry.summary: Latent Reward Steering is an adaptive inference-time framework that promotes cognitive behaviors in reasoning LLMs by optimizing sparse-autoencoder latent states that implicitly carry them, rather than relying on predefined behaviors or explicit steering directions. A latent reward model trained on traces by final-answer correctness estimates intermediate-state quality.

entry.title: SkillRevise: Improving LLM-Authored Agent Skills via Trace-Conditioned Skill Revision

author.name: Yuxuan Liu, Zhaochen Su, Lingyun Xie, Yuhao Zhang, Qing Zong, Jiahe Guo, Zhongwei Xie, Yiyan Ji, Yauwai Yim, Hongyu Luo, Xiyu Ren, Ruan Chenyu, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: SkillRevise proposes an execution-grounded framework that iteratively refines imperfect LLM-authored agent skills by diagnosing defects from execution traces, addressing the cold-start problem in self-evolving agents. It targets the gap where expert-authored skills are costly and one-shot generated skills are behaviorally weak.

entry.title: HomeFlow: A Data Flywheel for Smart Home Agent Training with Verifiable Simulation

author.name: Yi Gu, Huacan Wang, Shuo Zhang, Yuqing Hou, Lei Xue, Weipeng Ming, Chen Liu, Fangzhou Yu, Kuan Li, Ronghao Chen, Sen Hu, Xiaofeng Mou, Yi Xu

entry.summary: HomeFlow is a verifiable data flywheel for training smart-home agents, using a simulation environment (HomeEnv), procedural generation, and MCTS-based synthesis of verifiable multi-turn trajectories. It compiles open-ended user intents into executable success conditions.

entry.title: Self-Revising Discovery Systems for Science: A Categorical Framework for Agentic Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Fiona Y. Wang, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: This work develops a category-theoretic account of agentic scientific discovery for materials science, modeling system state as a copresheaf and discovery as verified regime transitions via left Kan extensions. It formalizes how representational schemas evolve while preserving provenance.

entry.title: Characterization of Multi-Model Agentic AI Systems on General Tasks via Trace-Driven Simulation

author.name: Donghwan Kim, Prakhar Singh, Younghoon Min, Jongryool Kim, Jongse Park, Kiwan Maeng

entry.summary: GAIATrace is the first token-level trace dataset of two state-of-the-art agentic systems (MiroThinker and OWL) running the GAIA benchmark, capturing full reasoning tokens and task structures for systems research. The trace-driven simulation enables characterization of multi-model agentic system behavior.

entry.title: Coordination Graphs for Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Santiago Amaya-Corredor, Miguel Calvo-Fullana, Anders Jonsson

entry.summary: Presents CG-CMARL, combining coordination graphs with Lagrangian duality to make constrained multi-agent RL scalable, decomposing the joint problem into pairwise regions with shared Q-functions. The number of learned models stays independent of agent count.

entry.title: BenHalluEval: A Multi-Task Hallucination Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models on Bengali

author.name: Shefayat E Shams Adib, Ahmed Alfey Sani, Ekramul Alam Esham, Ajwad Abrar, Ishmam Tashdeed, Md Taukir Azam Chowdhury

entry.summary: BenHalluEval is the first fine-grained hallucination evaluation framework for Bengali, covering four tasks and twelve hallucination types with 12,000 candidates, evaluating seven LLMs under a dual-track protocol. It fills a gap for the sixth most spoken language.

entry.title: CSRP: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Chinese Text Correction via Reinforcement Learning with Efficiency-Aware Rewards

author.name: Wei Tian, Yuhao Zhou, Man Lan

entry.summary: CSRP is a three-stage framework for Chinese grammatical error correction using continual pretraining, chain-of-thought SFT with explicit error reasoning, and GRPO with an efficiency-aware reward that penalizes unnecessary edits to reduce over-correction. It targets precision-focused metrics that standard SFT fails to optimize.

entry.title: Beyond Categories of Caste: Examining Caste Bias and Morality in Text-to-Image AI Models

author.name: Divyanshu Kumar Singh, Dipto Das, Deepika Rama Subramanian, Koustuv Saha, Stephen Voida, Bryan Semaan

entry.summary: Examines caste bias in text-to-image models by shifting from caste as an identity category to its relational aspect, combining algorithmic audit with critical discourse analysis. It develops a nuanced understanding of how caste discrimination operates through generative AI in South Asia.

entry.title: Business Utility of Large Language Models as Exploratory Data Analysis Agents

author.name: Rafa{\l} {\L}ab\k{e}dzki, Patryk Miziu{\l}a, Hubert Rutkowski, Szymon Betlewski, Cezary Depta, Szymon Janowski, Jaros{\l}aw Kochanowicz, Jan Kanty Milczek

entry.summary: Evaluates LLMs as exploratory data analysis agents in business settings using an agent-based supply chain simulation, assessing both average performance and repeatability across fifteen model-variant configurations from eight families. It identifies supplier-product combinations responsible for quality and sales loss from indirect operational traces.

entry.title: Hoeffding Concept Bottleneck Models with Applications to Overhead Images

author.name: Cl\'ement B\'enard, Manon Arfib, Christophe Labreuche, Victor Qu\'etu

entry.summary: Hoeffding Concept Bottleneck Models build on the Hoeffding functional decomposition to replace linear aggregation of concept scores with a nonlinear approach, reducing information leakage and improving explainability. Applied to overhead imagery classification with high-stakes decisions.

entry.title: Visual-Noise Guided In-Context Distillation for Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning

author.name: Junkai Chen, Yuhao He, Junxiang You, Ruiqi Liu, Chenyu Wang, Shu Wu

entry.summary: Presents a visual-noise guided in-context distillation method for unlearning sensitive knowledge from multimodal LLMs without retraining. It aims to balance unlearning effectiveness and model utility better than existing training-based or training-free approaches.

entry.title: Multi-Contrast MRI Motion Correction via Parameter-Informed Disentanglement and Adaptive Experts

author.name: Honglin Xiong, Yuxian Tang, Feng Li, Yulin Wang, Lei Xiang, Dinggang Shen, Qian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a unified multi-contrast MRI motion correction framework combining parameter-informed contrast disentanglement (ScanCLIP pretrained on 30k pairs) with severity-aware Mixture-of-Experts correction. It generalizes across modalities and artifact severities.

entry.title: RAFT: Data Refinement and Adaptive Distillation for Domain Fine-Tuning with Alleviated Forgetting

author.name: Yuduo Li, Xiaofeng Shi, Qian Kou, Longbin Yu, Hua Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes RAFT, a two-stage data refinement and adaptive distillation framework for domain fine-tuning that mitigates forgetting by addressing supervision-compatibility and trajectory-preservation gaps. It refines domain targets to match the model's natural style.

entry.title: Persona Attack: Incremental Memory Injection Jailbreak Attack against Large Language Models

author.name: Junyoung Park, Seongyong Ju, Sunghwan Park, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes Persona Attack, an incremental memory-injection jailbreak that manipulates LLM context windows step-by-step so accumulated injected instructions override safety alignment. It exploits conversational memory rather than single-prompt injection.

entry.title: ARCA: Adapter-Residual Credit Assignment When Token Signals Degenerate

author.name: Rodney Lafuente-Mercado

entry.summary: Introduces ARCA, analyzing how token-level credit assignment in LLM reinforcement learning degenerates under LoRA's low-rank constraint, where intrinsic credit signals become uniform or concentrate on task-agnostic positions. Proposes measuring and addressing this with adapter-residual signals.

entry.title: Hyperbolic and Evidence-Prioritized Experts for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zijie Zhou, Dandan Zhu, Hangxiangpan Wang, Heng Zhang, Huishen Jiao, Yi Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes hyperbolic and evidence-prioritized Mixture-of-Experts for large vision-language models, arguing visual and linguistic modalities have asymmetric, hierarchical structure better captured in hyperbolic space than Euclidean. It addresses containment relationships between text queries and visual scenes.

entry.title: GeoSAM-3D: Geodesic Prompt Propagation for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Segmentation from Monocular Video

author.name: Arun Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces open-vocabulary 3D scene segmentation from a single monocular video using frozen foundation models, Gaussian splatting reconstruction, and geodesic heat-kernel prompt propagation rather than Euclidean nearest neighbors. Reduces leakage across nearby discontinuous surfaces.

entry.title: MemGraphRAG: Memory-based Multi-Agent System for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Chuanjie Wu, Zhishang Xiang, Yunbo Tang, Zerui Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: Proposes MemGraphRAG, a memory-based multi-agent system for graph RAG that addresses fragmented, inconsistent knowledge graph construction by incorporating global corpus perspective. Aims for more coherent retrieval supporting complex reasoning.

entry.title: Collaborative Few-Step Distillation and Low-Bit Quantization for Wan2.2 Dual-Expert Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Jinyang Du, Shenghao Jin, Ziqian Xu, Ruihao Gong, Shiqiao Gu, Yang Yong, Jinyang Guo, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a deployment-oriented compression pipeline for the Wan2.2 dual-expert video diffusion model combining few-step distribution-matching distillation with low-bit quantization, calibrating high- and low-noise branches separately. Reduces denoising steps and parameter footprint for cheaper deployment.

entry.title: GIRL-DETR: Gradient-Isolated Reinforcement Learning for Video Moment Retrieval

author.name: Shihang Zhang, Mingjin Kuai, Ye Wei, Zhen Zhang, Wei Ji

entry.summary: Proposes GIRL-DETR, applying gradient-isolated reinforcement learning post-training to video moment retrieval to optimize non-differentiable localization metrics without disrupting fragile supervised features in lightweight networks. Addresses optimization stagnation from surrogate-metric mismatch.

entry.title: MLLM-Microscope: Unlocking Hidden Structure Within Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Ravil Mussabayev, Rustam Mussabayev

entry.summary: Presents MLLM-Microscope, a system analyzing hidden representations in multimodal LLMs by measuring linearity, intrinsic dimension, and anisotropy of token embeddings across layers for LLaVA-NeXT and OmniFusion on ScienceQA. Reveals architecture-specific differences in image-token geometry.

entry.title: Computation-Aware Kalman Filtering with Model Selection for Neural Dynamics

author.name: JR Huml, Jonathan Wenger, John P. Cunningham

entry.summary: Extends computation-aware Kalman filtering to include model selection, with a novel training loss and optimization scheme for tractable inference in large state-space models of single-cell neural recordings. Bridges Bayesian uncertainty quantification with the scalability needed for modern neural datasets.

entry.title: MURMUR: An Efficient Inference System for Long-Form ASR

author.name: Wei-Tzu Lee, Keisuke Kamahori, Baris Kasikci

entry.summary: Murmur is an inference system for long-form ASR that overcomes the accuracy-latency trade-off by operating at inter-chunk and intra-chunk levels, treating chunk size as a tunable hyperparameter. Combines benefits of chunk-based parallelism with long-context accuracy.

entry.title: The Role of Ambiguity in Error Prediction via Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Ieva Raminta Stali\=unait\.e, James Bishop, Andreas Vlachos

entry.summary: Studies how input ambiguity confounds uncertainty quantification when predicting LLM errors, showing UQ metrics predict errors better on unambiguous questions. Proposes disentangling aleatoric ambiguity from epistemic uncertainty using gated experts and selective prediction.

entry.title: Faster Synchronous On-Policy RL via Straggler-Aware Group Sizing

author.name: Azal Ahmad Khan, Ammar Ahmed, Zeshan Fayyaz, Sheng Di, Mingyi Hong, Ali Anwar

entry.summary: Proposes SAGC, a straggler-aware dynamic group-size controller for synchronous on-policy RL like GRPO, framing group sizing as online constrained optimization to reduce synchronization stalls. It speeds up wall-clock training while retaining the benefits of larger groups.

entry.title: PaSBench-Video: A Streaming Video Benchmark for Proactive Safety Warning

author.name: Yusong Zhao, Yuejin Xie, Youliang Yuan, Junjie Hu, Jitian Guo, Yujiu Yang, Pinjia He

entry.summary: Presents PaSBench-Video, a 740-video benchmark for proactive safety warning by video MLLMs, with frame-level risk onset and accident boundary annotations across driving, healthcare, daily life, and industrial domains. It tests timing-precise causal warning ability and false positives on safe scenes, which prior benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: LithoGRPO: Fast Inverse Lithography via GRPO Reinforced Flow Matching

author.name: Yao Lai, Xuyuan Xiong, Zeyue Xue, Guojin Chen, Jing Wang, Xihui Liu, Rui Zhang, Robert Mullins, Bei Yu, Ping Luo

entry.summary: Introduces LithoGRPO, an inverse lithography framework integrating flow matching with GRPO reinforcement learning fine-tuning to generate optimized photomasks guided by explicit physical metrics. It enables efficient exploration of diverse mask designs for semiconductor manufacturing.

entry.title: A Pre-Training Analogue of Grokking in Language Models: Tracing Delayed Grammatical Generalization

author.name: Sherin Muckatira, Namrata Shivagunde, Vijeta Deshpande, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Proposes an exposure-based framework to study grokking-like delayed grammatical generalization during LLM pretraining (rather than multi-epoch supervised settings), grounded in BLiMP minimal pairs and critical-phrase exposure tracking. It traces when grammatical phenomena generalize relative to data exposure.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Neural Activation Control in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Abhijith Babu, Ramneet Kaur, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Olivera Kotevska, Susmit Jha, Yanzhao Wu, Sumit Kumar Jha, Anirban Roy

entry.summary: CTRL-STEER replaces fixed-coefficient activation steering in Vision-Language-Action models with adaptive, time-varying closed-loop control signals, decoupling representation from regulation. This reduces overcorrection and oscillation when steering temporal embodied behaviors like speed and smoothness.

entry.title: Diagnosing LLM Arbitration Behavior over Pre-evidence Epistemic States in RAG-based Fact-Checking

author.name: Yuxi Sun, Wenbo Shang, Wei Gao, Xin Huang, Jing Ma

entry.summary: PAVE is a diagnostic testbed that stratifies an LLM verifier into four epistemic states by the correctness and confidence of its pre-evidence prior and measures how it arbitrates between parametric knowledge and retrieved context in RAG-based fact-checking. It assesses whether verifiers persist in correct priors under misleading evidence.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Sustain Long-Horizon Organizational Dynamics?

author.name: Xuancheng Zhu, Yang Yue, Shuaibing Wan, Zihan Dou, Xiaohan Zhang, Yongrui Liu, Guoshun Nan

entry.summary: TaskWeave is a hierarchical agentic framework that frames long-horizon organizational simulation as a memory-centered coordination problem, using a Formulate-Partition-Diagnose-Align cycle with dependency-aware trace memory. It is evaluated in a year-long simulated IT company against other multi-agent frameworks.

entry.title: Revisiting Ripple Effects in Knowledge Editing through Pressure-Aware Joint Neighborhood Optimization

author.name: Haoben Huang, Shuxin Liu, Ou Wu, Di Gao

entry.summary: This paper revisits ripple effects in knowledge editing by jointly modeling desirable propagation to related facts and unintended perturbation of preserved ones, identifying two coupled design pressures. It proposes Joint Neighborhood Optimization with Pressure-Aware Coordination at the target-planning stage.

entry.title: Stochastic convergence of parallel asynchronous adaptive first-order methods

author.name: Serge Gratton, Philippe L. Toint

entry.summary: This paper introduces a class of asynchronous adaptive first-order optimization methods including momentum and inexact normalization variants, with stochastic convergence analysis on non-convex functions at order O(1/sqrt(t)). Experiments suggest relevance for heterogeneous large-scale ML systems.

entry.title: SMH-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Environment-Grounded Reasoning and Action in Smart Homes

author.name: Kuan Li, Shuo Zhang, Huacan Wang, Fangzhou Yu, Zecheng Sheng, Yi Gu, Weipeng Ming, Lei Xue, Chen Liu, Sen Hu, Ronghao Chen, Siyue Lin, Yuqing Hou, Xiaofeng Mou, Yi Xu

entry.summary: SMH-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark of 1,100 tasks across 7 categories built on the executable HomeEnv simulator to evaluate whether LLMs can reason, interact, and act reliably in realistic smart-home scenarios with multi-device interactions. It stratifies tasks by difficulty beyond static instruction-to-API mapping.

entry.title: Bridging the Last Mile of Time Series Forecasting with LLM Agents

author.name: Yuhua Liao, Zetian Wang, Qiangqiang Nie, Zhenhua Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates last-mile forecasting where statistical forecasts must be revised using weakly structured business context like holidays, campaigns, and expert feedback, and presents an LLM-agent framework on top of a forecasting backbone. It addresses an underexplored practical stage in real-world forecasting.

entry.title: AEyeDE: An Attention-Based Attribution Framework for AI-Generated Text Detection

author.name: Aria Nourbakhsh, Adelaide Danilov, Christoph Schommer, Salima Lamsiyah

entry.summary: AEyeDE detects AI-generated text using model attention as a discriminative signal, extracting attention-based attribution matrices via a proxy Transformer with white-box access and training a lightweight CNN on these maps. It outperforms text-only baselines across translation and decoder-only settings.

entry.title: Understanding Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Documentation: A Paired Comparison of Ambient AI Drafts and Clinician Finalized Notes

author.name: Yiliang Zhou, Yawen Guo, Sairam Sutari, Jasmine Dhillon, Alexandra L. Beck, Emilie Chow, Steven Tam, Danielle Perret, Deepti Pandita, Gelareh Sadigh, Archana J. McEligot, Kai Zheng

entry.summary: Quantifies stigmatizing language changes between ambient AI clinical note drafts and clinician-finalized notes across over 66,000 paired sections using a lexicon-based NLP pipeline. It finds 21.4 percent of AI drafts contained stigmatizing language and analyzes removal versus introduction patterns.

entry.title: CLSP-REQA: A Real-Time Quality-Aware Closed-Loop Seizure Prediction Framework with Mamba-BiLSTM and Confidence-Gated Intervention

author.name: Mufeng Chen, Qi Wu, Bingchao Huang, Xiwen Lai, Zekai Chen, Xinge Ouyang, Quansheng Ren

entry.summary: CLSP-REQA is a closed-loop seizure prediction framework embedding a lightweight real-time EEG quality estimator within a Mamba-BiLSTM pipeline, modulating output confidence via a tiered fusion function. It addresses EEG signal-quality variability ignored by methods using non-strict evaluation protocols.

entry.title: Structured Visual Evidence Decomposition for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Screening of Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome

author.name: Chen Zhan, Yingchen Wei, Xiaoyu Tan, Jingjing Huang, Xihe Qiu

entry.summary: EviOSAHS is an evidence-grounded multimodal reasoning framework for obstructive sleep apnea screening that decomposes frontal facial images into seven fixed anatomical queries producing structured evidence cards before clinical adjudication. It separates image-only evidence acquisition from final decision to improve calibration.

entry.title: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs on Code Generation for Complex Interactive Webpages

author.name: Fan Wu, Lishuai Dong, Cuiyun Gao, Yujia Chen, Yiming Huang, Yang Xiao, Qing Liao

entry.summary: Benchmarks multimodal LLMs on generating code for complex interactive (not just static) webpages, evaluating interaction consistency beyond visual fidelity and code structure. It addresses a gap in front-end code generation evaluation.

entry.title: Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems

author.name: Xiangyu Wang, Yawen He, Shivendra Pratap Singh, Han Huang, Mengtong Hu, Sharath Ciddu, Yi-Hsuan Hsieh, Erik Groving, Yi Ding, Jieming Di, Tony Wang, Min Yun, Xiaoyu Chen, Ling Leng, Rob Malkin

entry.summary: Introduces SCALR, a framework generating synthetic cross-domain user-item interaction events for large-scale recommendation, inspired by synthetic-data success in LLMs. It decomposes cross-domain learning into event translation and target-domain learning to combat data sparsity.

entry.title: Interpretable Policy Distillation for Power Grid Topology Control

author.name: Aleksandra Dmitruka, Karlis Freivalds

entry.summary: Distills a PPO deep RL agent for power grid topology control into compact decision tree and random forest surrogates that match or exceed the teacher in reward and survival while being interpretable and cheap to deploy. Tested on Grid2Op's 14-bus environment.

entry.title: When Do Attention Circuits Form? Developmental Trajectories of Capability and Attention-Sink Emergence Across Three 1B-ClassArchitectures

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Tracks the developmental emergence of attention-head circuits (induction, previous-token, BOS-attractor) across three 1B-class models spanning dense and MoE architectures and two corpora, using participation-ratio and selectivity screens. Reports findings such as a layer-0/1 zero-BOS architectural floor.

entry.title: AdaCodec: A Predictive Visual Code for Video MLLMs

author.name: Haowen Hou, Zhen Huang, Zheming Liang, Qingyi Si, Chenglin Li, Shuai Dong, Kele Shao, Ruilin Li, Dianyi Wang, Nan Duan, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes AdaCodec, a predictive visual code interface for video MLLMs that spends full visual tokens on a reference frame only when its conditional predictive cost is high and otherwise encodes compact inter-frame changes. It exploits temporal redundancy to reduce repeated visual tokens.

entry.title: Balancing Learning Rates Across Layers: Exact Two-Step Dynamics and Optimal Scaling in Linear Neural Networks

author.name: Tianyu Pang, Vignesh Kothapalli, Shenyang Deng, Haohui Wang, Dawei Zhou, Yaoqing Yang

entry.summary: Derives exact closed-form gradients and test loss after one and two gradient-descent steps in two- and three-layer linear networks learning linear targets, characterizing optimal layer-wise learning-rate scaling. It reveals an early-training regime where unequal learning rates minimize loss.

entry.title: GLENS: Global Search via Learning from Solver Iterates with Diffusion Models

author.name: Anjian Li, Bartolomeo Stellato, Ryne Beeson

entry.summary: Proposes GLENS, a diffusion-model method that learns from intermediate solver iterates (not just final optima) to generate diverse, high-quality initial guesses for multimodal non-convex optimization. It produces starting points that converge quickly and represent many distinct local minima.

entry.title: Evaluating Bivariate Causal Statements Based on Mutual Compatibility

author.name: Erik Jahn, Dominik Janzing

entry.summary: This paper develops methods to evaluate collections of bivariate causal statements for mutual compatibility, introducing a compatibility score that flags implausible induced multivariate models requiring excessive confounding, without relying on faithfulness. It also defines an incompatibility score for purely graphical statements.

entry.title: TAPS: Target-Aware Prefix Tree Selection for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding

author.name: Zhuoyu Wang, Junnan Huang, Xinyu Chen

entry.summary: TAPS improves diffusion-drafted speculative decoding by selecting draft-tree nodes based on prefix-conditioned reachability rather than marginal probability, avoiding verification of unreachable descendants of rejected prefixes. This raises acceptance length per target-model call to reduce inference latency.

entry.title: Probe Before You Edit: Probing-Guided Molecular Optimization for LLM Agents in Structure-Based Drug Design

author.name: Zaifei Yang, Weiyu Chen, Yaqing Wang, James Kwok

entry.summary: This work introduces probing-guided molecular optimization for LLM agents in structure-based drug design, using diagnostic metrics to expose that agents edit ligands without understanding how the pocket-ligand complex responds, causing rare joint improvement of binding affinity and druggability. Probing pocket responses before editing aims to fix this failure mode.

entry.title: TriLens: Per-Layer Logit-Lens Entropy for White-Box Hallucination Detection

author.name: Bohan Yang, Yijun Gong, Zhi Zhang, Ge Zhang, Wenpeng Xing, Meng Han

entry.summary: TriLens is a white-box hallucination detector that reads per-layer entropy from the self-attention output, feed-forward output, and residual stream via the model's logit lens, producing a compact entropy trajectory describing how certainty forms across depth. It avoids storing high-dimensional hidden states or sampling multiple generations.

entry.title: SIRIUS-SQL: Anchoring Multi-Candidate Text-to-SQL in Execution Feedback

author.name: Leo Luo, Haining Xie, Siqi Shen, Zhipeng Ma, Rui Ling, Hang Xu, Hefeng Jiang, Dingwei Chen, Yang Li, Peng Chen, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: SIRIUS-SQL improves multi-candidate text-to-SQL by anchoring candidate generation and selection in execution feedback, addressing redundancy in sampling, undifferentiated error correction, and single-angle selection. It applies targeted correction based on the type of execution failure.

entry.title: Early Diagnosis of Wasted Computation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Failure-Aware Observability

author.name: Xianyou Li, Weiran Yan, Yichao Wu, Penghao Liang, Mengwei Yuan, Jianan Liu, Jing Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a failure-aware observability framework to diagnose wasted computation in tool-using multi-agent LLM traces, mapping recurring failure modes to online trace signals like tool reliability and budget pressure. It is evaluated on a three-agent QA system over GAIA validation tasks.

entry.title: Transferring Information Across Interventions in Causal Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Mohammad Ali Javidian

entry.summary: Graph-coupled causal Bayesian optimization ties intervention effects together via shared causal mechanisms rather than learning each in isolation, improving sample efficiency. It leverages a known causal graph and observational data to inform which interventions to perform.

entry.title: Evidence-Gated LLM Priors for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Jiangyu Chen, Banyi

entry.summary: This paper studies using LLM-generated expert priors in discrete multi-objective Bayesian optimization without blindly trusting them, proposing an objective-wise reputation-market mechanism that treats each expert-objective pair as a falsifiable source. Expert weights update online from observed objective values.

entry.title: OctoT2I: A Self-Evolving Agentic Text-to-Image Router

author.name: Xu Jiang, Bin Chen, Gehui Li, Yule Duan, Ronggang Wang, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: OctoT2I is a self-evolving agentic text-to-image router that reformulates T2I as joint optimization of generation quality and inference efficiency, using a stateful multi-round routing strategy to adaptively select among diverse models. It avoids reliance on expensive handcrafted priors or human annotations.

entry.title: eMoT: evolving Memory-of-Thought via Symbolic Anchoring and Memory Corrosion

author.name: Xiang Li, Jiwei Wei, Ke Liu, Yitong Qin, Jinyu Guo, Malu Zhang, Peng Wang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: eMoT (evolving Memory-of-Thought) stabilizes multi-step LLM reasoning by treating reasoning trajectories as dynamic evolving memories rather than static templates, using symbolic anchoring and a memory corrosion mechanism. It targets hallucinations and poor numerical computation in reasoning.

entry.title: Toward Robust In-Context Learning: Leveraging Out-of-distribution Proxies for Target Inaccessible Demonstration Retrieval

author.name: Hao Xu, Rite Bo, Fausto Giunchiglia, Yingji Li, Rui Song

entry.summary: DOPA is a demonstration retrieval framework for in-context learning that uses an out-of-distribution proxy to approximate inaccessible target domains and guide selection of distributionally similar examples. It addresses robustness degradation under severe distribution shift when the target domain is unknown.

entry.title: Examine Clinicians' Modification of Hedging Language in Ambient AI Documentation: A Comparative Study of AI Drafts and Final Notes

author.name: Yiliang Zhou, Yawen Guo, Di Hu, Sairam Sutari, Emilie Chow, Steven Tam, Danielle Perret, Deepti Pandita, Kai Zheng

entry.summary: Conducts a paired analysis of clinician-edited ambient AI documentation drafts versus final notes to examine how edits alter hedging language, across over 62,000 paired sections. It finds hedging is more often introduced into previously non-hedged text than removed.

entry.title: Measuring and Mitigating Bias in Code Generated by Large Language Models

author.name: Yuxi Chen, Yutian Tang, Timothy Storer

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for measuring bias in code generated by GPT-4o and Gemini using a code bias score and attribute change ratio, examining protected attributes, prompts, and web-search effects. It evaluates four lightweight mitigation strategies including few-shot and chain-of-thought.

entry.title: Rare Events, Real Signals: Functional Ensembles as Units of Computation in Deep Spiking Networks

author.name: Aditi Aravind, Konstantinos Ladakis, Mario Alexios Savaglio, Stelios M. Smirnakis, Maria Papadopouli

entry.summary: Introduces a neuroscience-inspired framework analyzing deep spiking neural networks through functional connectivity, forming first-order functionally-connected neuron groups based on statistically significant pairwise correlations. It shows biological-cortex connectivity principles are preserved in spiking ResNet architectures.

entry.title: Can Predicted Dynamics Exist in the Physical World?

author.name: Barak Or

entry.summary: Formulates physical admissibility as a prediction-control interface where decoded proposals from Physical AI systems are evaluated against kinematic, dynamic, and horizon conditions before execution, since low RMSE does not imply physical executability. Demonstrated on LeRobot PushT with controlled falsification.

entry.title: Versatile Framework with Semantic and Structural guidance for Image Reconstruction from Brain Activity

author.name: Yizhuo Lu, Changde Du, Qiongyi Zhou, Liuyun Jiang, Huiguang He

entry.summary: Presents a framework for reconstructing visual stimuli from brain recordings that adds structural guidance (position, orientation, size) alongside semantic guidance to improve fine-grained fidelity. It enhances controllability of brain-to-image decoding.

entry.title: MyoSem: Aligning Electromyography to Natural-Language Action Semantics for Hand Action Understanding

author.name: Chiyue Wang, Dong She, Yang Gao, Zhanpeng Jin

entry.summary: Presents MyoSem, an EMG-to-action-semantics alignment framework that maps EMG signals into a shared semantic space built from multi-view action descriptions, enabling bidirectional retrieval between signals and text. It moves beyond fixed-label classification toward open-vocabulary hand action understanding.

entry.title: Isolating LLM Lexical Bias: A Curation-Free Triangulated Metric for Preference-Stage Learning

author.name: Xiaoyang Ming, Jose Hernandez, Thomas Stephan Juzek

entry.summary: Proposes a curation-free triangulated metric to isolate LLM lexical bias (e.g., overuse of words like delve, furthermore) introduced during preference-learning stages such as RLHF. It avoids reliance on manual curation to measure preference-stage lexical misalignment.

entry.title: (HB-ARFM) History-Bootstrapped Flow Matching for Inverse Boiling Reconstruction

author.name: Xianwei Zou, Sheikh Md Shakeel Hassan, Arthur Feeney, Aparna Chandramowlishwaran

entry.summary: Proposes HB-ARFM, a history-bootstrapped autoregressive flow-matching method for reconstructing spatiotemporal fields (e.g., boiling, atmospheric states) from partial observations. It uses observation history to address the non-Markovian posterior induced by partial observability.

entry.title: Richer Representations for Neural Algorithmic Reasoning via Auxiliary Reconstruction

author.name: Jiafu Huang, Chao Peng, Chenyang Xu, Zhengfeng Yang, Kecheng Cai, Chenhao Zhang, Yi Wang, Yiwei Gong, Wanqin Zhou, Irene Zheng

entry.summary: Improves neural algorithmic reasoning by adding auxiliary reconstruction to enrich state representations in the encoder-processor-decoder framework, shifting focus from the typically-studied processor to representation quality. Aims to better replicate classical algorithm execution.

entry.title: Dive into Waves: Morlet Spectral Transformer for Cross-Subject Emotion Decoding from EEG

author.name: Jiaxin Qing, Lexin Li

entry.summary: Proposes the Morlet Spectral Transformer for cross-subject EEG emotion decoding, addressing the weak, noisy, spectrally-encoded nature of emotion signals with band-specific spatial modeling and improved frequency tokenization. Targets challenges of subject variability in brain-computer interfaces.

entry.title: Order within Chaos: Capturing Intrinsic Energy Anomalies for AI-Manipulated Image Forgery Localization

author.name: Yiming Wang, Baiqi Wu, Qingming Li, Jiahao Chen, Tong Zhang, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: Proposes FLAME, a forgery localization framework for AI-manipulated images that exploits a theoretically derived statistical energy gap from diffusion-suppressed high-frequency variance, using a SAM adapter for pixel-level detection. It targets detecting synthetic edits that evade noise-based methods.

entry.title: Learning When to Translate for Multilingual Reasoning

author.name: Deokhyung Kang, Hyounghun Kim, Gary Geunbae Lee

entry.summary: Proposes Luar, a reinforcement-learning framework that trains reasoning LLMs to selectively invoke English translation only when direct understanding of non-English input is unreliable. It reduces unnecessary translation while closing multilingual reasoning gaps.

entry.title: Inner Product Aware Quantization: Provably Fast, Accurate, and Adaptive Algorithms

author.name: Nathan White, Krish Singal

entry.summary: Develops inner-product-aware quantization schemes that approximately preserve inner products with unseen vectors rather than minimizing mean-squared error, with provably fast, accurate, adaptive, and unbiased algorithms. It connects to adaptive stochastic quantization theory.

entry.title: FLaG: Fine-Grained Latent Grouping for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Wentao Ye, Liyao Li, Zhiqing Xiao, Muzhi Zhu, Jiaqi Hu, Zhanming Shen, Xiaomeng Hu, Sean Du, Haobo Wang

entry.summary: Proposes FLaG, a lightweight hallucination detection framework that models correctness via latent evidence groups, softly routing instances through an energy-based mechanism and aggregating group-conditional reliability signals. It treats hallucination detection as mechanism-aware evidence aggregation across heterogeneous failure modes.

entry.title: TIGER: Traceable Inference with Graph-Based Evidence Routing for Mitigating Hallucinations in Multimodal Generation

author.name: Kaixiang Zhao, Tianrun Yu, Shawn Huang, Porter Jenkins, Yushun Dong, Amanda Hughes

entry.summary: TIGER is an inference-time framework for fact-level repair in multimodal generation that independently builds an observation graph from input and a claim graph from output, scoring each claim's risk by support and conflict. This avoids hallucinated claims biasing input interpretation and enables fact-level ranking of repairs.

entry.title: From "Weak" Signals to Strong Models: Preference Delta Aggregation with LoRA Merging

author.name: Qi Sun, Siyue Zhang, Yulin Chen, Yuxiang Xue, Ru Peng, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: Preference Delta Aggregation derives preference signals from weak-weaker model pairs, instantiates each as a LoRA adapter via preference optimization, and aggregates them via LoRA merging to improve a stronger model. It explores whether multiple weak supervision signals can be constructively combined.

entry.title: Threshold-Based Exclusive Batching for LLM Inference

author.name: Weifang Zhang, Yuzhou Nie, Bowen Pang, Guangrui Ma, Shining Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that prefill-decode interference makes mixed batching's marginal cost exceed pure decode, with the crossover threshold depending heavily on GPU memory bandwidth (80% on H200 vs 20% on bandwidth-constrained RTX PRO 6000). It derives a closed-form rule for choosing between mixed and exclusive batching for LLM inference.

entry.title: Efficient Test-time Inference for Generative Planning Models

author.name: Robert Gieselmann, Mihai Samson, Federico Pecora, Jeremy L. Wyatt

entry.summary: This paper shows a modified classical Open-Closed List search provides efficient test-time inference for generative planning models, combining a generative model for fast rollouts with a learned heuristic to prioritize reasoning paths. Novel exploration-control mechanisms optimize the inference process rather than just scaling compute.

entry.title: Brain-Atlas-Guided Generative Counterfactual Attention for Explainable Cognitive Decline Diagnosis Using Multimodal Connectomes

author.name: Xiongri Shen, Jiaqi Wang, Zhenxi Song, Yi Zhong, Leilei Zhao, Xin He, Baiying Lei, Zhiguo Zhang

entry.summary: GCAN is an atlas-knowledge-guided generative counterfactual attention network for explainable diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment and subjective cognitive decline using multimodal brain connectomes. It formulates diagnosis as source-to-target counterfactual connectome generation.

entry.title: Dive into Ambiguity: A*-Inspired Multi-Agents Commonsense Obfuscation Attack on LLM Prompts

author.name: Boxuan Wang, Zhuoyun Li, Xiaowei Huang, Yi Dong

entry.summary: This paper proposes an A*-inspired multi-agent framework that generates semantically aligned yet obfuscated prompts to induce commonsense hallucinations in LLMs, using a hierarchical rewrite strategy with a dynamic semantic dispersion coefficient. It targets factual reliability vulnerabilities in safety-critical settings.

entry.title: TERRA: Task-Embedded Reasoning and Representation Architecture for Cross-Domain Applications

author.name: Shayan Shokri

entry.summary: TERRA proposes a single action-conditioned latent predictive architecture trainable across structured-state domains (driving, robotics, finance) and formally studies when representations transfer between structurally analogous but unrelated domains. It models each domain as a controlled Markov process to quantify cross-domain transfer.

entry.title: MobEvolve: An Agentic Self-Evolving Heuristic System for Interpretable Human Mobility Generation

author.name: Junlin He, Yihong Tang, Tong Nie, Ao Qu, Yuebing Liang, Hamzeh Alizadeh, Bang Liu, Wei Ma, Lijun Sun

entry.summary: MobEvolve is an agentic self-evolving heuristic framework for human mobility generation that initializes a behavior-inspired heuristic system and uses an LLM agent to iteratively evolve its internal logic by diagnosing empirical misalignments. It aims for interpretability, behavioral plausibility, and distributional alignment.

entry.title: VET: A Framework for Analyzing AI Discourse

author.name: Meredith Ringel Morris

entry.summary: The VET Framework categorizes AI discourse along valence, effectiveness, and trajectory dimensions to identify and critique narratives of AI Hype, Doom, Denial, and Normalcy. It serves as an AI Literacy tool for vetting polarized public discourse about AI.

entry.title: S3TS: Stochastic Scenario-Structured Tree Search for Advanced Planning Under Uncertainty

author.name: Fabio Pavirani, Bert Claessens, Pierre Pinson, Chris Develder

entry.summary: S3TS (Stochastic Scenario-Structured Tree Search) is a planning method that simultaneously handles non-linear system models and uncertainty for energy scheduling, bridging the gap between MCTS-style non-linearity handling and stochastic optimization. It targets reliable grid operation with renewable integration.

entry.title: MOC: Multi-Order Communication in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yao Guan, Lin Wang, Zhihu Lu, Ziyi Wang, Wenzhu Yan, Qiang Duan

entry.summary: MOC reconstructs inter-agent communication in LLM multi-agent systems to capture multi-hop dependencies rather than concatenating only first-order neighbor responses, with a structural consolidation strategy for efficiency. It targets the underexplored problem of message optimization versus topology optimization.

entry.title: DraDDP: A Multimodal Multi-Party Dialogue Discourse Parsing Dataset

author.name: Shannan Liu, Peifeng Li, Yaxin Fan, Qiaoming Zhu

entry.summary: DraDDP is the first publicly available English multimodal multi-party dialogue discourse parsing dataset, built from American TV dramas with 495 segments, 6,374 utterances, and 9.1 hours of video. It extends discourse parsing beyond text-only or two-party settings.

entry.title: Flow-Based Generative Modeling for Optimizing Sampling Policies in Compressed Sensing Applications

author.name: Roman Pavelkin, Luis A. Zavala-Mondragon, Christiaan G. A. Viviers, Fons van der Sommen

entry.summary: Presents a task-aware flow-based generative framework reformulating Flow Matching training to optimize subsampling policies in compressed sensing applications. It targets acquiring high-dimensional signals under tight resource constraints in signal processing and medical imaging.

entry.title: Silent Failures in Physical AI: A Literature Review of Runtime Action Authorization for Autonomous Systems

author.name: Barak Or

entry.summary: A literature review of runtime action authorization for autonomous Physical AI systems, identifying silent failures where black-box models issue physically consequential actions while appearing confident despite sensor drift, occlusion, or hallucinated affordances. It distinguishes this safety problem from content moderation and classical robot safety.

entry.title: PEACE: A Planner-Executor Agent with Constraint Enforcement for UAVs

author.name: Erdem Uysal, Timo Kehrer, Sebastiano Panichella

entry.summary: Proposes a planner-executor agent for PX4 drones that decouples LLM high-level mission planning from low-level ROS 2/MAVLink control, reducing latency and hallucination risk. It builds a world model from modular detectors with depth projection.

entry.title: A Protocol-Language Model for Network Intrusion (Without Deep Packet Inspection)

author.name: Vivek Kumar Sharma

entry.summary: Presents PLM-NIDS, treating network flows as a language using only L3/L4 metadata (length, timing, TTL, flags) to detect intrusions without deep packet inspection, viable for encrypted TLS 1.3/QUIC traffic. A RWKV-4 state-space model learns flow grammar from unlabelled data.

entry.title: Detector-Evasive LLM Paraphrasing via Constrained Policy Optimization

author.name: Mingyi Wang, Zhuoer Shen, Yuheng Bu, Shaofeng Zou

entry.summary: Formulates detector-evasive LLM paraphrasing as a Constrained Markov Decision Process where evasion is the objective and semantic preservation is an explicit constraint, solved via DEPO, a Lagrangian primal-dual RL algorithm. It provides precise control over the evasion-semantics trade-off.

entry.title: Finer Parameter Steps for Low-Rank PEFT: A Controlled Study with CP Tensor Adapters

author.name: Xinjue Wang, Xiuheng Wang, Yejun Zhang, Sergiy A. Vorobyov, Esa Ollila, Zhi-Yong Wang

entry.summary: Investigates whether tensorized CP adapters with finer parameter increments improve the accuracy-budget trade-off versus LoRA in parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Demonstrates much smaller capacity steps than LoRA rank increments on OPT models.

entry.title: CAFOSat: A Strongly Annotated Dataset for Infrastructure-Aware CAFO Mapping Using High-Resolution Imagery

author.name: Oishee Bintey Hoque, Nibir Chandra Mandal, Mandy L Wilson, Samarth Swarup, Madhav Marathe, Abhijin Adiga

entry.summary: Introduces CAFOSat, a strongly annotated infrastructure-aware dataset for mapping concentrated animal feeding operations across the US using high-resolution NAIP imagery and multi-source inventories refined via human-in-the-loop. Addresses environmental and disease surveillance needs.

entry.title: MoEIoU: Rethinking Bounding-Box Regression as a Mixture of Experts

author.name: Vinay Edula, Priyanka Bagade

entry.summary: Reframes bounding-box regression as a mixture of experts (MoEIoU) that jointly models overlap, center alignment, and shape with experts that adapt to optimization dynamics, instead of fixed geometric penalties. Addresses the changing nature of localization errors during training.

entry.title: Multilingual Idioms in Sentences and Conversations Across High-, Medium-, and Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Saeed Almheiri, Bilal Elbouardi, Salsabila Zahirah Pranida, Irina Nikishina, Ashwath Rao B, Parameswari Krishnamurthy, Muhammad Cendekia Airlangga, Rifo Ahmad Genadi, Nguyen Phan Gia Bao, Amir Hossein Yari, Hawau Olamide Toyin, Nurdaulet Mukhituly, Mena Attia, Besher Hassan, Ahmad Fathan Hidayatullah, Tatsuki Kuribayashi, Haonan Li, Suma Bhat, Fajri Koto

entry.summary: Introduces MIDI, a multilingual idiom dataset across 18 high-, medium-, and low-resource languages with idioms in both sentence and conversational contexts. Benchmarking shows idiom comprehension degrades substantially in low-resource languages.

entry.title: Accurate Large-sample Uncertainty Quantification using Stochastic Gradient Markov Chain Monte Carlo

author.name: Yu Wang, Jie Ding, Jonathan H. Huggins

entry.summary: Proposes new discrete-time approximations to stochastic gradient (Langevin) dynamics with and without momentum to enable accurate large-sample uncertainty quantification, providing principled tuning guidance for large batch sizes and misspecified models. It offers quantitative non-asymptotic predictions of stationary covariance and autocorrelation.

entry.title: Large-scale Uncertainty Quantification for Latent Variable Models Using Subsampling Markov Chain Monte Carlo

author.name: Xiaoyu Wang, Jonathan H. Huggins

entry.summary: Develops a statistical scaling-limit theory for SGLD-Gibbs in latent variable models, deriving joint asymptotic limits where global parameters converge to a diffusion and latent variables to jump processes, providing principled hyperparameter tuning guidance. It addresses scalable Bayesian inference for latent variable models.

entry.title: Perturbative methods for non-parametric instrumental variable

author.name: Wei Bu, Arthur Gretton

entry.summary: Introduces a perturbation-theory-inspired approach to nonparametric instrumental variable estimation, extending kernel ridge methods with higher-order corrections that mix eigenmodes to improve accuracy, especially for ill-defined integral equations and high dimensions. It draws on physics perturbation theory.

entry.title: KACE: Knowledge-Adaptive Context Engineering for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Jayant Parashar, Suchendra M. Bhandarkar

entry.summary: KACE separates knowledge storage from usage in context engineering for mathematical reasoning, distilling training traces offline into an epistemic tree of typed cards stratified by difficulty and domain to avoid context bloat. This breaks the prompt-size ceiling that conflated what is learned with what is included per problem.

entry.title: SHARP: Sleep-based Hierarchical Accelerated Replay for Long Range Non-Stationary Temporal Pattern Recognition

author.name: Jayanta Dey, Shikhar Srivastava, Itamar Lerner, Christopher Kanan, Dhireesha Kudithipudi

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a structured agentic framework for automated data science that treats it as a model-selection problem, using memory-grounded model selection and workflow construction to make LLM-agent modeling decisions verifiable and reusable. It contrasts with both predefined-search AutoML and unstructured LLM-agent approaches.

entry.title: AnyEdit++: Adaptive Long-Form Knowledge Editing via Bayesian Surprise

author.name: Bowen Tian, Caixue He, Jiemin Wu, Jingying Wang, Wenshuo Chen, Zexi Li, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: AnyEdit++ is a structure-aware long-form knowledge editing framework with Bayes-Chunk, an adaptive segmentation mechanism that finds semantic boundaries via Bayesian Surprise rather than fixed-window chunking. It includes theory on structural independence via orthogonal anchor keys to minimize cross-segment interference.

entry.title: Algorithmic algorithm development with LLMs: A Case Study on LLM-Usage for Contraction Order Optimization in Tensor Networks

author.name: Fabian Hoppe, Melven R\"ohrig-Z\"ollner, Philipp Knechtges

entry.summary: This case study explores LLM-based algorithm development for tensor-network contraction-order optimization using OpenEvolve, examining the choice of LLM and design choices like evaluation metrics and test instances. It highlights both the promise of verifier-guided evolutionary coding agents and the continuing importance of human validation.

entry.title: An Abstract Worlds Semantic Framework for Belief Change Operators

author.name: Daniel Grimaldi, M. Vanina Martinez, Ricardo O. Rodriguez

entry.summary: This paper proposes Abstract Worlds Semantics, a set-theoretic framework for belief change with no assumed logical syntax, treating worlds as primitive elements over which contraction and revision operators are defined. It unifies classical and non-prioritized belief change models (AGM, KM, Multiple Change) within one framework.

entry.title: RASER: Recoverability-Aware Selective Escalation Router for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Yuyang Li, Zihe Yan, Tobias K\"afer

entry.summary: RASER is a family of cheap routers built on one-shot RAG that decides whether to escalate to expensive multi-hop retrieval, since many multi-hop questions are already answered by a single retrieval pass. It saves token budget by avoiding unnecessary extra retrieval.

entry.title: Update Opacity: Epistemic Accessibility and Governance Under AI System Change

author.name: Andrea Ferrario, Joshua Hatherley

entry.summary: Frames update opacity as a diachronic failure of epistemic accessibility, where users cannot understand why deployed AI now yields different outputs after routine model updates. It treats this as a governance problem requiring selective relevance-aware disclosure to avoid overload.

entry.title: Benchmarks for Vision-Language Models in Urban Perception Should Be Reliability-Aware and Negotiated

author.name: Rashid Mushkani

entry.summary: Argues that benchmarks for vision-language models in urban perception should treat annotator disagreement and abstention as measurement outcomes, report inter-annotator reliability, and treat label spaces as negotiable when informing governance. Grounded in a benchmark of 100 Montreal street scenes.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Reference-Aligned Machine Unlearning

author.name: Rasa Khosrowshahli, Stephen Asobiela, Beatrice Ombuki-Berman, Shahryar Rahnamayan

entry.summary: Proposes RAUL, a multi-objective machine unlearning framework that replaces unbounded loss maximization with bounded KL alignment of forgotten-sample predictions toward a reference distribution representing unseen data. It jointly optimizes forgetting and retention to avoid catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Agents on a Tree: Pathwise Coordination for Multi-Objective Molecular Optimization

author.name: Jia Zhang, Tengfei Ma, Tianle Li, Daojian Zeng, Xieping Gao, Xiangxiang Zeng

entry.summary: ATOM formulates multi-objective molecular optimization as a tree-structured search where each node hosts an agent specialized for a particular objective, coordinating along paths rather than enforcing global consensus. This enables maintaining diverse trade-offs across conflicting design goals in chemical space.

entry.title: Geodesic Flow Matching for Denoising High-Dimensional Structured Representations

author.name: Karim Habashy, Chris Eliasmith

entry.summary: This paper applies Geodesic Flow Matching to denoise Spatial Semantic Pointers in Vector Symbolic Algebras, showing that standard Euclidean flow matching cuts through the toroidal manifold and destroys phase/magnitude structure needed for decoding. Riemannian transport dynamics respect the geometric constraints of valid states.

entry.title: Coupling Language Models with Physics-based Simulation for Synthesis of Inorganic Materials

author.name: Edward W. Staley, Tom Arbaugh, Michael Pekala, Alexander New, Christopher D. Stiles, Nam Q. Le, Gregory Bassen, Wyatt Bunstine, Tyrel McQueen

entry.summary: This work introduces a hybrid framework that couples LLMs with thermodynamic databases and simplified kinetics models to evaluate LLM-generated synthesis routes for inorganic materials, using the niobium-oxygen system as a case study. It compares LLM proposals against physics-based simulation to assess realistic synthesis planning.

entry.title: Regularized Offline Policy Optimization with Posterior Hybrid Bayesian Belief

author.name: Hongqiang Lin, Pengfei Wang, Nenggan Zheng

entry.summary: This work proposes a regularized offline RL method using a posterior hybrid Bayesian belief over dynamics to unify sample-level and model-level epistemic uncertainty quantification. It aims to make Bayesian RL policy optimization computationally tractable compared to search-based or restrictive prior methods.

entry.title: LLM-Driven Co-Evolutionary Automated Heuristic Design for Bi-Component Coupled Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Mingen Kuang, Xudong Deng, Xi Lin, Ye Fan, Jianyong Sun, Jialong Shi

entry.summary: CoEvo-AHD is an LLM-driven dual-population co-evolutionary framework for automated heuristic design in coupled combinatorial problems like the Traveling Thief and Traveling Purchaser problems, co-evolving two related operator populations with a cooperative evaluation mechanism. It overcomes prior methods that evolve single heuristics in isolation.

entry.title: CAREAgent: Clinical Agent with Structured Reasoning and Tool-Integrated for Order Generation

author.name: Ruihui Hou, Ziyue Huai, Chennuo Zhang, Ziyan Liu, Siran Zhao, Yao Yu, Jie Zhai, Tong Ruan

entry.summary: CAREAgent is a clinical agent for fine-grained, executable medical order generation, supported by a two-stage agentic reasoning data-construction method that builds and filters verifiable reasoning trajectories aligned with realistic clinical tool usage. It targets the gap between coarse clinical decisions and concrete executable orders.

entry.title: "Skill issues'': data-centric optimization of lakehouse agents

author.name: Nicole Rose Schneider, Davide Ghilardi, Giacomo Piccinini, Jacopo Tagliabue

entry.summary: This work studies data-centric optimization of skill and environment files for coding agents operating on a branching lakehouse, reframing data-agent evaluation as a state-verification problem. It presents a pipeline that generates task-verifier pairs by inspecting concrete lakehouse state changes.

entry.title: Self-Healing Agentic Orchestrators for Reliable Tool-Augmented Large Language Model Systems

author.name: Rahul Suresh Babu, Adarsh Agrawal

entry.summary: This paper presents a self-healing agentic orchestrator that treats reliability as a bounded runtime control problem, mapping observable failure signals to inferred failure classes and selecting targeted recovery actions under budgets. It verifies recovered trajectories and records observability traces.

entry.title: EvoBrain: Continual Learning of EEG Foundation Models Across Heterogeneous BCI Tasks

author.name: Yangxuan Zhou, Sha Zhao, Jiquan Wang, Shijian Li, Gang Pan

entry.summary: EvoBrain formulates downstream EEG adaptation as a cross-task continual learning problem and proposes a dynamic, task-aware continual learning framework to unify heterogeneous BCI tasks without task-isolated fine-tuning. It addresses scalability and overhead limitations of current EEG foundation model post-training.

entry.title: Physically-Constrained Mamba-SDE for Remaining Useful Life Prediction under Irregular Observations

author.name: Deyu Zhuang, Peiliang Gong, Yang Shao, Liyuan Shu, Qi Zhu, Xiaoli Li, Daoqiang Zhang

entry.summary: PC-MambaSDE is a physically-constrained continuous-time framework for remaining useful life prediction under irregular observations, using a mask-aware continuous Mamba encoder and physical constraints to avoid implausible degradation trajectories. It addresses asynchronous sampling, burst missingness, and temporal jitter.

entry.title: Bayesian Spectral Emotion Transition Discovery from Multi-Annotator Disagreement

author.name: Keito Inoshita, Takato Ueno

entry.summary: Bayesian Spectral Emotion Transition Discovery (BSETD) discovers emotion-transition structure from multi-annotator soft labels rather than majority-voted hard labels, using a hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial posterior over transition matrices. It preserves annotator uncertainty needed to understand turn-to-turn emotional transitions.

entry.title: BADGER: Bridging Agentic and Deterministic Evaluation for Generative Enterprise Reasoning

author.name: Shannon Serrao, Soumitra Chatterjee, Dorina Strori, Abhishek Sharma, Nathan Miller

entry.summary: BADGER is a unified enterprise evaluation framework developed at Merkle that integrates text-to-SQL assessment with agentic behavior evaluation into a production-grade pipeline calibrated against human expert judgment. It bridges deterministic execution-accuracy protocols with LLM-based agentic assessment.

entry.title: Bridging the Sim-to-Real Gap in Semiconductor Visual Program Synthesis via Input Binarization

author.name: Yusuke Ohtsubo, Kota Dohi, Koichiro Yawata, Koki Takeshita, Tatsuya Sasaki

entry.summary: Proposes a visual program synthesis framework where a VLM converts semiconductor inspection images into editable DSL code for exact-parameter training data generation, using input binarization to bridge the sim-to-real domain gap. It addresses costly real-data requirements in nanometer-scale metrology.

entry.title: TCAR-Gen: Temporal Graph Retrieval with Evidence Fusion for Knowledge-Grounded Generation

author.name: Sidra Nasir, Muhammad Noman Zahid, Rizwan Ahmed Khan

entry.summary: TCAR-Gen combines query-conditioned graph neural networks, temporal evidence fusion, and chain-of-trees reasoning for knowledge-grounded generation over historical criminal case narratives. It outperforms vanilla, temporal, and graph RAG variants on the Victorian Crime Diaries benchmark.

entry.title: VDSB-GWSyn: Diffusion Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge for Controllable and Anatomically Feasible Guidewire Synthesis in Coronary Angiography

author.name: Haoyuan Tang, Zhuo Zhang, Jialin Li, Shuai Xiao, Jiachen Yang

entry.summary: Proposes VDSB-GWSyn, a Diffusion Schrodinger Bridge model for synthesizing controllable, anatomically realistic guidewire images in coronary angiography to address annotation scarcity. It uses shape priors to learn guidewire geometry.

entry.title: SpikeWFM: Spiking-Aided Wireless Foundation Model for Robust Channel Prediction

author.name: Liwen Jing, Yisha Lu, Tingting Yang, Li Sun, Yuxuan Shi, Yuwei Wang, Mengfan Zheng, Leiyang Xu

entry.summary: Proposes SpikeWFM, a hybrid spiking-neural-network and transformer architecture for wireless foundation models targeting noise-robust channel prediction. It applies self-supervised pretraining across diverse wireless scenarios.

entry.title: Completion at the Boundary (CaB): Deployable Switching with Completion-Aware Control under Limited Calibration

author.name: Yusuke Sano, Takeshi Itoga

entry.summary: Studies completion detection for vision-language-action agents—deciding when an instruction is finished—under a deployable low-calibration regime with a single global switching rule. It frames completion as a closed-loop intervention problem for sequential composite tasks.

entry.title: Agentic Authoring of Interactive Multiview Visualizations in Genomics

author.name: Astrid van den Brandt, Kiroong Choe, Sehi L'Yi, Devin Lange, Nils Gehlenborg

entry.summary: Explores agentic LLM authoring of interactive multiview genomics visualizations through natural-language conversational interfaces, aiming to democratize complex visualization creation. It addresses genomics-specific challenges in integrating heterogeneous data.

entry.title: CodeCytos: AI-assisted spatial molecular imaging analysis via code-augmented agent action space

author.name: Hung Q. Vo, Huy Q. Vo, Son T. Ly, Zhihao Wan, Anh-Vu Nguyen, Hong Zhao, Jianting Sheng, Stephen T. C. Wong, Hien V. Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes a coding-based reasoning agent framework for spatial molecular imaging analysis that enables dynamic, programmable interaction beyond fixed pre-implemented features. Improves automation and customization for complex tissue studies.

entry.title: Logit Distillation on Manifolds: Mapping by Learning

author.name: Yiru Yang, Junling Wang, Nishant Kumar Singh, Luohong Wu, Haoran Yan

entry.summary: Proposes a layer- and point-wise projection mapping that aligns student and teacher representations into a shared high-dimensional embedding space during knowledge distillation, combined with LoRA injection to reduce cost. Aims to capture ensemble benefits in a single deployable model.

entry.title: Extending Causal Metamodeling to a non-Markovian Queue

author.name: Pracheta Amaranath, Anant Bhide, David Jensen, Peter Haas

entry.summary: Extends modular dynamic Bayesian network metamodels for discrete-event simulation from Markovian to non-Markovian queues by approximating non-exponential distributions with phase-type distributions. Addresses challenges of accuracy-tractability trade-offs in phase count selection.

entry.title: Rethinking Evaluation Paradigms in IBP-based Certified Training

author.name: Konstantin Kaulen, Hadar Shavit, Holger H. Hoos

entry.summary: Critiques single-configuration reporting in IBP-based certified training, arguing the natural-vs-certified accuracy tradeoff makes such reporting misleading. Proposes evaluation paradigms that assess the full tradeoff curve for fairer comparison.

entry.title: On the Generalization in Topology Optimization via Sensitivity-Conditioned Bernoulli Flow Matching

author.name: Mohammad Rashed, Duarte F. Valoroso Madeira, Babak Gholami, Caglar Guerbuez, Yunjia Yang, Nils Thuerey

entry.summary: Studies OOD generalization in topology-optimization surrogates, hypothesizing that performance depends on how much the conditioning signal preserves adjoint sensitivity information, using a causal Markov chain and the Data Processing Inequality. Proposes sensitivity-conditioned Bernoulli flow matching.

entry.title: FOAM: Frequency and Operator Error-Based Adaptive Damping Method for Reducing Staleness-Oriented Error for Shampoo

author.name: Kyunghun Nam, Sumyeong Ahn

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical study of staleness in Shampoo optimizer preconditioner updates and proposes FOAM, an adaptive damping method based on frequency and operator error to mitigate staleness-induced instability. It targets the matrix-inversion bottleneck in large-scale optimization.

entry.title: Not All Errors Are Equal: A Systematic Study of Error Propagation in Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Yafan Huang, Sheng Di, Guanpeng Li

entry.summary: Presents a systematic study of soft-error propagation in LLM inference via LLMFI, a configurable fault-injection framework, injecting faults across three open models and thirteen tasks. It reveals that not all errors are equal in their impact on reasoning, coding, and multilingual outputs.

entry.title: Monitoring Agentic Systems Before They're Reliable

author.name: Marisa Ferrara Boston, Glen Hanson, Effi Georgala, JD Hudgens, Heather Frase

entry.summary: Presents a monitoring and triage methodology for immature agentic systems where structural defects rather than task-level errors dominate failures, decomposing evaluation across quality/suitability/efficiency and three monitoring scopes using variance signals and FMEA-style severity routing. It concentrates human attention on findings warranting investigation.

entry.title: PE-means: Improved Differentially Private $k$-means Clustering through Private Evolution

author.name: Thomas Humphries, Zinan Lin, Sergey Yekhanin

entry.summary: Studies the role of label encoding in neural collapse using the unrestricted feature model with MSE loss, showing class mean features transition from a simplex equiangular tight frame to an orthogonal frame as bias regularization increases for one-hot labels. It generalizes the analysis to arbitrary encodings.

entry.title: CRMA: A Spectrally-Bounded Backbone for Modular Continual Fine-Tuning of LLMs

author.name: Kiran Nayudu, Aswini Nutakki, Sai Vinay Naidu, Ashwin Shanmugasundaram

entry.summary: Introduces CRMA, a continual fine-tuning adapter whose internal mixing matrix is doubly-stochastic via Sinkhorn normalization, structurally guaranteeing a spectral-norm bound by Birkhoff's theorem. It provides a continuously trained shared substrate while preserving modular methods' forgetting guarantees.

entry.title: TravelEval: A Comprehensive Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating LLM-Powered Travel Planning Agents

author.name: Weiyi Chen, Shuaixiong Wang, Ziyun Gao, Kaichun Hu, Wangze Ni, Shimin Di, Chen Jason Zhang, Lei Chen

entry.summary: TravelEval is a comprehensive benchmark for LLM-powered travel-planning agents featuring a six-dimensional evaluation framework covering accuracy, cost, and spatio-temporal quality, with more realistic data on lodging and transport and whole-plan assessment. It addresses prior benchmarks' overemphasis on constraint compliance and isolated daily plans.

entry.title: Structure-Guided Adaptive Propagation for Protein-Protein Interaction Site Prediction

author.name: Enqiang Zhu, Yizi Liu, Yilong Luo, Yao Chen, Yu Zhang, Baoshan Ma

entry.summary: SGAP-PPIS is a structure-guided adaptive propagation graph model for protein-protein interaction site prediction that adapts information diffusion to local geometric environments rather than treating all residues uniformly. It aims to better distinguish true interaction sites from similar non-interacting neighbors.

entry.title: EVA-Net: Subject-Independent EEG Motor Decoding with Video-Derived Motor Priors

author.name: Ziyuan Li, Yueyu Sun, Yimeng Zhang

entry.summary: EVA-Net is a two-stage framework for subject-independent EEG motor decoding that uses action videos as dynamic semantic priors instead of sparse text, aligning EEG and video features in a shared space via cross-modal and supervised contrastive objectives. It targets cross-subject generalization with minimal calibration.

entry.title: From Capability Models to Automated Planning: An AAS-Native Approach for Automatic PDDL Generation

author.name: Hamied Nabizada, Thomas Wirt, Luis Miguel Vieira da Silva, Felix Gehlhoff, Alexander Fay

entry.summary: This work shows that Asset Administration Shell capability models structured with four Industry 4.0 standards contain enough information to automatically generate PDDL planning problems, removing the need for specialized planning expertise from production engineers. It provides an AAS-native approach to automated planning for manufacturing.

entry.title: Tracing GenAI Literacy: Uncovering Student-AI Interaction Patterns in Academic Writing through Epistemic Network Analysis

author.name: Angxuan Chen, Jiyou Jia

entry.summary: Uses epistemic network analysis on interaction logs from 162 students in a GenAI-assisted writing task to model questioning strategies by literacy level, moving beyond self-reported scales. It finds high-literacy students engage in iterative refinement while low-literacy students rely on direct generation.

entry.title: Regime-Adaptive Continual Learning for Portfolio Management

author.name: Chaofan Pan, Lingfei Ren, Linbo Xiong, Yonghao Li, Wei Wei, Xin Yang
