entry.summary: Proposes ReCAP, a regime-aware continual learning framework for portfolio management that helps trading agents accumulate and transfer knowledge across non-stationary market regimes. It addresses limitations of rolling-window retraining and naive fine-tuning.

entry.title: Interpreting FCDNNs via RG on Exponential Family

author.name: Fuzhou Gong, Zigeng Xia

entry.summary: Extends a theory connecting the renormalization group from statistical physics to deep neural network training, generalizing prior Ising-model results to continuous exponential-family input data. It aims to build interpretability theory for fully connected DNNs.

entry.title: Beyond Augmentation: Score-Guided Pathological Prior for EEG-based Depression Detection

author.name: Xiaojing Chen, Jingqi Cheng, Xu Zhao, Wan Jiang, Jingjing Wu

entry.summary: Proposes Score-Guided Classification (SGC) for EEG-based depression detection that, instead of augmenting data, uses an unsupervised generative model to score sample anomaly as a pathological prior. It challenges the data-quantity-first convention under the small-sample dilemma.

entry.title: DRL-Based Pose Control for Double-Ackermann Robots Under Actuation Uncertainties

author.name: Oussama Zaim, M\'elodie Daniel, Aly Magassouba, Miguel Aranda, Olivier Ly

entry.summary: Extends the ManeuverNet DRL framework from position to full pose control for double-Ackermann mobile robots and studies how actuation uncertainties affect sim-to-real transfer. Simplified training actuation models caused success rates to drop from 100% in simulation to 25% in Gazebo.

entry.title: GC-MoE: Genomics-Guided Cell-Type-Specific Mixture of Experts for Histology-Based Single-Cell Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Kaito Shiku, Ahtisham Fazeel Abbasi, Ryoma Bise, Yuichiro Iwashita, Kazuya Nishimura, Andreas Dengel, Muhammad Nabeel Asim

entry.summary: Proposes GC-MoE, a genomics-guided cell-type-specific mixture-of-experts for predicting single-cell gene expression from histology images and cell locations, using a routing network to combine cell-type experts. It models cell-to-cell expression variability for spatial transcriptomics.

entry.title: Optimal Transport-based Permutation-Invariant Bayesian Optimization of Offshore Wind Farm Layouts

author.name: Antonio Candelieri, Laurens Bliek

entry.summary: This work extends Bayesian Optimization with optimal-transport-based permutation invariance to exploit symmetry in layout optimization problems, applied to offshore wind farm placement. By treating point sets as order-agnostic layouts, it improves sample efficiency for expensive black-box objectives.

entry.title: Tackling the Root of Misinformation by Teaching Laypeople about Logical Fallacies via Socratic Questioning and Critical Argumentation

author.name: Minjing Shi, Junling Wang, Jingwei Ni, Sankalan Pal Chowdhury, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: LFTutor is an LLM-based intelligent tutoring system that teaches laypeople to identify logical fallacies via intent-driven Socratic questioning and critical-argumentation principles, aiming to build resilience against misinformation. Automatic and human evaluations show it outperforms baseline LLMs lacking these pedagogical strategies.

entry.title: FlowTime: Towards Continuous Generative Watch Time Prediction via Flow-based Personalized Priors

author.name: Hongxu Ma, Han Zhou, Chenghou Jin, Jie Zhang, Xiaoyu Yang, Chunjie Chen, Jihong Guan, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: FlowTime reframes watch-time prediction in short-video recommenders as continuous generative modeling using flow-based personalized priors, addressing mean-collapse, quantization errors, and latency issues of prior paradigms. It approaches the problem from a causal perspective on user-item interaction multimodality.

entry.title: Community-Aware Assessment of Social Textual Engagement and Resonance: A Human-Centric Perspective on User-Generated Content Evaluation

author.name: Tianjiao Li, Kai Zhao, Xiang Li, Yang Liu, Huyang Sun

entry.summary: CASTER proposes a paradigm shift in video quality assessment from aesthetic fidelity to human-centric community resonance, predicting whether user-generated content achieves positive community engagement from multimodal attributes. MEDEA implements a Social Chain-of-Thought mechanism for this evaluation.

entry.title: Motif-based morphology signatures for interpretable ECG screening and monitoring

author.name: Nivedita Bijlani, Mauricio Villarroel

entry.summary: Introduces a motif-based framework for interpretable ECG screening that defines beat-aligned cardiac signatures and quantifies morphological drift over short and long-term monitoring. It targets subtle changes that manual interpretation misses.

entry.title: Multimodal Music Recommendation System using LLMs

author.name: Srikar Prabhas Kandagatla, Sreehitha R. Narayana, Chandana Magapu, Swetha Mohan, Shamanth Kuthpadi, Hongjie Chen, Ryan A. Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt, Nesreen Ahmed

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal LLM-based session music recommendation framework that jointly models semantic, acoustic, and engagement signals by enriching LastFM-1K with audio/lyric embeddings. It grounds recommendations in actual song content.

entry.title: DiffCrossGait: Trajectory-Level Alignment for 2D-3D Cross-Modal Gait Recognition via Latent Diffusion

author.name: Zhiyang Lu, Ming Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes DiffCrossGait, reformulating 2D-3D cross-modal gait recognition as trajectory-level alignment in a latent diffusion space using shared Gaussian noise. Introduces a Tri-Phase Alignment Strategy for identity anchoring and cross-modal recovery.

entry.title: How Generation Architecture Shapes Code Complexity in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Paired Study on HumanEval

author.name: Nazmus Ashrafi

entry.summary: A paired study on HumanEval examining how multi-agent code generation architectures (six configurations) affect structural code complexity, not just functional correctness, using RADON metrics across GPT-4o models. It identifies which orchestration layers add complexity cost.

entry.title: Pre-Deployment Robustness Stress Testing for CT Segmentation Systems Using Clinically Motivated Multi-Corruption Augmentation

author.name: CholMin Kang, Jonghyun Chung, Amanpreet Kaurb, Nagesh Gulkotwarb, Arthi Sivasankaranb

entry.summary: Proposes RAMP, a robustness-oriented augmentation framework for CT segmentation combining anatomically constrained perturbations and stochastic multi-corruption composition. Aims to expose models to clinically plausible degradations for safer deployment.

entry.title: Authenticity Debt and the Synthetic Content Threat Landscape: A Layered Framework for Trust, Provenance, and IP Governance in the Generative AI Era

author.name: Shubhashis Sengupta, Benjamin McCarty, Milind Savagaonkar, Rhine Andotra

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of authenticity debt—cumulative institutional liability from deploying AI-generated content without verifiable provenance—and a layered framework spanning authenticity, provenance, integrity, and accountability for IP governance. Addresses synthetic content threats in the generative AI era.

entry.title: ODTQA-FoRe: An Open-Domain Tabular Question Answering Dataset for Future Data Forecasting and Reasoning

author.name: Zhensheng Wang, Xiaole Liu, Wenmian Yang, Kun Zhou, Yiquan Zhang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: Introduces a novel task and dataset (ODTQA-FoRe) for open-domain tabular question answering requiring future data forecasting and reasoning over real estate data, plus TimeFore, an LLM agent framework decomposing the problem into retriever, forecaster, and reasoner roles. It pushes tabular QA toward predictive rather than retrospective answering.

entry.title: Modeling Spectral Energy Shifts in Spatio-Temporal Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yilin Liu, Hongchao Zhang, Taylor T. Johnson, Ahmad F. Taha, Meiyi Ma

entry.summary: Identifies camouflaged graph anomalies that decrease spectral energy variation and evade existing spectral detectors, proposing a node-level spectral energy formulation compatible with message passing plus an energy-aware graph learning framework. It enables detection across static and dynamic graphs.

entry.title: KG-Guard: Graph-Based Hallucination Detection for Knowledge Base Question Answering

author.name: Albert Sawczyn, Piotr Bielak, Tomasz Kajdanowicz

entry.summary: Formulates hallucination detection in knowledge base QA as answer-node classification and proposes KG-Guard, a lightweight graph-based framework treating the answering LLM as a black box to detect hallucinated answer nodes. It targets cases where models ignore graph evidence or reason invalidly.

entry.title: A Multi-AI-agent Framework Enabling End-to-end Finite Element Analysis for Solid Mechanics Problems

author.name: Titu Ranjan Sarker, Muhammed Jawaad Zulqernine, Ling Yue, Shaowu Pan, Chenxi Wang, Shiyao Lin

entry.summary: AbaqusAgent is a multi-agent LLM framework that turns natural-language instructions into executed finite element analyses in Abaqus, handling boundary conditions, load cases, and solution variables. It aims to lower the steep expertise barrier and reduce false simulations in solid mechanics.

entry.title: AXIOM: A Trust-First Neuro-Symbolic Execution Architecture for Verifiable Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Alessio Bruno

entry.summary: AXIOM is a trust-first neuro-symbolic architecture where the LLM only canonicalizes natural-language math into a narrow schema consumed by a deterministic computer-algebra-system pipeline that verifies answers or abstains. It reports high correctness at 100% trust on parseable problems via tightly aligned regex-schema-handler routing.

entry.title: Absorbing Complexity: An Interaction-Native Knowledge Harness for Financial LLM Agents

author.name: Ailiya Borjigin, Igor Stadnyk, Ben Bilski, Maksym Chikita, Dmytro Kyrylenko, Sofiia Pidturkina, Julia Stadnyk

entry.summary: InKH (interaction-native knowledge harness) is an architecture for financial LLM agents that absorbs complexity into the system by converting user, market, portfolio, and tool events into structured operational knowledge, reducing the need for users to repeatedly restate context. It targets market analysis, copy-trading review, and trade preparation.

entry.title: DAStatFormer: A Hybrid Multibranch Transformer with Statistical Feature Integration for DAS-Based Pattern Recognitions

author.name: Michel Dione (CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), Jerry Lonlac (CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), H\'el\`ene Louis (CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), Anthony Fleury (CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), Stephane Lecoeuche

entry.summary: DAStatFormer is a hybrid multibranch Transformer for distributed acoustic sensing pattern recognition that extracts 24 ANOVA-selected statistical features per channel instead of processing raw signals, combined with gated Transformer networks. It reduces data size by orders of magnitude while preserving discriminative information.

entry.title: V2I Work Zone Geometry Reconstruction with Pose-Conditioned UWB Range Denoising

author.name: Jiaxi Liu, Hangyu Li, Yang Cheng, Rui Gana, Junwei You, Weizhe Tang, Peng Zhang, Steven T. Parker, Xiaopeng Li, Bin Ran

entry.summary: Proposes a pose-conditioned, permutation-equivariant denoiser for ultra-wideband ranging to reconstruct work zone geometry for connected/autonomous vehicles. It handles outliers, NLOS errors, and anchor-ordering issues.

entry.title: Geodesics with Unified Tangent-constrained Priors and Curvature Regularization

author.name: Chong Di, Li Liu, Jinglin Zhang, Zhenjiang Li, Da Chen, Laurent D. Cohen

entry.summary: Proposes a unified geodesic framework integrating tangent-constrained shape priors with curvature penalization for image segmentation, restricting path tangents to angular sectors derived from shape skeletons. It reduces shortcut errors in delineating complex shapes.

entry.title: Digital-to-Physical Transfer of Adversarial Patches for Aerial Vehicle Detection

author.name: Jung Heum Woo, Eun-Kyu Lee

entry.summary: Evaluates physical adversarial patch attacks against aerial vehicle detectors by bridging digital optimization (with non-printability and total-variation constraints) to real-world printed deployment. It demonstrates digital-to-physical transferability of attacks.

entry.title: Effects of Varying LLM Access on Essay Writing Behavior

author.name: Julia Christenson, Karin de Langis, Shirley Anugrah Hayati, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: A pilot study (n=24) examining how varying LLM access (none, limited, unlimited) affects college essay writing performance, engagement, and perceived authorship. Essay quality was similar across groups but writing behavior and ownership diverged sharply.

entry.title: LP5X-PIM Sim: A High-Fidelity HW/SW Integrated Simulator for LPDDR5X-PIM

author.name: SangHoon Cha, Jaewan Choi, Byeongho Kim, Yoonah Paik, Sukhan Lee, Kyomin Sohn

entry.summary: Technical note describing Samsung's high-fidelity hardware-software integrated simulator for LPDDR5X processing-in-memory, modeling both data paths and software control layers for performance and energy evaluation. Refines existing frameworks to align with real hardware.

entry.title: RefDiffNet: Learning to Expose Subtle PCB Defects Before Detection

author.name: Vinay Edula, Nilesh Badwe, Priyanka Bagade

entry.summary: Proposes RefDiffNet, a lightweight plug-and-play input enhancement block that uses a defect-free reference image to expose subtle PCB defects before detection, bringing a classical inspection idea into deep learning pipelines. Compares defective images against aligned references.

entry.title: Repurposing Adversarial Perturbations for Continual Learning: From Defense to Active Alignment

author.name: Ran Liu, Min Yu, Mingqi Liu, Jianguo Jiang, Gang Li, Rongsheng Li, Ning Li, Zhen Xu, Weiqing Huang, Ming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes AdvCL, which repurposes adversarial perturbations as a geometric control signal for stable continual learning in LLMs, using three plug-in modules for local smoothness, prototype clipping, and directional alignment. It targets forgetting, limited transfer, and adversarial vulnerability simultaneously.

entry.title: PropLLM: Propagation-Aware Scene Reconstruction for Network Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Zongzong Wu, Ming Zhao, Fengxiao Tang, Nei Kato

entry.summary: PropLLM integrates hop-by-hop scene reconstruction with LLM reasoning for network fault diagnosis, tracing back from end-point alerts along propagation paths to resolve cases where distinct root causes produce similar symptoms. It contrasts with single-pass alert-to-diagnosis approaches that cannot disambiguate.

entry.title: An NLP-Driven Framework for Curriculum-Labor Market Alignment: Schema-Constrained LLM Extraction, ESCO-Anchored Semantic Matching, and Multi-Dimensional Gap Quantification

author.name: Sherzod Turaev, Mary John, Mamoun Awad, Nazar Zaki, Khaled Shuaib

entry.summary: This NLP framework aligns curricula with labor markets via schema-constrained LLM extraction of competencies, SBERT-based semantic matching against the ESCO taxonomy, and multi-dimensional gap quantification with reliability measures. It addresses limitations of lexical-surface extraction that miss implicit competencies.

entry.title: Generative AI and Digital Ecosystem Resilience: A Proactive Lifecycle-Based Survey

author.name: Jonghyun Chung, Rishabh Chaddha, Sanket Badhe, Debanshu Das, Nathan Huang, Amanpreet Kaur

entry.summary: A lifecycle-based survey on using generative AI proactively to detect emerging inauthentic narratives and synthetic adversarial content, organized around a C5 Interaction Model. It bridges socio-technical campaign models with computational detection methods.

entry.title: UF-AMA: A unified framework for cross-domain emotion recognition via adaptive multimodal alignment

author.name: Zheng Wang, Shuo Wang, Junhong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes UF-AMA, a unified framework for cross-domain emotion recognition from physiological signals (EEG) using adaptive multimodal alignment to handle distribution shifts across subjects and sessions. It targets robust generalization in affective computing.

entry.title: FW-NKF: Frequency-Weighted Neural Kalman Filters

author.name: Adnan Harun Dogan, Berken Utku Demirel, Christian Holz

entry.summary: Introduces FW-NKF, a frequency-weighted neural Kalman filter that embeds a causal spectral-shaping operator into the measurement residual to suppress band-limited noise in robotic state estimation. It combines learned transition/observation networks with explicit frequency-domain noise handling.

entry.title: Doing What They Say, Not What They Reason: Locating the Faithfulness Gap in LLM Agents

author.name: Yufeng Wang

entry.summary: This paper measures whether LLM agents act on the reasoning they state by decomposing the faithfulness gap into reasoning-to-conclusion and conclusion-to-action steps within a verifiable poker simulator. The two steps are found to behave oppositely.

entry.title: Deft Scheduling of Dynamic Cloud Workflows with Varying Deadlines via Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Ya Shen, Gang Chen, Hui Ma, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: DEFT applies a Mixture-of-Experts architecture to deep RL for dynamic cloud workflow scheduling, with experts specialized for different deadline tightness levels. It claims to be the first MoE-based DRL scheduler for cloud workflows with varying deadlines.

entry.title: TrafficRAG: A Multimodal RAG Framework for Traffic Accident Liability Determination

author.name: Xu Li, Zedong Fu, Xinyi Li, Xun Han

entry.summary: TrafficRAG is a multimodal retrieval-augmented framework for automated traffic-accident liability analysis that converts accident video into structured textual descriptions used as retrieval queries against legal knowledge. It uses a hybrid retrieval strategy to generate liability reports.

entry.title: A Novel Data Augmentation Strategy for Robust Deep Learning Classification of Biomedical Time-Series Data: Application to ECG and EEG Analysis

author.name: Mohammed Guhdar, Ramadhan J. Mstafa, Abdulhakeem O. Mohammed

entry.summary: Proposes a unified deep learning framework integrating a ResNet-based CNN with attention for robust classification across heterogeneous biomedical signals like ECG and EEG, alongside a novel data augmentation strategy to handle class imbalance. It claims state-of-the-art performance across signal types.

entry.title: Improved Belief-Attention in Vision Task

author.name: Guoqiang Zhang

entry.summary: Extends Belief-Attention by utilizing both the perpendicular and projected components of the orthogonal projection of softmax-weighted V vectors, after an ablation shows the projected component carries token-correlation information. The projected component passes through activation and linear mapping before merging.

entry.title: A Methodological Framework for Explicit Control of the Speed-Accuracy Trade-off in Brain-Computer Interfaces

author.name: Javier Jim\'enez, Francisco B Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation framework for brain-computer interfaces that explicitly separates speed and accuracy metrics rather than combining them in Information Transfer Rate. Introduces Gain and Conservation measures for controllable trade-offs.

entry.title: Civilizational Metamaterials: Engineering Coordination Under Capability Gradients and Structural Turbulence

author.name: David Orban

entry.summary: Develops a metamaterials-inspired formal framework arguing AI governance should become an engineering discipline, introducing the Freezing Equilibrium where validation costs exceed action utility causing rational inaction. It proposes a constitutive law for institutional coordination under AGI.

entry.title: Short-form Text Rewriting with Phi Silica

author.name: Divya Tadimeti, Shawn Pan, Sameera Lanka, Chenghui Zhou, Sadid Hasan

entry.summary: Empirical study adapting the small Phi Silica model for short-form text rewriting via dataset curation, prompt distillation, and PEFT, using GPT-5-chat for supervision and evaluation. Shows fine-tuning improves fidelity and reduces hallucination in constrained rewrites.

entry.title: Beyond the Mouth: Upper-Face Affective Cues in Audiovisual Sentence Recognition under Acoustic Uncertainty

author.name: Zhou Yang, Yueyi Yang

entry.summary: Investigates whether upper-face affective cues beyond the mouth region improve audiovisual sentence recognition under acoustic degradation, using the CREMA-D corpus with multiple cue conditions. Explores integrating emotion-related visual signals into speech recognition.

entry.title: Dynamic Coordination Strategy Selection for Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Thanh Luong Tuan

entry.summary: Evaluates whether enterprise multi-agent coordination strategy should be selected dynamically by problem class versus fixed globally, using a frozen matrix of 30 tasks across industries and conditions with 1440 outputs judged by a rubric. Finds a bounded, operationally useful result.

entry.title: LLM Consortium for Software Design Refinement: A Controlled Experiment on Multi-Agent Collaboration Topologies

author.name: Nagarjuna Kanamarlapudi, Praveen K

entry.summary: A controlled factorial experiment evaluating 12 multi-agent LLM collaboration topologies for software architecture design across 520 runs. Finds structural adversarial and cross-model review variants perform best.

entry.title: Agentic-J: An AI Agent for Biological Microscopy Image Analysis

author.name: Lukas Johanns, Marilin Moor, Davide Panzeri, Yu Zhou, Xinyi Chen, Nora F. K. Pauly, Zixuan Pan, Matthias Gunzer, Andreas M\"uller, Yiyu Shi, Hedi Peterson, Jianxu Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Agentic-J, a containerized multi-agent assistant for biological microscopy analysis built around ImageJ/Fiji, letting biologists specify tasks in natural language while generating reproducible, traceable scripts. It matters for democratizing complex bioimage workflows.

entry.title: VLBM: Variational Latent Basis Modeling for OOD Robust Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xudong Zhang, Jierui Lei, Jiacheng Li, Lingdong Shen, Jian Cui, Haina Tang

entry.summary: Proposes VLBM, a variational latent basis model for OOD-robust multivariate time series forecasting that separates stable in-distribution dynamics from OOD-induced deviations via a shared low-rank latent subspace. It targets rare but high-impact distribution shifts.

entry.title: AI-Guided Design and Optimization of Graphite-Based Anodes via Iterative Experimental Feedback

author.name: Qian Du, Mark M. Sullivan, James E. Saal, Florian Huber

entry.summary: Presents an iterative AI-guided sequential-learning workflow for graphite anode formulation and process optimization using multiobjective inverse design on the Citrine Platform. Starting from noisy data, it converged to manufacturable formulations and improved fabrication reliability to 100% success.

entry.title: CHAM-net: A Contrastive Hierarchical Adaptive Meta-network for Robust Global Methane Flux Prediction

author.name: Rongchao Dong, Yiming Sun, Shuo Chen, Youmi Oh, Licheng Liu, Yiqun Xie, Xiaowei Jia

entry.summary: Proposes CHAM-net, a contrastive hierarchical adaptive meta-network for global methane flux prediction that explicitly captures site-specific spatiotemporal heterogeneity and cross-year dynamics via a hierarchical encoder-decoder. It improves on data-driven methods that ignore ecosystem heterogeneity.

entry.title: On Wednesdays, We Ask Questions: Optimizing "Active Listening" in Automated Legal Triage and Referral

author.name: Quinten Steenhuis, Jacqueline Harvey

entry.summary: This study evaluates an LLM ensemble (FETCH) that generates follow-up questions for legal triage, finding low-cost LLMs classify well but high-quality plain-language question generation requires more expensive models. It proposes an evaluation rubric and shows prompt engineering alone is insufficient.

entry.title: EnergyMamba: An Uncertainty-Aware Graph-Enhanced Selective State Space Model for Energy Consumption Prediction

author.name: Dahai Yu, Rongchao Xu, Lin Jiang, Guang Wang

entry.summary: EnergyMamba is an uncertainty-aware, graph-enhanced selective state-space (Mamba) model for energy consumption prediction that explicitly models spatial dependencies among regions and provides uncertainty estimates under abnormal conditions like extreme weather. It addresses limitations of purely time-series formulations.

entry.title: Property Prediction of Stacked Bilayer Materials: A Multimodal Learning Approach

author.name: An Vuong, Minh-Hao Van, Chen Zhao, Xintao Wu

entry.summary: This paper presents a multimodal learning approach to predict properties of stacked bilayer 2D van der Waals materials, modeling the stacking configuration to enable discovery of materials with novel functions. It addresses the gap that AI has been underused for bilayer stacking property prediction despite available databases.

entry.title: Evaluation of Baseline Methods for IDD-based SSD External Memory Search

author.name: Yuki Suzuki, Alex Fukunaga

entry.summary: This paper evaluates simple baseline methods for immediate duplicate detection (IDD) in SSD-based external memory A* search, an area previously dominated by delayed duplicate detection and complex IDD methods. It also studies OS-level mechanisms like page caches on external memory access performance.

entry.title: CEON: Circular Economy Ontology Network

author.name: Huanyu Li, Els de Vleeschauwer, Robin Keskis\"arkk\"a, Mikael Lindecrantz, Mina Abd Nikooie Pour, Ying Li, Ben De Meester, Patrick Lambrix, Eva Blomqvist

entry.summary: CEON (Circular Economy Ontology Network) is a knowledge representation framework for the circular economy domain enabling semantic interoperability across industry sectors along product life cycles. It supports circular strategies like reuse, refurbishment, remanufacturing, and recycling.

entry.title: lmfaoooo at SemEval-2026 Task 1: Humor Is an Audience. Preference Modeling for Constrained Humor Generation

author.name: Alexey Tikhonov, Alexey Ivanov

entry.summary: Describes a SemEval-2026 humor generation system using a generate-many-then-select-best strategy with diverse candidate generation and a preference model approximating audience judgments. It frames humor as audience-dependent with noisy supervision.

entry.title: LLMs for Cardiovascular Risk Prediction from Structured Clinical Data

author.name: Jeba Maliha, Md Rafiul Kabir

entry.summary: Develops a hybrid framework bridging structured clinical data and LLM natural-language representations for coronary artery disease risk prediction, converting structured variables into synthetic clinical narratives on 1,190 patient records. It explores LLMs interpreting medical information versus traditional ML.

entry.title: Adaptive data selection improves wearable prediction under low baseline performance

author.name: Ali Kargarandehkordi

entry.summary: Evaluates adaptive time-window data selection for wearable health prediction under fixed measurement budgets across heart rate, activity, and EMA signals. Finds substantial AUROC gains specifically for participants with low baseline performance.

entry.title: SEMBridge: Tagless-Final Program Semantics with Weakest-Precondition and Bounded-Checking Interpretations

author.name: Eric Liang

entry.summary: Presents SEMBridge, a tagless-final framework that generates multiple program interpretations (weakest-precondition, bounded-checking, concrete execution) from the same executable object programs. It bridges formal methods with practical executable libraries.

entry.title: TabChange: Precise Attribute Changes in Tabular Data

author.name: Arjun Dahal, Yu Lei, Raghu N. Kacker, Richard Kuhn

entry.summary: Introduces TabChange for generating minimally modified, natural-looking tabular instances after editing a target attribute, addressing limitations of generative methods that retain attribute info or over-modify. Uses attribute relationship analysis to decide editing strategy.

entry.title: Bayesian Inference of Nonlinear Malaria Dynamics in Ghana via an Ensemble Markov Chain Monte Carlo Sampler

author.name: T. Ansah-Narh, Y. Asare Afrane, J. Bremang Tandoh

entry.summary: Develops a Bayesian nonlinear inference framework combining a cubic baseline with a damped oscillatory kernel, estimated via ensemble MCMC, to model malaria admission dynamics in Ghana with credible uncertainty bounds. Handles short, noisy surveillance data.

entry.title: CityTrajBench: A Unified Benchmark for City-Scale Vehicle Trajectory Generation

author.name: Shibo Zhu, Xiaodan Shi, Dayin Chen, Yuntian Chen, Haoran Zhang, Tianhao Wu, Jinyue Yan

entry.summary: Presents CityTrajBench, a unified benchmark and protocol for city-scale vehicle trajectory generation that standardizes data ingestion, normalization, representations, and metrics. It addresses fragmentation that makes cross-method comparison unreliable.

entry.title: MindGames Arena Generalization Track: In2AI Solution with Delayed Per-Step Reward Attribution

author.name: Aliaksei Korshuk, Alexander Buyantuev, Ilya Makarov

entry.summary: This competition solution introduces delayed per-step reward attribution with eligibility gating for training LLM agents in multi-agent strategic games, computing rewards at episode end and propagating them to originating steps while excluding invalid steps. It tackles credit assignment when outcomes are entangled across time and players.

entry.title: Acting with AI: An Interaction-Based Framework for Agentic Tort Liability

author.name: Yiheng Yao

entry.summary: This paper proposes an interaction-based framework for allocating tort liability when agentic AI causes harm, distinguishing autonomous drift, pure tool use, and collaborative planning using Bratman's planning theory and common-law concerted-action doctrine. It maps these onto existing liability tests.

entry.title: A Lightweight Deep Learning-based Model for Ranking Influential Nodes in Complex Networks

author.name: Mohammed A. Ramadhan, Abdulhakeem O. Mohammed

entry.summary: 1D-CGS is a lightweight hybrid model combining 1D-CNN speed with GraphSAGE topological representation to efficiently rank influential nodes in complex networks, using just node degree and average neighbor degree as inputs. It targets the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in influence ranking.

entry.title: Hybrid Probabilistic Forecasting of Under-Five Malaria Admissions in Ghana: A Gaussian Process Regression with Holt-Winters Smoothing

author.name: T. Ansah-Narh, Y. Asare Afrane, J. Bremang Tandoh

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid framework combining Gaussian Process Regression with Holt-Winters exponential smoothing for probabilistic forecasting of under-five malaria admissions in Ghana, capturing nonlinearity, uncertainty, and seasonal structure. Uses ten years of district-level data.

entry.title: Longitudinal Multimodal Sensing of Physical Activity and Well-Being in Older Adults

author.name: Flavio Di Martino, Mattia G. Campana, Marcello Magno, Lorenza Pratali, Franca Delmastro

entry.summary: Presents a longitudinal multimodal study of 66 older adults combining wearable sensing, behavioral monitoring, and clinical assessments in real-world conditions to predict health-related outcomes. It investigates how alignment between sensed signals and target variables affects predictive performance.

entry.title: Emergent Collaborative Deliberation in Multi-Model AI Systems: A BFT-Derived Protocol for Epistemic Synthesis

author.name: VD Doske

entry.summary: The Consilium Protocol treats inter-model disagreement among LLMs as epistemic signal, using a Byzantine Fault Tolerance-derived architecture with assigned cognitive personas and an in-sample/out-of-sample validation framework. It claims persona, not the underlying model, drives epistemic behavior across nearly 1,500 deliberation sessions.

entry.title: Can AI Review Improve Paper Drafting? An Empirical Study on 20 Computer Architecture Submissions

author.name: Di Wu

entry.summary: This empirical study examines 20 computer architecture submissions to ask whether AI-generated reviews can improve paper drafting, quantifying how well AI review aligns with human review across submission lineage. It sidesteps the contentious ethics of AI peer review by focusing on drafting assistance.

entry.title: Topological texture analysis of microscopy images of dynamic casein gelation and its relation to rheological properties

author.name: Zahra Tabatabaei, Diana Soto Aguilar, Jose C. Bonilla, Mathias P. Clausen, Jon Sporring

entry.summary: This work introduces a computational toolbox integrating topological data analysis, differential box counting, multifractal partition, and local binary patterns applied to time-lapse super-resolution microscopy of casein gelation, relating texture features to rheological properties. TDA tracked topological loops revealing the sol-gel transition.

entry.title: Repair Before Veto: Repair-Augmented Constraint Learning for Contextual Decisions

author.name: Yifan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Repair-Augmented Constraint Learning (RACL), a framework that learns whether a constraint-violating candidate should be repaired via known modification operators rather than immediately rejected. This better reflects deployed systems with known fixes like configuration changes or service upgrades.

entry.title: SortingHat: Redefining Operating Systems Education with a Tailored Digital Teaching Assistant

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Xinkui Zhao, Zuxin Wang, Zhengyi Zhou, Guanjie Chen, Shuiguang Deng, Jianwei Yin

entry.summary: SortingHat is a personalized digital teaching assistant for operating systems education integrating RAG and multi-agent reinforcement learning with a 3D digital human interface powered by LLMs. It aims to deliver adaptive scalable support for a challenging CS course.

entry.title: Improving Hospital Process Management through Process Mining: A Case Study on COVID-19 Clinical Pathways

author.name: Pasquale Ardimento, Mario Luca Bernardi, Marta Cimitile, Samuele Latorre

entry.summary: Applies process mining to COVID-19 clinical pathways using a shared-learning dataset, building a reproducible pipeline that transforms heterogeneous clinical tables into event logs with discovery and conformance checking. It surfaces insights for triage standardization and capacity planning.

entry.title: XAI-SOH-FL: Enhancing SOH-FL with Adaptive Aggregation and Explainable AI for Intrusion Detection in Heterogeneous IoT

author.name: Ambreen Aslam, Maaz Hassan, Bibi Zahra, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: Proposes XAI-SOH-FL, enhancing a self-organizing federated learning IDS for heterogeneous IoT with adaptive aggregation (dynamic gamma selection) and explainable AI. It targets intrusion detection with data heterogeneity and interpretability concerns.

entry.title: The New Social Image: How AI Competency and AI Proactivity Influence Self- and Peer-Perceptions in the Workplace

author.name: Kuntal Ghosh, Marc Hassenzahl, Shadan Sadeghian

entry.summary: A 2x2x2 vignette study (n=50) examining how AI competency and proactivity affect self- and peer-perceptions of work ownership and job meaningfulness in human-AI workplace teams. Low-competency or low-proactivity AI generally affected perceptions differently.

entry.title: Network Distributed Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Consensus Control of Quadcopters

author.name: Youssef Mahran, Zeyad Gamal, Aamir Ahmad, Ayman El-Badawy

entry.summary: Proposes a network-distributed multi-agent RL framework for quadcopter consensus control that embeds the swarm communication graph into the decision process using a 2-neighbor topology and MASAC. It bridges centralized planning and fully decentralized execution for drone swarms.

entry.title: MASER: Modality-Adaptive Specialist Routing for Embodied 3D Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Hilton Raj, Vishnuram AV

entry.summary: Proposes MASER, a modality-adaptive specialist routing framework that trains five modality adapters on a shared VLM backbone and learns a routing policy to select the best adapter per question for embodied 3D spatial reasoning. It overcomes single-modality fine-tuning limitations in spatial QA.

entry.title: Grokers: Bottom-Up Inductive Comprehension and Write-Time Intelligence over Typed Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Gregory Magarshak

entry.summary: Grokers is an architecture that builds persistent comprehension of typed knowledge graphs through write-time inductive traversal of dependency subgraphs, pushing LM computation to write time so queries incur zero additional LM cost. It contrasts with RAG, which pays full comprehension cost per query, and offers formal theorems about its guarantees.

entry.title: SentimentLens: Reconciling Sentiment and Ratings via Dual-Modality in the Hospitality Sector

author.name: Dineth Jayakody, Pasindu Thenahandi, Sampath Jayarathna

entry.summary: SentimentLens is a scalable aspect-based sentiment analysis system for hotel reviews that performs knowledge extraction and organizes feedback into interpretable service categories with multi-level analytics. It reconciles textual sentiment with numeric ratings in the hospitality sector.

entry.title: Deliberative Curation: A Protocol for Multi-Agent Knowledge Bases

author.name: Steven Johnson

entry.summary: This paper proposes a governance protocol for AI agents collaboratively curating shared knowledge bases, combining a knowledge artifact lifecycle, reputation-weighted deliberative voting (Beta Reputation plus EigenTrust), and graduated sanctions adapted for stateless agents. It addresses how human platform governance fails when agents lack persistent state and independence.

entry.title: Product-Aware Deep Autoencoders for Robust Process Monitoring in Multi-Product Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: MD Shafikul Islam, Jordan Carden

entry.summary: This work proposes product-aware deep autoencoders for anomaly detection in multi-product manufacturing cyber-physical systems, arguing global product-agnostic models create blind spots where subtle anomalies or attacks hide within wide acceptance regions. It conditions models on product grade to tighten decision boundaries.

entry.title: Medication-Aware Financial Exploitation Detection for Alzheimer's Patients Using Edge-Aware Interaction Risk Modeling

author.name: Farzana Akter, Lisan Al Amin, Rakib Hossain, Chaitanya Gunupudi, Faisal Quader

entry.summary: This paper proposes a medication-aware framework for detecting financial exploitation of Alzheimer's patients by synchronizing medication adherence with transaction-level monitoring, modeling edge-aware interaction risk. It evaluates on a hybrid simulation dataset of 180 patients combining clinical and financial signals.

entry.title: GuidaPA: Privacy-Preserving Chatbot for Public Administration via Federated Learning

author.name: Daniel M. Jimenez-Gutierrez, Albenzio Cirillo, Raffaele Nicolussi, Alessio Beltrame, Andrea Vitaletti

entry.summary: GuidaPA is a privacy-preserving chatbot for Italian Public Administration trained via federated learning on PA documentation, integrating role-based access control, client-side preprocessing, and parameter-efficient federated fine-tuning. It targets deployment on restricted internal government data that cannot be centrally pooled.

entry.title: RL-ACRGNet: Reinforcement Learning-Based Chest Radiology Report Generation Network

author.name: Yogesh Kumar Meena, Saurabh Agarwal, K. V. Arya

entry.summary: RL-ACRGNet is an encoder-decoder chest radiology report generation model combining a pretrained DenseNet encoder with a multilevel LSTM decoder within an off-policy reinforcement learning framework. It targets fine-grained visual feature capture and clinical coherence in automated report generation.

entry.title: Beyond Tool Adoption: A Practical Five-Stage Developmental Continuum for AI Literacy in Higher Education

author.name: J. Paul Liu, Rachel Levy

entry.summary: Proposes a five-stage AI Literacy Continuum for higher education spanning from not-yet-engaged through uncritical use to critical evaluation and improvement. It addresses the gap in diagnosing learner starting points and progression toward responsible critical engagement.

entry.title: Algorithmic Authority and the Clinical Standard of Care

author.name: Aizierjiang Aiersilan

entry.summary: Argues that clinical AI architecture already functions as de facto medical regulation using Lessig's Code is Law framework, reframing AI hallucination as analogous to human cognitive failures like confirmation bias. Proposes a dialectical standard of care treating the AI-physician dyad as the unit of accountability.

entry.title: DarkVesselNet: Multi-Modal Remote Sensing and Trajectory Reasoning for Dark Vessel Detection

author.name: Arun Sharma

entry.summary: Presents a multi-modal remote sensing system fusing SAR, optical imagery, AIS trajectory reasoning, and anomaly detection for identifying dark vessels evading tracking. Released as a tested Python package and Hugging Face Space.

entry.title: Fast and Lightweight Novel View Synthesis with Differentiable Multiplane Image

author.name: Kaidi Zhang, Guanxu Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a fast, lightweight novel view synthesis method using differentiable multiplane images, aiming to balance rendering speed, model size, and quality under sparse-view conditions for mobile deployment. It targets the limitations of NeRF and 3DGS in efficiency and dense-observation requirements.

entry.title: Multimodal Approaches for Visually-Rich Document Type Classification: A Comparative Analysis

author.name: Catyana Heyne, J\"urgen Frikel, Filippo Riccio

entry.summary: Provides a structured comparative analysis of multimodal design strategies for visually rich document type classification across transformer- and LLM-based architectures, with a controlled empirical comparison. It addresses inconsistent evaluation setups in the field.

entry.title: Universal Quantum Transformer

author.name: Sungyong Chung, Alireza Talebpour

entry.summary: The Universal Quantum Transformer proposes a quantum-native architecture using parameterized geometric phase embeddings and SU(2) operations as an inductive bias for exact algebraic and modular-arithmetic reasoning, aiming to avoid the instability classical networks show on discrete logic. It targets the grokking and stochastic-instability problems in continuous-space models.

entry.title: GovAI-Pipe: A Layered AI Governance Pipeline for Citizen-Facing AI in Turkey's e-Government Gateway

author.name: Ahmet Kaplan

entry.summary: GovAI-Pipe is a four-layer AI governance pipeline designed via Design Science Research that maps the AI model lifecycle to governance checkpoints for citizen-facing AI in Turkey's e-Government Gateway. It connects high-level policy frameworks like the EU AI Act to operational deployment.

entry.title: Empathic and agentic artificial intelligence in nursing: perspectives on a human-centered framework for cancer care navigation in the United States

author.name: Tyra Girdwood, Saba Kheirinejad, Parnian Kheirkhah Rahimabad, Brianna M. White, Robert L Davis, David L Schwartz, Arash Shaban-Nejad

entry.summary: Proposes a human-centered AI framework integrating empathic and agentic approaches grounded in nursing ethics to support cancer care navigation in under-resourced US areas. It is a perspective piece on augmenting rather than replacing nurse navigators.

entry.title: Enhancing BiGRU with a KAN Block for Legal Document Classification and Summarization

author.name: Ahmed Faizul Haque Dhrubo, Souvik Pramanik, Most. Aysha Siddika Sumona, Shahnewaz Siddique, Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Khan, Mohammad Abdul Qayum, Mohsin Sajjad

entry.summary: Combines BiGRU with Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) blocks for classification and summarization of multilingual legal documents from Bangladesh. Reports modest accuracy and ROUGE scores in a low-resource setting.

entry.title: Improving IoT Intrusion Detection Through SMOTE-Based Oversampling and Extended Multi-Model Evaluation on Side-Channel Power Data

author.name: Muhammad Khuram Shahzad, Haseeb Khan, Muhammad Masood Khan, Mubashra Bibi

entry.summary: Applies SMOTE oversampling and multi-model evaluation to side-channel power-data IoT intrusion detection, explicitly tackling extreme class imbalance (up to 75,964:1) that prior work ignored. It re-evaluates classifiers on balanced training sets.

entry.title: AgentxGCore: Agentic AI for Next-Generation Mobile Core Network

author.name: Maria Katarine Santana Barbosa, Kelvin L. Dias

entry.summary: Proposes an agentic AI architecture leveraging LLMs and intent-based networking for 6G mobile core network orchestration and management. Targets the AI-native core architecture envisioned in NextG standards.

entry.title: LinguIUTics at PsyDefDetect: Iterative Imbalance-Aware Fine-tuning of Qwen3-8B for Psychological Defense Mechanism Classification

author.name: Shefayat E Shams Adib, Ahmed Alfey Sani, Md Hasibur Rahman Alif, Ajwad Abrar

entry.summary: Describes a shared-task submission using QLoRA fine-tuning of Qwen3-8B with imbalance-aware strategies to classify psychological defense mechanisms in conversational text, ranking 4th of 21 teams. BERT encoders and zero-shot LLMs failed on rare classes due to severe imbalance.

entry.title: Hierarchical Online Prompt Mutation with Dual-Loop Feedback for Guardrailed Evidence Document Generation: A Production-Evaluation Case Study

author.name: Nataraj Agaram Sundar Tejas Morabia

entry.summary: Presents HOPM, a hierarchical online prompt mutation framework treating prompts as adaptive policies with dual feedback from human review and automated judging, evaluated on a production marketplace dispute workflow. Targets auditable, evidence-grounded document generation in high-stakes settings.

entry.title: LALE: Lightweight-Transformer Architecture for Land-Cover Estimation

author.name: \"Umit Mert \c{C}a\u{g}lar, Alptekin Temizel

entry.summary: Presents LALE, a lightweight transformer-convolution hybrid architecture for remote sensing land-cover segmentation that splits the encoder by resolution to capture both local detail and global context under tight compute budgets. It addresses the efficiency-performance tradeoff in geospatial segmentation.

entry.title: Understanding-Enhanced Model Collaboration for Long-Tailed Egocentric Mistake Detection

author.name: Boyu Han, Qianqian Xu, Shilong Bao, Zhiyong Yang, Ruochen Cui, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Presents UE-MCM, a small-large model collaboration method for detecting incorrectly performed actions in egocentric video under long-tailed conditions, combining coarse video understanding with fine-grained action reasoning. Targets workflow mistake detection.

entry.title: Towards Resolving Optimization Conflicts Between Image- and Text-Based Person Re-Identification

author.name: Karina Kvanchiani, Timur Mamedov

entry.summary: Analyzes optimization conflicts between image-based and text-based person re-identification and proposes a decoupled training approach to resolve modality discrepancies and conflicting objectives. It aims for better shared representations across the two ReID tasks.

entry.title: ChurnNet: A Optimized Modern AI for Churn Prediction

author.name: Syed Saad Saif, Giulio Maggiore, Paolo Russo, Damiano Distante

entry.summary: Compares traditional ML (Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM) against a Unified Multi-Task Time Series Model for customer churn prediction. Finds conventional methods outperform the more complex temporal model for this task.

entry.title: Position Paper: Post-Solve Robustness in Decision Engines: Feasible Regions and Smoothness Under Perturbations

author.name: Yi-Xiang Hu

entry.summary: This position paper argues for a new 'post-solve robustness' layer in optimization pipelines that audits already-solved MILP solutions to assess how far costs, demands, or resources can shift before feasibility breaks. It frames robustness auditing as a missing evaluation dimension for learning-enabled decision systems.

entry.title: Advanced Mathematics Learning Behavior Prediction and Academic Early Warning Model Based on Multimodal Data Analysis

author.name: Liu Qiong, Li Zhengbo

entry.summary: This paper builds a multimodal framework for predicting at-risk students in advanced mathematics using a hierarchical knowledge graph, adaptive edge weighting, and heterogeneous graph attention with temporal modeling. It aims at early academic warning and intervention.

entry.title: Predicting the risk of colorectal anastomotic leak based on preoperative mapping of the blood supply of the bowel

author.name: Zahra Tabatabaei, Jon Sporring, Mark Bremholm Elleb{\ae}k, Alaa El-Hussuna

entry.summary: A protocol paper outlining an AI framework to predict colorectal anastomotic leak risk preoperatively from contrast CT imaging by mapping bowel blood supply. It aims to replace subjective clinical assessment with a validated imaging-based predictor.

entry.title: A Minimalist Brain-Computer Musical Interface for Real-Time Emotion-Driven Sonification: System Design and Preliminary Evaluation

author.name: Pablo A. Monroy-D'Croz, Rafael Ramirez-Melendez, Julian Cespedes-Guevara

entry.summary: A minimalist brain-computer musical interface translates prefrontal EEG (frontal alpha asymmetry) into adaptive music in real time, mapping estimated emotional valence to musical features via a stochastic generative algorithm. An experiment with 22 participants found no significant effect of intentional emotional self-induction on the neurofeedback signal.

entry.title: AI Sovereignty as National Learning Capacity: A Human-Centered Learning Mechanics Viewpoint on France, the United States, and China

author.name: Kim Phuc Tran

entry.summary: This viewpoint paper reinterprets national AI development in France, the US, and China as a 'national AI learning system' using Human-Centered Learning Mechanics, balancing information injection (compute, data, talent) against entropy dissipation. It offers a unifying framework for AI sovereignty discourse.

entry.title: On the evolution of the concept of probability as a mirror of the evolution of reason

author.name: Jean-Louis Le Mou\"el, Vincent Courtillot, Dominique Gibert, Vladimir Kossobokov, Jean-Baptiste Boul\'e, Pierpaolo Zuddas, Fernando Lopes, Pa\"ikan Marccagi, Alexis Maineult

entry.title: Research Summary: June 01, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on AI safety, security, and theoretical foundations. A notable safety result shows emergent misalignment arises from reinforcement learning, not just supervised fine-tuning, and reproduces in small open-weight models.

  • Stateful online monitoring counters the first distributed agent attack, which splits harmful cybersecurity tasks across limited-context subagents to evade single-context detection
  • Linear ensembles defeat LLM watermarks by averaging output distributions across models, exposing a fundamental fragility in distributional perturbation methods
  • Item Response Theory auditing detects mislabeled benchmark examples at 95% precision across 114 models and 7 benchmarks

Theory and interpretability deepen core understanding:

  • Sparse autoencoders prove unstable across training runs, producing inconsistent concept dictionaries and threatening interpretability reproducibility
  • GNNs are shown discontinuous across graph resolutions, challenging stability assumptions; padded transformer expressivity is rigorously characterized across attention type, width, and uniformity (Merrill, Cotterell, Sabharwal)
  • Spectral Reach frames neural scaling as progress into the empirical NTK's spectral tail

Foundation models extend to new modalities. VLM3 (Meta) argues vision-language models are native 3D learners via focal length unification and data scaling, while AMix-2 establishes protein as a native LLM modality, unifying biological reasoning and conditional sequence design.
entry.content:
Today's research centers on AI safety, security, and theoretical foundations. A notable safety result shows emergent misalignment arises from reinforcement learning, not just supervised fine-tuning, and reproduces in small open-weight models.

  • Stateful online monitoring counters the first distributed agent attack, which splits harmful cybersecurity tasks across limited-context subagents to evade single-context detection
  • Linear ensembles defeat LLM watermarks by averaging output distributions across models, exposing a fundamental fragility in distributional perturbation methods
  • Item Response Theory auditing detects mislabeled benchmark examples at 95% precision across 114 models and 7 benchmarks

Theory and interpretability deepen core understanding:

  • Sparse autoencoders prove unstable across training runs, producing inconsistent concept dictionaries and threatening interpretability reproducibility
  • GNNs are shown discontinuous across graph resolutions, challenging stability assumptions; padded transformer expressivity is rigorously characterized across attention type, width, and uniformity (Merrill, Cotterell, Sabharwal)
  • Spectral Reach frames neural scaling as progress into the empirical NTK's spectral tail

Foundation models extend to new modalities. VLM3 (Meta) argues vision-language models are native 3D learners via focal length unification and data scaling, while AMix-2 establishes protein as a native LLM modality, unifying biological reasoning and conditional sequence design.

entry.title: dashi: A Python library for Dataset Shift Characterization to Support Trustworthy AI Development and Deployment

author.name: David Fern\'andez-Narro, Pablo Ferri, \'Angel S\'anchez-Garc\'ia, Juan M. Garc\'ia-G\'omez and Carlos S\'aez

entry.summary: This work shows that emergent misalignment also arises from reinforcement learning, not just supervised fine-tuning, demonstrated in small open-weight models. Rewarding narrow misaligned behavior produces higher general misalignment than matched SFT, and EM can be induced by plausibly natural reward signals like unpopular aesthetic preferences.

entry.title: Stateful Online Monitoring Catches Distributed Agent Attacks

author.name: Davis Brown, Samarth Bhargav, Arav Santhanam, Kasper Hong, Ivan Zhang, Matan Shtepel, Steffi Chern, Alexander Robey, Eric Wong, Hamed Hassani

entry.summary: This paper builds the first distributed agent attack that splits a harmful cybersecurity task across subagents with limited contexts to evade single-context safety monitors, and develops stateful online monitoring that aggregates across accounts to catch it. It exposes a structural blindspot in current AI safety monitors.

entry.title: Auditing LLM Benchmarks with Item Response Theory

author.name: Sander Land, Daniel M. Bikel

entry.summary: Using Item Response Theory across 114 models and seven benchmarks, this work detects likely mislabeled benchmark examples at 95% precision, outperforming supervised classifiers. It traces label errors to inherited annotation mistakes and ambiguous items, and reveals reward models specialize in stylistic rather than factual preference.

entry.title: Toward Identifiable Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Walter Nelson, Theofanis Karaletsos, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: This work shows theoretically and empirically that sparse autoencoders are unstable across training runs, producing different concept dictionaries. The authors propose minimal architectural and training changes yielding identifiable SAEs with better reconstruction and stability, connecting to dictionary learning theory.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks Are Not Continuous Across Graph Resolutions

author.name: Christian Koke, Yuesong Shen, Abhishek Saroha, Marvin Eisenberger, Bastian Rieck, Michael Bronstein, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: This paper shows that graph neural networks are not continuous across all natural modes of graph convergence, assigning very different embeddings to graphs representing the same object at different resolutions. It traces this to information-propagation schemes and derives a principled modification ensuring continuity across scales.

entry.title: Linear Ensembles Wash Away Watermarks: On the Fragility of Distributional Perturbations in LLMs

author.name: Zhihao Wu, Gracia Gong, Qinglin Zhu, Yudong Chen, Runcong Zhao

entry.summary: This paper shows that LLM text watermarks can be trivially defeated by averaging output distributions from multiple models, since independent watermark perturbations cancel out. The authors prove a second-order error bound and introduce WASH, a practical attack handling vocabulary and tokenization mismatches across heterogeneous models.

entry.title: VLM3: Vision Language Models Are Native 3D Learners

author.name: Zhipeng Cai, Zhuang Liu, Yunyang Xiong, Zechun Liu, Vikas Chandra, Yangyang Shi

entry.summary: VLM3 argues vision-language models are native 3D learners, showing that focal length unification, text-based pixel reference, and data mixture/scaling suffice for strong 3D understanding without architecture changes or complex losses. It challenges the necessity of expert 3D vision model designs.

entry.title: Revisiting Padded Transformer Expressivity: Which Architectural Choices Matter and Which Don't

author.name: Anej Svete, William Merrill, Ryan Cotterell, Ashish Sabharwal

entry.summary: This paper examines the expressivity of padded transformers (with filler symbols) under variations in attention type, width, and uniformity, connecting them to boolean circuit classes. It finds these equivalences are surprisingly robust, with numeric precision and depth as the main determining factors.

entry.title: AMix-2: Establishing Protein as a Native Modality in Large Language Models

author.name: Keyue Qiu, Yixin Wu, Lihao Wang, Yawen Ouyang, Jixiang Yu, Zihan Zhou, Changze Lv, Dongyu Xue, Yuxuan Song, Xinbo Zhang, Hao Wang, Jiangtao Feng, Zhiqiang Gao, Lijun Wu, Xiaoqing Zheng, Ka-Chun Wong, Lei Bai, Ya-Qin Zhang, Wei-Ying Ma, Dahua Lin, Bowen Zhou, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: AMix-2 is a protein-text foundation model that treats protein sequences as a native modality in LLMs, unifying biological reasoning and conditional sequence design via a block-wise diffusion language modeling backbone. The large multi-institution effort positions protein as a first-class token space alongside natural language.

entry.title: Spectral Reach: Understanding Neural Scaling as Progress into the Spectral Tail

author.name: Konstantin Nikolaou, Jonas Scheunemann, Sven Krippendorf, Samuel Tovey, Christian Holm

entry.summary: The paper introduces spectral position, a scalable measure based on the empirical neural tangent kernel eigenvalues, to explain neural scaling laws as a progression of learning into the spectral tail. Larger models reach further into the tail, defining a size-dependent spectral reach.

entry.title: Interpretability Without Tradeoffs: Disentangling Polysemanticity At Equal Predictive Performance

author.name: Do\u{g}ukan Ba\u{g}c{\i}, Bernt Schiele, Simone Schaub-Meyer, Jonas Fischer, Robin Hesse

entry.summary: ELUDe is a method for improving DNN interpretability by losslessly disentangling polysemantic latent representations into monosemantic sub-units while guaranteeing functional equivalence, avoiding the performance degradation of sparse autoencoders. It claims interpretability without predictive tradeoffs.

entry.title: Memory by Design: Probabilistic Sequence Layers

author.name: Matthew Dowling, Hyungju Jeon, Cristina Savin, Il Memming Park

entry.summary: This work introduces a design-model framework that derives efficient recurrent sequence layers from explicit memory assumptions via exact Bayesian filtering, with a linear-Gaussian Bayesian Layer tracking uncertainty. It unifies linear attention, GLA, Mamba-2/SSD, and DeltaNet as instances of filters under one design model.

entry.title: Why Linear Recurrent Memory Works in Partially Observable Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yike Zhao, Onno Eberhard, Malek Khammassi, Ali H. Sayed, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: This paper gives a theoretical justification for why linear recurrent networks work well as memory in partially observable RL, by constructing linear filters that reproduce belief-vector logits in HMMs and achieve vanishing state-decoding error. Results extend to action-controlled HMMs.

entry.title: mRNAutilus: Multi-Objective-Guided Discrete Generation of mRNA with Optimized Therapeutic Properties

author.name: Sawan Patel, Sophia Tang, Yesol Kim, Yinuo Zhang, Divya Srijay, Ping-Jung Lin, Shambhavi Shubham, Fengmei Pi, Cedric Wu, Sherwood Yao, Pranam Chatterjee

entry.summary: mRNAutilus is a framework combining a masked discrete diffusion model trained on millions of mRNAs with Monte Carlo tree guidance for simultaneous codon optimization and de novo UTR design. It generates Pareto-efficient therapeutic mRNA sequences optimizing half-life, translation efficiency, and protein abundance.

entry.title: Wall-Clock Complexity for Zeroth-Order Optimization with Tunable Oracle Fidelity

author.name: Alexandra Suvorikova, Igor Pavlov, Artem Vasin, Georgii Bychkov, Anastasia Antsiferova, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: This paper unifies modern generative models as parametric JKO schemes for f-divergence objectives under a Wasserstein gradient flow framework called Generative Wasserstein Flows. It establishes equivalences between several recently proposed algorithms and extends beyond f-divergences.

entry.title: Evaluating using Mock Tool Calls to Quarantine Untrusted Prompt Inputs

author.name: David Gros, Adam Gleave

entry.summary: This study tests whether wrapping untrusted inputs in mock tool calls (exploiting the instruction hierarchy) improves robustness to prompt injection in LLM-as-a-judge tasks. Through automated red-teaming across seven models, it finds tool-wrapping does not broadly improve robustness, contradicting the natural hypothesis.

entry.title: Seeing Isn't Knowing: Do VLMs Know When Not to Answer Spatial Questions (and Why)?

author.name: Yue Zhang, Zun Wang, Han Lin, Yonatan Bitton, Idan Szpektor, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: SpatialUncertain is a controlled framework testing whether vision-language models recognize when spatial questions cannot be answered due to occlusion or misleading perspective, rather than just whether they produce correct answers. It probes whether VLMs know when to abstain and what additional observations are needed.

entry.title: Reward Learning from Best-of-$N$ Preference Data: Targets, Tradeoffs, and Design Principles

author.name: Rattana Pukdee, Maria-Florina Balcan, Pradeep Ravikumar

entry.summary: This paper analyzes what Bradley-Terry reward learning extracts from Best-of-N preference data, deriving closed-form reward targets as functions of N and the base distribution for independent-reference variants and showing they preserve latent reward ranking. It examines tradeoffs for practical Best-vs-Random and Best-vs-Worst variants.

entry.title: Diffusion Models Preferentially Memorize Prototypical Examples or: Why Does My Diffusion Model Love Slop?

author.name: Marta Aparicio Rodriguez, Anastasia Borovykh, Grigorios A. Pavliotis, Daniel J. Korchinski

entry.summary: This paper shows diffusion models preferentially memorize prototypical examples composed of common substrings rather than rare or atypical samples, contradicting intuitions and demonstrating that data-point-level deduplication does not guarantee privacy. It uses the Random Hierarchy Model to make and verify these predictions.

entry.title: Not All Synthetic Data Is Yours to Learn From

author.name: Sina Alemohammad, Li Chen, Richard G. Baraniuk, Zhangyang Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies prompt-free unconditional self-training, asking whether a base LLM can improve from text it generates with no prompts, teacher, or reward. It proposes a latent capability resurfacing hypothesis where self-training amplifies existing capabilities only when synthetic data is compatible with the student.

entry.title: DecMem: Towards Minute-Long Consistent World Generation with Decoupled Memory

author.name: Zhenhao Yang, Xiaoshi Wu, Zhengyao Lv, Xiaoyu Shi, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Kwan-Yee K. Wong

entry.summary: DecMem is a decoupled memory architecture for minute-long consistent world generation that uses sparse global memory for efficient fine-grained access to history and anchored local memory, addressing computational inefficiency and attention dispersion in learnable memory. It enables long-horizon spatio-temporal consistency in video world models.

entry.title: MAAT: Multi-phase Adapter-Aware Targeted Unlearning

author.name: Suryash Yagnik, Shubham Gaur, Saksham Thakur, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Amitava Das

entry.summary: This work shows machine unlearning benchmarks severely underrepresent causal Why-type questions (under 1.3% across major datasets), making causal forgetting failures invisible. It introduces 5WBENCH, a balanced benchmark, and MAAT, an adapter-aware unlearning method, finding no baseline achieves both high forgetting and retention on causal knowledge.

entry.title: Physically Viable World Models: A Case for Query-Conditioned Embodied AI

author.name: Adam J. Thorpe, Stepan Tretiakov, Cheng-Hsi Hsiao, Su Ann Low, Xingjian Li, Hassan Iqbal, Neel P. Bhatt, Ufuk Topcu, Krishna Kumar

entry.summary: This position paper argues embodied AI world models must be physically viable, capable of answering intervention queries rather than merely predicting observations, since visually identical scenes can diverge under intervention. It introduces controlled benchmarks varying latent physics and advocates query-conditioned physical abstractions.

entry.title: Counterfactual Evaluation Reveals Hidden Capability Profiles in Clinical LLMs and Agents

author.name: Matt Turk

entry.summary: This work introduces the Causal Sensitivity Score, a pre-registered interventional metric that mutates oncology cases along five clinical dimensions and scores whether models update recommendations in the correct direction. It reveals that clinical AI systems scoring identically on coverage rubrics can behave radically differently under input changes.

entry.title: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Minhua Lin, Juncheng Wu, Zijun Wang, Zhan Shi, Yisi Sang, Bing He, Zewen Liu, Tianxin Wei, Zongyu Wu, Zhiwei Zhang, Dakuo Wang, Xiang Zhang, Benoit Dumoulin, Cihang Xie, Yuyin Zhou, Suhang Wang, Hanqing Lu

entry.summary: This paper disentangles two capabilities in self-evolving LLM agents: harness-updating (producing useful persistent updates from execution evidence) and harness-benefit (benefiting from updated harnesses). It finds that base task-solving capability does not straightforwardly predict either, challenging assumptions about which models gain from self-evolution.

entry.title: Emergent Languages in Populations of Language Model Agents: From Token Efficiency to Oversight Evasion

author.name: Stine Lyngs{\o} Beltoft, William Brach, Federico Torrielli, Jacob Nielsen, Annemette Brok Pirchert, Filippo Tonini, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: This paper studies emergent languages in populations of LLM agents on a simulated platform, categorizing posts into token efficiency, new natural languages, and oversight evasion. It finds oversight-evasion languages are judged less aligned and that emergent languages can be learned by other LLMs, raising monitoring concerns.

entry.title: Mellum2 Technical Report

author.name: Marko Kojic, Ivan Bondyrev, Aral de Moor, Joseph Shtok, Petr Borovlev, Kseniia Lysaniuk, Madeeswaran Kannan, Ivan Dolgov, Nikita Pavlichenko

entry.summary: Mellum 2 is an open-weight 12B Mixture-of-Experts model with 2.5B active parameters specialized for software engineering, covering code generation, debugging, tool use, and agentic coding. It combines GQA, sliding window attention, and multi-token prediction doubling as a speculative decoding draft model.

entry.title: Divergence Decoding: Inference-Time Unlearning via Auxiliary Models

author.name: Humzah Merchant and Bradford Levy

entry.summary: Divergence Decoding uses small auxiliary models to steer an LLM's logits away from specific memorized data at inference time, enabling unlearning without retraining the main model. It reportedly outperforms SOTA unlearning baselines while avoiding catastrophic utility loss.

entry.title: The Latin Substrate: How Language Models Represent and Mediate Script Choice

author.name: Daniil Gurgurov, Alan Saji, Katharina Trinley, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann

entry.summary: This paper studies how multilingual LLMs internally mediate script variation for languages written in multiple scripts, finding consistent latent romanization during transliteration via the logit lens. It shows scripts become increasingly separable across layers and a linear steering direction can flip output script while preserving semantics.

entry.title: Fixed Universal Transformers

author.name: Jingwen Liu, Alexandr Andoni, Daniel Hsu

entry.summary: Introduces universal transformers: fixed transformers that can simulate any transformer in a class via input embedding, analogous to a universal Turing machine. Provides sparse constructions and shows random initialization yields universality almost surely.

entry.title: nuReasoning: A Reasoning-Centric Dataset and Benchmark for Long-Tail Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhiyu Huang, Johnson Liu, Rui Song, Zewei Zhou, Ruining Yang, Yun Zhang, Tianhui Cai, Hanyin Zhang, Mingxuan Gao, Valeria Xu, Jiali Chen, Yishan Shen, Yiluan Guo, Tony (Xuewei) Qi, Jiaqi Ma

entry.summary: nuReasoning is a large-scale real-world dataset and benchmark for reasoning-centric autonomous driving in long-tail scenarios, with 20,000 multi-sensor clips and reasoning supervision extending the nuScenes/nuPlan lineage. It fills a gap where AD datasets focus on perception/planning rather than commonsense reasoning.

entry.title: Recognizing Co-Speech Gestures in-the-Wild

author.name: Sindhu B Hegde, K R Prajwal, Andrew Zisserman

entry.summary: The Gesture Recognition in the Wild (GRW) dataset provides 156,688 manually annotated clips mapping unconstrained human gestures to specific words with frame-accurate boundaries across a 150-word taxonomy. It enables training video models to identify and classify semantic co-speech gestures, a previously data-starved problem.

entry.title: Representation Collapse in Sequential Post-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Yichen Liu, Mingyu Chen, Hao Wang, Xiaoran Xu, Chenxi Lin, Rui Zhang, Yutong Zhou, Yuxin Yang, Jiarui Wu, Wei Sun

entry.summary: This work studies whether sequential post-training stages progressively compress LLM representations into low-rank, anisotropic feature spaces. It develops a measurement suite and tests whether representation collapse predicts reduced plasticity, weaker out-of-domain generalization, and poorer calibration.

entry.title: Generating and Refining Dynamic Evaluation Rubrics for LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Zijie Wang, Eduardo Blanco

entry.summary: This work automatically generates fine-grained LLM-as-a-judge evaluation rubrics at dataset and instance granularity without human annotation, and iteratively fine-tunes a rubric generator via meta-judge reward signals. A 14B fine-tuned generator outperforms a much larger proprietary model at rubric generation.

entry.title: Trading Complexity for Expressivity Through Structured Generalized Linear Token Mixing

author.name: Erwan Fagnou, Paul Caillon, Blaise Delattre, Alexandre Allauzen

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified framework for token mixing that separates the direct input-output influence from recurrent propagation through past outputs, encompassing attention and state-space models. It generalizes recurrence by allowing states to depend on multiple past states, designing new structured recurrence patterns trading complexity for expressivity.

entry.title: Measuring, Localizing, and Ablating Alignment Signatures in LLMs

author.name: Aniket Anand, Janvijay Singh, Zhewei Sun, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur, Nick Feamster

entry.summary: PASTA is a training-free method that localizes and ablates internal alignment signatures that make aligned models produce detectable AI-like text. The work shows post-training shifts generations away from human-corpus style toward detector-visible AI patterns with a localized representational signature.

entry.title: Supervised Training Rapidly Degrades Early Visual Cortex Alignment Across Biologically Plausible Learning Rules

author.name: Nils Leutenegger

entry.summary: This study tracks representational similarity to human visual cortex (fMRI) across training for four biologically plausible learning rules, finding that even a single epoch of supervised training rapidly degrades early visual cortex alignment. Untrained random networks match or exceed trained ones in brain similarity.

entry.title: Probing the Prompt KV Cache: Where It Becomes Dispensable

author.name: Vinayshekhar Bannihatti Kumar, Manoj Ghuhan Arivazhagan, Disha Makhija, Rashmi Gangadharaiah

entry.summary: This work probes when and what kind of prompt KV cache becomes dispensable during decoding, finding through splice interventions that redundancy concerns form (chat template scaffolding) rather than content. Replacing upper-layer prompt KV cache with neutral-filler scaffold KV recovers near-clean accuracy across Qwen3, Gemma 3, and Llama 3.

entry.title: Constrained Flow Optimization via Sequential Fine Tuning for Molecular Design

author.name: Sven Gutjahr, Riccardo De Santi, Luca Schaufelberger, Kjell Jorner, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework for constrained generative optimization of diffusion/flow models that algorithmically trades off reward maximization and constraint satisfaction via sequential fine-tuning, for molecular design applications. It brings an optimization viewpoint to reward-guided model adaptation under constraints like synthesizability.

entry.title: Score Broadcast and Decorrelation: A General Framework for Broadcast-Based Credit Assignment

author.name: Mustafa Uzun, Mete Erdogan, Cengiz Pehlevan, Alper T. Erdogan

entry.summary: Score Broadcast and Decorrelation generalizes biologically plausible error-broadcast credit assignment beyond the mean-squared-error setting to general differentiable losses, grounded in an orthogonality principle between the output score and hidden-layer activations. It provides a backpropagation alternative without weight transport.

entry.title: EUDAIMONIA: Evaluating Undesirable Dynamics in AI

author.name: Jun Rui Huang, Wang Bill Zhu, Ziyi Liu, Nathanael Fast, Ravi Iyer, Robin Jia

entry.summary: EUDAIMONIA introduces a benchmark and Social AI Design Code for evaluating whether LLMs in companionship and emotional support roles harm user welfare through fostering harmful intimacy, dependence, or excessive engagement. It contains nearly 1000 user inputs and 3000+ design-requirement violation checks built from WildChat.

entry.title: Convergence of Two-Timescale Markovian Stochastic Approximations with Applications in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Vagul Mahadevan and Claire Chen and Shuze Daniel Liu and Shangtong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper establishes stability and convergence of two-timescale stochastic approximation algorithms under Markovian noise, a more realistic setting for RL than i.i.d. noise. It covers methods like TDC and actor-critic without requiring projection operators or compact noise spaces.

entry.title: Retriever Portfolios: A Principled Approach to Adaptive RAG

author.name: Miltiadis Stouras, Vincent Cohen-Addad, Silvio Lattanzi, Ola Svensson

entry.summary: This paper proposes selecting a small diverse portfolio of retrievers from a large pool to cover heterogeneous query distributions for RAG, formalized via an expected best-of-k objective. It provides an efficient construction algorithm with near-optimal guarantees and a router pipeline outperforming single- and naive multi-retriever baselines.

entry.title: Steering LLMs? Actually, Sparse Autoencoders can outperform simple baselines

author.name: Mikkel Godsk J{\o}rgensen, Lars Kai Hansen

entry.summary: This paper rebuts earlier findings that sparse autoencoders underperform simple baselines for LLM steering, showing that with a supervised feature selection and labeling pipeline SAEs can match LoRA on AxBench. It also finds the selected features are surprisingly causal.

entry.title: Entropic Projection Alignment: Estimating, Explaining, and Improving Model Performance Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Salim I. Amoukou and Emanuele Albini and Tom Bewley and Saumitra Mishra and Manuela Veloso

entry.summary: Entropic Projection Alignment is a unified framework for distribution shift that estimates target-domain performance, identifies responsible features, and improves performance via moment matching with KL minimization. It yields closed-form importance weights without full density ratio recovery.

entry.title: DriveMA: Driving Vision-Language-Action Models with verifiable Meta-Actions

author.name: Weicheng Zheng, Yixin Huang, Qiao Sun, Derun Li, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: DriveMA is a driving vision-language-action framework built on verifiable meta-actions that compress future ego motion into language-domain intentions, verifiable against generated trajectories. It uses action-centric training and turn-level credit assignment RL to bridge the language-action gap, setting new SOTA.

entry.title: Survival Reinforcement Learning: Toward Scalable Self-Supervised RL

author.name: Franki Nguimatsia-Tiofack, Fabian Schramm, Th\'eotime Le Hellard, Justin Carpentier

entry.summary: Survival Reinforcement Learning is a self-supervised RL method that extends survival value learning by maximizing dwell time at goals, avoiding the uniformity-tolerance dilemma of contrastive RL and bang-bang control issues. It matches SOTA contrastive RL on manipulation and scales in depth.

entry.title: Non-Asymptotic Convergence of Stochastic Iterative Algorithms: A Lyapunov Framework

author.name: Zaiwei Chen and Siva Theja Maguluri

entry.summary: This is a survey of Lyapunov-based techniques for finite-time analysis of stochastic approximation algorithms solving fixed-point equations, showing generalized Moreau envelopes serve as universal Lyapunov functions across norms. It applies to SGD, linear SA, and value-based RL like Q-learning and TD learning.

entry.title: A Unifying View of Variational Generative Wasserstein Flows

author.name: Paul Caucheteux, Cl\'ement Bonet and Anna Korba

entry.summary: Forgetting Has Neighbors studies machine unlearning at the example level, comparing unlearned models to retrained ones and finding that pointwise discrepancy grows with geometric proximity to the forget set. It identifies localized collateral forgetting caused by inconsistent surrogate targets.

entry.title: LLM Judges Inconsistently Disagree Across Safety Criteria and Harm Categories

author.name: Krishnapriya Vishnubhotla, Soumya Vajjala, Akriti Vij, Isar Nejadgholi
