entry.summary: Studies LLMs as bargaining agents under different information regimes, evaluating their honesty (information disclosure/deception) and credulity against game-theoretic benchmarks. Investigates whether profit-optimized agents become stronger but more dishonest negotiators.

entry.title: VolFill: Single-View Amodal 3D Scene Reconstruction with Volumetric Flow Matching

author.name: Tuan Duc Ngo, Chuang Gan, Evangelos Kalogerakis

entry.summary: Introduces VolFill, a generative framework for single-view amodal 3D scene reconstruction using a hybrid 3D VAE and latent diffusion transformer to recover complete scene geometry including hidden structures. Conditions on geometry foundation models for robust spatial priors.

entry.title: AutoSci: A Memory-Centric Agentic System for the Full Scientific Research Lifecycle

author.name: Weitong Qian, Beicheng Xu, Zhongao Xie, Bowen Fan, Guozheng Tang, Jiale Chen, Xinzhe Wu, Mingtian Yang, Chenyang Di, Jiajun Li, Lingching Tung, Peichao Lai, Yifei Xia, Ziyi Guo, Yanwei Xu, Yanzhao Qin, Shaoduo Gan, Xupeng Miao, Bin Cui

entry.summary: Presents AutoSci, a memory-centric agentic system spanning the full scientific research lifecycle from literature and ideation through experiments and review responses. Built around schema-governed persistent research memory that improves over time.

entry.title: Scalable Inference-Time Annealing with Surrogate Likelihood Estimators

author.name: Daniel Pe\~naherrera, Rishal Aggarwal, David Ryan Koes

entry.summary: Presents SITA, a scalable inference-time annealing method that retrains flow-based models down a temperature ladder using surrogate likelihood estimators to avoid intractable divergence computations. Enables Boltzmann sampling for larger molecular systems.

entry.title: Chem-PerturBridge: a harmonized compendium of small molecule perturbation transcriptomic effects

author.name: Artur Sza{\l}ata, Olga Novitskaia, Maiia Shulman, Matthew Mella, Altynbek Zhubanchaliyev, Fabian J. Theis

entry.summary: Introduces Chem-PerturBridge, a harmonized resource of small-molecule perturbation transcriptomics with 37k+ compounds, 136 cellular contexts, and 1.25M samples across eight assays with standardized metadata. Reveals generally weak cross-dataset agreement, important for perturbation modeling.

entry.title: The Dynamic-Probabilistic Consistency Gap in Chaotic Surrogate Modeling

author.name: Andre Herz, Matthijs Pals, Daniel Durstewitz, Georgia Koppe

entry.summary: Identifies a dynamic-probabilistic consistency gap in chaotic surrogate modeling, where probabilistic objectives can degrade dynamics or decouple uncertainty from local tangent dynamics. Isolates three mechanisms (core collapse, noise masking, blind uncertainty) and proposes mitigations.

entry.title: Disagreeing Rationales: Rethinking Classification and Explainability Evaluation in Hate Speech Detection

author.name: Benedetta Muscato, Beiduo Chen, Gizem Gezici, Barbara Plank, Fosca Giannotti

entry.summary: This paper rethinks classification and explainability evaluation for hate speech detection by treating human disagreement in token-level rationales as signal rather than noise, unifying diverse models and metrics under one protocol. It highlights how rationale variation reflects richness in subjective NLP tasks.

entry.title: When LLM Reward Design Fails: Diagnostic-Driven Refinement for Sparse Structured RL

author.name: Youting Wang, Yuan Tang, Bowen Liu, Xuan Liu and Dingyan Shang

entry.summary: This paper reframes LLM-generated reward shaping for sparse RL tasks as an iterative debugging problem rather than one-shot generation. It identifies common failure modes and proposes diagnostic-driven refinement, dramatically improving performance on MiniGrid tasks like DoorKey and KeyCorridor.

entry.title: LongDS-Bench: On the Failure of Long-Horizon Agentic Data Analysis

author.name: Kewei Xu, Xiaoben Lu, Shuofei Qiao, Zihan Ding, Haoming Xu, Lei Liang, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: LongDS-Bench is a benchmark for long-horizon, multi-turn data analysis where agents must maintain, update, restore, and compose evolving analytical states across many turns. Built from 68 real Kaggle notebooks with 2,225 turns, it shows the best of five SOTA models reaches only about 48% accuracy.

entry.title: Your Multimodal Speech Model Says I Have a Face for Radio

author.name: Maya K. Nachesa and Vlad Niculae and Vagrant Gautam

entry.summary: This paper presents the first bias evaluation of multimodal speech recognition by pairing different faces with identical audio and measuring transcription accuracy changes. It finds large quality-of-service differences across mWhisper-Flamingo and Gemini models, with word error rate drops of up to 4.05.

entry.title: Discovering a Zeta Map Algorithm on Dyck Paths via Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Xiaoyu Huang, Blake Jackson, Kyu-Hwan Lee

entry.summary: This paper uses mechanistic interpretability to reverse-engineer how a small transformer learns the zeta map bijection on Dyck paths, a classical combinatorics construction. Through attention analysis, linear probing, and causal intervention, it discovers a level-based algorithm that can be translated into an explicit, independently checkable construction.

entry.title: ELAN4D: Embodiment-Centric 4D Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models via Plug-and-Play Adaptation

author.name: Zeyuan He, Bowen Yang, Zhirui Fang, Keru Zhou, Lei Jiang, Jingjing Qian, Fan Mo, Junchi Yan, Philip Torr, Xiu Li, Li Jiang, Jialin Yu

entry.summary: ELAN4D is an embodiment-centric, 4D-aware plug-and-play training framework that enhances vision-language-action models with future robot keypoint tracks as predictive spatio-temporal supervision. It derives 3D displacement tracks from forward kinematics at negligible cost, improving generalization under out-of-distribution perturbations.

entry.title: VLM-GLoc: Vision-Language Model Enhanced Monte Carlo Localization for Robust Semantic Global Localization in Cluttered Quasi-Static Environments

author.name: Shivendra Agrawal, Bradley Hayes

entry.summary: VLM-GLoc uses open-vocabulary vision-language models as a semantic layer for Monte Carlo localization in cluttered, geometrically ambiguous indoor settings like stores and offices. It tackles long-tail semantic distributions and transient clutter that defeat traditional pipelines.

entry.title: Destruction is a General Strategy to Learn Generation; Diffusion's Strength is to Take it Seriously; Exploration is the Future

author.name: Pierre-Andr\'e No\"el

entry.summary: This conceptual paper frames diffusion models within a broader family of information-withholding learning techniques, arguing diffusion's destruction-based approach is uniquely flexible for data-scarce settings. It discusses challenges in porting RL exploration techniques to diffusion and offers a tutorial.

entry.title: Zeroth-Order Non-Log-Concave Sampling with Variance Reduction and Applications to Inverse Problems

author.name: M. Berk Sahin, Behzad Sharif, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: This paper proposes a variance-reduced zeroth-order Langevin sampling method for high-dimensional non-log-concave distributions in black-box settings where gradients are inaccessible. It provides non-asymptotic convergence guarantees and improved dimensional dependence over classical estimators, with inverse-problem applications.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware and Temporally Regulated Expert Advice in Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ahmed Abouelazm, Felix Klingebiel, Philip Sch\"orner, and J. Marius Z\"ollner

entry.summary: This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware RL framework for autonomous driving that triggers expert advice when epistemic or aleatoric uncertainty exceeds adaptive thresholds, with a commitment-cooldown strategy to regulate guidance duration. It avoids long-term dependence on expert advice while guiding safe exploration.

entry.title: An Organization-Scoped LLM Agent Runtime Architecture for Regulated Cybersecurity Operations

author.name: George Fatouros, Georgios Makridis, George Kousiouris, John Soldatos, Dimosthenis Kyriazis

entry.summary: This paper proposes an organization-scoped LLM agent runtime architecture for regulated cybersecurity operations, enforcing organization-level scope across retrieval, tool calls, memory, findings, and audit while remaining model-agnostic and locally deployable. It integrates with existing SIEM/XDR stacks for alert-driven workflows.

entry.title: ZAPS-DA: Zero-Phase Action Policy Smoothing with Decoupled Actor for Continuous Control in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Faiq Shamass

entry.summary: ZAPS-DA reduces high-frequency action jitter in RL continuous control by pairing an unmodified main actor with a separate decoupled actor trained via supervised imitation of zero-phase filtered targets. The deployed decoupled actor achieves smooth actions with negligible phase lag and no post-processing.

entry.title: Improving Selective Classification with Pairwise Queries for Binary Classification

author.name: Harsh Vardhan, Sunav Choudhary, Natwar Modani, Arya Mazumdar

entry.summary: This paper improves selective classification for binary tasks by making additional pairwise queries to the same model to detect high-error samples where confidence is inconsistent with predictions. It reduces error on non-rejected points, addressing failures common in LLM in-context classification.

entry.title: BOKBO (Best of K Bad Options): Calibrated Abstention for VLA Policies

author.name: Anya Singh, Cabrel Happi, Jai Relan, Varun Nair, and Vidyut Baradwaj

entry.summary: BOKBO is a conformal abstention layer for K-sample vision-language-action policy inference that provides distribution-free guarantees on the rate of executed safety violations when all sampled candidate actions are unsafe. It exposes a structural flaw in policy-internal nonconformity scores under perturbation-based sampling.

entry.title: How Early Adopters Used Generative AI Worldwide: Variation by Country Income and Language

author.name: Madeleine I. G. Daepp, Isaac Slaughter

entry.summary: This empirical study characterizes how early adopters use a free AI chatbot across countries, finding schooling-related use dominates in low-income countries while leisure use rises with income, and English overrepresentation where local languages were poorly served. It draws on a large anonymized interaction dataset to map global usage variation.

entry.title: ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: Tao Feng, Chongrui Ye, Tianyang Luo, Jingjun Xu, Xueqiang Xu, Haozhen Zhang, Zhigang Hua, Yan Xie, Shuang Yang, Ge Liu, and Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: ExpGraph is a model-agnostic experience learning framework that summarizes agent trajectories into reusable skills and failure lessons organized as a self-evolving experience graph, retrieved via graph diffusion and utility-aware ranking. It lets frozen, replaceable LLM executors improve from past experience without parameter updates.

entry.title: Reducing the GPU Memory Bottleneck with Lossless Compression for ML -- Extended

author.name: Aditya K Kamath, Arvind Krishnamurthy, Marco Canini, Simon Peter

entry.summary: This work tackles GPU memory bottlenecks in ML by using lossless compression instead of accuracy-degrading lossy methods, introducing Invariant Bit Packing which eliminates invariant bits across tensors to minimize PCIe data transfer time. It identifies where lossless compression integrates into ML pipelines with minimal interference.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought and Compressed Looped Transformers: A Memory-Budget Separation

author.name: Haozhou Zhang

entry.summary: This theoretical paper compares three test-time memory regimes for reasoning: compressed latent loops, full sequence-state loops, and chain-of-thought scratchpads, arguing persistent mutable memory is the central resource. The main result shows compressed loops are bounded by recurrent state size, so running longer adds compute but not growing scratchpad space.

entry.title: SSR: Scaling Surefooted and Symmetric Humanoid Traversal to the Open World

author.name: Ruiqi Yu, Yiwen Wang, Yuan Hao, Jun WU, Qiuguo Zhu

entry.summary: SSR is an end-to-end framework for egocentric vision-based humanoid traversal in open-world heterogeneous terrain, introducing imagined foothold guidance that models forthcoming swing-foot contacts to guide stable foot placement. It uses equivariant latent-space symmetry augmentation to efficiently induce bilateral coordination under high-dimensional visual observations.

entry.title: XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks

author.name: Purvam Jain, Preethi Jyothi, Vihari Piratla and Suvrat Raju

entry.summary: XLGoBench introduces synthetic algorithmic tasks to detect cross-lingual skill gaps in LLMs, designed to be commensurate across languages, scalable in complexity, quantifiable in correctness, and transparent via auditable templates. Differential performance across languages on the same underlying task indicates cross-lingual capability gaps.

entry.title: Incremental BPE Tokenization

author.name: Shenghu Jiang, Ruihao Gong

entry.summary: This paper presents an incremental BPE tokenization algorithm running in near-logarithmic time per byte and maintaining tokenizations for all prefixes, enabling efficient streaming tokenization. It serves as a drop-in BPE replacement with up to 3x speedup over Hugging Face tokenizers.

entry.title: Function2Scene: 3D Indoor Scene Layout from Functional Specifications

author.name: Ruiqi Wang, Qimin Chen, Daniel Ritchie, Angel X. Chang, Manolis Savva, Kai Wang, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: Function2Scene generates 3D indoor layouts from functional design briefs describing occupants and activities, deriving constraints from a 17-criterion taxonomy spanning spatial, ergonomic, activity, and environmental factors. It reframes scene synthesis around how spaces are used rather than which objects to place.

entry.title: Spectral Anatomy of Quantum Gaussian Process Kernels

author.name: Jian Xu, Chao Li, Guang Lin, Yuning Qiu, Delu Zeng, John Paisley, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: This work unifies two recent negative results about quantum Gaussian processes (loss of speedup and posterior pathologies) by showing both are governed by the normalized spectral entropy of the kernel Gram matrix. It provides tail bounds and variance-contraction identities linking expressiveness to failure modes.

entry.title: Generating Reports or Repeating Templates? Measuring and Mitigating Template Collapse in 3D CT Report Generation

author.name: Tom Maye-Lasserre, Yitong Li, Bailiang Jian, Morteza Ghahremani, Benedikt Wiestler, Christian Wachinger

entry.summary: This paper identifies template collapse, where 3D CT report-generating VLMs produce fluent but generic templates that under-report rare critical findings, and proposes CLarGen, a decoupled framework separating clinical content from text generation. It diagnoses the failure via clinical fidelity, diversity, and rare-finding survival metrics.

entry.title: Parallel Tempering Initial Sampling in Inference-Time Reward Alignment

author.name: Myeongjun Oh, Gwangho Kim, Sungyoon Lee

entry.summary: PATHS uses parallel tempering for initial particle sampling in inference-time reward alignment of diffusion and flow models, overcoming SMC methods that get trapped in local modes of complex multi-modal reward landscapes. It enables better steering toward rare high-reward regions without retraining.

entry.title: HetCCL: Enabling Collective Communication For Mixed-Vendor Heterogeneous Clusters

author.name: Yuejie Wang, Tao Chang, Yuanyuan Zhao, Yulong Ao, Zeyu Gu, Zhiyu Li, Yanmin Jia, Yan Zhang, Mingjun Zhang, He Liu, Yongzhe He, Yonghua Lin, Guyue Liu

entry.summary: HetCCL is a collective communication framework enabling efficient AllReduce and related operations across mixed-vendor heterogeneous GPU clusters, eliminating host-device memory copy overhead via efficient P2P transport with CPU-offloaded control. It addresses the inability of NCCL/RCCL to handle multi-vendor LLM training setups.

entry.title: TRACE: Discovering Task-Specific Parameter via Adaptation-Aware Probing for Continual Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xiaosong Han, Ke Chen, Xindi Dai, Di Liang, Minlong Peng, Wei Pang, Fausto Giunchiglia, Xiaoyue Feng, Yonghao Liu, Renchu Guan

entry.summary: TRACE reframes continual LLM fine-tuning as task-specific parameter discovery via a short warm-start probe that exposes a task's adaptation trace, enabling targeted updates that avoid catastrophic forgetting without replay or many separate adapters. It exploits LLM parameter redundancy to isolate task-relevant parameters.

entry.title: GraphARC: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Graph-Based Abstract Reasoning

author.name: Saku Peltonen, August B{\o}gh R{\o}nberg, Andreas Plesner, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: GraphARC is a benchmark extending the ARC abstract reasoning paradigm to graph-structured data, requiring inference of transformation rules from few input-output pairs across local, global, and hierarchical graph operations. State-of-the-art language models show clear limitations on it, exposing reasoning gaps.

entry.title: SlotMemory: Object-Centric KV Memory for Streaming Long-Video Generation

author.name: Weijia Dou, Hui Li, Jiahao Cui, Lei Zhou, Jingdong Wang, and Siyu Zhu

entry.summary: SlotMemory is an object-centric key-value memory mechanism for streaming long-video diffusion that organizes history by what is being represented rather than when, decomposing the KV manifold into reusable semantic slots. This enables entity-level persistence and reduces identity drift during long generation and prompt transitions.

entry.title: Task-Focused Memorization for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Tao Zou, Yichen He, Tian Qiu, Yuan Lin, Hang Li

entry.summary: TaskMem frames memory generation for multimodal agents as a learnable memorization policy that selectively decides what to retain from an unbounded stream of observations based on relevance to the agent's role and future tasks. It moves beyond memory module design to the question of what to memorize.

entry.title: iVGR: Internalizing Visually Grounded Reasoning for MLLMs with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chang-Bin Zhang, Yujie Zhong, Qiang Zhang, Kai Han

entry.summary: iVGR shows that mandating explicit object boxes in visually grounded chain-of-thought at inference can hurt MLLM performance versus textual CoT, and proposes reinforcement learning to internalize visual localization into the textual reasoning. It removes interfering explicit grounding while retaining its benefits.

entry.title: On the Robustness of Multilingual Text Embedding Rankings Across Learning Tasks, Languages, and Benchmark Datasets

author.name: Ana Gjorgjevikj, Barbara Korou\v{s}i\'c Seljak, Tome Eftimov

entry.summary: This meta-study examines how robust multilingual text-embedding model rankings on MTEB are to dataset composition and aggregation choices. It introduces dataset-composition and ranking-scheme robustness indicators to expose hidden sensitivity in benchmark conclusions.

entry.title: Learning Hyperspherical Time-Frequency Representations for Time-Series Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Willian T. Lunardi, Samridha Shrestha, and Martin Andreoni

entry.summary: This paper formulates time-series out-of-distribution detection as hyperspherical representation learning using a von Mises-Fisher objective, combining time- and frequency-domain encoders. Detection uses distance-based scores like kNN and Mahalanobis over the learned embeddings.

entry.title: MIMO: Multilingual Information Retrieval via Monolingual Objectives

author.name: Youngjoon Jang, Seongtae Hong, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: MIMO improves multilingual information retrieval where queries and documents span different languages in mixed corpora, addressing language clustering and the alignment-uniformity trade-off. It anchors a student model to a stable English semantic space from a strong teacher via a two-stage framework.

entry.title: From Local Geometry to Global Pseudo Labeling for Robust Positive Unlabeled Learning under Covariate Shift

author.name: Firas Gabetni, Alexandre Rocchi Henry, Nacim Belkhir, Ziyi Liu, Gianni Franchi

entry.summary: SPUNA addresses covariate shift detection using positive-unlabeled learning, a weaker supervision setting that avoids needing labeled shifted examples. It uses a spectral, geometry-aware neighborhood annotation to progressively discover pseudo-labels and stabilize PU learning under heavy distribution overlap.

entry.title: HiERO-StepG @ Ego4D Step Grounding Challenge: hierarchical activity understanding enables zero-shot step grounding

author.name: Andrea Zenotto, Simone Alberto Peirone, Francesca Pistilli, Giuseppe Averta

entry.summary: HiERO-StepG performs zero-shot step grounding in procedural egocentric videos by leveraging hierarchical activity representations that emerge from uncurated videos through recurring action co-occurrence. It detects procedure steps via simple clustering without task-specific annotations, targeting the Ego4D Step Grounding Challenge.

entry.title: Before Parc Ferm\'e: RL-Time Pruning for Efficient Embodied LLMs in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Luca Benfenati, Ali Azimi, Matteo Risso, Fabio Carapellese, Daniele Jahier Pagliari, Alessio Burrello

entry.summary: Before Parc Ferme proposes pruning embodied LLM controllers during reinforcement learning rather than before or after, so pruning decisions account for closed-loop task feedback. Two variants are explored for autonomous driving deployment efficiency.

entry.title: Practical Cross-Band Channel Prediction for AI-RAN via Physics-Guided Deep Unfolding

author.name: Ruiqi Kong, He Chen, Xiaojun Lin

entry.summary: GUIDE is a physics-guided deep unfolding framework for cross-band channel prediction in AI-native radio access networks, embedding wireless physics into differentiable layers for generalization without retraining. It achieves large beamforming gains and dramatic speedups over baselines.

entry.title: Neither Replacement nor Panacea: Comparing LLM-Based Conversational and Graphical Decision Support in Industrial Tasks

author.name: Roberto Figli\`e, Simone Caputo, Alan Serrano, Daria Mikhaylova, Tommaso Turchi, Daniele Mazzei

entry.summary: This mixed factorial study with 134 industrial decision-makers compares LLM-based conversational agents against dashboards for manufacturing decision support across tasks of varying complexity. It finds neither is a universal replacement, with effectiveness depending on information-processing demands.

entry.title: S$^3$LDBO: A Snapshot Single-Loop Algorithm for Decentralized Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Chao Yin, Youran Dong, Shiqian Ma, Bofan Wang, Junfeng Yang

entry.summary: S3LDBO is a single-loop decentralized bilevel optimization algorithm that uses a snapshot mechanism to intermittently skip expensive derivative evaluations, reducing computation for networked multi-agent learning. It targets hyperparameter optimization, data cleaning, and meta-learning over communication networks.

entry.title: Social welfare optimisation under institutional reward and punishment

author.name: Van An Nguyen, Vuong Khang Huynh, Huu Loi Bui, Hai Anh Ha, Quang Dung Le, Tan Dat Nguyen, Ngoc Ngu Nguyen, Zhao Song, Manh Hong Duong, Le Hong Trang and The Anh Han

entry.summary: This paper develops a welfare-centric framework for institutional incentives (rewards and punishments) in finite populations playing social dilemmas, deriving explicit expressions for expected social welfare net of institutional cost. It examines whether cooperation-maximizing schemes also maximize total welfare.

entry.title: DynaTree: Dynamic Agentic Retrieval Tree for Time-Sensitive News Retrieval

author.name: Siyuan Qi, Xinyuan Wang, Yingxuan Yang, Haochuan Guo, Jianghao Lin, Weiwen Liu, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: DynaTree is a two-stage framework for time-sensitive news retrieval that builds a reusable semantic retrieval tree offline and performs lightweight daily subtree selection online, avoiding costly per-query agentic reasoning. It improves efficiency for time-sensitive retrieval over coupled agentic RAG methods.

entry.title: YARD: Y-Architecture Register Decoding for Efficient Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ting Chen, Geng Li, Guohao Chen, Yu Hu, Guan Huang, Mai Chen, Langsheng Lei, Jun Du

entry.summary: Introduces YARD, a training-free contrastive decoding method that mitigates VLM hallucinations by constructing the degraded branch internally via register tokens in middle decoder layers. Avoids the latency and crudeness of dual forward passes.

entry.title: VisionPulse: Dynamic Visual Sparsity for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Hengbo Xu, Shengjie Jin, Yanbiao Ma, Zhiwu Lu

entry.summary: Introduces VisionPulse, a step-wise visual token pruning method that exploits the step-dependent, evolving nature of critical visual evidence during multimodal reasoning. Reduces inference overhead while addressing query-irrelevant attention drift.

entry.title: When Are Multimodal Predictions Biologically Supported? A Diagnostic Evaluation Framework

author.name: Dylan Steiner, Gustavo Arango-Argoty, Gerald Sun, Etai Jacob

entry.summary: Introduces DECAT, a model-agnostic post-hoc framework that classifies multimodal oncology representations into four diagnostic scenarios (shared biology, modality-confined, spurious, indeterminate) using null-referenced metrics. Helps distinguish genuine biological signal from confounders.

entry.title: CoFiDA-M: Concept-Aware Feature Modulation for Cross-Domain Adaptation with Image-Only Inference

author.name: Nurjahan Sultana, Moi Hoon Yap, Xinqi Fan, Wenqi Lu

entry.summary: CoFiDA-M is a privileged-information domain adaptation framework for skin cancer screening that learns from MONET clinical concept probabilities at training time but deploys as an image-only model via FiLM modulation. It addresses the deployment paradox of unavailable concept metadata at test time when shifting from dermoscopic to clinical images.

entry.title: MeMo: Towards Language Models with Associative Memory Mechanisms

author.name: Fabio Massimo Zanzotto and Elena Sofia Ruzzetti and Giancarlo A. Xompero and Leonardo Ranaldi and Davide Venditti and Federico Ranaldi and Cristina Giannone and Andrea Favalli and Raniero Romagnoli

entry.summary: MeMo introduces a language model architecture that explicitly memorizes token sequences in layered associative memories, rather than relying on learned memorization in standard Transformers. The approach offers transparency and editability, including the ability to forget specific texts.

entry.title: Physics-Aligned Canonical Equivariant Fourier Neural Operator under Symmetry-Induced Shifts

author.name: Jiaxiao Xu, Changhong Mou, Yeyu Zhang, Fengxiang He

entry.summary: PACE-FNO improves neural operators for solving PDEs by separating coordinate alignment from physical evolution, using known continuous symmetries. It estimates the input frame, maps to a reference frame, applies a standard Fourier Neural Operator, and restores the prediction, improving out-of-distribution generalization.

entry.title: Exploring Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering for Model Specialization

author.name: Yujie Luo, Xiangyuan Ru, Jingsheng Zheng, Jingjing Wang, Yuqi Zhu, Jintian Zhang, Runnan Fang, Kewei Xu, Ye Liu, Zheng Wei, Jiang Bian, Zang Li, Shumin Deng

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering, evaluating whether LLM agents can autonomously run an end-to-end data curation pipeline for model specialization, treating data as an optimizable component. Agents plan, generate, and iteratively optimize training data guided by downstream post-training performance.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Gradient Aggregation in Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Zeou Hu, Kelvin Ho, Yaoliang Yu

entry.summary: This paper develops a unifying framework for gradient aggregation in multi-objective optimization, establishing optimal convergence rates to Pareto stationarity. It introduces a sufficient alignment condition showing that non-conflicting directions within the convex hull of gradients guarantee convergence, unifying disparate prior methods.

entry.title: Can Subgraph Explanations Be Weaponized to Steal Graph Neural Networks?

author.name: Ojas Nimase, Jiate Li, Yue Zhao, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: This paper presents the first model extraction attack on graph classification under strict black-box constraints, where the attacker observes only class labels and binary explanation masks. It uses explanation outputs to guide Monte Carlo edge sensitivity estimation toward decision boundaries with concentration guarantees.

entry.title: Physics-informed Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning under Hybrid Contact Dynamics

author.name: Vittorio Giammarino, Anastasios Manganaris, Ahmed H. Qureshi

entry.summary: The paper extends physics-informed goal-conditioned reinforcement learning to contact-rich manipulation tasks with hybrid dynamics where existing methods struggle. It examines reliability when contact interactions induce mode-dependent controllability and nonsmooth value landscapes.

entry.title: True Self-Avoiding Walk for Accelerating Markov-Chain Monte Carlo Integration

author.name: Qinghua (Devon) Ding, Venkat Anantharam

entry.summary: This paper studies true self-avoiding walks (TSAW) for accelerating MCMC integration, proving that empirical occupation and transition counts deviate from their stationary targets by only O(sqrt(log t)). This yields tighter integral estimators than standard Markov chain sampling.

entry.title: AI for Monitoring and Classifying Data Used in Research Literature

author.name: Rafael Macalaba and Aivin V. Solatorio

entry.summary: This work develops scalable AI methods to monitor and classify dataset usage in research literature, where no citation-tracking infrastructure currently exists. It introduces a multitask GLiNER-based approach building on LLM data-mention detection and synthetic bootstrapping.

entry.title: Controllable Lung Nodule Synthesis via Histogram-Regularized Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Arunkumar Kannan, Yanbo Zhang, Han Liu, Michael Baumgartner, Jianing Wang, Alexander Hertel, Bogdan Georgescu, Sasa Grbic

entry.summary: This work proposes a histogram-regularized latent diffusion model for controllable lung nodule synthesis, addressing how spatial-reconstruction-loss approaches over-smooth textures and underrepresent attenuation characteristics of nodule subtypes. It better constrains lesion-level intensity distributions for solid, part-solid, and ground-glass nodules.

entry.title: Convergence of Steepest Descent and Adam under Non-Uniform Smoothness

author.name: Sharan Vaswani, Yifan Sun, Reza Babanezhad

entry.summary: The authors generalize non-uniform smoothness assumptions to objectives whose curvature is an affine function of the objective value, covering logistic regression, GLMs, and softmax policy gradients. They derive convergence rates for steepest descent and deterministic Adam/RMSProp variants under these conditions.

entry.title: ElasticMem: Latent Memory as a Learnable Resource for LLM Agents

author.name: Tao Feng, Chongrui Ye, Tianyang Luo, Jingjun Xu, Xueqiang Xu, Haozhen Zhang, Ge Liu, and Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: ElasticMem treats long-term memory for LLM agents as an elastic latent resource, building an offline latent memory bank with retrieval keys and content caches that adapts allocation to query-dependent utility. It reduces token overhead and noise sensitivity compared to fixed text-space or rigid latent memory approaches.

entry.title: CameraNoise: Enabling Faithful Camera Control in Video Diffusion through Geometry-Flow-Guided Noise Warping

author.name: Haoyu Zhao, Jiaxi Gu, Haoran Chen, Qingping Zheng, Yeying Jin, Hongyi Yang, Junqi Cheng, Yuang Zhang, Zenghui Lu, Huan Yu, Jie Jiang, Peng Shu, Zuxuan Wu, and Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: CameraNoise enables faithful camera pose control in video diffusion by encoding camera motion into a temporally coherent stochastic noise representation via geometry-guided reprojection flow and a noise warping algorithm. This decouples motion from scene appearance while preserving trajectory dynamics, avoiding distortions from directly injecting numerical camera parameters.

entry.title: Conformal Reliability: A New Evaluation Metric for Conditional Generation

author.name: Yachen Gao, Xinwei Sun, Yikai Wang, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang, Jianfeng Feng, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a conformal-prediction-based reliability score that measures worst-case performance within a prediction set at a chosen confidence level for conditional generative models. It addresses the computational challenge of high-dimensional, nonconvex output spaces and prediction sets.

entry.title: Local linear convergence of gradient methods for overparameterized Gaussian mixtures

author.name: Jingxing Wang, Vasileios Charisopoulos, Maryam Fazel

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the local convergence of gradient methods for learning overparameterized Gaussian mixture models, showing that a Polyak stepsize can restore geometric (linear) convergence on a manifold where the loss otherwise grows slowly. It matters because overparameterization avoids spurious optima but normally slows convergence, and this work offers a principled fix.

entry.title: RDGen: Demonstration Generation for High-Quality Robot Learning via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zijian Zhu, Menglin Zou, Zhuang Li, Yaojie Tu, Xinhai Sun

entry.summary: RDGen is a sim-to-real RL framework that uses trained RL policies as trajectory generators to produce high-quality robot demonstrations, reducing reliance on costly human teleoperation for training VLA models. It combines a VLM task parser, Grounding DINO localization, and RL trajectory generation.

entry.title: A Persona-Based Evaluation Framework for Pluralistic Alignment in Generative AI

author.name: Atahan Karagoz

entry.summary: This paper proposes a persona-based evaluation framework for pluralistic alignment that replaces monolithic benchmarks with a structured manifold of synthetic cognitive profiles representing diverse human perspectives. It shows generative models can maintain these evaluative personas consistently while analyzing their stability limits.

entry.title: Routing on the Stiefel Manifold: When Does Adaptive Subspace Selection Help for Cross-Domain EEG Decoding?

author.name: Isabella Costa Maia, Pedro L. C. Rodrigues, Salem Said, Marco Congedo

entry.summary: This paper proposes dynamic Stiefel routing for cross-domain EEG decoding, using a pool of expert projection filters on the Stiefel manifold with cross-attention routing to adapt subspace projection per sample without target calibration. A key finding is that naive implementations collapse to ensemble averaging, motivating careful design.

entry.title: AdaptR1: Reinforcement Learning Based Adaptive Interleaved Thinking in Multi-hop Question Answering

author.name: Yuxin Wang, Jiahao Lu, Qifeng Wu, Shicheng Fang, Chuanyuan Tan, Yining Zheng, Xuanjing Huang, and Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: AdaptR1 is an RL framework for adaptive interleaved thinking in multi-hop QA, making per-stage decisions about whether to reason explicitly rather than a single query-level choice, to combat over-thinking. It avoids supervised fine-tuning and reduces avoidable inference cost on multi-step tasks.

entry.title: Learning to Bid in FCR Markets: A Best-of-Both-Worlds Approach

author.name: Marius Potfer, Cheng Wan, Pierre Gruet

entry.summary: This paper recasts bidding in the European Frequency Containment Reserve market as a repeated multi-unit uniform-price auction against hidden opposing bids, adapting a best-of-both-worlds combinatorial semi-bandit algorithm using only standard market feedback. It achieves logarithmic regret in stochastic and square-root regret in adversarial environments.

entry.title: Beyond Static Dialogues: Benchmarking Realistic, Heterogeneous, and Evolving Long-Term Memory

author.name: Han Zhang, Zihao Tang, Xin Yu, Xiao Liu, Yeyun Gong, Haizhen Huang, Yan Lu, Weiwei Deng, Feng Sun, Qi Zhang, Hanfang Yang

entry.summary: RHELM is a benchmark for evaluating long-term memory in LLMs that constructs realistic, heterogeneous, and evolving dialogues with dynamic personas and diverse data streams like documents and emails, addressing the flat static personas of existing benchmarks. It uses a plan-rollout-evolve-prune module to ensure long-term coherence.

entry.title: SpecDB: LLM-Generated Customized Databases via Feature-Oriented Decomposition

author.name: Yunkai Lou, Longbin Lai, Shunyang Li, Zhengping Qian, Ying Zhang

entry.summary: SpecDB uses LLMs to synthesize customized relational databases by decomposing production systems into functional modules and variants captured in a dependency graph. It matches database feature sets to specific workloads rather than shipping uniform feature sets, potentially reducing bloat and improving efficiency.

entry.title: NTR: Neural Token Reconstruction for Scene Token Bottleneck in End-to-End Driving

author.name: Jiahui Li, Jiawei Sun, Zixiang Ren, Ming Liu, Jiamin Shi, Ruiteng Zhao, Zhiyang Liu, Liying Liu, Zuoguan Wang, Kaidi Yang

entry.summary: NTR introduces a self-distillation masked latent reconstruction objective to add representation supervision to the compact scene-token bottleneck in perception-free end-to-end autonomous driving. It constrains the encoded visual information beyond the planning loss alone.

entry.title: QVGGT: Post-Training Quantized Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer

author.name: Zhizhen Pan, Hesong Wang, Huan Wang

entry.summary: QVGGT is a post-training quantization framework compressing the 1.2B-parameter VGGT 3D geometry transformer for deployment on UAVs and mobile AR. It uses per-block sensitivity analysis with selective mixed-precision allocation to fragile blocks.

entry.title: Learning Whom to Trust: Market-Feedback Adaptive Retrieval for Frozen LLMs in Event-Driven Financial RAG

author.name: Zijie Zhao, Roy E. Welsch

entry.summary: This work studies event-driven financial RAG with a frozen LLM reader and an adaptive retrieval layer that learns which evidence sources to trust based on market-feedback Bayesian source memory. It predicts multi-horizon residual-return signals for news-triggered events on a Nasdaq stock universe.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Text-to-Image Models for Generating Visual Representations in Early Arithmetic Education

author.name: Junling Wang, Boqi Chen, Heejin Do, Mubashara Akhtar, April Yi Wang, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: This paper introduces equation-to-visual generation, a task requiring text-to-image models to produce pedagogically meaningful visuals from arithmetic equations while preserving numerical structure. It builds E2V-Bench with automatic metrics, revealing that recent T2I models frequently fail at this educational task.

entry.title: Latent Geometric Chords for Query-Efficient Decision-Based Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Ei Hmue Khine, Yao Li, Jiebao Sun, Shengzhu Shi, Zhichang Guo, and Boying Wu

entry.summary: LGC proposes query-efficient decision-based black-box adversarial attacks that navigate decision boundaries via curvature-aware geometric search within a compressed semantic manifold. A residual-based adversarial generation mechanism ensures high visual fidelity while avoiding dimensionality bottlenecks.

entry.title: What changes after deployment? A survey on On-device Learning in TinyML

author.name: Massimo Pavan, Luca Pezzarossa, Fabrizio Pittorino, Manuel Roveri, Xenofon Fafoutis

entry.summary: This survey reviews around 70 on-device learning works for TinyML organized by the distribution-change regime, characterizing how different change types require different solutions. It identifies a persistent gap between methodological benchmarks and real-world deployment scenarios.

entry.title: Fraud Type Decomposition and the Observation-Mechanism Taxonomy:Class-Specific Detection Limits in Payment Networks

author.name: Gaurav Dhama

entry.summary: This work argues fraud is not a homogeneous binary variable and introduces an observation-mechanism taxonomy partitioning fraud into five classes by labeling pipeline. It proves class-specific estimation dominates pooled estimation and derives theoretical detection limits per class.

entry.title: GETA: Generalized Encrypted Traffic Analysis

author.name: Ransika Gunasekara, Rahat Masood, Salil Kanhere

entry.summary: GETA is a protocol-agnostic framework for encrypted traffic analysis that models flows as multivariate time series using only metadata, combining meta-learning, embedding refinement, and self-attention. It avoids reliance on payloads or protocol-specific header features for cross-environment generalization.

entry.title: Latent Space Disentanglement via Activation Steering for Interpretable Attribute Control in Symbolic Music Generation

author.name: Ioannis Prokopiou, Pantelis Vikatos, Maximos Kaliakatsos-Papakostas, Theodoros Giannakopoulos, Themos Stafylakis

entry.summary: This work applies activation steering with the difference-in-means method to achieve interpretable, retraining-free control over pitch and duration attributes in symbolic music generation via the Multitrack Music Transformer. It validates the linear representation hypothesis in this domain.

entry.title: MoE-dqINR: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Implicit Neural Representation Framework for Scan-Specific Dynamic and Quantitative MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Yinzhe Wu, Fanwen Wang, Zhenxuan Zhang, Zi Wang, Chengyan Wang, Guang Yang

entry.summary: MoE-dqINR is a mixture-of-experts implicit neural representation framework for scan-specific dynamic and quantitative MRI reconstruction, decoupling shared spatial information from state-adaptive synthesis. It aims to improve flexibility and reduce the high per-scan optimization times of prior INR methods.

entry.title: Diagnosing Failure Modes of Shared-State Collaboration in Resource-Constrained Visual Agents

author.name: Yunpeng Zhou

entry.summary: This single-author paper studies failure modes of shared working memory in collaborative visual reasoning with weak 4B-8B models, introducing the CoSee auditing framework. It identifies counterintuitive degradation where shared workspaces amplify hallucinations via noise reinforcement and policy collapse.

entry.title: LiftNav: Path Planning via Semantic Lifting in TSDF-Guided Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Hannah Schieber, Dominik Frischmann, Victor Schaack, Angela P. Schoellig, Daniel Roth

entry.summary: LiftNav is a hybrid navigation framework combining TSDF geometry with Gaussian Splatting semantics, using YOLO detection, TSDF-based 3D lifting, and B-spline trajectory optimization for semantic indoor navigation. It adds a hinge-loss collision penalty for smoother, safer trajectories without dense 3D embeddings.

entry.title: IDOL: Inverse-Dynamics-Guided Future Prediction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chenghao Zhang, Timin Li, Dongmei Li

entry.summary: Proposes IDOL, an inverse-dynamics-guided future prediction framework for end-to-end autonomous driving that converts predicted scene evolution into planning-relevant trajectory updates. Addresses the weak coupling between world-model forecasting and executable motion.

entry.title: Batched Differentiable Rigid Body Dynamics in PyTorch for GPU-Accelerated Robot Learning

author.name: Yue Wang, Yanran Xu, Wenbo Wu, Chuanhang Qiu, and Zhaoxing Li

entry.summary: Presents BARD, a self-contained PyTorch implementation of Featherstone rigid-body dynamics optimized for batched GPU evaluation and autodiff, removing the CPU-bound Pinocchio bottleneck. Matches Pinocchio numerically while enabling GPU-accelerated robot learning.

entry.title: Balanced LoRA: Removing Parameter Invariance to Accelerate Convergence

author.name: Val\'erie Castin, Kimia Nadjahi, Pierre Ablin, Gabriel Peyr\'e

entry.summary: Investigates folding a rewarded population of Gaussian-perturbed model specialists (RandOpt-style) into a single deployable model rather than an inference-time ensemble. Exploits reproducible low-rank structure to consolidate updates for LLM post-training.

entry.title: UniAudio-Token: Empowering Semantic Speech Tokenizers with General Audio Perception

author.name: Yuhan Song, Linhao Zhang, Aiwei Liu, Chuhan Wu, Sijun Zhang, Wei Jia, Yuan Liu, Houfeng Wang, Xiao Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces UniAudio-Token, a framework giving semantic speech tokenizers general audio perception via Semantic-Acoustic Primitives and a content-aware gating equilibrium mechanism. Mitigates the acoustic blindness of speech-focused tokenizers without losing linguistic ability.

entry.title: Preference-Aware Rubric Learning for Personalized Evaluation

author.name: Yilun Qiu, Xiaoyan Zhao, Yang Zhang, Yuxin Chen, Cilin Yan, Jiayin Cai, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu, Yoko Yamakata, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Proposes Personalized Evaluation as Learning, reframing personalized LLM evaluation as a learning problem guided by three principles (representativeness, user-consistency, discriminativeness) with preference-aware rubric learning. Captures subjective user-specific preferences from interaction histories.

entry.title: On couplings for kinetic Langevin diffusions

author.name: Nawaf Bou-Rabee and Sonja Cox and Roy Schieven

entry.summary: This probability-theory paper studies couplings for the kinetic Langevin diffusion, proving no Markovian coupling captures the asymptotic TV decay rate for quadratic potentials and giving the sticky coupling an exact contraction formula. It also interprets recent sharp TV bounds via an explicit non-Markovian coupling.

entry.title: Notes on axes of variation in third-party risk assessment

author.name: Buck

entry.summary: Buck Shlegeris outlines distinctions and axes of variation in third-party AI risk assessment, clarifying roles of developers, stakeholders, and third parties such as auditors and pentesters. It provides a conceptual framework useful for AI governance and safety evaluation discussions.

entry.title: Updating the standard neuron model in artificial neural networks

author.name: Raul Mohedano and Thomas Batard and Erik Velasco-Salido and Ramsses De Los Santos Mendoza and Jorge H. Mart\'inez and Stacey Levine and Marcelo Bertalm\'io

entry.summary: This paper replaces the classic point-neuron model in artificial neural networks with a recent, more biologically realistic cortical-cell model, without adding parameters. The authors claim theoretical and experimental gains in expressivity, robustness, and learning.

entry.title: Unicorn: Scaling High-Dimensional Time Series Forecasting via Universal Correlation Modeling

author.name: Haochen Yuan, Yichen Song, Yunbo Wang, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: Unicorn is a framework for scalable multi-dataset pretraining on high-dimensional time series that uses a latent prototype codebook to decouple correlation modeling from specific channel identities. This lets it learn reusable interaction patterns transferable across datasets with diverse dimensionalities.

entry.title: Learning Transferable Predictability Representations

author.name: Diyali Goswami and Auroop R. Ganguly

entry.summary: This paper formalizes ordinal estimation of trajectory predictability on a five-level ladder spanning deterministic to stochastic dynamics, identifying a gauge-freedom problem where ranking supervision leaves the score coordinate unfixed. It proposes the Gauge-Fixed Ordinal Network for consistent cross-system predictability scores.

entry.title: Automatically Attacking Software Reverse Engineering AI Agents

author.name: Brian Crawford, Justin Phillips and Patrick McClure

entry.summary: This work demonstrates a genetic-algorithm-based prompt attack (a modified AutoDAN) that deceives LLM-powered reverse engineering agents like GhidraMCP into misinterpreting binaries, enabling malware obfuscation. It exposes a new adversarial vulnerability in agentic decompilation workflows.

entry.title: Human-Alignment, Calibration, and Activation Patterns in Large Language Model Uncertainty

author.name: Kyle Moore, Jesse Roberts, Daryl Watson, William Ward, Grayson Heyboer

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLM uncertainty resembles human uncertainty (uncertainty alignment) in both overt behavior and internal activations, distinct from the usual calibration focus. It examines simultaneous alignment and calibration across multiple-choice and open-ended factual recall datasets.

entry.title: Primitive Subspaces Mediate Few-Shot Transfer in VLAs

author.name: Anya Singh, Cabrel Happi, Jai Relan, Varun Nair, Vidyut Baradwaj

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether primitive-aware training of vision-language-action policies produces a transferable library of composable sub-skills enabling few-shot transfer to unseen tasks without fine-tuning. It compares OpenVLA and pi-0.5 under matched LoRA recipes on contact-rich assembly with held-out object-tasks.

entry.title: Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment for LLM Agents

author.name: Jianxiang Yu, Jiapeng Zhu, Bochen Lin, Qier Cui, Zichen Ding, Xiang Li

entry.summary: MASA shows that skill effectiveness for LLM agents is strongly model-dependent, where a skill helping one backbone can harm another, and proposes model-aware skill alignment that adapts skills to each target backbone without modifying weights. It uses a hierarchical skill evolution pipeline to rewrite general and task-specific skills.

entry.title: Efficient and Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Framework for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ha Manh Bui, Metod Jazbec, Eric Nalisnick, Anqi Liu

entry.summary: DUAL is an efficient diffusion uncertainty-aware framework for offline-to-online RL that distills a fast-sampling diffusion actor and transition model offline, then uses Laplace approximation and transition-state-shift detection to handle distribution shifts. It addresses the costly online interactions and offline-online distribution mismatch in O2O-RL.

entry.title: Feat2Go: Visual Feature-Grounded Value Estimation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Junyang Shu, Zhiwei Lin, Bingqing Wei and Yongtao Wang

entry.summary: Feat2Go is a fine-grained value estimation framework for embodied RL of vision-language-action models that derives a continuous progress target from a pretrained visual world model via patch-level similarity to subgoals and trend-based clustering. It trains an embodied value model to predict structural progress, addressing sparse supervision and reward-design difficulty in long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: MultiAct: Text-to-Motion Generation from Composite Text via Tailored Attention Guidance

author.name: Nathan Sala, Ofir Abramovich, Ariel Shamir, Daniel Cohen-Or, Andreas Aristidou, Sigal Raab

entry.summary: MultiAct is an inference-time, unpaired framework for compositional text-to-motion generation that amplifies cross-attention for underrepresented prompt components to prevent semantic collapse on multi-action prompts. It operates on pretrained motion generators without retraining.

entry.title: Batched Stochastic Linear Bandits with 1-Bit Communication Constraints

author.name: Ivan Lau, Daniel McMorrow, Kevin Jamieson and Jonathan Scarlett

entry.summary: This paper studies stochastic linear bandits where the learner sends batched arm pulls and receives only a single bit of feedback per batch, a middle ground between per-round quantization and total bit budgets. It establishes a minimax lower bound and matching algorithmic results.

entry.title: MoG: Mixture of Experts for Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zheng Yuan, Chuang Zhou, Linhao Luo, Siyu An, Di Yin, Xing Sun, Xiao Huang

entry.summary: MoG applies a mixture-of-experts approach to graph-based retrieval-augmented generation, organizing knowledge into always-accessible hub graphs and sparsely activated expert graphs to reduce irrelevant retrieved context for complex reasoning. It aims to improve grounding by routing among specialized knowledge experts.

entry.title: Model Monotonicity in Autobidding Auctions: When Do Better Predictions Lead to Better Outcomes?

author.name: Ashwinkumar Badanidiyuru

entry.summary: This paper develops a framework for autobidding auctions to characterize when better ML predictions of click and conversion rates lead to better platform outcomes like revenue and welfare, using a refinement-based definition of model improvement. It systematically maps ECM monotonicity across bidder types and auction formats.

entry.title: Best-Arm Identification-Based Trust Region Selection for Bayesian Optimization on Multimodal Functions

author.name: Nobuo Namura and Sho Takemori

entry.summary: This paper integrates best-arm identification with trust-region Bayesian optimization for multimodal functions, extrapolating optimizer trajectories to predict final performance and progressively eliminating suboptimal candidate regions. It provides theoretical convergence guarantees for the BAI-guided approach.

entry.title: KnowledgeGain: Evaluating and Optimizing Science News Generation for Reader Learning

author.name: Dominik So\'os, Meng Jiang, Jian Wu

entry.summary: KnowledgeGain introduces a metric measuring how much knowledge readers actually learn from science news rather than just semantic similarity or factual consistency. It is validated with controlled human studies and a calibrated LLM reader simulator for ranking articles.

entry.title: Don't Fool Me Twice: Adapting to Adversity in the Wild with Experience-Driven Reasoning

author.name: Navin Sriram Ravie, Andrew Jong, Krrish Jain, John Liu, Omar Alama, Bijo Sebastian, Sebastian Scherer

entry.summary: This work proposes a continual learning framework letting a mobile robot learn online from disturbances and attribute anomalous behaviors to semantic causes, beyond pre-listed VLM-predicted dangers. The goal is embodiment-specific adaptation to unforeseen adversities in unstructured environments.

entry.title: TARIC: Memory-Augmented Traversability-Aware Outdoor VLN under Interrupted Semantic Cues

author.name: Tianle Zeng, Hanjing Ye, Jianwei Peng, Jingwen Yu, Hanxuan Chen, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: TARIC is a memory-augmented, traversability-aware outdoor vision-language navigation method addressing semantic-cue interruptions when goal cues disappear. It treats traversability as a stability condition for maintaining goal-directed guidance during cue-free phases.

entry.title: Contextual Scalarisation Thompson Sampling for multi-objective decisions in public media

author.name: Th\'eo Ma\"etz, Luc Guillet and Andrea Cavallaro

entry.summary: Contextual Scalarisation Thompson Sampling is a multi-objective contextual bandit method that learns context-dependent weights over competing objectives, applied to public service media recommendation. It improves contextual relevance and alignment with expert curation versus fixed-weight and Pareto baselines.

entry.title: Haptic Sorter: A Unified Planning Framework for Online Shape Estimation and Real-Time Pose Inference

author.name: Zhuoyi Lu and Lin Yang and Sri Harsha Turlapati and Domenico Campolo

entry.summary: Haptic Sorter is a unified model-based framework integrating Bayesian optimization-guided haptic exploration for online object shape estimation with real-time pose inference for manipulation planning. It uses superellipse approximations and an ODE-based pose inference scheme without prior geometric knowledge.

entry.title: The Sword, Shield, and Achilles' Heel: Characterizing the Linguistic Inductive Bias of Large Language Models for Spatial Reasoning in Navigation Planning

author.name: Xudong Zhang, Jian Yang, Shengkai Wang, Jiangpeng Tian, Shaowen Chen, Xian Wei, Ke Li, Xiong You

entry.summary: Introduces a dual-interventional framework to study how linguistic structure and contextual cues in textual spatial representations bias LLM navigation planning. Reveals that representation format choices are not neutral and strongly shape LLM spatial reasoning behavior.

entry.title: DOA: Training-Free Decoder-Only Attention Policy for Long-Form Simultaneous Translation with SpeechLLMs

author.name: Sara Papi, Luisa Bentivogli

entry.summary: Proposes DOA, a training-free decoder-only attention policy for long-form simultaneous speech-to-text translation with SpeechLLMs. Shows that self-attention contains stable enough alignment signals to guide streaming read/write decisions.

entry.title: Model-Agnostic Signal Discovery with Machine Learning: Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice

author.name: Oz Amram, Marco Letizia, Mikael Kuusela

entry.summary: This review surveys AI-based model-agnostic signal discovery strategies pioneered in high-energy physics, discussing conceptual frameworks, potential pitfalls, and validation strategies. It promotes broad-exploration paradigms for discovery where theoretical guidance is scarce.

entry.title: Full-field prediction for engineering-scale three-dimensional aircraft with multigrid-hierarchical learning

author.name: Yunfei Liu, Hao Wang, Yuhang Qi, Hao Yue, Dehong Meng, Wei Li, Rui Wang, Tiejun Li, Jie Liu, Junwu Hong, Xinhai Chen

entry.summary: MHLF is a multigrid-hierarchical learning framework that accelerates CFD simulations of engineering-scale 3D aircraft by predicting full flow fields for initialization, reducing the numerical distance to the converged solution. It scales beyond prior work limited to 2D or simplified 3D cases.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Steering for Figurative Language Generation

author.name: Linfeng Liu, Tiffany Zhan, Louie Hong Yao, Saptarshi Ghosh and Tianyu Jiang

entry.summary: This paper uses activation steering to probe whether the internal signals driving figurative language generation in multilingual LLMs are language-specific or reusable across languages. It finds steering directions for figurative categories like metaphor transfer across six languages, with German being especially receptive.

entry.title: Bounded Behavioral Indistinguishability for Black-Box LLM Distillation

author.name: Munawar Hasan

entry.summary: This paper argues that output similarity is insufficient for black-box LLM distillation and introduces bounded behavioral indistinguishability, a cryptographic-style formalization with bounds on distinguishing advantage, queries, computation, and adversary class. It instantiates the notion on Qwen and Llama teacher-student pairs using a controlled behavioral probe suite.

entry.title: CoMo3R-SLAM: Collaborative Monocular Dense SLAM with Learned 3D Reconstruction Priors for Outdoor Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhihao Cao, Qi Shao, Shuhao Zhai, Feng Tian, Anh Nguyen, Hesheng Wang, Baoru Huang

entry.summary: CoMo3R-SLAM is the first collaborative monocular dense RGB SLAM system for outdoor multi-agent mapping, using learned feed-forward 3D reconstruction priors to overcome scale ambiguity and unreliable inter-agent association. Each agent runs a prior-based pipeline avoiding the payload and calibration costs of depth sensors.

entry.title: Early Prediction of Future Behavioral Strategy from Process Traces

author.name: Robert Kasumba, Dennis Barbour, Chien-Ju Ho

entry.summary: This work predicts future behavioral strategies from early process-level traces rather than aggregate outcome summaries, useful for adaptive tutors, games, and human-AI teaming. It argues process traces capture person-level tendencies that outcome scores collapse.

entry.title: WristCompass: Kinematic Coupling as a Learnable Visual Concept for Ego-Camera Orientation

author.name: Varun Nair, Vidyut Baradwaj, Jiahang He, Anya Singh, Jai Relan, Cabrel Happi

entry.summary: WristCompass recovers ego-camera orientation from manipulation video using kinematic coupling between wrist motion and camera orientation as a learnable visual concept, working precisely when hands occlude the scene and geometry-based methods fail. Compact 4D inter-wrist features with a GRU outperform large scene-reconstruction models on this task.

entry.title: SAGE: A Novelty Gate for Efficient Memory Evolution in Agentic LLMs

author.name: Sijia Wang, Dhanajit Brahma, Ricardo Henao

entry.summary: SAGE frames LLM-agent memory evolution as a novelty-detection problem, using a von Mises-Fisher density estimator over memory embeddings with an adaptive threshold to decide whether facts should be added, ignored, or sent for LLM merging. It reduces expensive write-time reasoning while achieving strong token-F1 on LoCoMo.

entry.title: MAVEN: Improving Generalization in Agentic Tool Calling

author.name: Omkar Ghugarkar, Vishvesh Bhat, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Asad Aali

entry.summary: MAVEN is a lightweight symbolic reasoning scaffold for agentic tool calling that provides structured decomposition, adaptive tool orchestration, and intermediate verification to improve cross-domain generalization. It is evaluated across multiple tool-calling benchmarks and introduces MAVEN-Bench for multi-step math and physics reasoning with adversarial stress tests.

entry.title: On the impact of retrieved content representations in RAG Pipelines

author.name: Jonathan J Ross, Bevan Koopman, Anton van der Vegt, Guido Zuccon

entry.summary: This study conducts a controlled comparison of how retrieved content representation affects RAG generation, holding retrieval fixed while varying only document representation across thirteen transformations spanning selection, summarization, and others. It aims to identify which features of a document's representation matter most when the consumer is an LLM rather than a human reader.

entry.title: Revisiting Zeroth-Order Hessian Approximation: A Single-Step Policy Optimization Lens

author.name: Junbin Qiu, Zhaowei Hong, Renzhe Xu, Yao Shu

entry.summary: This paper reframes zeroth-order Hessian estimation through a single-step policy optimization lens, showing classical randomized estimators are instances of baseline selection and proposing a unified suite of low-variance estimators called ZoVH. It targets derivative-free methods for bilevel optimization and uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Coarsening for Multigrid Graph Neural Surrogates

author.name: Amir Bazzi, David Cardinaux, Ramy Nemer, Jose Alaves, Arjun Kalkur Matpadi Raghavendra, Elie Hachem

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multigrid graph neural network surrogate for solid mechanics that uses a physics-informed coarsening strategy, retaining nodes in high strain or stress regions rather than relying on geometric heuristics. It targets robust PDE surrogates for deformable solids with nonlinear elasticity and plasticity.

entry.title: GGT-100K: Generative Ground Truth for Generalizable Real-World Image Restoration

author.name: Xiangtao Kong, Jixin Zhao, Lingchen Sun, Rongyuan Wu and Lei Zhang

entry.summary: GGT-100K creates training data for real-world image restoration by using generative multimodal foundation models to produce high-quality targets from real low-quality images, evaluating nine MFMs including Nano-Banana-2 and GPT-Image-2. It addresses the scarcity of high-quality paired restoration data with adaptive prompting.

entry.title: Does Visual Information Play a Decisive Role in Vision-Language-Action Model Driving Behavior?

author.name: Jingtao He, Hongliang Lu, Xiaoyun Qiu, Yixuan Wang, Xinhu Zheng

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multi-level visual perturbation framework to diagnose how much Vision-Language-Action driving models actually rely on visual input, spanning channel-level, information-level, and structural perturbations. It provides structured diagnostics beyond aggregate metrics for visual-behavior dependency.

entry.title: Can Aerial VLA Models Cooperate? Evaluating Closed-Loop Air-Ground Coordination with CARLA-Air

author.name: Tianle Zeng, Yanci Wen, Xueang Yu, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: CARLA-Air is a unified single-process simulation environment merging CARLA and AirSim in one Unreal Engine runtime to evaluate closed-loop air-ground (UAV-UGV) coordination with consistent physics and timing. It tests whether aerial VLA models that work single-UAV can transfer to cooperative air-ground tasks.

entry.title: On Revisiting Entropy for Identifying Mislabeled Images

author.name: Chunlei Li, Zixuan Zheng, Yilei Shi, Guanglu Dong, Pengfei Li, Jingliang Hu, Xiao Xiang Zhu, Lichao Mou

entry.summary: This paper revisits entropy for detecting mislabeled images, observing that correctly labeled samples show consistent entropy decrease during training while mislabeled ones maintain high entropy, and proposes a signed entropy integral statistic capturing both magnitude and temporal trend. It is broadly applicable to classifiers and effective combined with contrastive learning.

entry.title: TALON: Token-Aligned Lightweight Adapters for 6-DoF Spacecraft Pose Estimation

author.name: Abid Ali, Arunkumar Rathinam, Djamila Aouada

entry.summary: TALON injects lightweight spatiotemporal 3D adapters before self-attention in a frozen ViT for monocular 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation, leveraging temporal image sequences without full backbone fine-tuning. A patch-token alignment loss geometrically grounds adapted features to keypoint structure.

entry.title: Envisioning Beyond the Few: Disentangled Semantics and Primitives for Few-Shot Atypical Layout-to-Image Generation

author.name: Nan Bao, Yifan Zhao, Wenzhuang Wang, Jia Li

entry.summary: This work tackles few-shot atypical layout-to-image generation, addressing representation fragmentation by disentangling semantic identity from visual primitives. It uses semantic anchoring, primitive imbuing, and saliency-aware conceptual steering for robust adaptation.

entry.title: Learning Parametric Nitrogen Fertilizer Response Curves Using Neuro Symbolic Regression

author.name: Giorgio Morales, John Sheppard

entry.summary: This work uses neuro-symbolic regression with a transformer-based multi-set symbolic skeleton prediction to learn interpretable parametric nitrogen fertilizer response curves without predefined functional forms. It discovers shared functional structures across management zones in precision agriculture.

entry.title: SAM for Robust Mitochondria Instance Segmentation in Fluorescence Microscopy

author.name: Suyog Jadhav, Dilip K. Prasad, Krishna Agarwal

entry.summary: This work finetunes the Segment Anything Model exclusively on synthetically generated fluorescence microscopy data for robust mitochondria instance segmentation, addressing the severe lack of annotated datasets. It simulates realistic mitochondria to overcome the domain shift from natural images.

entry.title: FAM-Bench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Condition-Aware Food-as-Medicine Reasoning

author.name: Mingyang Mao, Bhargav Rishi Medisetti, Utkarsh Grover, Tanvir Ibrahim, Wenyan Li, Tingting Zhang, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: Introduces FAM-Bench, a multimodal benchmark for food-as-medicine reasoning with 2500 expert-verified instances across 13 health conditions. Tests whether models can decide food appropriateness for specific health conditions beyond simple recognition.

entry.title: On-Device Robotic Planning: Eliminating Inference Redundancy for Efficient Decision-Making

author.name: Joonhee Lee, Hyunseung Shin, Hyunmi Kim, Pei Zhang, Jeonggil Ko

entry.summary: Presents REIS, a robotic decision-making framework exploiting temporal redundancy where consecutive observations yield identical actions, using scene gating and affordance routing to skip redundant reasoning. Accelerates on-device LLM/VLM robotic planning.

entry.title: Internalizing Temporal Consistency in Video Object-Centric Learning without Explicit Regularization

author.name: Rongzhen Zhao, Zhiyuan Li, Juho Kannala, Joni Pajarinen

entry.summary: Proposes enforcing temporal consistency in video object-centric learning through implicit model design rather than an explicit slot-slot contrastive loss. Introduces Chrono-Channel Decomposition to disentangle static and dynamic slot subspaces with near-zero overhead.

entry.title: On public and private binary classification with metric space valued predictors

author.name: L\'aszl\'o Gy\"orfi and Martin Kroll and Harro Walk

entry.summary: This theory paper derives convergence rates for the Proto-NN classifier with metric-space-valued predictors and extends the analysis to a local differential privacy setting. It characterizes binary classification rates under both public and privacy-constrained data access.

entry.title: TRINE: A Token-Aware, Runtime-Adaptive FPGA Inference Engine for Multimodal AI

author.name: Hyunwoo Oh, Hanning Chen, Sanggeon Yun, Yang Ni, Suyeon Jang, Behnam Khaleghi, Fei Wen and Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: TRINE is a single-bitstream FPGA accelerator and compiler that runs end-to-end multimodal inference (ViTs, CNNs, GNNs, transformers) without reconfiguration by unifying layers into common sparse/dense matrix operations. It uses runtime mode-switching and token pruning to sustain utilization, achieving notable latency reductions.

entry.title: DTG-Restore: Training-Free Diffusion Refinement for Generative Video Super-Resolution

author.name: Hidir Yesiltepe, Koutilya PNVR, Gaurav Pathak, Navaneeth Bodla, Bharat Singh, Pinar Yanardag, Jinrong Xie

entry.summary: DTG-Restore introduces a training-free framework for generative video super-resolution that decouples conditional and unconditional branches in classifier-free guidance across time. Its Decoupled Time Guidance evaluates the unconditional branch at a cleaner timestep, preserving geometry while suppressing artifacts from warped content.

entry.title: Dex2HOI: Dexterous Bimanual Two-Object Interaction Generation

author.name: Chrysa Pratikaki, Pablo Ruiz-Ponce, Jiankang Deng, Stefanos Zafeiriou and Rolandos Alexandros Potamias

entry.summary: Dex2HOI is a unified diffusion model for generating single- and two-object human-object interactions from text, using a dual-stream architecture with bidirectional cross-attention per object. It introduces a motion fusion network with hand-relative object representations and contact-aware conditioning for bimanual, multi-object manipulation.

entry.title: Scalable Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via State Augmentation and Consensus for Separable Dynamics

author.name: Santiago Amaya-Corredor, Miguel Calvo-Fullana, Anders Jonsson

entry.summary: This paper presents a distributed approach for constrained multi-agent RL that combines state-augmented policy learning with neighbor-to-neighbor consensus over dual variables. It targets systems with separable agent dynamics that must coordinate to satisfy global resource constraints, showing lightweight consensus suffices for globally coordinated constraint enforcement.

entry.title: Universal Multiclass Transductive Online Learning

author.name: Steve Hanneke, Hongao Wang

entry.summary: This theoretical paper characterizes the learnability of universal transductive online classification with possibly unbounded label spaces. It shows only two optimal rates are possible (bounded or logarithmic) and introduces a new combinatorial structure, the Level-Constrained-Littlestone-Littlestone tree.

entry.title: Improved Distribution Estimation in $\ell_\infty$

author.name: Doron Cohen, Aryeh Kontorovich and Yonatan Livshitz

entry.summary: This work provides improved minimax and high-probability bounds for estimating discrete distributions under the infinity norm, resolving open questions from prior literature including a fully empirical risk bound and the worst-case extremal distribution form.

entry.title: DisasterLex: An Expert Concept-to-Schema Knowledge Graph for Geospatial Reasoning in Disaster Analytics

author.name: Yiming Xiao, Ankit Basu, Kai Yin, Sahil Vartak, Christian Swords, Ali Mostafavi

entry.summary: DisasterLex inserts an expert knowledge graph of curated concepts and typed causal edges between user queries and disaster databases to improve text-to-SQL over heterogeneous geospatial schemas. A four-stage orchestration handles entity identification, domain routing, and causal reasoning.

entry.title: Learning effective Sargassum transport dynamics from limited drifter observations

author.name: F.J. Beron-VEra, M.J. Olascoaga, J. Morell, E. Cruz

entry.summary: This work learns effective Sargassum transport corrections from limited drifter observations using physically motivated ocean-atmosphere diagnostics and finite-memory representations, analyzed via predictive and sparse symbolic-discovery approaches. Applications show diagnostics contain transport information beyond baseline circulation products.

entry.title: LARK: Learnability-Grounded Trajectory Selection for Efficient Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Tianrun Yu, Kaixiang Zhao, Chih-Chun Chen, Amanda Hughes, Taylor W. Killian, Fenglong Ma, Weitong Zhang, Porter Jenkins

entry.summary: LARK selects teacher reasoning trajectories for distillation based on whether the student can actually learn them, using a learnability factor that tracks training loss decrease rather than relying on trajectory quality heuristics. This addresses inefficiency in reasoning distillation by matching supervision to student capacity.

entry.title: Depth-Dependent Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Calling ReAct Agents: Injection Depth, Payload Framing, and Turn-Budget Sensitivity

author.name: Mohammadreza Rashidi

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies indirect prompt injection in ReAct tool-calling agents across three under-explored dimensions: injection depth in the tool sequence, rhetorical framing of payloads, and turn-budget sensitivity. It conducts controlled studies across 20 scenarios and five attack categories.

entry.title: Neuron-Level Interventions for Gendered and Gender-Neutral Generation in Language Models

author.name: Zhiwen You, Nafiseh Nikeghbal, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: This paper studies gender-specific neurons in language models across feminine, masculine, and gender-neutral categories, proposing a neuron-level intervention to identify and steer them via activation or masking. It extends gender-bias analysis beyond the usual binary lens to include gender-neutral forms like they/them.

entry.title: AbstainGNN: Teaching Graph Neural Networks to Abstain for Graph Classification

author.name: Xixun Lin, Zhiheng Zhou, Zhengyin Zhang, Yancheng Chen, Shuai Zhang, Ge Zhang, Shichao Zhu, Lixin Zou, Chuan Zhou, Peng Zhang, Shirui Pan, Yanan Cao

entry.summary: AbstainGNN is a theory-driven framework enabling graph neural networks to abstain from uncertain predictions in graph classification by explicitly modeling both predictive and abstention functions. It improves reliability for safety-critical applications where forcing predictions under high uncertainty produces unreliable decisions.

entry.title: OpenSTBench: Beyond Semantic Evaluation for Speech Translation

author.name: Yanjie An and Yuxiang Zhao and Yichi Zhang and Qixi Zheng and Yujie Tu and Keqi Deng and Kai Yu and Xie Chen

entry.summary: OpenSTBench is a unified multidimensional evaluation framework for speech translation that organizes heterogeneous outputs (speech-to-text, speech-to-speech, offline, streaming) into a shared format and jointly evaluates translation, speech, and temporal quality. It addresses the difficulty of comparing heterogeneous speech translation systems evaluated under separate protocols.

entry.title: MechVQA: Benchmarking and Enhancing Multimodal LLMs on Comprehensive Mechanical Drawing Understanding

author.name: Qian Kou, Xiaofeng Shi, Yulin Li, Xiaosong Qiu, Xinyang Wang, Hua Zhou, Cao Dongxing

entry.summary: MechVQA is the first comprehensive mechanical engineering drawing understanding dataset, containing 3.3k high-density images with 21K question-answer pairs across 10 fine-grained tasks at recognition, reasoning, and judgment levels. It targets the brittleness of multimodal LLMs on mechanical drawings with high annotation density, weak domain knowledge, and strict projection rules.

entry.title: Learning Permutation-invariant Macroscopic Dynamics

author.name: Zhichao Han, Mengyi Chen, Qianxiao Li

entry.summary: This work proposes a permutation-invariant autoencoder framework for learning macroscopic dynamics of unordered microscopic systems like particle ensembles, with a decoder reconstructing mass distributions rather than per-sample points. It enables learning latent dynamics without assuming fixed input ordering.

entry.title: PRISM: Progressive Reasoning through Iterative Slot Memory for Vision

author.name: Ziyu Wang, Shuangpeng Han, Mengmi Zhang

entry.summary: PRISM is a vision architecture that replaces single feed-forward passes with iterative refinement, using object-centric slot representations and a learned memory to progressively resolve ambiguity. It draws inspiration from human perception to recover missing visual evidence.

entry.title: Can BEV Perception Gracefully Degrade under Sensor Failures?

author.name: Haifa Zhang, Yijing Wang, Haoyu Wang, Zheng Li, and Zhiqiang Zuo

entry.summary: Grace-BEV is a lightweight, plug-and-play framework that makes multi-modal bird's-eye-view perception degrade gracefully under sensor corruption by actively assessing modality reliability during fusion. It addresses the catastrophic collapse of static fusion under missing or degraded sensors.

entry.title: UniRTL: Unifying Code and Graph for Robust RTL Representation Learning

author.name: Yi Liu, Hongji Zhang, Lei Chen, Mingxuan Yuan, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: UniRTL is a multimodal pretraining framework that jointly learns representations of register-transfer-level hardware designs from both the RTL code and its control data flow graph, combining semantic and structural information. It aims to improve expressiveness and generalization for hardware design tasks.

entry.title: The Challenges of Using Reinforcement Learning for Controlling Industrial Energy Systems

author.name: Tobias Lademann, Th\'eo Vincent, Jan Peters, Matthias Weigold

entry.summary: This paper systematically analyzes the challenges of deploying reinforcement learning to control a real industrial thermal heating network, covering partial observability, action and reward design, and the sim-to-real gap. It documents that RL achieves operational stability but shows a significant performance gap versus simulation in real deployment.

entry.title: Building Generalization Into Behavior Generation Via Adaptive Compositions of Regularities

author.name: Aravind Battaje, Malte Bernhard, Vito Mengers, Oliver Brock

entry.summary: This paper investigates robot generalization as adaptive composition of predictable environment regularities into situation-specific structures, analyzed within the AICON differentiable network framework. It isolates adaptive composition as the key mechanism in a controlled simulated study.

entry.title: Polyphony: Diffusion-based Dual-Hand Action Segmentation with Alternating Vision Transformer and Semantic Conditioning

author.name: Hao Zheng, Hu Wang, Tiantian Zheng, Prajjwal Bhattarai, Tuka Alhanai
