entry.summary: Polyphony is a three-stage diffusion-based method for dual-hand action segmentation that alternates training between left and right hands, conditions on compositional action descriptions, and addresses inter-hand dependencies and gradient monopolization. It targets fine-grained understanding of bimanual activities in untrimmed video.

entry.title: Learning Cardiac Latent Representations in Vectorcardiogram Space

author.name: Bosong Huang, Panzhen Zhao, Zengxiang Li, Patricia Lee, Wei Jin, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Ming Jin, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: This paper proposes learning unified cardiac latent representations directly in vectorcardiogram space rather than the redundant twelve-lead ECG signal space, motivated by the Frank VCG model. This reduces redundancy and spurious correlations for downstream cardiac tasks.

entry.title: Memristor-Based Spiking Neural Network Accelerator for Bio-inspired Interception Task

author.name: Qianhou Qu, Sheng Lu, Liuting Shang, Jaihan Utailawon, Sungyong Jung, Qilian Liang, and Chenyun Pan

entry.summary: This paper proposes an analog memristor-based spiking neural network accelerator integrating in-memory synaptic computation with analog integrate-and-fire neurons for a bio-inspired interception task, eliminating multi-transistor CMOS synapse circuits. It is compared against a digital 5nm SNN accelerator for energy efficiency.

entry.title: Constrained Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Max-Min Criterion

author.name: Giseung Park, Hyunyoung Nam, Woohyeon Byeon, Amir Leshem, Youngchul Sung

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-objective RL framework combining max-min fairness criteria with explicit constraint satisfaction, with convergence analysis and theoretical foundations. Validated on building thermal control, locomotion, and traffic emissions management.

entry.title: Knowledge Boundary Probing and Demand-Guided Intervention for LLM-Based Power System Code Generation

author.name: Hui Wu, Xiaoyang Wang, Zhong Fan

entry.summary: Shows that LLM failures in power-system code generation are dominated by structured API-knowledge boundary errors rather than reasoning, and introduces PowerCodeBench plus a documentation-driven probing and demand-guided intervention method. Targets reliable on-premise open-weight model deployment.

entry.title: Joint Multi-Camera LiDAR Extrinsic Calibration via Learned Pairwise Initialization and Geometric Refinement

author.name: Aziz Al-Najjar, Marzieh Amini, James R. Green, Felix Kwamena

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-stage framework for joint multi-camera LiDAR extrinsic calibration combining learned pairwise matching (CMRNext) with multi-frame bundle adjustment for globally consistent calibration. It corrects the system-level inconsistency that arises when camera-LiDAR pairs are calibrated independently.

entry.title: Abstention Geometry: Knowledge and Behaviour Are Dissociable in Llama 3.1 8B

author.name: AdeOlu

entry.summary: This interpretability study on Llama 3.1 8B finds that the model has a salient internal representation of question answerability that is dissociable from its propensity to actually abstain, drawing an analogy to vincible ignorance. It suggests knowledge and behavior are separable in the model's activations.

entry.title: Attention-based optimizer for symmetry finding

author.name: Shreya Banerjee, Vinodh Raj Rajagopal Muthu, Charlie Nation, Rick P.A. Simon, Francesco Martini, Alessandro Ricottone, Federico Cerisola, and Luca Dellantonio

entry.summary: This work presents a Set-Transformer-based optimization framework for finding Pauli symmetries of quantum Hamiltonians, using self-attention to encode correlations among Pauli strings and a commutation-based objective. It succeeds near-deterministically on physical models like the Ising and Toric code Hamiltonians.

entry.title: DisjunctiveNet: Neural Symbolic Learning via Differentiable Convexified Optimization Layers

author.name: Shraman Pal, Can Li

entry.summary: DisjunctiveNet integrates differentiable convexified optimization layers to enforce hard logical and linear-inequality constraints in neural-symbolic learning, rather than approximate soft penalties or non-differentiable post-processing. It supports input-dependent rules expressed as logical propositions with linear inequalities.

entry.title: idSCD: Identifying Training Datasets through Semantic Correlation Descriptors

author.name: Andrada Gobeaja, Ionut Hodoroaga, Elena Burceanu, Marius Leordeanu

entry.summary: idSCD studies dataset-level membership inference by recognizing the spurious correlation traces a dataset induces during training. It introduces white-box semantic correlation descriptors that capture a model's learned semantic correlation structure and make it comparable across dataset mixtures.

entry.title: Immuno-VLM: Immunizing Large Vision-Language Models via Generative Semantic Antibodies for Open-World Trustworthiness

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Wei Ji

entry.summary: Immuno-VLM is a bio-inspired framework adapting immunological negative selection to high-dimensional latent spaces to address vision-language models' tendency to force-fit unknown anomalies into known categories with high confidence. It generates semantic antibodies for open-set recognition rather than relying on passive density estimation or pixel-space outliers.

entry.title: Eywa: Provenance-Grounded Long-Term Memory for AI Agents

author.name: Resham Joshi

entry.summary: Eywa is a provenance-grounded long-term memory architecture for AI agents that stores immutable source evidence before deriving canonical facts, validates extracted memories against typed signals and source support, and retrieves through a deterministic multi-route path with zero LLM calls. It enables diagnosable, auditable, updatable, and erasable agent memory.

entry.title: Object-Informed Model Predictive Path Integral Control for Non-Prehensile Robot Manipulation

author.name: Nikola Raicevic, Bharath Raam Radhakrishnan, Chenbin Yu, Ki Myung Brian Lee, and Nikolay Atanasov

entry.summary: This work proposes a hierarchical model predictive path integral control formulation for non-prehensile robot manipulation that first solves a simplified object-only plan and uses it as a reference for joint robot-object planning. It enables efficient long-horizon non-myopic reasoning for pushing tasks, validated on a 6-DoF manipulator in simulation and hardware.

entry.title: EvoGens: A Population-Based Heuristic Search Framework for Scientific Idea Generation

author.name: Xu Li, Hanzhe Tu, Xinyi Li, Kuncheng Zhao, Xun Han, and Zhonghui Liu

entry.summary: EvoGens recasts scientific idea generation as an evolutionary search over a population of ideas, using rank-based mutation with retrieval and semantic crossover to combat the semantic convergence and low diversity of LLM-generated ideas. It aims to sustain novelty while avoiding premature convergence.

entry.title: SDM-Q: Cost-Aware Staged Decision-Making for Multi-Omics Classification with Deep Q-Learning

author.name: Nan Mu, Xiaoyang Fan, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: SDM-Q is a deep Q-learning framework for cost-aware staged multi-omics classification, reformulating diagnosis as a sequential decision problem that decides which expensive omics modalities to acquire. It avoids assuming full modality availability and reduces redundant data collection in clinical settings.

entry.title: Multi-Scale Separable Fourier Neural Networks for Solving High-Frequency PDEs

author.name: Qihong Yang, Qiaolin He

entry.summary: MS-SFNN is a separable Fourier neural network with randomly initialized, fixed weights for solving high-frequency linear and nonlinear PDEs, using per-coordinate subnetworks and least-squares-determined coefficients. The random-feature design with tunable scaling targets accurate, efficient high-frequency PDE solutions.

entry.title: AnchorSteer: Self-Discovered Concept Injection for Structure-Preserving Music Editing

author.name: Chih-Heng Chang, Keng-Seng Ho, Chih-Yu Tsai, Kuan-Lin Chen, Yi-Hsuan Yang, and Jian-Jiun Ding

entry.summary: AnchorSteer enables controllable music editing by combining structural anchoring with self-discovered, label-free semantic concept vectors extracted via self-supervised reconstruction, then injected into diffusion hidden states. It disentangles the tension between editing semantics and preserving rhythmic and melodic structure.

entry.title: Fighting Numerical Hallucinations via Data-centric Compilation for Online Financial QA

author.name: Hao Chen, Xing Tang, Qirui Liu, Weijie Shi, Shiwei Li, Fuyuan Lyu, Weihong Luo, Xiku Du, Xiuqiang He

entry.summary: This work proposes a data-centric framework to combat numerical reasoning hallucinations in financial QA RAG systems, addressing noise sensitivity, calculation fragility, and auditability rather than optimizing retriever or generator in isolation. It targets reliability in high-stakes financial applications.

entry.title: Seeing Fast and Slow: Bimodal 3D Scene Graphs for Open-set Tasks

author.name: Marcel Bartholomeus Prasetyo, Shrutika Vishal Thengane, A Manicka Praveen, Yi Loo, Malika Meghjani

entry.summary: BiMoSG is a bimodal 3D scene graph generation method for open-set tasks that defaults to a fast coarse scene graph and switches to a slow, fine-grained open-vocabulary graph only in regions likely to contain task-relevant objects. It mirrors human dual-process perception for efficient robotic scene understanding.

entry.title: Towards Effective Long-Video Event Prediction via Multi-Level Event Semantics Mining

author.name: Bo Peng, YuanJie Lyu, PengGang Qin, Tong Xu

entry.summary: VISTA is a multi-level event semantics mining framework for long-video event prediction, addressing the inability of long-video language models to extract event-related details and perform fine-grained analysis of event development. It targets the underexplored task of predicting future events in long, multimodal video narratives.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Clinical Knowledge Integration for Mammography Report Generation

author.name: Jiayi Zhu, Fuxiang Huang, Yu Xie, Xi Wang, Zhixuan Chen, Yuan Guo, Qingcong Kong, Zhenhui Li, Qiong Luo, Hao Chen

entry.summary: MammoRG is a mammography report generation framework that explicitly simulates radiologists' clinical reasoning by following the BI-RADS guideline and incorporating prior clinical knowledge, rather than direct visual-to-text mapping. It uses a two-stage process to produce structured diagnostic reports.

entry.title: Neuro-symbolic Syntactic Parsing: Shaping a Neural Network with the CYK Algorithm

author.name: Fabio Massimo Zanzotto, Federico Ranaldi, Giorgio Satta

entry.summary: Proposes CYKNN, a recurrent neural architecture that directly encodes the CYK parsing algorithm in trainable matrix-vector operations. Outperforms 20B+ in-context LLMs and LoRA-finetuned smaller models on simple grammars.

entry.title: Modeling Covariate Transition for Efficient Estimation of Longitudinal Treatment Effects in Randomized Experiments

author.name: Naoki Chihara, Tatsushi Oka, Yasuko Matsubara, Yasushi Sakurai, Shota Yasui

entry.summary: Develops a regression-adjustment framework for estimating longitudinal treatment effects in randomized experiments by modeling covariate transition kernels. Establishes asymptotic normality and semiparametric efficiency bounds for time-varying effects.

entry.title: Language Models Can Resolve Reference Compositionally, But It's Not Their Native Strength: The Case of the Personal Relation Task

author.name: Bart Evelo and Meaghan Fowlie and Denis Paperno

entry.summary: Evaluates whether LLMs and humans resolve compositional reference in the Personal Relation Task, distinguishing extensional (who) from intensional (formula) interpretation. Finds LLMs can do compositional reference resolution but it is not their native strength.

entry.title: On Efficient Scaling of GNNs via IO-Aware Layers Implementations

author.name: Daria Fomina and Daniil Krasylnikov and Alexey Boykov and Andrey Dolgovyazov and Vyacheslav Zhdanovskiy and Fedor Velikonivtsev

entry.summary: Takes an IO- and arithmetic-intensity-centric view of GNN scaling, categorizing common layers into three kernel families and developing GPU kernels that reduce data movement. Also studies how graph reordering interacts with kernel mapping.

entry.title: Discovering Thermodynamically Admissible Dissipation Potentials via Grammar-Based Symbolic Regression

author.name: Federico Califano and Jacopo Ciambella

entry.summary: Proposes a grammar-based symbolic regression framework to discover thermodynamically admissible dissipation potentials within the Generalized Standard Materials formalism. Enforces convexity and non-negativity from the Clausius-Duhem inequality to guarantee physical consistency while retaining interpretability.

entry.title: Semantic Triplet Restoration: A Novel Protocol for Hierarchical Table Understanding in Large Language Models

author.name: Yibin Zhao, Fangxin Shang, Dingrui Yang, Yuqi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Semantic Triplet Restoration, a protocol rewriting each table cell as an atomic fact triplet (item path, feature path, value) instead of HTML/Markdown serialization for LLM table understanding. Adds a query-aware router (TripletQL) to select renderings.

entry.title: Mental Damage: Caption Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Text-to-Music Generation

author.name: Yizhu Wen, Shuhao Zhang, Nan Zhang, Long Cheng, Hanqing Guo

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a caption-poisoning attack on retrieval-augmented text-to-music systems, where injecting a few crafted captions into the knowledge database biases prompt augmentation and steers generation without modifying the user prompt. It proposes a dual-layer poisoning strategy preserving retrieval anchors while injecting acoustic descriptors.

entry.title: From Mean-Field Limits to Semiclassical Concentration: Global Convergence of the Canonical Evolutionary Strategy

author.name: Mat\'ias Neto, Nicol\'as Garay, Luis Mart\'i, Nayat Sanchez-Pi

entry.summary: This theoretical paper analyzes global convergence of the Canonical Evolutionary Strategy via the semiclassical limit of a Schrodinger-type replicator-mutator equation. It establishes a hierarchy from discrete dynamics to a mean-field limit and shows convergence is governed by a principal eigenfunction, justifying the survival-of-the-flattest phenomenon.

entry.title: Smaller and Faster 3DGS via Post-Training Dictionary Learning

author.name: Jiarong Gong, Jonas Unger, Ehsan Miandji

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first dictionary-learning-based post-training compression framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting that reduces memory footprint without retraining or modifying existing models. It is straightforward to deploy and preserves image quality while achieving significant compression.

entry.title: Calibrated Preference Learning: The Case of Label Ranking

author.name: Santo M. A. R. Thies, Viktor Bengs, Timo Kaufmann, Sebastian J. Vollmer, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: This paper formalizes calibration for probabilistic label ranking, developing a hierarchy of calibration notions for full rankings, sub-rankings, and top-k rankings. It proves implication relationships among them and empirically finds popular label ranking models are poorly calibrated.

entry.title: Clustering Guided Domain-Specific Pretrained Foundation Model Very High-Resolution Arctic Remote Sensing

author.name: Amal S. Perera, Chandi Witharana, Elias Manos, Michael Pimenta, Anna K. Liljedahl

entry.summary: This work builds an Arctic-focused remote sensing foundation model by combining diversity-aware image curation with masked autoencoder self-supervised pretraining of a ViT encoder on very-high-resolution satellite imagery. Affinity-propagation clustering selected about 3 million chips from 267 TB to reduce oversampling while preserving scene diversity.

entry.title: CanLegalRAGBench: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Canadian Case Law

author.name: Ethan Zhao, Maksym Taranukhin, Wei Cui, Moira Aikenhead, Vered Shwartz

entry.summary: CanLegalRAGBench is a Canadian legal QA benchmark built from realistic queries and expert-annotated answers grounded in case law, addressing the underrepresentation of Canadian law and reliance on synthetic queries. Evaluation shows open-source embedding models are competitive with closed-source ones and that automatic metrics unfairly penalize retrieval of alternative relevant documents.

entry.title: Generalistic or Specific Embeddings, Which is Better? An Empirical Study on Search for Clinical Coding in Non-English Languages

author.name: David Rey-Blanco, Roberto Cruz

entry.summary: This empirical study compares generalist versus specialized embeddings for clinical ICD-10 code retrieval in non-English languages, using Gemini-generated synthetic multilingual data to fine-tune a two-stage retriever. The fine-tuned bi-encoder matches or exceeds biomedical baselines on recall metrics.

entry.title: Prior Availability in Industrial Visual Sim-to-Real: A Review of CAD-Guided and CAD-Unavailable Regimes

author.name: Chenxi Tao, Seung-Kyum Choi

entry.summary: This review reframes industrial visual sim-to-real as a domain-gap problem organized by prior availability, distinguishing CAD-available settings (supporting rendering, pose estimation, geometric verification) from CAD-unavailable regimes. It surveys methods across the spectrum of available evidence versus deployment mismatch.

entry.title: Rationalize: Shared Semantic Reasoning for Human-AI Alignment

author.name: Aritra Dasgupta, Naga Datha Saikiran Battula, Avina Nakarmi, Sohom Sen, Subhodeep Ghosh, Xun Song

entry.summary: Rationalize is a role-pair framework (Explorer-Guide, Investigator-Informant, Teacher-Student, Judge-Advocate) for shared semantic reasoning between humans and AI in data sensemaking, making purposes, assumptions, evidence, and inferences explicit. It connects these role pairs to bidirectional human-AI alignment.

entry.title: Structure-Induced Information for Rerooting Levin Tree Search

author.name: Jake Tuero, Michael Buro, Laurent Orseau, Levi H. S. Lelis

entry.summary: This paper introduces learned rerooter designs for the sqrt-LTS subgoal-based policy tree search algorithm, including clustering-based, heuristic-based, and hybrid variants that implicitly decompose problems into soft subtasks. It avoids explicit subgoal generation overhead while improving scalability on single-agent deterministic problems.

entry.title: Equivariant Latent Alignment via Flow Matching under Group Symmetries

author.name: Sunghyun Kim, Jaehoon Hahm, Jeongwoo Shin, Joonseok Lee

entry.summary: This paper addresses latent misalignment in equivariant generative models for novel view synthesis, where intended group actions diverge from actually required latent transformations. It proposes a flow-matching method to enforce equivariant latent alignment under group symmetries.

entry.title: Simple Token-Efficient Vision-Language Model for Case-level Pathology Synoptic Report Generation

author.name: Zhiyuan Yang, Jiahao Cheng, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Mahdi S. Hosseini

entry.summary: This work presents a token-efficient vision-language model for case-level pathology synoptic report generation from gigapixel whole-slide images, using a frozen patch encoder, lightweight MLP aligner, and LLM decoder with WSI marker tokens. It enables case-level reasoning over multiple heterogeneous slides under constrained GPU memory.

entry.title: OrcaRouter: A Production-Oriented LLM Router with Hybrid Offline-Online Learning

author.name: Zhenghua Bao, Fengya Tian, Chris Zhang, Zhenjun Chen, Xile Ma and Yi Shi

entry.summary: OrcaRouter is a production-oriented LLM router combining a LinUCB contextual bandit over lexical and embedding features with hybrid offline-online learning, initializing from an offline reward matrix and optionally continuing to learn from bandit feedback online. It targets the practical question of routing requests to the best model by capability and cost.

entry.title: GSAM: A Generalizable and Safe Robotic Framework for Articulated Object Manipulation

author.name: Beichen Shao, Mengying Xie, Heng Su, Wanyi Zhang, Mingyan Li, Yan Ding, Fausto Giunchiglia, and Chao Chen

entry.summary: GSAM is a generalizable and safe framework for articulated object manipulation that uses a vision-based perceiver for kinematic parameters refined by a fine-tuned VLM applying chain-of-thought commonsense reasoning. It addresses limited generalization and destructive collisions in prior end-to-end and LLM/VLM manipulation methods.

entry.title: DisPlace: Discriminative Place Projections for Multi-Reference Visual Place Recognition

author.name: Dhyey Manish Rajani, Michael Milford, Tobias Fischer

entry.summary: DisPlace fuses multiple reference descriptors for visual place recognition into a single compact discriminative representation by formulating fusion as a generalized eigenvalue problem maximizing between-place separability while suppressing within-place variation. It distinguishes stable place-identity descriptor variations from those caused by changing conditions or viewpoints.

entry.title: Extending AI for Research to the Humanities: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evidence-Grounded Scholarship

author.name: Yating Pan (1 and 2), Jiajun Zhang (2), Jun Wang (1, 2 and 4), Qi Su (3 and 4) ((1) Department of Information Management, Peking University, (2) Research Center for Digital Humanities, Peking University, (3) School of Foreign Languages, Peking University, (4) Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Peking University)

entry.summary: SPIRE is a multi-agent LLM framework designed for humanities scholarship, emphasizing evidence-grounded interpretation, faithful quotation, and verifiable provenance rather than executable experiments. It extends AI research agents to interpretive disciplines that have been largely neglected.

entry.title: An Efficient and Scalable Graph Condensation with Structure-Preserving

author.name: Yulin Hu, Fuyan Ou, Ye Yuan

entry.summary: SP-ESGC is a graph condensation method that decouples node condensation from structure generation, using heat-kernel feature propagation and hybrid clustering to compress large graphs into compact synthetic ones efficiently. It addresses computational inefficiency and poor cross-architecture generalization of existing methods.

entry.title: HADT: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Differential Transformer for Autonomous Earth Observation Satellite Cluster

author.name: Mohamad A. Hady, Muhammad Anwar Masum, Siyi Hu, Mahardhika Pratama, Jimmy Cao, Ryszard Kowalczyk

entry.summary: HADT is a heterogeneous multi-agent differential transformer for autonomous resource management in clusters of optical and SAR Earth observation satellites, enabling real-time onboard decision-making without explicit mathematical models. It targets dynamic, uncertain space missions where traditional optimization-based scheduling fails.

entry.title: PEEK: Picking Essential frames via Efficient Knowledge distillation

author.name: Killian Steunou, Anas Filali Razzouki, Khalil Guetari, Moun\^im A. El-Yacoubi, Yannis Tevissen

entry.summary: PEEK is an efficient adaptive frame-sampling method for video captioning that distills caption-conditioned frame relevance rankings from a strong teacher into a lightweight model operating only on visual content. It outperforms state-of-the-art frame selection on ActivityNet Captions and MSR-VTT at lower cost.

entry.title: STEP: Learning STructured Embeddings for Progressive Time Series

author.name: Lucas Thil, Jesse Read, Rim Kaddah, Guillaume Doquet

entry.summary: STEP learns interpretable representations of progressive (irreversible) time series via a self-supervised contrastive objective that places observations on a manifold anchored between two orthogonal prototype vectors. The resulting polar latent compass reads off progression and operating mode without proxy labels.

entry.title: Redefining Instance Matching: A Unified Framework for Part-Aware Matching in Panoptic Segmentation Evaluation

author.name: Erik Gro{\ss}kopf, Soumya Snigdha Kundu, Hendrik M\"oller, Nicolas M\"unster, Mehdi Astaraki, Paula Tamara Buzduga, Kerstin Ritter, Benedikt Wiestler, Jan Kirschke, Jonathan Shapey, Tom Vercauteren, Florian Kofler

entry.summary: This paper systematically analyzes the underexplored problem of segment matching in Panoptic Quality evaluation when IoU is below 0.5, recasting it as a constrained bipartite assignment with four matching strategies (one-to-one, many-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many). It shows which strategies are well-defined within the PQ framework and proposes a unified part-aware matching framework.

entry.title: SWIM: Single-Instance Whole-Body Imitation for swiMming

author.name: Binglun Wang, Edmond S. L. Ho, He Wang

entry.summary: SWIM presents a physics-based character animation method for synthesizing realistic swimming motions, handling full-body coordination and continuous fluid interactions. It pushes physically-based control to a harder regime of volatile environmental forces.

entry.title: Guidance for Low-Level Perceptual Editing in Unconditional Diffusion Models

author.name: Shreyansh Modi, Akshat Tomar, Aarush Aggarwal

entry.summary: This paper introduces a training-free framework for low-level perceptual and aesthetic editing in unconditional diffusion models, showing standard h-space patching fails for global transformations. It extracts degradation concept vectors and combines bottleneck patching with classifier-free guidance to steer away from degraded outputs.

entry.title: FlagGAM: Rule-Based Generalized Additive Modeling for Explainable Tabular Prediction

author.name: Zijie Zhao, Roy E. Welsch

entry.summary: FlagGAM is a rule-defined basis framework for explainable tabular prediction that converts variables into sparse human-readable univariate bases combined in a GAM-style additive head. It retains a sparse rule-basis matrix supporting mixed-type tasks and robustness to imperfect inputs.

entry.title: Wind Turbine Maintenance Log Labelling Framework: LLM-Driven Data Correction and Enrichment via Semantic Extraction of Reliability Intelligence

author.name: Max Malyi, Jonathan Shek, Alasdair McDonald, Andre Biscaya

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-driven framework to standardize and structure 16,316 unstructured wind turbine maintenance logs, autonomously correcting hierarchical system codes and extracting reliability intelligence. It enables quantitative reliability analysis from free-text records.

entry.title: Authentication of Copy Detection Patterns via Cross-Camera Dual-Synthetic Referencing

author.name: Ivan Oleksiyuk, Roman Chaban, Slava Voloshynovskiy

entry.summary: This work introduces an enrolment-based cross-camera dual-synthetic referencing framework for authenticating copy detection patterns, jointly modeling both printing variability and camera distortions. A deep translator generates high-quality references improving robustness against counterfeiting.

entry.title: Bundesrecht: An Open Library and Corpus for German Statutory Reference Processing

author.name: Harshil Darji, Martin Heckelmann, Christina Kratsch, Gerard de Melo

entry.summary: Bundesrecht is an open library and structured corpus for German statutory reference processing that parses, normalizes, and resolves compact and variable citation strings to canonical statutory provisions. It addresses gaps in existing German legal NLP tools.

entry.title: "In\^{t}elegi Rom\^ane\c{s}te?'' A Recipe for Romanian Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mihai Masala, Marius Leordeanu, Mihai Dascalu, Traian Rebedea

entry.summary: Provides a systematic recipe for building Romanian vision-language models, covering data translation, vision/language backbone selection, and culturally grounded evaluation. Addresses degradation of VLMs on low-resource languages.

entry.title: Flow map learning in nonlinear vector autoregressive models: influence of the feature-library structure on the training error

author.name: Markus Gross

entry.summary: Analyzes how the feature-library structure in nonlinear vector autoregressive models (next-gen reservoir computers) affects training error, deriving asymptotic scaling laws tied to flow-map Lie-series representation. Connects model expressivity to Koopman-operator approximation.

entry.title: BenHalluEval: A Multi-Task Hallucination Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models on Bengali

author.name: Shefayat E Shams Adib, Ahmed Alfey Sani, Ekramul Alam Esham, Ajwad Abrar, Ishmam Tashdeed, Md Taukir Azam Chowdhury

entry.summary: Introduces BenHalluEval, the first fine-grained hallucination evaluation framework for Bengali, covering four tasks and 12k hallucinated candidates across twelve hallucination types. Evaluates seven LLMs under a dual-track false-positive and detection protocol.

entry.title: Personalize Your Large Vision-language Models With In-context Prompt Tuning

author.name: Yanshu Li, Jiaqian Li, Kuai Yu, Xi Xiao, Dongfang Liu, Tianyang Wang, Ruixiang Tang

entry.summary: Proposes in-context prompt tuning (ICPT) for personalizing large vision-language models without inference-time training, using a lightweight projection module to extract fine-grained visual semantics. Targets efficient multi-image, multi-concept personalization.

entry.title: Choosing the Lens: Strategic Perspective Activation in Context-Dependent Argumentation

author.name: Albert Sadowski and Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: This paper introduces context-dependent argumentation frameworks (CDAFs), extending Dung's abstract argumentation with a per-context defeat function that an agent can strategically manipulate. It formalizes an ACTIVATION-MANIPULATION decision problem capturing strategic perspective control not expressible in standard frameworks.

entry.title: Benchmark of Likelihood-Free Inference Methods based on Neural and Optimal Transport Approaches

author.name: Samira Aka, Marie Kratz, Philippe Naveau

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks likelihood-free / simulation-based inference methods (MLE, NBE, EOT, AW-NBE) under structural features like heavy tails and discreteness often ignored by prior benchmarks. It shows that evaluation-tool choice matters greatly for extremes and discrete data.

entry.title: Inspectable Neural Markov Models for Non-Stationary Time Series

author.name: Jan Rovirosa and Jesse Schmolze

entry.summary: This paper parameterizes the manifold of stochastic transition matrices with a neural network to estimate time-inhomogeneous Markov chains in sparse-data regimes, using financial markets as a testbed. It shows conditioning on realized volatility yields more internally consistent Markovian structure than return-based states.

entry.title: Functional MRI Time Series Generation via Wavelet-Based Image Transform and Spectral Flow Matching for Brain Disorder Identification

author.name: Hwa Hui Tew, Junn Yong Loo, Fang Yu Leong, Julia K. Lau, Ding Fan, Hernando Ombao, Rapha\"el C.-W. Phan, Chee Pin Tan, Chee-Ming Ting

entry.summary: This paper proposes Dual-Spectral Flow Matching, a generative framework that synthesizes fMRI BOLD time series using wavelet-based image transforms cascaded with spectral flow matching. It aims to better replicate the non-stationarity and spatiotemporal dynamics of brain signals for downstream disorder identification.

entry.title: Domain Adaptation and Reasoning Frameworks in Language Models: A Controlled Experiment with Historical Cosmology

author.name: Francesco De Bernardis

entry.summary: This controlled experiment studies how domain adaptation reshapes explanatory behavior in language models using pre-Copernican cosmology. It trains a small model from scratch on a corpus with heliocentric references removed and fine-tunes a larger model via QLoRA, evaluating whether modern cosmological framing nonetheless emerges.

entry.title: Mitigating Content Shift and Hallucination in GenAI Image Editing via Structural Refinement

author.name: Luxi Zhao, Michael S. Brown

entry.summary: This paper addresses structure-preserving GenAI image fusion, aiming to retain perceptual enhancements from black-box GenAI editors while enforcing structural faithfulness to the original input. It proposes a post-processing framework that fuses input and enhanced images to mitigate spatial misalignment, texture distortion, and hallucination.

entry.title: ImmigrationQA: A Source-Grounded Dataset and Small-Model Adaptation for U.S. Immigration Law

author.name: Nazarii Shportun

entry.summary: ImmigrationQA is a source-grounded QA dataset of over 17,000 pairs across 13 US immigration subdomains, assembled from primary sources like USCIS Policy Manual and CFR, with a LoRA fine-tuned Llama 3.2 3B model. QA pairs were generated using Claude Sonnet 4.6.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Control Barrier Functions for Collision Avoidance via Bernstein Polynomial Approximations

author.name: Siwon Jo, Yanze Zhang, Yupeng Yang, and Wenhao Luo

entry.summary: This work introduces geometry-aware Control Barrier Functions based on Bernstein-Polynomial Signed Distance Fields for collision avoidance with irregularly shaped robots and obstacles. It provides a unified differentiable representation that avoids conservatism of simple shape surrogates while keeping constraint counts low for real-time performance.

entry.title: SemStruct: Contextualizing Semantic Embeddings with Structural Information for Schema Matching

author.name: Inwon Kang, Kavitha Srinivas, Nandana Mihindukulasooriya, Sola Shirai, Parikshit Ram, Horst Samulowitz, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: SemStruct combines frozen pre-trained language models with graph neural networks for schema matching, modeling tables as heterogeneous graphs of columns and values connected by rows to capture relational context lost in serialized text. This recovers row-level co-occurrence structure that standard PLM serialization discards.

entry.title: Generating Graph-like Rules for Knowledge Graph Reasoning via Diffusion Models

author.name: Haoxiang Cheng, Yunfei Wang, Chao Chen, Kewei Cheng, Zhipeng Lin, Haoxuan Li, Changjun Fan, Shixuan Liu

entry.summary: SLAP proposes a Semantic Least Action Principle for variational video-language modeling, treating latent video trajectories as paths on a Riemannian manifold governed by a Semantic Lagrangian to fill temporal gaps from sparse frame sampling. It frames frame interpolation as variational mechanics rather than probabilistic generation to maintain semantic consistency.

entry.title: BiSegMamba: Efficient Bidirectional Tri-Oriented Mamba for 3D Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Bakht Zada, Chao Tong, Qile Su, Shuai Zhang

entry.summary: BiSegMamba is a bidirectional tri-oriented Mamba network for 3D medical image segmentation that reduces the cost of repeated high-resolution scanning and improves directional aggregation over forward-only designs. It uses a compact-to-detail architecture for efficient volumetric reasoning.

entry.title: Traceable by Design: An LLM Pipeline and Dashboard for EU Regulatory Consultation Analysis

author.name: Thales Bertaglia, Haoyang Gui, Catalina Goanta, Gerasimos Spanakis

entry.summary: This work presents an LLM pipeline and dashboard for analyzing EU regulatory consultation submissions, grounding every extracted topic in a verbatim source quote for full traceability and transparency. It was applied to thousands of submissions to the Digital Fairness Act, producing tens of thousands of evidence-backed annotations.

entry.title: Skill Availability and Presentation Granularity in Large-Language-Model Agents: A Controlled SkillsBench Study

author.name: Xiaonan Xu, Wenjing Wu

entry.summary: Conducts a controlled SkillsBench study on how the availability and presentation granularity of skill documents affect LLM agent task success. Finds that skill availability is the dominant factor, boosting pass rates by 18-36 points across GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek V4-Flash.

entry.title: Institutions and the transmission of upper-tail human capital: scientific lineages across a millennium

author.name: Hiroyuki Chuma, Kanji Otsuka, and Yoichi Sato

entry.summary: Maps the millennium-long network of master-student knowledge transmission using 470k Wikidata mentor-student records and Fields Medalists as tracers, building a 25.5-million-path directed acyclic graph. Documents institutional transitions like the 17th-century concentration on Leibniz.

entry.title: Moment-Based Inference for Regression with Latent Dirichlet Covariates

author.name: Ziyu Jiang

entry.summary: This econometrics paper develops moment-based inference for regression where latent Dirichlet (LDA topic) shares serve as covariates, correcting spectral moments to propagate topic-estimation uncertainty. It addresses inference difficulties in the common plug-in topic-then-regress workflow.

entry.title: Forecasting threshold exceedance of atmospheric variables at a specific location

author.name: Roberta Baggio and Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Muzy

entry.summary: This study compares direct binary-classification and full-distribution probabilistic approaches for forecasting site-specific threshold exceedances of temperature and wind speed, using a toy model and the MeteoNet dataset. It finds the full-distribution approach consistently outperforms for rare extreme events.

entry.title: Few-Shot Adaptation Benchmark for Remote Sensing Vision-Language Models

author.name: Karim El Khoury, Maxime Zanella, Christophe De Vleeschouwer, Benoit Macq

entry.summary: This work presents the first structured benchmark for few-shot adaptation of remote sensing vision-language models across ten scene classification datasets. It reveals that models with similar zero-shot performance can behave very differently under few-shot adaptation.

entry.title: Enhancing Regime Shift Detection Using Unstructured Data: A Study on the Treasury Market

author.name: Mingxuan Yi, Vidal Mehra, Jing Chen, John Cartlidge

entry.summary: This paper proposes a text-enhanced regime shift detection pipeline that combines LLM reasoning over central-bank communications with statistical validation on financial time series. The detector-agnostic framework uses unstructured policy text to propose candidate shifts before they appear in prices.

entry.title: Improving Small Language Models for Code Generation with Reinforcement Learning from Verification Feedback

author.name: Egor Skopin, Evgeny Kotelnikov

entry.summary: This empirical study applies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to improve small language models (Qwen3-0.6B, Llama3.2-1B) for Python code generation on MBPP, using unit-test, static-analysis, and combined rewards with GRPO and GSPO. The combined reward improves pass@1 by up to 13 points.

entry.title: Graph-Conditioned Mixture of Graph Neural Network Experts for Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Amirhossein Ghaffari, Saeid Sheikhi, Ekaterina Gilman

entry.summary: GC-MoE is a graph-conditioned mixture-of-experts framework for traffic forecasting that assigns each road node a personalized combination of frozen pretrained spatio-temporal GNN experts based on topology and recent input. It trains only a lightweight routing module while keeping experts frozen.

entry.title: On-Device Generative AI for GDPR-Compliant Visual Monitoring: Natural Language Alerts from Local Object Detection

author.name: Gudrun Schappacher-Tilp, Nicoletta Kaehling, Jan Kornberger, Egon Teiniker

entry.summary: This proof-of-concept builds a GDPR-compliant edge visual monitoring pipeline using on-device YOLOv5n-seg on a Hailo accelerator and a locally hosted Phi-3 Mini to generate natural-language alerts, discarding raw pixels after inference. No image data leaves the device.

entry.title: Transforming and Encoding FTS for SAT Solving: What Helps, What Hurts (Extended Version)

author.name: Jo\~ao Filipe, \'Alvaro Torralba, Gregor Behnke

entry.summary: This paper investigates encoding factored planning tasks (which extend SAS+ with disjunctive preconditions and conditional effects) into SAT, proposing several translation strategies for the factored transition relation. It analyzes parallelism and the impact of task transformations on solver performance.

entry.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Uncertainty Quantification Methodologies for Predicting Turbine Gas Temperature Degradation

author.name: Jostein Barry-Straume, Changmin Son, Adrian Sandu, Gavan Burke, Rekha Sundararajan, Andrew Rimell, James G. Steinrock

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks five uncertainty quantification methods (Delta, Bayesian MC Dropout, Bootstrap, LUBE, Mean-Variance Estimation) for predicting turbine gas temperature degradation in a unified experimental framework. It evaluates both accuracy and prediction-interval tightness via coverage metrics.

entry.title: Universal Decision Learners

author.name: Sridhar Mahadevan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a category-theoretic Universal Decision Learner framework unifying planning, RL, causal intervention, online learning, and game-theoretic equilibrium via left and right Kan extensions of a decision functor. The claim is that many decision formalisms instantiate the same universal problem of canonically extending local behavioral data.

entry.title: Annotations Are Not All You Need: A Cross-modal Knowledge Transfer Network for Unsupervised Temporal Sentence Grounding

author.name: Xiang Fang, Daizong Liu, Wanlong Fang, Pan Zhou, Yu Cheng, Keke Tang, Kai Zou

entry.summary: This paper tackles unsupervised temporal sentence grounding without paired video-query or segment boundary annotations by transferring cheap cross-modal alignment knowledge from other tasks, using entity-aware object-guided alignment. It reduces the heavy annotation cost that limits real-world temporal grounding.

entry.title: IRIS: time-structured manifold projections

author.name: Brian Ondov, Chia-Hsuan Chang, Weipeng Zhou, Xingjian Zhang, Xueqing Peng, Yutong Xie, Huan He, Qiaozhu Mei and Hua Xu

entry.summary: IRIS is a manifold learning algorithm that incorporates time-ordering into low-dimensional layouts, unlike t-SNE or UMAP, so that temporal dynamics in biomedical data like single-cell RNA-seq are visible. It applies to scRNA-seq, metagenomics, and literature data.

entry.title: ImmersiveTTS: Environment-Aware Text-to-Speech with Multimodal Diffusion Transformer and Domain-Specific Representation Alignment

author.name: Jun-Hak Yun, Seung-Bin Kim, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: ImmersiveTTS jointly generates speech together with environmental audio using a multimodal diffusion transformer and domain-specific representation alignment, addressing the acoustic mismatch between speech and ambient sound. It targets immersive, context-aware speech synthesis.

entry.title: How Much Do LLMs Know About Chinese Zero Pronouns?

author.name: Yifei Li, Guanyi Chen, Tingting He

entry.summary: This paper systematically investigates how well LLMs handle Chinese zero pronouns across identification, classification, resolution, and translation tasks, finding that zero pronouns remain highly challenging especially for upstream identification. It evaluates a diverse set of models on this pervasive pro-drop phenomenon.

entry.title: LLM-FACETS: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Evaluating LLM Transparency and Accountability

author.name: Tom Lucas, Alessio Buscemi, Alfredo Capozucca, German Castignani, Barbara Delacroix

entry.summary: LLM-FACETS is an open-source, privacy-preserving framework with a browser interface for evaluating LLM factuality, calibration, and reproducibility, designed for non-technical practitioners. It uses a plugin architecture structured around technical experts, domain experts, and compliance officers.

entry.title: How well does Classification Accuracy capture Concept Drift Detection Quality? An overview of Concept Drift Detection evaluation

author.name: Joanna Komorniczak

entry.summary: This work provides an in-depth overview of how classification accuracy relates to concept drift detection quality in synthetic nonstationary data streams. It studies eight drift detection metrics, arguing classification metrics may not reliably reflect detection quality and pushing for a unified evaluation framework.

entry.title: Simulation of collision avoidance behavior in crowd movement by data-driven approach

author.name: Xuanwen Liang, Eric Wai Ming Lee

entry.summary: CPGAN is a data-driven crowd simulation model that incorporates a pedestrian collision mechanism into the loss to reduce the high collision rates of prior trajectory-prediction models. It uses a lateral-acceleration-based collision loss and Voronoi-based motion features within a GAN architecture.

entry.title: Appropriateness of Empathy in AI: A Signal-Cost Perspective

author.name: Chi-Ching Juan and Tao Wang and Harold Lee

entry.summary: This paper applies signaling theory to evaluate whether AI empathy is contextually appropriate, proposing signal cost proxies (emotional richness, perspective-taking, contextual tailoring) mapped to affective, cognitive, and associative empathy. The framework evaluates empathy not just by presence but by appropriateness relative to user demand.

entry.title: Deep-learning-based low-energy trigger algorithms for the Hyper-Kamiokande experiment

author.name: Katharina Lachner and Sa\'ul Alonso-Monsalve and Benjamin Richards and Davide Sgalaberna

entry.summary: Develops deep-learning trigger algorithms for low-energy neutrino events in the Hyper-Kamiokande detector, comparing supervised classifiers against anomaly-detection approaches. Achieves meaningful signal identification efficiency for sub-7 MeV events under tight runtime constraints.

entry.title: DG-CoLearn: An Efficient Collaborative Learning Framework for Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Ashley Hoi-Ting Au, Zikun Zhang, Ligang He, Qiang Ni

entry.summary: Proposes DG-CoLearn, a privacy-preserving collaborative dynamic graph learning framework using incremental snapshot processing to avoid full retraining. Handles cross-partition edges without sharing graph structure between clients.

entry.title: If LLMs Have Human-Like Attributes, Then So Does Age of Empires II

author.name: Adrian de Wynter

entry.summary: A critical/philosophical argument that purported anthropomorphic attributes of LLMs are empirically non-unique by training a simple neural network on Age of Empires II and noting any sufficiently powerful substrate could present similar attributes. Cautions against anthropomorphizing conclusions.

entry.title: Separating Secrets from Placeholders: A Hybrid CNN-CodeBERT Framework for Three-Class Credential Leakage Detection

author.name: Maksuda Bilkis Baby, Khushika Shah, Naiyue Liang and Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid CNN-CodeBERT framework for three-class credential leakage detection that explicitly models placeholder/weak credentials as a distinct class to reduce false positives. Evaluated on a new 9,426-sample dataset across 10 languages with strong MCC and F1.

entry.title: Automated Prediction of Postoperative Pancreatic Fistula Using Preoperative Computed Tomography

author.name: Ashok Choudhary, Chris Varghese, Leo Y. Li-Han, Frank G. Lee, Ellen L. Larson, Elizabeth B. Habermann, Cornelius A. Thiels, Hojjat Salehinejad

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end deep learning pipeline from pancreas segmentation to classification for preoperative postoperative pancreatic fistula risk estimation using CT scans. Benchmarks multiple 3D architectures for pancreas-specific risk stratification.

entry.title: SPECTRA: Synthetic IR Test Collections with Relevance Oracles and Controlled Distractor Diagnostics

author.name: Eric Liang

entry.summary: SPECTRA is a reproducible framework for generating synthetic IR test collections with deterministic relevance oracles and controlled distractor diagnostics, scaling to 60,000 documents. It serves as a diagnostic complement to human-judged TREC/Cranfield evaluation when documents are private or unavailable.

entry.title: Bayesian Classification with Probit-link Split-and-merge Gaussian Process Prior in EEG-based Brain-Computer Interfaces

author.name: Yunong Wu, Jane E. Huggins, Jian Kang, and Tianwen Ma

entry.summary: This work proposes a Bayesian generative framework with a Probit-link Split-and-merge Gaussian Process prior for classifying EEG ERP responses in BCI spellers, performing interpretable spatio-temporal feature selection. It targets accurate P300 detection while improving interpretability and efficiency.

entry.title: Unsupervised LiDAR-Based Multi-UAV Detection and Tracking Under Extreme Sparsity

author.name: Nivand Khosravi, Rodrigo Ventura, and Meysam Basiri

entry.summary: This paper introduces an unsupervised LiDAR-only pipeline for detecting and tracking multiple UAVs under extreme point sparsity, where small drones produce only 1-2 returns per scan. It combines range-adaptive DBSCAN with temporal consistency checks and is validated on real air-to-air flight data.

entry.title: Gradient-Free Training of Spiking Neural Networks via Low-Rank Evolution Strategies

author.name: Dhruv Patankar, Sachit Ramesha Gowda

entry.summary: This paper trains spiking neural networks without gradients using EGGROLL, a low-rank factorization of evolution-strategy perturbations that cuts memory cost substantially. Applied to a Leaky Integrate-and-Fire SNN on N-MNIST, it enables gradient-free training suited to on-chip neuromorphic learning.

entry.title: Social Reasoning in Machines: Investigating Collective Truth-Seeking Dynamics in Large Language Model Debate

author.name: Tom Pecher

entry.summary: This thesis simulates the Argumentative Theory of Reasoning through multi-agent debate among LLMs, investigating whether collective adversarial discourse produces emergent truth-seeking. It treats truth as an emergent property of social epistemology rather than individual reasoning.

entry.title: Protocol for evaluating ChatGPT in biomedical association generation and verification using a RAG-enabled, cross-model majority voting workflow

author.name: Ahmed Abdeen Hamed, Luis M. Rocha

entry.summary: This paper presents a protocol for evaluating ChatGPT's ability to generate disease-centric biomedical associations, validating entities against ontologies and verifying claims against literature. It uses a RAG-enabled cross-model majority voting workflow with self-consistency to detect hallucinations.

entry.title: 3DAE: Binaural Quality Assessment for Audio Novel View Synthesis with Spatial Maps and Benchmark

author.name: Jialu Xu, Yifan Zhou

entry.summary: 3DAE introduces a full-reference diagnostic framework and benchmark for binaural quality assessment in audio novel-view synthesis, using time-frequency error maps for magnitude, interaural level/phase differences, timing, and loudness. It reveals where and why binaural prediction fails rather than relying on global metrics alone.

entry.title: Refining Word-Based Grammatical Error Annotation for L2 Korean

author.name: Jungyeul Park and Kyungtae Lim and Wonjun Oh and Benjamin Nguyen and Zihao Huang and Mengyang Qiu and Jayoung Song

entry.summary: This paper refines word-based grammatical error annotation for L2 Korean, addressing the mismatch between word-level evaluation and morpheme-level error loci in bound postpositions and verbal endings. It reconstructs targets from the NIKL corpus and defines a Korean ERRANT-style edit framework.

entry.title: Scientific Machine Learning for Engine Health Management and Remaining Useful Life Prediction

author.name: Jostein Barry-Straume, Changmin Son, Adrian Sandu, Gavan Burke, Rekha Sundararajan, Andrew Rimell, James G. Steinrock

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-task scientific ML framework for engine health management, jointly predicting turbine gas temperature, delta temperature, and remaining useful life with quantified prediction intervals. A shared sequence encoder feeds task-specific heads with mean-variance estimation for uncertainty.

entry.title: Jamming-Resilient PRB Reservation for Latency-Critical O-RAN Network Slicing

author.name: Elahe Delavari, and Junaid Farooq

entry.summary: This paper proposes a reserve-based resilience framework for physical resource block allocation in sliced O-RAN deployments, where a near-RT RIC xApp controls a pool of reserved PRBs to mitigate adversarial jamming. It provides hybrid proactive backlog clearing and reactive reserve allocation for latency-critical industrial 5G.

entry.title: TeachObs: A Human-Validated Benchmark for Multimodal Teaching Observation and Model Evaluation

author.name: Yeil Jeong, Youngjin Yoo, Seobin Sohn, Hyejin Han, Jinseo Lee, Scott Howard, Unggi Lee

entry.summary: TeachObs is a human-validated multimodal benchmark of classroom lesson videos from eight countries, annotated at 15-second scene granularity with 39 binary teaching observation codes for evaluating models on pedagogical and visual practices. It uses reliability-aware rules for constructing gold labels.

entry.title: Two Degree-of-Freedom Vibratory Transport in a Grasp

author.name: C. L. Yako, Shenli Yuan, and Kenneth Salisbury

entry.summary: This paper uses asymmetric vibrations via closed-loop position control of a moving surface to achieve two degree-of-freedom in-hand manipulation of grasped parts, analyzing how sticking and slipping acceleration parameters affect part velocity. It develops a 2-DoF vibratory surface supporting translation and rotation, validated experimentally.

entry.title: Design and Evaluation of Multi-Agent AI Oracle Systems for Prediction Market Resolution

author.name: Tarun Kota

entry.summary: This work evaluates whether multi-agent LLM architectures improve prediction-market oracle resolution accuracy over single-model baselines, comparing independent aggregation and deliberative consensus on 1,189 resolved KalshiBench questions. All agents share a common Exa evidence layer with date-filtered retrieval against GPT-5 Nano, DeepSeek V3, and Llama-3.3-70B baselines.

entry.title: Variational Adapter for Cross-modal Similarity Representation

author.name: WenZhang Wei, Zhipeng Gui, Dehua Peng, Tiandi Ye, Huayi Wu

entry.summary: VACSR is a variational adapter that reformulates image-text matching to capture fine-grained continuous cross-modal similarity, reducing false negatives caused by binary matching annotations. It models annotation flaws to improve uncertainty allocation in vision-language models.

entry.title: Omni-Supervised Motion Editing: Balancing Change and Invariance through Positive-Negative Learning

author.name: Zhenwu Shi, Jingyu Gong, Peiwei Wang, Xingzan Wang, Tianwen Qian, Wenxi Li, Yuan Fang, Jiao Xie, Lizhuang Ma, Shaohui Lin

entry.summary: OmniME is an omni-supervised framework for text-based human motion editing that balances precise editing of target regions with preservation of unedited motion via positive-negative learning and multi-level feature supervision. It tackles motion distortion and semantic misalignment in diffusion-based editing.

entry.title: Benchmarking Single-Step Inpainting Methods for Multi-Object 3D Gaussian Splatting Scenes

author.name: Finn Dr\"oge, Cecilia Curreli, Abhishek Saroha, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: This work benchmarks single-step inpainting methods for object removal in multi-object 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, finding reconstruction-based 2D inpainters outperform generative diffusion models in 3D consistency and that initializing scenes from scratch beats finetuning. It also addresses the lack of real-world 360-degree ground truth.

entry.title: DEM: A Distilled Explanation Model for Interpretable Anomaly Detection in Physiological Sensor Networks

author.name: Jyotirmoy Singh, Anushka Roy, Shreea Bose, Chittaranjan Hota

entry.summary: DEM is a glass-box framework for anomaly detection in physiological sensor networks that distills a gradient boosting model's knowledge into an interpretable decision tree operating on residuals from a linear baseline, so the explanation is the prediction itself. It targets clinically interpretable, low-false-alarm detection in wireless body area networks.

entry.title: Rethinking Efficient Crack Segmentation with Task-Aligned Structural-Directional Modeling

author.name: Shipeng Liu, Liang Zhao, Dengfeng Chen, Weihua Zhang

entry.summary: RIFT reframes crack segmentation as sparse structural recovery rather than generic semantic segmentation, using morphology-aligned modeling to preserve weak directional evidence and suppress background coupling. It proposes a compact family of efficient crack-segmentation models tailored to thin, anisotropic structures.

entry.title: FSM-Net: An Efficient Frequency-Spatial Network for Real-World Deblurring

author.name: Vinh-Thuan Ly

entry.summary: Presents FSM-Net, an efficient frequency-spatial network for real-world image deblurring that placed 2nd in the NTIRE 2026 challenge. Combines FFT-based frequency attention with a linear-complexity transformer bottleneck.

entry.title: Shaft-integrated Force Sensing with Transformer-based Dynamics Compensation for Telesurgery

author.name: Shuyuan Yang, Grant Boone, Timo Markert, Sebastian Matich, Andreas Theissler, Martin Atzmueller, Zonghe Chua

entry.summary: Integrates a six-axis force sensor into the distal end of a standard cable-driven surgical instrument and uses a transformer for dynamics compensation. Enables accessible end-effector force sensing for robot-assisted surgery research.

entry.title: Reliable Multilingual Orthopedic Decision Support from Clinical Narratives: Language-Aware Adaptation and Verification-Guided Deferral

author.name: Danish Ali, Li Xiaojian, Sundas Iqbal, Farrukh Zaidi

entry.summary: Presents a reliability-oriented multilingual framework for classifying orthopedic clinical notes in English, Hindi, and Punjabi, introducing IndicBERT-HPA with language-aware adapter heads and verification-guided deferral. Targets low-resource clinical decision support.

entry.title: SMART: SMPLest-X Mesh Adaptation and RAFT Tracking for Soccer Pose Estimation

author.name: Parthsarthi Rawat

entry.summary: Presents SMART for the FIFA Skeletal Tracking Challenge 2026, finetuning SMPLest-X with RAFT optical-flow camera tracking, foot-plane anchoring, and temporal smoothing for 3D world-space soccer pose estimation. Achieves a 38.6 percent improvement over the FIFA baseline.

entry.title: The main impact from automated AI production: concentration of power?

author.name: Oliver Sourbut

entry.summary: This post argues that the main impact of automated AI R&D may be concentration of power rather than just an intelligence explosion, situating the discussion historically from I.J. Good through recent statements by Altman and Clark. It is conceptual analysis of AI feedback loops and their societal implications.

entry.title: QASM-Eval: A Dataset to Train and Evaluate LLMs on OpenQASM-3 Beyond Quantum Circuits

author.name: Zhenxiao Fu, Lei Jiang, Fan Chen

entry.summary: QASM-Eval is a dataset for training and evaluating LLMs on OpenQASM-3 programs that use advanced hardware-oriented features like mid-circuit measurement, pulse-level control, and dynamical decoupling, going beyond basic gate-sequence circuits. It fills a gap in quantum code generation evaluation.

entry.title: Hamiltonian-Inspired Attention Mechanism for Scalable RF Transmitter Fingerprinting

author.name: Chitraksh Singh, Monisha Dhanraj, Akram Sheriff

entry.summary: The Hamiltonian Transformer introduces a physics-informed attention mechanism for RF transmitter fingerprinting that enforces norm-preserving value dynamics using a skew-symmetric generator and leapfrog integration. It aims to improve robustness under receiver and channel distribution shifts on raw I/Q signals.

entry.title: CodeGolf Bench: A Multi-Language Benchmark for Evaluating Concise Code Generation Capabilities of Large Language Models

author.name: Vedant Padwal

entry.summary: CodeGolf Bench is a multi-language benchmark using the code.golf platform to evaluate LLMs on producing concise, minimal-byte code across 60 programming languages with live human baselines. Evaluation of nine LLMs shows reasoning models substantially outperform non-reasoning ones, especially in C++.

entry.title: Can LLM Teams Play What? Where? When?

author.name: Anastasia Kotelnikova, Viktor Byzov, Maria Dolzhenkova, Evgeny Kotelnikov

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether team-based LLM interaction improves performance on the What? Where? When? quiz game, which rewards collective reasoning and cultural knowledge. Three team strategies (Voting, Silent Team, Talkative Team) outperform single-model baselines by up to 20 points, with the best team reaching 44% accuracy on 2025 questions to limit data leakage.

entry.title: Investigating Detection and Obfuscation of Prompt Injection Attacks Against Software Reverse Engineering AI Agents

author.name: Brian Crawford and Patrick McClure

entry.summary: This companion security paper demonstrates defensive detection of prompt injection strings embedded in decompiler output for reverse engineering AI agents, plus obfuscation techniques and counter-defenses. It advances understanding of risks for deploying agentic software analysis in production cyber workflows.

entry.title: Agnosiophobia in a virtual agent: behavioral and dynamical architecture in Lenia

author.name: Jesse Cool, Benedikt Hartl, Michael Levin, Samantha Petti

entry.summary: This study introduces sensory-deprivation regions into Lenia virtual agent environments and discovers that emergent creatures avoid blind spots, a behavior termed agnosiophobia, complementing infotaxis. It analyzes the behavioral and dynamical architecture underlying this avoidance using occlusion-sensitivity mapping.

entry.title: Text-guided Feature Disentanglement for Cross-modal Gait Recognition

author.name: Zhiyang Lu and Ming Cheng

entry.summary: TCFDNet addresses LiDAR-Camera cross-modal gait recognition by using LLM-generated modality-aware textual priors as semantic anchors to guide learning of disentangled modality-shared representations. It bridges the substantial gap between 2D videos and 3D point cloud sequences for biometric identification.

entry.title: Reading Between the Citations: A Typed Claim Network for Scientific Literature

author.name: Ning Ding, Sergio J. Rodr\'iguez M\'endez and Pouya G. Omran

entry.summary: This paper proposes the claim network, a representation that reifies each cross-document citation as a typed claim with source, target, text, and a four-class stance label rather than an untyped edge. It enables richer community-level queries about how documents are received, demonstrated on a 3D point-cloud segmentation corpus.

entry.title: DRIFT: Joint Channel Estimation and Prediction Towards Pilotless 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks

author.name: Bruno De Filippo, Carla Amatetti, Alessandro Vanelli-Coralli

entry.summary: DRIFT is an iterative joint channel estimation and prediction framework for pilotless 6G non-terrestrial (satellite) networks, designed to be accurate yet computationally efficient under strict onboard power constraints in low Earth orbit. It aims to reduce pilot overhead and improve spectral efficiency.

entry.title: HQ-JEPA: Hybrid Quantum Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Cross-Modal Remote Sensing Representation Learning

author.name: Md Aminur Hossain, Ayush V. Patel, Sanjay K. Singh, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: HQ-JEPA is a hybrid quantum-classical joint-embedding predictive architecture for cross-modal remote sensing, predicting masked target representations across Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery while aligning modalities, using a quantum SWAP-test-based fidelity similarity loss. It learns semantic representations in latent space rather than via pixel reconstruction.

entry.title: MAECO-Lite: Modular Ontology for Dynamic Malware Analysis

author.name: Zekeri Adams, Peter \v{S}vec, J\'an K\v{l}uka, Roderik Ploszek, Monday Onoja, \v{S}tefan Balogh and Martin Homola

entry.summary: MAECO-Lite is a modular ontology for dynamic malware analysis built on foundational ontological analysis of MAEC and STIX constructs using the Unified Foundational Ontology. It separates enduring malware artifacts from execution-generated events to improve semantic precision in threat intelligence.

entry.title: Developing a novel Comorbidities Index for predicting 10-year mortality in Prostate Cancer patients: A computational data-driven approach

author.name: Davide Farinati and Francesco Barletta and Paolo Zaurito and Simone Scuderi and Nicholas Raison and Alejandro Granados and Prokar Dasgupta and Giorgio Gandaglia and Alberto Briganti

entry.summary: This paper develops a data-driven comorbidity index tailored to prostate cancer patients considered for radical prostatectomy, recalibrating Charlson index weights using population-based bio-inspired algorithms. The goal is more accurate ten-year other-cause mortality estimation to avoid overtreatment.

entry.title: Adaptive Artificial Time-Delay Control with Barrier Lyapunov Constraints for Euler-Lagrange Robots

author.name: Saksham Gupta, Rishabh Dev Yadav, Sarthak Mishra, Amitabh Sharma, Sourish Ganguly, Wei Pan, Spandan Roy, Simone Baldi

entry.summary: Develops an adaptive control framework for Euler-Lagrange robots combining time-delay estimation with barrier Lyapunov functions to enforce time-varying state constraints without prior model knowledge. Provides analytical error bounds and online adaptation.

entry.title: Actuator-Aware Inverse Kinematics with Joint-Limit Admissibility for Torque-Controlled Redundant Robots

author.name: Mohammad Dastranj, Mahdi Hejrati and Jouni Mattila

entry.summary: Proposes actuator-aware inverse kinematics for torque-controlled redundant robots, formulating a convex QP whose decision variable is joint-level required velocity with control-barrier-function joint-limit bounds. Improves realized motion under downstream torque control.

entry.title: Towards a Humanized Social-Media Ecosystem: AI-Augmented HCI Design Patterns for Safety, Agency & Well-Being

author.name: Mohd Ruhul Ameen and Akif Islam

entry.summary: This paper proposes Human-Layer AI, user-owned browser-based intermediaries that sit between social platform logic and the interface to give users moment-to-moment control over their feed and well-being. It includes a working Chrome/Edge prototype with five interaction patterns and a mathematical formulation balancing utility, autonomy, and risk.

entry.title: Lightweight SAR Ship Detection via Contrastive Distillation

author.name: Surendar Devasundaram, Saber Latibari Banafsheh, Abhijit Mahalanobis

entry.summary: SURGE is a structured relational knowledge distillation framework for lightweight SAR ship detection that transfers relational geometry from a teacher detector to a compact student via a contrastive InfoNCE objective. It improves over feature/logit matching by capturing geometric relationships among objects.

entry.title: Procedural Generation of First Person Shooter Maps using Map-Elites

author.name: Simone de Donato, Pier Luca Lanzi, Daniele Loiacono

entry.summary: This paper applies MAP-Elites quality-diversity algorithms to procedurally generate first-person shooter maps, introducing two novel map representations and metrics for topological and gameplay-emergent properties. New representations generate more diverse maps.

entry.title: Bidirectional Incremental Generalized Hybrid A*

author.name: Sidharth Talia, Oren Salzman, Siddhartha Srinivasa

entry.summary: This paper improves the Incremental Generalized Hybrid A* kinodynamic planner by making it bidirectional, addressing how frozen vertices can hide solution-supporting states during anytime search. It targets efficient planning for systems with complex dynamics in unstructured environments where precomputed motion primitives are infeasible.

entry.title: A Padding Method for Enhanced Encoding of Inorganic Structures with Varying Chemical Compositions

author.name: Thang Dang, Haderbache Amir, Tzanakakis Alexandros, Yoshimoto Yuta

entry.summary: This work introduces a domain-specific symmetry-aware padding and encoding method for generating inorganic materials with varying chemical compositions via generative models. It aims to improve generative accuracy and stability across the vast combinatorial space of inorganic compounds.

entry.title: PolSAR Image Classification using a Hybrid Complex-Valued Network (HybridCVNet)

author.name: Mohammed Q. Alkhatib

entry.summary: HybridCVNet is a complex-valued hybrid CNN-Transformer network for PolSAR image classification that preserves phase information often discarded by real-valued networks. It combines complex-valued 3D/2D CNNs with a complex-valued vision transformer.

entry.title: Lightweight CNN-Based Anomaly Detection for High Voltage Converter Modulators in the Spallation Neutron Source

author.name: Alberto D. Cencillo, Leonardo Concepci\'on, Juli\'an Luengo, Isaac Triguero

entry.summary: The paper presents a lightweight CNN for anomaly detection in high voltage converter modulators at the Spallation Neutron Source, designed to capture both temporal structure and cross-channel statistical dependencies. It targets reducing unscheduled downtime at large accelerator facilities.

entry.title: Multi-Turn Multi-Agent Dialogue for Collaborative Reconstruction Improves VLM Performance on Spatial Reasoning, But Only Barely

author.name: Chalamalasetti Kranti, Sherzod Hakimov, David Schlangen

entry.summary: Studies whether multi-turn multi-agent dialogue between vision-language models improves spatial reasoning in collaborative structure-building tasks. Finds only marginal gains, highlighting persistent VLM limitations in grounded collaborative spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Scaling Conversational Hungarian ASR: The BEA-Dialogue+ Corpus

author.name: M\'at\'e Gedeon, Piroska Zs\'ofia Barta, P\'eter Mihajlik, Katalin M\'ady

entry.summary: Introduces BEA-Dialogue+, an expanded 200-hour Hungarian conversational ASR corpus that relaxes speaker-disjoint splits while preserving primary speaker separation. Enables controlled study of training-data versus speaker-overlap trade-offs with Whisper and FastConformer models.

entry.title: NLA Thought Anchors

author.name: Realmbird

entry.summary: This LessWrong post investigates Natural Language Autoencoders (NLA) thought anchors, finding that the first sentence is most counterfactually important for reconstruction and for the autoencoder output containing the correct final answer, while degenerate outputs appear only for incorrect-response activations. It connects reconstruction loss to answer correctness in interpretability terms.

entry.title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning for Wind Farm Control via Expert Demonstrations

author.name: Marcus Binder Nilsen, Julian Quick, Tuhfe G\"o\c{c}men, Nikolay Dimitrov, Pierre-Elouan R\'ethor\'e

entry.summary: This work accelerates reinforcement learning for wind farm control by pretraining Soft Actor-Critic agents via behavior cloning from steady-state wake-model expert demonstrations. Experiments show pretraining eliminates poor initial performance, addressing a key deployment barrier.

entry.title: Reinterpreting Safety Thresholds as Neuron Spiking Thresholds

author.name: Enrico Del Re, Mohamed Sabry, Cristina Olaverri-Monreal

entry.summary: This work reinterprets fixed surrogate safety thresholds in automated driving as spiking thresholds of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons in a spiking neural network, trained to align spikes with human braking onsets. It captures human responses to sustained borderline and brief high-risk conditions better than fixed thresholds.

entry.title: Learning effective models from network dynamics data with multiple initial conditions using weak form SINDy

author.name: Moyi Tian, Daniel A. Messenger, Vanja Dukic, Nancy Rodr\'iguez, David M. Bortz

entry.summary: This paper applies weak-form SINDy to learn governing equations of coupled online-offline social activity dynamics on networks from data with multiple initial conditions. It evaluates recovery accuracy under different noise levels using mean-field-generated data.

entry.title: Pairwise Reference Alignment as a Model-Level Ordinal Observable

author.name: Mujing Li

entry.summary: This note formalizes pairwise reference alignment as an ordinal observable: the probability that a model's score ordering agrees with reference pairwise preferences, given a reference distribution over preference triples. It clarifies what model-level quantity is actually estimated in preference-based evaluation and alignment.

entry.title: GP-GOMEA with GPU-Based Fitness Evaluations: Design and Performance Analysis

author.name: Jasper Post, Johannes Koch, Anton Bouter, Tanja Alderliesten and Peter A.N. Bosman

entry.summary: This paper introduces GPU-accelerated fitness evaluation for GP-GOMEA, a leading symbolic regression evolutionary algorithm, substantially increasing evaluation throughput. It is a step toward making interpretable symbolic regression scalable to larger datasets.

entry.title: Linear Ordering Problem: Time for a Change

author.name: Fabrizio Fagiolo, Marco Baioletti, Valentino Santucci

entry.summary: This paper revisits the Linear Ordering Problem, introducing a modern benchmark suite derived from up-to-date economic input-output data and addressing the issue of many distinct global optima that complicate applications needing a single solution. It updates outdated benchmarks and proposes algorithmic strategies.

entry.title: A Pilot Study on Curator-Guided Multilingual Art Description for Blind and Low-Vision Audiences with Small Vision-Language Models

author.name: Iosif Tsangko, Andreas Triantafyllopoulos, George Margetis, Ioana Crihana, and Bj\"orn W. Schuller

entry.summary: This pilot study explores curator-guided multilingual art description for blind and low-vision audiences using a small on-premise vision-language model fine-tuned with LoRA for German, Romanian, and Serbian. It compares language-specific versus single multilingual adapters and includes an LLM-as-judge evaluation calibrated against a small human pilot.

entry.title: Comparing LLM-Based Conversational and Graphical Interfaces for Industrial Decision Tasks: An Exploratory Mixed-Methods Study

author.name: Roberto Figli\`e, Simone Caputo, Alan Serrano, Tommaso Turchi, Daniele Mazzei

entry.summary: This exploratory mixed-methods study compares LLM-based conversational interfaces with graphical interfaces for industrial decision tasks using IoT data. It scopes whether natural-language CUIs deliver on promises of directness and reasoning support versus traditional GUIs.

entry.title: Answer-Set-Programming-based Abstractions for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Rafael Bankosegger, Thomas Eiter, Johannes Oetsch

entry.summary: Explores using Answer-Set Programming to realize relational RL abstractions (CARCASS framework) in a fully declarative manner instead of Prolog. Leverages domain knowledge to abstract large state spaces for RL.

entry.title: Fine-grained Verification via Diagnostic Reasoning Supervision for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction

author.name: Wenna Lai, Haoran Xie, Guandong Xu, Qing Li, S. Joe Qin

entry.summary: Proposes FiVeD, a fine-grained verification framework using diagnostic reasoning supervision to filter and re-rank aspect-sentiment triplet extraction outputs. Addresses locally plausible but globally invalid predictions in ASTE.

entry.title: Visualize Cyclical Structure in Llama Model

author.name: Talib Mirza

entry.summary: This post presents an interactive tool for generating and visualizing 3D cyclical and smooth geometric structures in Llama-3-8b activations at arbitrary layers. It explores geometric structure in concept representations beyond the linear representation hypothesis.

entry.title: Gait2Hip-60: A Unified Deep Learning Benchmark for Predicting Hip Muscle Forces and Joint Moments from Multi-Cadence Gait Kinematics

author.name: Jiaqi Zhang, Ji Hou, Qing Sun, Xianzhi Gao, Bo Huo

entry.summary: Gait2Hip-60 is a deep learning benchmark for predicting hip muscle forces and joint moments directly from lower-limb gait kinematics, avoiding time-consuming musculoskeletal simulation. It compares LSTM, Transformer, and Mamba models on data from 60 adults across multiple cadences under a unified protocol.

entry.title: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Zero-Shot Topic Classification: A Multi-Strategy Comparative Study

author.name: Shahana Akter, Yatharth Vohra, Ankita Shukla, Souvika Sarkar

entry.summary: This study presents a zero-shot multi-label topic classification framework and investigates how per-article knowledge graph augmentation affects performance. It compares eight method variants (article-only, keyword-enhanced, with self-consistency, and graph-augmented) across fifteen datasets.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Evaluating Efficiency, Robustness and Explainability in Deep Learning for Malaria Diagnosis

author.name: Olivier Kanamugire, Kerol Djoumessi

entry.summary: This study benchmarks four deep learning models for malaria diagnosis on the NLM-Malaria dataset, jointly evaluating accuracy, robustness, and explainability, finding lightweight efficient models match heavier ones with no statistically significant difference. It emphasizes deployment-relevant criteria beyond accuracy for resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: Self-Tuning Regularization for Image Scanning Microscopy

author.name: Sofia Agostoni, Lisa Cuneo, Christian Daniele, Giacomo Garr\'e, Laurent Le, Alessandro Zunino, Giuseppe Vicidomini, Luca Calatroni

entry.summary: Proposes a self-tuning regularization method for image scanning microscopy reconstruction that avoids the noise amplification of Richardson-Lucy early-stopping. Improves super-resolved fluorescence image reconstruction quality.

entry.title: Translation Analytics for Freelancers II: Benchmarking Local LLMs for Confidential Translation Workflows

author.name: Yuri Balashov, Rex VanHorn, Mingxi Xu, Austin Downes

entry.summary: Benchmarks locally runnable LLMs (via Ollama) for confidential offline translation across four language directions on 1000+ sentences. Provides practical evaluation methods for freelance translators with privacy constraints.

entry.title: XOResNet: Exclusive-OR Meta-Residuals Facilitate Deep Spiking Neural Networks Learning

author.name: Jianfang Wu, Junsong Wang

entry.summary: XOResNet introduces an OR-ADD shortcut connection and exclusive-OR meta-residuals to address spike redundancy and information loss in deep residual spiking neural networks. The design aims to reduce redundant learning while enabling effective deep SNN training.

entry.title: Extracting accent features in spoken Brazilian Portuguese without sociolinguistic labels

author.name: Pedro H. L. Leite, Pedro Benevenuto Valadares and Luiz W. P. Biscainho

entry.summary: This work extracts regional accent features in Brazilian Portuguese using only acoustic labels and a phoneme-based forced aligner, avoiding unreliable sociolinguistic labels. The targeted feature set captures dialectal variance more effectively than utterance embeddings from large self-supervised speech models.

entry.title: A Novel Global Context-aware Deep Neural Network for Enhanced Brain Tumor Segmentation using Magnetic Resonance Images
