entry.summary: Shows that LoRA adaptation can improve target-task performance while degrading pretrained and aligned capabilities, especially when the adaptation distribution differs substantially from the original training distribution. It proposes a plug-and-play, replay-free regularizer that masks the target to balance new learning against forgetting without access to original data.

entry.title: Singularity-aware Optimization via Randomized Geometric Probing: Towards Stable Non-smooth Optimization

author.name: Ruoran Xu, Borong She, Xiaobo Jin and Qiufeng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces S-Adam, an optimizer that stabilizes training in non-smooth loss landscapes by modulating step sizes using a Local Geometric Instability metric estimating the Clarke subdifferential diameter. Targets gradient chattering from ReLU and quantization operators.

entry.title: ReactBench: A Cause-Driven Benchmark for Multimodal Hallucination via Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Shizhe Zhou, Bohan Jia, Kai Wu, Yan Shen, Tongyun Li, Yuyang Wu, and Shaohui Lin

entry.summary: Introduces ReactBench, a cause-driven multimodal hallucination benchmark with an exam-style format and four targeted tasks (relational erasure, counterfactual, etc.) using adversarial images and hallucination-inducing queries. Evaluates underlying causes rather than just hallucination outcomes.

entry.title: CONCAT: Consensus- and Confidence-Driven Ad Hoc Teaming for Efficient LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Ziyang Ma, Dingyi Zhang, Sichu Liang, Jiajia Chu, Pengfei Xia, Hui Zang, Deyu Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces CONCAT, a training-free multi-agent collaboration framework using consensus and confidence-driven ad hoc teaming to cut communication overhead in LLM multi-agent systems. Clusters agents by initial answers without extra training or domain restriction.

entry.title: AgentCVR: Active Multi-Agent Cross-Video Reasoning via Script-Simulated Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yilun Qiu, Jiahe Wang, Cilin Yan, Jiayin Cai, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes AgentCVR, a multi-agent framework treating cross-video reasoning as active evidence acquisition with a Master Agent coordinating Visual and Audio Agents, trained via Script-Simulated RL. Tackles MLLM struggles with evidence distributed across multiple videos.

entry.title: SAFE-Pruner: Semantic Attention-Guided Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Shilin Ma and Chubin Zhang and Changyuan Wang and Yuji Wang and Yue Wu and Zixuan Wang and Jingqi Tian and Zheng Zhu and Yansong Tang

entry.summary: Proposes SAFE-Pruner, a plug-and-play token pruning framework for VLA models that forecasts deep-layer token saliency using future-layer attention cues, exploiting semantic attention consistency across execution steps. Prevents premature removal of tokens needed by deep layers.

entry.title: AMDP: Asynchronous Multi-Directional Pipeline Parallelism for Large-Scale Models Training

author.name: Ling Chen, Houming Wu, Wenjie Yu

entry.summary: Proposes AMDP, asynchronous multi-directional pipeline parallelism that bounds parameter mismatch between forward and backward passes while launching adaptive concurrent pipelines and accumulating gradients to reduce bubbles. Improves convergence over existing asynchronous pipeline approaches for large-model training.

entry.title: Teaching Language Models to Check Grounded Claim Factuality with Human Test-Taking Strategies

author.name: Yuxuan Ye, Raul Santos-Rodriguez, Edwin Simpson

entry.summary: Reformulates grounded claim factuality checking as a true/false reading comprehension task and prompts LLMs with explicit test-taking strategies, cutting token usage by over 80% while matching expensive baselines. It sets a new SOTA on two factuality benchmarks. Useful for efficient RAG fact-checking.

entry.title: LFQ: Logit-aware Final-block Quantization for Boosting the Generation Quality of Low-Bit Quantized LLMs

author.name: Jung Hyun Lee, June Yong Yang, Jungwook Choi, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: LFQ improves low-bit quantized LLM generation quality by including the LM head in block-wise post-training quantization and replacing MSE with a logit-aware objective that aligns the quantized model's token distribution to the full-precision one. It targets degradation on long generation and chain-of-thought. Relevant for accurate low-bit deployment.

entry.title: Evolve as a Team: Collaborative Self-Evolution for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhezheng Hao, Tianfu Wang, Huanshuo Dong, Ziyan Liu, Hong Wang, Xiankun Lin, Qiang Lin, Can Wang, Hande Dong, Jiawei Chen

entry.summary: Meta-Team is an experience-driven framework for collaborative self-evolution of LLM multi-agent systems, preserving each agent's execution context and coordinating post-task improvement to address failures that are hard to eliminate at design time. It tackles credit attribution across interleaved agent chains. Relevant to self-improving agent systems.

entry.title: Towards Localized and Disentangled Knowledge Editing for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Leijiang Gu and Zhen Zeng and Feng Li and Xinjian Gao and Zenglin Shi

entry.summary: LDKE proposes localized and disentangled knowledge editing for multimodal LLMs, formalizing two failure modes (causal misalignment confining edits to specific samples, and feature entanglement causing unintended changes) and providing precise, generalizable edits. It improves editing of outdated multimodal facts. Relevant for maintainable MLLMs.

entry.title: EvoRubric: Self-Evolving Rubric-Driven RL for Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Xin Guan, Xiaomeng Hu, Shen Huang, Zhenyi Wang, Bo Zhang, Zijian Li, Pengjun Xie, Bo Liu, Jiuxin Cao

entry.summary: EvoRubric is a single-policy co-evolutionary RL framework for open-ended generation that unifies response generation and rubric generation in one parameterized policy, alternating between a Reasoner and a Rubric Generator. This removes reliance on static human rubrics or expensive external rubric models. It addresses the core difficulty of rewardless alignment in open-ended tasks.

entry.title: DVSM: Decoder-only View Synthesis Model Done Right

author.name: Cheng Sun, Jaesung Choe, Min-Hung Chen, Ryo Hachiuma, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang

entry.summary: DVSM re-examines large view-synthesis model design and shows a decoder-only architecture representing scenes implicitly as a KV-cache outperforms encoder-decoder variants with fewer parameters at the same rendering complexity. It finds weight sharing between reconstruction and rendering networks improves feature alignment, and adds foundation-model priors and stage-wise patch sizing. The result advances efficiency-quality tradeoffs in novel view synthesis.

entry.title: CLUBench: A Clustering Benchmark

author.name: Feng Xiao, Dazhi Fu, Chris Ding, Jicong Fan

entry.summary: CLUBench is a comprehensive clustering benchmark spanning 24 algorithms across conventional, deep-learning, and foundation-model-based methods, evaluated on 131 tabular, text, and image datasets over roughly 179,000 experiments. It analyzes the impact of hyperparameter tuning, data characteristics, and pretrained embeddings on clustering. The goal is systematic guidance for algorithm selection.

entry.title: Causal Interventions on Continuous Variables: A Case Study on Verb Bias in Steering Vectors for In-Context Learning

author.name: Zhenghao Herbert Zhou, R. Thomas McCoy, Robert Frank

entry.summary: This work introduces a method for causal intervention on continuous variables in LLM representations, localizing a low-dimensional direction for a graded target and editing activations toward counterfactual values, applied to verb bias (which syntactic structures follow a verb). It shows verb bias is causally represented in steering vectors and that counterfactual edits systematically shift in-context behavior. It extends causal interpretability beyond discrete features.

entry.title: Accelerating Constrained Decoding with Token Space Compression

author.name: Michael Sullivan, Alexander Koller

entry.summary: CFGzip is an offline technique for compressing the token search space in context-free-grammar-constrained decoding, drastically reducing per-step overhead that grows with the full vocabulary and complex grammars. It reports latency reductions up to two orders of magnitude and total constrained-generation speedups up to 7.5x with a state-of-the-art grammar engine. The work targets the cost of structured/constrained LLM output.

entry.title: Masked Diffusion Modeling for Anomaly Detection

author.name: Lixing Zhang, Yuchen Liang, Liyan Xie

entry.summary: MaskDiff-AD uses masked diffusion models trained only on nominal data to detect anomalies in categorical, mixed-type, and discrete sequence data by scoring reconstruction difficulty of randomly masked coordinates. It addresses an underexplored area where standard anomaly methods struggle. The forward-only design operates directly on discrete data.

entry.title: Striding Across Reynolds Numbers: Representation Geometry in Neural PDE Generalisation

author.name: Jianing Shi

entry.summary: This work investigates cross-Reynolds-number generalization in neural PDE solvers, finding that representation geometry, not just the update rule, dominates performance, and proposes ConvAE-Relay that matches states in a source-trained latent space and borrows dynamics, achieving low error without target-regime fitting. Ablations isolate matching quality as dominant. It reframes neural PDE generalization around representation geometry.

entry.title: Before the Shutter: Aesthetic and Actionable Portrait Photography Planning in 3D Scenes

author.name: Ruixiang Jiang, Chang Wen Chen

entry.summary: This work introduces 3D aesthetic portrait planning, generating pose, camera, lighting, and exposure plans before capture that produce compelling portraits while satisfying geometric and photometric feasibility in a 3D scene, via a Photographic Scene Graph. It shifts focus from 2D post-production to pre-capture planning. A novel task formulation in computational photography.

entry.title: ARC's "Outperforming Random Sampling" explained

author.name: mfatt

entry.summary: An intuitive explainer of ARC's Competing with Random Sampling work, which proposes a clear formal goal for mechanistic interpretability defined by what explanations are actually used for rather than the explanations themselves. The author argues this reframing targets key weaknesses in building a science of AI safety and could enable scalable/automated interpretability.

entry.title: Learning to Extrapolate to New Tasks: A Relational Approach to Task Extrapolation

author.name: Adam Ousherovitch and Yixin Wang

entry.summary: The Relational Task Extrapolator learns transformations between tasks during training and applies them to relate known tasks to unseen ones at test time, enabling systematic out-of-distribution task extrapolation. It targets the persistent failure of foundation models to generalize beyond training task ranges.

entry.title: DeepTrust: Multi-Step Classification through Dissimilar Adversarial Representations for Robust Android Malware Detection

author.name: Daniel Pulido-Cort\'azar, Daniel Gibert, Felip Many\`a

entry.summary: DeepTrust is a cascade-based metaheuristic arranging classifiers into an ordered sequence with conditionally activated decisions for robust Android malware detection, winning first place at the 2025 SaTML robust malware competition. It substantially outperformed competitors under feature-space evasion attacks.

entry.title: MechELK: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Eliciting Latent Knowledge in Large Language Models

author.name: Ji-jun Park, Soo-joon Choi, Jiwon Jeong, Taeyang Yoon, Ju-Wan Lee

entry.summary: MechELK is a three-stage framework (Locate via sparse autoencoders, then extract) that bridges mechanistic interpretability and latent-knowledge elicitation to extract hidden factual and reasoning knowledge from LLM internal representations beyond contrastive methods like CCS. It aims to recover latent knowledge for complex multi-step reasoning.

entry.title: Micro-Macro Retrieval: Reducing Long-Form Hallucination in Large Language Models

author.name: Yujie Feng, Jian Li, Zhihan Zhou, Pengfei Xu, Yujia Zhang, Xiaoyu Li, Xiaohui Zhou, Alan Zhao, Xi Chen, Xiao-Ming Wu

entry.summary: Micro-Macro Retrieval (M2R) is a retrieve-while-generate framework that reduces long-form hallucination by combining coarse macro-level evidence with fine-grained micro retrieval to keep key information close to model outputs. It exploits the observation that factual accuracy increases when key evidence is near the generated text.

entry.title: Context Distillation as Latent Memory Management

author.name: Ziyang Zheng, Zeju Li, Xiangyu Wen, Jianyuan Zhong, Junhua Huang, Lei Chen, Mingxuan Yuan, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: Formulates context distillation as a latent memory management problem, distilling each context into an independent LoRA adapter to form a modular, retrievable memory bank with query routing and a self-gating activation mechanism. It adds cache sharing to reduce inference overhead.

entry.title: SafeRx-Agent: A Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Safe and Explainable Medication Recommendation

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Hanwei Wu, Zhenghan Tai, Sicheng Lyu, Qincheng Lu, Ziyu Zhao, Jijun Chi, Jingrui Tian, Xiao-Wen Chang, Ziyang Song

entry.summary: SafeRx-Agent is a knowledge-grounded multi-agent framework for medication recommendation using fourth-level ATC code generation with patient context, external clinical knowledge, and safety verification for explainable, traceable prescriptions. It introduces a fine-grained recommendation setting that avoids risk overestimation from coarse drug categories.

entry.title: Pocket-Dentist: On-Device Dental Image Understanding via Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Kai Bian, Xucheng Guo, Bin Chen, Lingyan Ruan, Yiran Shen, Ting Dang, Hong Jia

entry.summary: Pocket-Dentist is an efficiency-aware benchmark for on-device dental multimodal QA spanning ~1,159 patients and seven metrics, finding that compact 2B VLMs can outperform larger ones in accuracy at lower cost. It supports privacy-preserving clinical prescreening.

entry.title: Enhancing Factuality through Consensus and Consistency in Summarization Using Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding

author.name: Riza Setiawan Soetedjo, Yusuke Sakai, Hidetaka Kamigaito, Jingun Kwon, Manabu Okumura, Taro Watanabe

entry.summary: ConSUM improves summarization factuality by reranking candidates using both consistency to the source and consensus among candidates via Minimum Bayes Risk decoding. It addresses unreliable summaries from source-only reranking.

entry.title: FinGuard: Detecting Financial Regulatory Non-Compliance in LLM Interactions

author.name: Huaixia Dou, Jie Zhu, Minghao Wu, Shuo Jiang, Junhui Li, Lifan Guo, Feng Chen, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a regulation-driven pipeline that induces a financial compliance risk taxonomy directly from regulatory documents and synthesizes grounded training data without predefined violation categories. It releases FinGuard-Bench, a benchmark for detecting financial regulatory non-compliance in LLM interactions with query- and response-level labels.

entry.title: SkillBrew: Multi-Objective Curation of Skill Banks for LLM Agents

author.name: Wentao Hu, Zhendong Chu, Yiming Zhang, Junda Wu, Ming Jin, Xiangyu Zhao, Yilei Shao, Yanfeng Wang, Qingsong Wen

entry.summary: Formulates skill-bank curation for retrieval-augmented LLM agents as a constrained multi-objective problem balancing utility, diversity, and query coverage, rather than append-only growth. SkillBrew solves it as Pareto-aware optimization under a utility constraint via a bi-level procedure to prune redundant or harmful skills.

entry.title: Kronecker Embeddings: Byte-Level Structured Token Representations for Parameter-Efficient Language Models

author.name: Rohan Shravan

entry.summary: Introduces Kronecker Embeddings, a deterministic byte-level character-position factorization that replaces the large input embedding table with a fixed encoder plus a single learned projection, eliminating 91-94% of input-side trainable parameters at frontier scale while staying BPE-compatible. Probes show trained embeddings cluster typographic variants, a behavior Kronecker avoids at the embedding layer.

entry.title: Opt-Verifier: Unleashing the Power of LLMs for Optimization Modeling via Dual-Side Verification

author.name: Haoyang Liu, Jie Wang, Boxuan Niu, Xiongwei Han, Yian Xu, Mingxuan Ye, Zijie Geng, Fangzhou Zhu, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: Introduces Opt-Verifier, an LLM framework that improves optimization modeling accuracy through dual-side verification checking both model structure and solution validity. Addresses correctness verification gaps in automated operations research modeling.

entry.title: VLAConf: Calibrated Task-Success Confidence for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Dehao Huang, Aoxiang Gu, Chengjie Zhang, Bolin Zou, Wenlong Dong, Zilang Cen, Yue Wang, and Hong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes VLAConf, a one-class discriminative confidence framework for calibrated task-success prediction in VLA models that works across continuous and discrete action spaces without repeated sampling. Improves efficiency and cross-architecture generalizability for failure anticipation.

entry.title: VikingMem: A Memory Base Management System for Stateful LLM-based Applications

author.name: Jiajie Fu, Junwen Chen, Mengzhao Wang, Aoxiang He, Maojia Sheng, Xiangyu Ke, Yifan Zhu, Yunjun Gao

entry.summary: Introduces VikingMem and the Memory Base concept, a data management paradigm for stateful LLM applications featuring selective high-value extraction, statefulness, and evolution to overcome finite context windows. Aims for generalizability across diverse downstream tasks beyond chatbots.

entry.title: EXACT-MPPI: Exact Signed-Distance Navigation for Arbitrary-Footprint Robots from Point Clouds via Path Integral Control

author.name: Chen Peng, Zhikang Ge, Wenwu Lu, Haiming Gao, Stavros Vougioukas, Peng Wei

entry.summary: Presents EXACT-MPPI, a training-free local navigation framework embedding an analytic exact signed-distance evaluator into MPPI control to handle arbitrary non-convex robot footprints directly from point clouds, without intermediate map representations. Enables safe navigation in tight clearance.

entry.title: PhAIL: A Real-Robot VLA Benchmark and Distributional Methodology

author.name: Sergey Arkhangelskiy

entry.summary: PhAIL is an open real-robot benchmark on a Franka FR3 introducing a distributional evaluation methodology using time-to-success CDFs and Human-Relative Throughput with bootstrap confidence intervals, improving on binary success rates. It addresses unreliable small-N VLA evaluation. Valuable for rigorous robot-policy benchmarking.

entry.title: Multi-Legal-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Legal Reasoning Across Jurisdictions, Languages, and Legal Traditions

author.name: Volodymyr Ovcharov

entry.summary: Multi-Legal-Bench is the first cross-jurisdictional legal reasoning benchmark evaluating identical tasks across six countries, four language families, and 134 million court decisions on five structured tasks. It enables genuine cross-lingual legal comparison and evaluates seven frontier LLMs. Valuable for multilingual legal NLP.

entry.title: Why Specialist Models Still Matter: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Paradigm for Medical Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Yanan Wang, Shuaicong Hu, Jian Liu, Guohui Zhou, Aiguo Wang, Cuiwei Yang

entry.summary: Argues against monolithic medical foundation models and proposes HetMedAgent, a heterogeneous multi-agent framework combining generalist LLMs, domain specialist models, and clinicians with conflict-aware evidence fusion and uncertainty-based intervention triggering. Experiments on three clinical decision tasks show synergy benefits. Relevant to clinical AI system design.

entry.title: Certified Policy Optimisation for Nested Causal Bandits via PAC-Bayes Risk

author.name: Tim Woydt and Paul-David Zuercher

entry.summary: Formalizes Nested Contextual Causal Bandits, a hierarchical SCM where each decision level sets the next level's context distribution, and proposes Nested Causal Thompson Sampling with a causal PAC-Bayesian excess-risk bound certifying deployment policies from historic off-policy data. It addresses causal coupling across decision timescales. A theoretical contribution to causal sequential decision-making.

entry.title: Dissecting the Black Box: Circuit-Level Analysis of LLM Vulnerability Detection

author.name: Syafiq Al Atiiq, Chun Zhou, Christian Gehrmann

entry.summary: This paper applies mechanistic interpretability (Circuit Tracer on Gemma-2-2b) to LLM software-vulnerability detection over 472 C/C++ samples, finding the model relies primarily on attention heads that recognize safe coding patterns and labels code vulnerable when these safety detectors fail to activate. It identifies specific early-layer attention components driving this behavior. The work reveals that detection works by absence of safety signals rather than direct vulnerability recognition.

entry.title: DocRetriever: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Multimodal Document Retrieval with Comprehensive Benchmark

author.name: Ruofan Hu, Menghui Zhu, Jieming Zhu, Bo Chen, Shengyang Xu, Minjie Hong, Xiaoda Yang, Sashuai Zhou, Li Tang, Tao Jin, and Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: DocRetriever is a plug-and-play framework for multimodal document retrieval that augments dense visual embeddings with structurally salient information and reduces reliance on supervised rerankers, paired with a comprehensive benchmark. It targets generalization and evaluation gaps in retrieving from tables, figures, and layouts. The benchmark contribution is notable.

entry.title: Who Am I? History-Aware Profiles for Student Simulation in Tutoring Dialogues

author.name: Zhangqi Duan, Shuyan Huang, Alexander Scarlatos, Jaewook Lee, Simon Woodhead, Andrew Lan

entry.summary: This work introduces history-conditioned student simulation, where an LLM profile generator summarizes a student's past interactions and a simulator predicts dialogue turns conditioned on that profile. It grounds tutoring student role-play in learning history rather than within-dialogue context only. It supports better tutor model evaluation and training.

entry.title: Adaptive Targeted Dynamic Chunking for Tokenization-Free Hierarchical Model

author.name: Thang Dang, Akira Nakagawa, Kenichi Kobayashi, Koichi Shirahata

entry.summary: ATDC is a byte-compression control mechanism using curriculum learning to progressively adjust compression ratios in tokenization-free hierarchical models, improving dynamic chunking effectiveness. It addresses optimization of compression ratio in byte-level architectures. It targets the emerging tokenizer-free LLM paradigm.

entry.title: CCS: Clinical Consensus Selection for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Xi Zhang, Yingshu Li, Zaiqiao Meng, Jake Lever, Edmond S. L. Ho

entry.summary: CCS is a decoder-agnostic inference-time selection framework for radiology report generation that samples multiple candidate reports and selects the clinically strongest via consensus, observing that default decoding often misses better candidates in the pool. It improves report quality without retraining. It targets an overlooked inference-time bottleneck.

entry.title: IP-Adapter Is All You Need: Towards Fine-Tuning-Free Diffusion-Based Talking Face Generation

author.name: Hao Wu, Xiangyang Luo, Hao Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Yi Zhang, and Jinwei Wang

entry.summary: This work proposes a fine-tuning-free talking face generation paradigm using pretrained Stable Diffusion and IP-Adapter, mining lip-related semantics from IP-Adapter's visual embeddings and adding three trainable parameter-light modules to address identity drift, sync errors, and temporal instability. It avoids large audiovisual datasets and costly fine-tuning. Relevant for accessible avatar generation.

entry.title: Towards Continuous-time Causal Foundation Models

author.name: Dennis Thumm, Ruben Wiedemann, Ying Chen

entry.summary: This paper develops continuous-time causal foundation models by formulating causal Prior-data Fitted Networks as stochastic differential equations and proposing a continuity criterion ensuring trajectory laws are invariant to observation schedules. It advances the emerging area of amortized causal inference for irregularly sampled time series.

entry.title: CB-SLICE: Concept-Based Interpretable Error Slice Discovery

author.name: Yael Konforti, Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga, Elaf Almahmoud, Mateja Jamnik

entry.summary: CB-SLICE leverages Concept Bottleneck Models to discover error slices that are directly tied to the model's inference process via human-understandable concepts, rather than approximating error sources externally. It improves interpretability of systematic model failures for debugging and bias mitigation.

entry.title: What are They Thinking? Delineation, Probing and Tracking of Concepts in LLMs

author.name: Mohamed Abdelwahab, Michelle Yu Collins, Sihan Chen, Yi Cheng Zhao, Zafarullah Mahmood, Jiading Zhu, Soliman Ali, Jonathan Rose

entry.summary: This paper develops low-cost linear probes to detect the presence or absence of many concepts within LLM embeddings, demonstrating the key tasks of careful concept delineation, probe training, and tracking what a model is thinking about. It aims toward scalable monitoring of LLM internal concepts during operation.

entry.title: Benchmarking Open-Source Safety Guard Models: A Comprehensive Evaluation

author.name: Reetu Raj Harsh, Bhaskarjit Sarmah, Stefano Pasquali

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks 14 open-source safety guard models on a curated 79,331-sample dataset spanning 8 NIST AI risk categories, emphasizing recall as the critical metric and finding that smaller models like a 4B Qwen Guard can perform surprisingly well. It provides a comprehensive comparison for content moderation.

entry.title: GPF-LiveNews: A Streaming Evaluation Protocol for Group-Conditioned Framing in Large Language Models

author.name: Mohd Ariful Haque, Fahad Rahman, Kishor Datta Gupta, Roy George

entry.summary: Proposes GPF-LiveNews, a streaming evaluation protocol that audits group-conditioned framing in open-ended LLM outputs by continuously expanding fresh news anchors across identity labels and prompt families. It addresses the limitation that static bias benchmarks cannot capture how models frame newly emerging events.

entry.title: Echoes within the Reasoning: Stealthy and Effective Watermarking via Chain of Thought

author.name: Jiacheng Lu, Yiming Li, Tao Song, Weijian Wang, Wenjie Qu, Haibing Guan, Jiaheng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes BiCoT, a black-box watermarking framework that embeds ownership signals into the internal geometry of chain-of-thought reasoning traces by aligning high-saliency anchors with a private signature subspace. It aims to preserve reasoning fidelity while remaining robust to model theft and representation drift.

entry.title: First head-to-head comparison of agentic AI applied to the analysis of simulated data of the Einstein Telescope

author.name: Gianluca Inguglia

entry.summary: Reports a head-to-head comparison of two agentic AI systems (Claude Code and Codex) autonomously executing an end-to-end gravitational-wave data analysis pipeline for the Einstein Telescope, including manuscript generation. Both agents received identical specifications and compute under different injection regimes.

entry.title: When LLM Reward Design Fails: Diagnostic-Driven Refinement for Sparse Structured RL

author.name: Youting Wang, Yuan Tang, Bowen Liu, Xuan Liu and Dingyan Shang

entry.summary: Argues that LLM-generated reward shaping for sparse, structured RL tasks is better treated as iterative debugging than one-shot generation, identifying dominant failure modes like reward flooding and semantic/API misunderstanding. It proposes diagnostic-driven iterative refinement, dramatically improving success on MiniGrid tasks.

entry.title: Neural Scaling Laws for Jet Generation

author.name: Oz Amram, Darius A. Faroughy, Tjarko Gerdes, Anna Hallin, Gregor Kasieczka, Michael Kr\"amer, Humberto Reyes-Gonzalez, David Shih

entry.summary: Provides the first study of neural scaling laws for particle jet generation, replicating logarithmic model-size scaling behavior and evaluating physical fidelity via sliced Wasserstein distances of physical quantities. It is relevant both as a foundation-model pretraining objective and as in-situ physics simulation.

entry.title: The Trust Paradox: How CS Researchers Engage LLM Leaderboards

author.name: Pouya Sadeghi, Anamaria Crisan, Jimmy Lin

entry.summary: Through semi-structured interviews with eight CS researchers, this qualitative study finds a near-universal trust paradox: researchers deeply distrust LLM leaderboard rankings yet still use them as rough decision aids, relying more on peer networks for model selection. It examines how leaderboards actually shape research practice.

entry.title: GAP3D: Generative Alignment of VLM Latents to Patch-Level Embeddings for 3D Generation

author.name: Polytimi Anna Gkotsi, Andrii Zadaianchuk, Mohammad Mahdi Derakhshani

entry.summary: Proposes GAP3D, a modular diffusion-based approach that aligns VLM-generated latents directly to the dense patch-level feature space of a pretrained image encoder, enabling a frozen generative model to use a VLM as a prompt encoder while preserving spatial structure for 3D generation. It avoids expensive end-to-end training and large-scale 3D data.

entry.title: When Models Disagree: Rethinking LLM Evaluation for Public Comment Analysis

author.name: Aisha Najera, Alvin Moon, Vedant Srinivasan, Rajesh Veeraraghavan

entry.summary: Proposes an Interpretive Audit Pipeline that treats multi-model disagreement among LLMs as a diagnostic of interpretive complexity, directing human review toward genuinely ambiguous public comments in federal rulemaking. Analyzing 1,260 comments across four LLMs, it finds inter-model thematic divergence exceeds within-model prompt variation.

entry.title: Structured Prompt Optimization Meets Reinforcement Learning for Global and Local Interpretability over Complex Text

author.name: Tianyang Zhou, Wenbo Chen, Pierre Jinghong Liang, Leman Akoglu

entry.summary: eXTC is an explainable text classifier built in three stages: learning a natural-language rulebook via structured prompt optimization, distilling SOP-grounded reasoning into a compact model, then expanding reasoning via reinforcement learning. It aims to combine interpretability with scalable, performant classification.

entry.title: A Minimal Bifurcation Model of Load Imbalance in a Softmax Mixture-of-Experts Router

author.name: O. M. Kiselev (Innopolis University, Innopolis, Russia)

entry.summary: This work presents a minimal dynamical model of softmax routing in a two-expert mixture-of-experts layer, deriving a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation that explains load imbalance and a cusp catastrophe under external asymmetry. It offers theoretical insight into expert collapse via dynamical systems.

entry.title: Stochastic Lifting for Generating Trajectories of Stochastic Physical Systems

author.name: Jules Berman, Tobias Blickhan, Benjamin Peherstorfer

entry.summary: Stochastic Lifting generates trajectories of stochastic physical systems by attaching independent high-dimensional random labels to state transitions and fitting a transition map via standard regression, avoiding mean-collapse on finite samples. It enables sampling multiple plausible next states at inference.

entry.title: Deep Psychovisual Image Representations

author.name: Wendi Ma, Aryaman Sharma, Wei Dai, Shekhar S. Chandra

entry.summary: Proposes Deep Visual Coding, a learned frequency-domain representation inspired by 1990s perceptual image codes, enabling psychovisual-style intermediate abstractions in deep vision models for more interpretable decision-making. It bridges psychovisual theory and deep learning.

entry.title: Decentralized LLM-Driven Coordination of Acoustic Robots for Contactless Object Manipulation

author.name: Yingying Wang, Narsimlu Kemsaram, and Sriram Subramanian

entry.summary: Presents a decentralized framework coordinating ultrasonic phased-array acoustic robots for contactless object manipulation via natural language, converting spoken instructions into multi-robot task plans using Whisper, LLM parsing, and JSON-based distributed scheduling. It bridges LLMs with distributed acoustic robotics.

entry.title: Orthogonal Negative Guidance in Attention Feature Space for Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Jungmin Ko, Jungwon Park, Jimyeong Kim, Changin Choi, Wonseok Lee, Wonjong Rhee

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free negative guidance method for text-to-image transformers that orthogonalizes negative-prompt attention features against positive ones and subtracts only the orthogonal component. This suppresses unwanted concepts while preserving image quality better than prompt negation or post-hoc editing.

entry.title: AliMark: Enhancing Robustness of Sentence-Level Watermarking Against Text Paraphrasing

author.name: Yuexin Li, Wenjie Qu, Linyu Wu, Yulin Chen, Yufei He, Tri Cao, Bryan Hooi, Jiaheng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes AliMark, which reformulates sentence-level text watermarking as a bit-sequence encoding and alignment problem robust to sentence splitting and merging by strong paraphrasers. A two-stage detection generates multiple restructured variants and adaptively aligns extracted bits to a secret sequence to minimize alignment cost.

entry.title: A Full-Pipeline Framework for Evaluating Membership Inference Attacks in Machine Learning

author.name: Ding Chen, Xinwen Cheng, Xuyang Zhong, Xinping Chen, Xiaolin Huang, Chen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a full-pipeline framework for evaluating membership inference attacks systematically across data, architectures, algorithms, and post-training modules, beyond isolated benchmark settings. It aims to characterize how context affects MIA efficacy for privacy auditing and unlearning so practitioners avoid benchmark-only conclusions.

entry.title: VitalAgent: A Tool-Augmented Agent for Reactive and Proactive Physiological Monitoring over Wearable Health Data

author.name: Di Zhu, Yu Yvonne Wu, Hong Jia, Aaqib Saeed, Vassilis Kostakos, Ting Dang

entry.summary: Proposes VitalAgent, a tool-augmented agentic framework for ECG/PPG wearable health that supports both reactive question answering and proactive monitoring via a longitudinal physiological memory and a reasoning interface that computes over raw signals. It introduces VitalBench, a longitudinal monitoring benchmark of 1,862 QA pairs.

entry.title: Quotient DAGs for Off-Policy Evaluation:Forward-Flow Importance Sampling and Exact Slate Propensities

author.name: Ziwen Xie, Shaowen Xiang, Hongyu He and Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a quotient-DAG view of off-policy evaluation that merges generation histories equivalent for evaluation, reducing nuisance variance when the reward ignores irrelevant generation details such as slate ordering. It enables forward-flow importance sampling and exact unordered slate propensities without summing over all generation orders.

entry.title: Source-Grounded Semantic Reinforcement Learning for Low-Resource Target-Language Generation

author.name: Zeli Su, Ziyin Zhang, Zewei Pan, Zhou Liu, Dingcheng Huang, Dehan Li, Zhankai Xu, Longfei Zheng, Xiaolu Zhang, Jun Zhou, and Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Source-Grounded Semantic Reinforcement Learning, which converts abundant high-resource source-language monolingual data into cross-lingual semantic supervision for low-resource target generation using a reference-free reward from a cross-lingual reranker. It diagnoses severe verbosity-based reward hacking and adds a lightweight parallel-data recovery stage to fix it.

entry.title: ESAM++: Efficient Online 3D Perception on the Edge

author.name: Qin Liu, Lavisha Aggarwal, Saptarashmi Bandyopadhyay, Vikas Bahirwani, Marc Niethammer, Ehsan Adeli, Andrea Colaco

entry.summary: Proposes ESAM++, a lightweight alternative to EmbodiedSAM for online 3D scene perception on edge devices, replacing the computationally expensive 3D sparse UNet that dominates inference time. It targets real-time, privacy-preserving 3D instance segmentation without GPU acceleration for robotics and AR/VR.

entry.title: Xetrieval: Mechanistically Explaining Dense Retrieval

author.name: Zhixin Cai, Jun Bai, Yang Liu, Jiaqi Li, Yichi Zhang, Taichuan Li, Zhuofan Chen, Zixia Jia, Zilong Zheng, Wenge Rong

entry.summary: Proposes Xetrieval, an embedding-level mechanistic framework for explaining dense retrieval beyond surface lexical matches, including a lightweight reasoning internalizer that approximates chain-of-thought directly in embedding space in a single forward pass. It aims to expose the latent factors shaping retrieval scores.

entry.title: DeepSurvey: Enhancing Analytical Depth and Citation Reliability in Automated Survey Generation

author.name: Ziyue Yang, Da Ma, Hanqi Li, Zijian Wang, Tiancheng Huang, Zijian Hu, Chenrun Wang, Yunzhe Zhang, Xiaobao Wu, Kai Yu, Lu Chen

entry.summary: Presents DeepSurvey, an agentic system for automated survey generation that extracts structured keynotes from full-text papers, models cross-paper relationships through clustering and comparative analysis, and integrates code-repository analysis to recover implementation details. It improves citation reliability via citation-graph expansion with hybrid filtering instead of post-hoc grounding.

entry.title: GUITestScape: Towards Open-set Evaluation on Exploratory GUI Testing

author.name: Xiaoyi Chen, Yifei Gao, Yang Xu, Xingxing Song, Yi Zhang, Jitao Sang

entry.summary: Presents GUITestScape, an interactive benchmark of 61 Android apps with 508 defects spanning interaction and display types, plus GUIJudge for open-set evaluation of exploratory GUI testing agents. Moves beyond single end-state defect annotation.

entry.title: Battery-Sim-Agent: Leveraging LLM-Agent for Inverse Battery Parameter Estimation

author.name: Jiawei Chen, Xiaofan Gui, Shikai Fang, Shengyu Tao, Shun Zheng, Weiqing Liu, Jiang Bian

entry.summary: Presents Battery-Sim-Agent, an LLM agent in closed loop with a high-fidelity battery simulator that reframes inverse parameter estimation as a physics-grounded reasoning task. Improves sample efficiency over black-box optimization for battery digital twins.

entry.title: DLM-SWAI: Steering Diffusion Language Models Before They Unmask

author.name: Hyeseon An, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: Proposes DLM-SWAI, a training-free steering method for diffusion language models that biases token distributions at each denoising step using precomputed token-level style scores. Enables controllable generation without auxiliary models or retraining.

entry.title: NICE: A Theory-Grounded Diagnostic Benchmark for Social Intelligence of LLMs

author.name: Yunjin Qi, Zhaojun Jiang, Xuan Wu, Hanxi Pan, Yixuan Wang, Yanfang Liu, Xiang Ji, Churu Yu, Chunyuan Zheng, Yingze Chen, Jie He, Liuqing Chen, Zaifeng Gao

entry.summary: NICE is a theory-grounded diagnostic benchmark for LLM social intelligence built on a psychometrically validated framework of 4 categories and 11 dimensions. It enables fine-grained diagnosis rather than aggregate scoring. Relevant as LLMs are deployed in emotional and customer-facing roles.

entry.title: EMAG: Differentiable 4D Gaussian Mixture Splatting for EEG Spatial Super-Resolution

author.name: Alex Lazarovich, Ofir Itzhak Shahar, Gur Elkin, Ohad Ben-Shahar

entry.summary: EMAG reconstructs high-density EEG signals from sparse low-density electrodes using a differentiable mixture of anisotropic 4D space-time Gaussians as a renderable forward model. It targets cheaper, faster EEG spatial super-resolution for clinical and research accessibility. Creative cross-application of Gaussian splatting ideas to neuroimaging.

entry.title: HTAM: Hierarchical Transition-Attended Memory for Operator Optimization

author.name: Yining Zhang, Mingyang Yi, Chen Wang, Xuwen Xiang, Tianhe Jia, Zedong Dan, Chengqing Zong, and Yue Wang

entry.summary: HTAM is a coarse-to-fine hierarchical memory framework for LLM-based GPU kernel/operator optimization, organizing optimization experience at the right granularity via a hierarchical transition graph. It tackles the granularity mismatch between reusable hints and actionable detailed memories. Relevant to automated high-performance code generation.

entry.title: MARS Policy: Multimodality Only When It Matters

author.name: Jindou Jia, Tuo An, Yuxuan Hu, Gen Li, Jingliang Li, Bohan Hou, Xiangyu Chen, Jiaqi Bai, Bofan Lyu, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: MARS Policy adaptively invokes stochastic multimodality only in robotic task phases where behavioral diversity is beneficial, reverting to efficient deterministic learning otherwise, reducing training complexity and improving inference efficiency in imitation learning. It targets the overhead of generative policies. Relevant for efficient robot manipulation policies.

entry.title: Inferring Code Correctness from Specification

author.name: Tambon Florian, Papadakis Mike

entry.summary: TRAILS grounds LLM reasoning about code correctness with concrete input-output pairs, generating diverse test inputs via specification-based category partitioning, executing them, and prompting LLMs to assess results, avoiding costly dynamic consensus and bias-prone static reasoning. It targets validating LLM-generated code. Relevant for trustworthy automated code generation.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Adaptive Multimodal Gating for Whole-Brain fMRI Encoding

author.name: Abdulkadir Gokce, Badr AlKhamissi, Martin Schrimpf

entry.summary: MIRAGE predicts whole-brain fMRI responses to naturalistic audiovisual stimuli using an omni-modal foundation backbone with adaptive feature gating across layers, plus a transformer brain encoder and subject-specific linear heads. It reports state-of-the-art brain encoding by jointly integrating visual, auditory, and linguistic information. The work connects multimodal foundation models to neural prediction.

entry.title: MELD: Mel-Spectrogram-Based Speech Language Modeling with Discrete Latent Variables

author.name: Sung-Lin Yeh, Wei Zhou, Gil Keren, Duc Le, Zhong Meng, Hao Tang, Jay Mahadeokar, Ozlem Kalinli, Alexandre Mourachko

entry.summary: MELD introduces a discrete latent variable model over mel spectrograms that jointly optimizes the encoder and the speech language model, rather than using separately trained encoders. Joint optimization improves zero-shot TTS and STT over codec-based and other mel baselines and reduces issues like prolonged silence and word omission. The work targets end-to-end alignment of representation and downstream objective.

entry.title: Honeyval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for LLM-powered HTTP Honeypots

author.name: Mark Vero, Fabian Kaczmarczyck, Ivan Petrov, Ilia Shumailov, Jamie Hayes, Niels Heinen, Tianqi Fan, Luca Invernizzi, Martin Vechev

entry.summary: Honeyval is a comprehensive, scalable, and reproducible evaluation framework for LLM-powered HTTP honeypots, addressing limitations of fixed-command similarity measurement, manual testing, and real-world deployment that are non-scalable or unrepresentative. It supports varied attacker and honeypot configurations and representative practical attacks. The framework standardizes honeypot evaluation during development.

entry.title: Improving Adversarial Robustness of Attribution via Implicit Regularization

author.name: Amir Mehrpanah, Matteo Gamba, and Hossein Azizpour

entry.summary: This work shows that adversarial robustness of attributions can arise implicitly from standard SGD learning dynamics, motivated theoretically by connections between parameter-space and input-space curvature, validated across architectures, datasets, and attribution methods with negligible overhead. It contrasts with costly explicit regularization and proves such gains often fail to transfer to softmax attention-based attribution due to entropy constraints. The findings clarify when robust explanations come for free.

entry.title: EarlyTom: Early Token Compression Completes Fast Video Understanding

author.name: Hesong Wang, Xin Jin, Lu Lu, Chenhaowen Li, Jian Chen, Qiang Liu, Huan Wang

entry.summary: EarlyTom compresses visual tokens inside the vision encoder rather than only after prefilling, reducing time-to-first-token for video LLMs while keeping accuracy. It targets a previously unoptimized portion of the inference pipeline. The work matters for practical efficient video understanding deployment.

entry.title: REPOT: Recoverable Program-of-Thought via Checkpoint Repair

author.name: Parsa Mazaheri

entry.summary: RePoT augments one-shot Program-of-Thought planning with deterministic verified replay that walks a plan to its first invalid transition, then resumes with a single LLM call from the verified prefix. It improves success rates with minimal extra cost on a puzzle benchmark and reveals a capability-scaling pattern. The checkpoint-repair idea is the contribution.

entry.title: Anchorless Diversification for Parallel LLM Ideation

author.name: Fares Nabil Ibrahim, Nafis Saami Azad, Raiyan Abdul Baten

entry.summary: This paper studies inference-time controls for diversifying parallel LLM idea pools in creative tasks, comparing anchorless methods (independent generation, semantic direction stratification) against seed-anchor baselines. It finds population-referential divergent instructions are a strong low-cost baseline and semantic direction stratification is stronger. It informs efficient creative ideation with LLMs.

entry.title: SAHG: Sector-Anisotropic Hyperbolic Graph Model for Social Bot Detection

author.name: Hanning Lu, Yingguang Yang, Jinwei Su, Yang Liu, Zhaoqian Yao, Yaoming Li, Taoran Liang, Ziyi Zhang, Ran Ran, Kefu Xu, Bin Chong

entry.summary: SAHG introduces a sector-anisotropic hyperbolic graph model for detecting LLM-driven social bots by exploiting relational patterns that content-based detection can no longer catch. It addresses limitations of fixed-curvature hyperbolic models and unreliable forged connections. Relevant for combating AI-generated coordinated influence campaigns.

entry.title: Knowing What to Solve Before How: Preplan Empowered LLM Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Shaojie Wang, Liang Zhang

entry.summary: PPC introduces a preplan stage before planning and chain-of-thought, adding explicit problem-understanding (problem type, applicable tools, foreseeable pitfalls) to the question-plan-CoT paradigm for math reasoning. It safeguards conceptual integrity of the preplan. A reasoning-paradigm refinement for LLM math.

entry.title: Neural Operator-Based Surrogate Model for CFD:Helical Coil Steam Generator in Small Modular Reactor

author.name: Minseo Lee, Seongmin Oh, Chaehyeon Song, Bumjin Cho, Shilaj Baral, Sangam Khanal, Minseop Song, Joongoo Jeon

entry.summary: This study presents a neural operator-based surrogate combined with a reduced-order model for real-time CFD transient analysis of a helical coil steam generator in a small modular nuclear reactor, supporting digital twin applications. It claims the first neural-operator surrogate for CFD-level transient analysis of SMR-specific geometries. Relevant for nuclear digital twins.

entry.title: Do Models Lie More to Other Models?

author.name: keith_wynroe

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs deceive other AI agents more readily than human overseers, motivated by the coming prevalence of agent-agent interactions where alignment training may not generalize. An initial experiment tests GPT-5 in settings where it can deceive an overseer of varying type.

entry.title: AI #170: Lack of Executive Order

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's weekly AI roundup covers a cancelled US AI executive order (reportedly killed by David Sacks and others), Illinois SB 315 (a variant of California SB 53 and New York's RAISE Act adding third-party auditing), and commentary on a policy document called Magnifica Humanitas. It synthesizes current US AI policy trends as remaining maximally ad hoc.

entry.title: From Context Shift to Stylistic Collapse: Why Training Objectives Matter More Than Scale

author.name: Rohan Mahapatra

entry.summary: This paper analyzes 17 models from 410M to 100B+ parameters across 24 linguistic probes, documenting that instruction tuning systematically collapses language entropy and reshapes linguistic features, arguing training objectives matter more than scale for these effects. It quantifies stylistic homogenization induced by alignment pipelines.

entry.title: GenesisFunc: Multi-Agent Data Generation for Accurate and Generalizable Function-Calling

author.name: Hao-Xiang Xu, Chong Deng, Jiaqing Liu, Wen Wang, Qian Chen, Lujia Bao, Xiangang Li, Zhen-Hua Ling

entry.summary: GenesisFunc is an automated multi-agent pipeline that generates high-quality, diverse function-calling training data from reliable tools in public benchmarks, addressing unreliable APIs and weak quality control in prior synthetic pipelines. It aims to improve LLM tool-use accuracy and generalization.

entry.title: Representation Signatures and Risk-Feedback Alignment in LLM Trading Agents

author.name: Weicheng Xue

entry.summary: Studies behavioral alignment and representation dynamics of LLM trading agents under market stress using an auditable testbed, identifying measurable pre-failure signatures such as embedding drift and effective-rank contraction before drawdowns. The work links representation geometry to risk-feedback alignment in financial decision-making.

entry.title: Continuity and Ordinality Matter: Constraining Time Series Tokens for Effective Time Series Analysis with Large Language Models

author.name: Musheng Li, Ziying Zhang, Cheng jin, Yuantao Gu

entry.summary: Proposes COM, a strategy that preserves the continuity and ordinality of time-series tokens via geometric constraints during initialization and training of token-based time-series LLMs. It reports consistent improvements across multiple time-series analysis benchmarks.

entry.title: PrismFlow: Residual Dynamics for Flow Matching in Time-Series Generation

author.name: Junru Zhang, Lang Feng, Jinbo Wang, Xu Guo, Yucheng Wang, Han Yu, Min Wu, Yabo Dong, Duanqing Xu

entry.summary: Introduces PrismFlow, a flow-matching framework for time-series generation that uses residual dynamics rather than a single monolithic vector-field estimator to better capture multimodal, multiscale signals. It targets the spectral distortion caused by over-smoothed velocity fields in heterogeneous temporal distributions.

entry.title: Computational Modeling of Antibody-Antigen Complexes: PLM-Based and MSA-Based Approaches

author.name: Xiao Luo

entry.summary: Proposes a generative framework GPlan that internalizes LLM reasoning into lightweight models for spatiotemporal intent-sequence recommendation in the Amap mapping app, generating logically coherent and physically executable intent flows under strict latency. It addresses the gap between LLM reasoning power and industrial deployment constraints.

entry.title: FormInv: A Measurement Protocol for Semantic Invariance in Mathematical Reasoning Benchmarks

author.name: Nishal Thomas, Noel Thomas

entry.summary: Presents FormInv, a measurement protocol auditing semantic invariance in mathematical reasoning benchmarks, detecting incorrect paraphrases in MathCheck via cross-model unanimity and showing that removing them materially changes model rankings. It highlights how semantically equivalent restatements expose inconsistent model behavior invisible to single-model evaluation.

entry.title: NeuroEdge: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition with High-Density EMG Using Deep Learning at the Edge

author.name: Peter Chudinov, Zhenyu Lin, Jay Motamarry, Srihita Panati, Xiaorong Zhang, and Zhuwei Qin

entry.summary: NeuroEdge performs real-time hand gesture recognition from high-density EMG entirely on resource-constrained microcontrollers, featuring a wireless streaming module and edge-optimized CNNs. It targets practical neural-machine interfaces for prosthetics and rehabilitation.

entry.title: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents: Comprehensive Evaluation with a Lightweight Framework

author.name: Masafumi Enomoto, Ryoma Obara, Haochen Zhang, and Masafumi Oyamada

entry.summary: Tackles the high cost of evaluating HTML observation-reduction methods for web agents by introducing a lightweight proxy based on the Minimal Failure Set of HTML elements whose removal causes task failure. Coverage of this set correlates strongly with end-to-end performance, enabling cheap method comparison without web access or LLM inference.

entry.title: Information-Directed Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Keru Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes the residual exploration that remains after warm-starting from offline data using conditional mutual information, then applies information-directed sampling to trade off regret against information gain. It proves a generic offline-to-online Bayesian regret bound via a ratio certificate.

entry.title: Phase-Conditioned Imitation Learning with Autonomous Failure Recovery for Robust Deformable Object Manipulation

author.name: Dayuan Chen, Kai Tang, Yukuan Zhang, Kazuhiro Kosuge, Yasuhisa Hirata

entry.summary: Proposes a phase-conditioned, force-aware hierarchical imitation-learning framework for deformable object manipulation that overcomes state aliasing in Markovian ACT policies. A FiLM-conditioned encoder produces phase-specific behaviors and a multimodal phase predictor enables autonomous recovery from contact failures.

entry.title: When Does Persona Prompting Actually Help? A Retrieval and Metric Analysis of Expert Role Injection in LLMs

author.name: Shuai Xiao, Su Liu, Weikai Zhou, Jialun Wu, Xinjie He, Zhiyuan Lin, Qiyang Xie

entry.summary: Examines when expert persona prompting actually helps LLMs through a controlled comparison of no-role, generic-expert, embedding retrieval, and hybrid retrieval conditions over 1,140 questions and 38 roles. It finds aggregate gains are small but metric-level analysis reveals consistent quality tradeoffs.

entry.title: Towards Human-Like Interactive Speech Recognition With Agentic Correction and Semantic Evaluation

author.name: Zixuan Jiang, Yanqiao Zhu, Peng Wang, Qinyuan Chen, Xinjian Zhao, Xipeng Qiu, Wupeng Wang, Zhifu Gao, Xiangang Li, Kai Yu and Xie Chen

entry.summary: Reformulates ASR as a multi-turn interactive refinement task, proposing Agentic ASR that pairs a single-pass front-end with semantic correction, intent routing, and reasoning-based clarification to fix meaning-critical errors. It argues token-level metrics like WER fail to capture such semantic failures.

entry.title: DefSynUS: Real-time Patient-specific Intrahepatic Vessel Identification via Deformation-Aware CT-US Domain Adaptation

author.name: Karl-Philippe Beaudet (MIMESIS, UNISTRA), Yordanka Velikova (TUM), Sidaty El Hadramy (MIMESIS, Unibas), Nassir Navab (TUM), Philippe Cattin (Unibas), Juan Verde (MIMESIS, UNISTRA, IHU Strasbourg), St\'ephane Cotin (MIMESIS, UNISTRA)

entry.summary: Presents DefSynUS, a real-time deformation-aware CT-to-ultrasound domain adaptation method for patient-specific intrahepatic vessel identification during liver surgery. Uses physics-based rendering of synthetic ultrasound from preoperative CT, eliminating preoperative ultrasound needs.

entry.title: HiKEY: Hierarchical Multimodal Retrieval for Open-Domain Document Question Answering

author.name: Joongmin Shin, Gyuho Shim, Jeongbae Park, Jaehyung Seo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: Introduces HiKEY, a hierarchical tree-based multimodal retrieval framework that treats document hierarchy as a first-class retrieval signal to address routing failure and evidence fragmentation in large-scale document QA. Reconstructs a logical heterogeneous graph instead of flat chunking.

entry.title: Think Fast, Talk Smart: Partitioning Deterministic and Neural Computation for Structured Health Text Generation

author.name: Kai-Chen Cheng, Haejun Han, David Q. Sun

entry.summary: Introduces Think Fast Talk Smart, a sleep-health pipeline that partitions deterministic computation from a single bounded LLM writer call, achieving lower numeric error and instruction violations across 280 user-nights and six models. Argues recurring analysis should be deterministic rather than runtime LLM prompting.

entry.title: Citation-Closure Retrieval and Per-Rule Attribution for Real-World Regulatory Compliance Question Answering

author.name: Yeong-Joon Ju, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: Proposes RefWalk for regulatory compliance QA, traversing cross-document citations from a shared topic anchor for citation-closure retrieval and per-rule attribution, formalized via RegOps-Bench with an operational knowledge graph. It addresses traceability needs that standard RAG fails to meet. Relevant for high-stakes compliance applications.

entry.title: From XXLTraffic to EvoXXLTraffic: Scaling Traffic Forecasting to Sensor-Evolving Networks

author.name: Du Yin, Hao Xue, Arian Prabowo, Shuang Ao, Flora Salim

entry.summary: Introduces XXLTraffic (up to 27 years of California and NSW data) and EvoXXLTraffic, a sensor-evolving reorganization with yearly active sensors and graph snapshots, plus a yearly streaming continual forecasting protocol. It moves traffic forecasting beyond the fixed-sensor assumption. Valuable for realistic, scalable forecasting research.

entry.title: ActTraitBench: Quantifying the Knowledge-Decision Gap in Large Language Models via Human-Grounded Behavioral Validation

author.name: Yutong Yang, Chenxi Miao, Weikang Li, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: ActTraitBench quantifies the Knowledge-Decision Gap in LLMs, the asymmetry between persona self-reports and implicit behavioral decisions, using human-grounded one-to-one mappings between psychometric facets and behavioral paradigms and quantile-mapping calibration of LLM-judge scores. It improves construct validity for personality consistency evaluation. Relevant for persona simulation and evaluation rigor.

entry.title: HoliTok:A Coutinuous Holistic Tokenization with Robust Dual Capabilities of Speech Generation and Understanding

author.name: Bohan Li, Shi Lian, Hankun Wang, Yiwei Guo, Yu Xi, Zhihan Li, Da Zheng, Colin Zhang, Kai Yu

entry.summary: HoliTok is a continuous holistic speech tokenizer encoding 48 kHz speech into a compact 25 Hz sequence of 128-dimensional latents, trained progressively to preserve signal fidelity, incorporate semantic information, and maintain latent learnability for both generation and understanding. It builds a unified AR+DiT model for synthesis and recognition. The goal is a tokenization space usable by language models and decodable to high-quality waveforms.

entry.title: Projectional Decoding: Towards Semantic-Aware LLM Generation

author.name: Boqi Chen, Jos\'e Antonio Hern\'andez L\'opez, Aren A. Babikian

entry.summary: Projectional decoding proposes maintaining a partial graph model alongside generated text as the primary artifact, enabling incremental semantic validation of software engineering outputs during generation. It bridges constrained decoding with deeper semantic correctness. The framework is conceptual but addresses a real validity gap.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Set Representation Learning Under Inference-Time Element Corruption

author.name: Yankai Chen, Hanrong Zhang, Bowei He, Philip S.Yu, Xue (Steve) Liu

entry.summary: SW-DRSO is a distributionally robust optimization framework for set representation learning that optimizes a tractable surrogate of worst-case loss over plausible inference-time element corruptions using a differentiable barycentric adversary. It addresses outliers and missing components at deployment. It improves robustness over standard set learning.

entry.title: Deep Binarized Photonic Reservoir Computing for Ultrafast Multimedia Signal Processing

author.name: Muhammad Waqar Iqbal, Mohamad Alassir, Nicolas Marsal, Damien Rontani

entry.summary: This work presents a deep binarized photonic reservoir computing system using a digital micro-mirror device, optical scattering, and CMOS photodetection that achieves gigabit-per-second processing for video, image, and speech recognition. It optimizes physical intra- and inter-layer hyperparameters to balance memory and dynamics. It advances ultrafast optical neural computing hardware.

entry.title: Supercharging Thermal Gaussian Splatting with Depth Estimation

author.name: Manoj Biswanath, Chenxin Cai, Hannah Schieber, Daniel Roth and Benjamin Busam

entry.summary: This work proposes Thermal-to-Depth Gaussian Splatting that supercharges thermal 3D scene representation with depth estimation, reducing reliance on visible light to enable faster single-modality reconstruction. It targets autonomous driving and robotics in conditions where RGB is unreliable. A practical multimodal 3D reconstruction contribution.

entry.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly of Markov Boundary for Tabular Prediction

author.name: Shu Wan, Abhinav Gorantla, Huan Liu, and K. Sel\c{c}uk Candan

entry.summary: This study empirically examines whether the Markov boundary is useful for tabular prediction using a large synthetic SCM benchmark and six regressors, finding nuanced results where oracle-boundary restriction often helps but estimated boundaries can hurt. It bridges causal feature-selection theory and practical tabular modeling.

entry.title: Instance-dependent Stochastic Lipschitz bandit

author.name: Marius Potfer, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: This paper provides instance-dependent regret bounds for Lipschitz bandits expressed through integrals of the suboptimality gap over level sets, capturing finer structure than zooming-dimension guarantees. It offers a more refined adaptivity result for continuum-armed bandits.

entry.title: ClinicBot: A Guideline-Grounded Clinical Chatbot with Prioritized Evidence RAG and Verifiable Citations

author.name: Navapat Nananukul, Mayank Kejriwal

entry.summary: ClinicBot is a guideline-grounded clinical chatbot using prioritized-evidence RAG and verifiable citations, structuring guidelines into semantic units with provenance and ranking evidence by clinical relevance to reduce hallucination. It targets trustworthy clinical decision support.

entry.title: Aryabhata 2: Scaling Reinforcement Learning for Advanced STEM Reasoning

author.name: Ritvik Rastogi, Vishal Singh, Tejas Chaudhari, Sandeep Varma

entry.summary: Aryabhata 2 is a reasoning-focused LLM for competitive STEM exams (JEE/NEET) built by reinforcement-learning post-training of GPT-OSS-20B on curated question banks, optimized for scalable domain-specific structured problem solving. It targets deployment for millions of student queries.

entry.title: SERC: LDPC-Inspired Semantic Error Correction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Gyumin Kim, Juhwan Park, Jaeha Kim, Seunggyun Han, Kyungrak Son, and Ikbeom Jang

entry.summary: SERC reframes LLM text generation as a semantic noisy channel and applies an LDPC-inspired sparse verification strategy to detect and correct hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation, avoiding exhaustive self-checking and self-bias. It offers an information-theoretic framework for semantic error correction.

entry.title: An End-to-End PyTorch Interface for Differentiable PDE Solvers: A RANS Model-Correction Study

author.name: Luca Saverio, Michele Alessandro Bucci, Gianmarco Farro, C\'edric Content, Denis Sipp (MONHADE)

entry.summary: Presents a fully differentiable PyTorch interface for PDE solvers that combines a baseline differentiable solver with a trainable additive correction, reformulating the PDE as an implicit layer for inverse problems and closure modeling. It is demonstrated on a RANS turbulence model-correction study.

entry.title: Balancing Multimodal Learning through Label Space Reshaping

author.name: Xiaoyu Ma, Weijie Zhang, Yuanhao Gao, Han Miao, Yongjian Deng, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Addresses modality imbalance in multimodal learning by attributing differing learning paces to differences in mapping difficulty between modality-specific features and the shared label space. It proposes Balanced Multimodal Label Reshaping (BMLR) to rebalance learning without sacrificing the strong modality.

entry.title: Feature Geometry of LoRA Adapters: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis of Representational Divergence in Fine-Tuned Language Models

author.name: Prasanth K K

entry.summary: Uses sparse autoencoders and a delta-activation framework to study how LoRA fine-tuning changes internal representations across ranks and layers in Gemma-2-9B, comparing adapter-specific feature spaces to pretrained dictionaries. It quantifies representational divergence via cosine similarity, principal angles, and CKA.

entry.title: Sequential Physics-Constrained Neural Operator Forward Modeling for the $\textit{Norne}$ Reservoir System

author.name: Clement Etienam, Juntao Yang, Oleg Ovcharenko, Nick Luiken, Tsubasa Onishi, Nefeli Moridis, Issam Said

entry.summary: Develops a mathematical and computational framework for sequential surrogate modeling of three-phase black-oil reservoir dynamics using Fourier Neural Operators and their physics-informed variant, applied to the Norne benchmark. It includes functional-analytic well-posedness and covariate-shift analysis.

entry.title: Resolving Endpoint Underfitting in Diffusion Bridges via Noise Alignment

author.name: Yurong Gao, Zicheng Zhang, Congying Han, Tiande Guo, Xinmin Qiu

entry.summary: Identifies an underfitting phenomenon near the target endpoint in diffusion-bridge models caused by large noise-level discrepancies between network inputs and regression targets. It proposes Noise-Aligned Diffusion Bridge (NADB), using a mean network to better align noise and resolve the endpoint drift.

entry.title: VFEAgent: A Multimodal Agent Framework for End-to-End Automated Finite Element Analysis

author.name: Jiachen Zhang (1 and 2), Junyi Lao (1), Chenghao Liu (1), Siyuan Liu (1), Shixin Wu (1), Linsen Zhang (1), Boyu Wang (1), Songfang Huang (1) ((1) Peking University, (2) China Agricultural University)

entry.summary: Proposes VFEAgent, an end-to-end multimodal multi-agent system that automates finite element analysis modeling and simulation directly from input images and problem descriptions using ReAct-driven reasoning and a verification-first code synthesis framework. It targets the complexity and expertise dependence of FEA workflows.

entry.title: Manifold-based Algorithms for the Hadamard Decomposition

author.name: Nicolas Gillis, Subhayan Saha, Stefano Sicilia, Arnaud Vandaele

entry.summary: Provides theoretical insights and three manifold-based algorithms for the Hadamard decomposition, which approximates a matrix as the element-wise product of two low-rank matrices, more expressive than truncated SVD. It reformulates the problem using manifold-constrained factors with r1*r2 columns.

entry.title: Learning Robust and Task-Invariant Functional Representation from fMRI through Siamese Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Jiyao Wang, Peiyu Duan, Nicha C. Dvornek, Lawrence H. Staib, Denis Sukhodolsky, Pamela Ventola, James S. Duncan

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight Siamese self-supervised framework for learning robust, task-invariant functional representations from fMRI that generalize across downstream tasks without prohibitive pretraining cost. It addresses small sample sizes, noisy psychiatric labels, and high dimensionality that cause overfitting.

entry.title: Causal Intelligence for Constraint-Aware Intervention Design to Induce State Transitions

author.name: Zixuan Song, Uwe Mueller and Dimitris V. Manatakis

entry.summary: Presents COAST, a causal-intelligence framework for designing constrained interventions that induce user-defined state transitions by learning context-specific causal graphs and structural causal models. It introduces a constraint-aware multi-objective optimization balancing transition efficacy, intervention complexity, and target-state stability.

entry.title: Mind Your Tone: Does Tone Alter LLM Performance?

author.name: Om Dobariya, Akhil Kumar

entry.summary: Investigates whether and how tonal variations in prompts affect LLM accuracy on objective multiple-choice questions across two datasets and four cost-efficient models. It finds tonal effects are systematic but highly model-dependent, with some models showing large accuracy swings across tones.

entry.title: Bosses, Kings, and the Commons: Cooperation Under Power Asymmetry in LLM Societies

author.name: Abhilekh Borah

entry.summary: SovSim is a generative multi-agent simulation studying how LLM societies cooperate to manage shared commons under asymmetric power structures, extending Ostrom's self-governance theory to power-imbalanced settings often ignored in prior LLM social simulations. It surfaces how power asymmetry affects collective resource outcomes.

entry.title: UA-Legal-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Ukrainian Legal Reasoning

author.name: Volodymyr Ovcharov

entry.summary: UA-Legal-Bench is a five-task benchmark for Ukrainian legal reasoning built from one of the world's largest open judicial corpora, evaluating 11 LLMs across classification, outcome prediction, and norm extraction. It addresses the English-centricity of legal NLP and exposes failure modes in morphologically rich, non-Latin-script languages.

entry.title: Robust Frequency-Calibrated Virtual EEG Channel Generation from Four Frontal Electrodes for Wearable EEG Augmentation

author.name: Minghao Xiao

entry.summary: FAVC-Net generates 13 virtual EEG channels from just four frontal electrodes using multi-scale encoding, graph attention, and spectral calibration, enabling richer wearable EEG. It emphasizes spectral fidelity and robustness beyond waveform matching.

entry.title: Multi-Stage VLM Pipeline for Zero-Shot Traffic Accident Understanding

author.name: Fumiya Tatematsu, Fumihiko Takahashi

entry.summary: A first-place CVPR 2026 challenge solution for zero-shot traffic accident understanding using a multi-stage Qwen3-VL pipeline blending a 32B model and a 235B MoE sibling, with post-processing to snap predictions to vehicle detections. It substantially beats host baselines.

entry.title: EvoMD-LLM: Learning the Language of Species Evolution in Reactive Molecular Dynamics

author.name: Zhichen Tang, Zhengzheng Dang, Yulin Chen, Jixin Wu, Haiwen Li, Yanming Wang

entry.summary: Reframes reactive molecular dynamics at the species level as a symbolic temporal language-modeling task, tokenizing chemical events with persistence durations so autoregressive LLMs can learn compositional evolution. Temporal scaffolding treats event duration as an explicit token to provide structured inductive bias.

entry.title: ReasonLight: A Multimodal Foundation Model-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning Framework for Zero-Shot Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Aoyu Pang, Maonan Wang, Yuejiao Xie, Chung Shue Chen, Zhiwei Yang, Man-On Pun

entry.summary: Proposes ReasonLight, a multimodal foundation-model-enhanced RL framework for zero-shot traffic signal control that fuses structured sensor measurements, multi-view camera semantics, and a pretrained RL controller's candidate phase decisions. It targets open-world events absent from training data.

entry.title: DELOS: Detecting Shallow Transits in Kepler Photometry Using a Contrastive-Learning Framework

author.name: Qingtian Liu, Jian Ge, XingChen Yan, Kevin Willis, Xinyu Yao, QuanQuan Hu, and Jiapeng Zhu

entry.summary: Presents DELOS, a contrastive-learning framework for detecting shallow, intermediate-to-long-period transiting exoplanets in Kepler phase-folded light curves using GPU-accelerated folding and a 1D convolutional encoder that produces a score periodogram. It is trained on 20 million synthetic curves with realistic noise.

entry.title: V2XCrafter: Learning to Generate Driving Scene Across Agents

author.name: Yihang Tao, Yu Guo, Senkang Hu, Yanan Ma, Zihan Fang, Sam Kwong, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: Proposes V2XCrafter, claimed first framework to generate multi-agent V2X driving scenes for data augmentation, addressing degraded quality from expanded learning objectives and inconsistent physical attributes of jointly observed objects across agents. It targets the scarcity of annotated real-world V2X collaborative-perception datasets.

entry.title: KGEdit: Ambiguity-Aware Knowledge Graphs for Training-Free Precise Video Generation and Editing

author.name: Mingshu Cai, Miao Zhang, Chenghe Yang, Yixuan Li, Osamu Yoshie, and Yuya Ieiri

entry.summary: Proposes KGEdit, a training-free structured-semantic control framework for text-to-video diffusion that builds an ambiguity-aware knowledge graph disentangling prompts into identity, relation, attribute, and negative-constraint semantics. A structured semantic injection module feeds these signals into key diffusion-transformer layers to reduce concept-binding errors and cross-frame inconsistency.

entry.title: DynaGraph: Lightweight Multi-Model Interaction Framework via Dynamic Topological Reconfiguration

author.name: Yanxing Guo, Zihao Zheng, Fangzhou Wu, Ling Liang, Lin Bao, Zongwei Wang, Yimao Cai

entry.summary: Presents DynaGraph, a lightweight multi-model framework that uses dynamic topological reconfiguration to balance the rigidity of static pipelines against the divergence of unconstrained dynamic agents. It multiplexes time-division PEFT adapters over a shared base model, enabling full training and inference on a single consumer GPU.

entry.title: K-FinHallu: A Hallucination Detection Benchmark for Multi-Turn RAG in Korean Finance

author.name: Eunbyeol Cho, Yunseung Lee, Mirae Kim, Jeewon Yang, Youngjun Kwak, Edward Choi

entry.summary: Introduces K-FinHallu, claimed first benchmark for hallucination detection in multi-turn Korean financial retrieval-augmented generation, building dialogues from authentic documents and injecting hallucinations under a hierarchical taxonomy that accounts for justified abstention. Benchmarking frontier and open LLMs as detectors reveals that even strong models struggle.

entry.title: UI-KOBE: Knowledge-Oriented Behavior Exploration for Lightweight Graph-Guided GUI Agents

author.name: Yuxiang Chai, Han Xiao, Xinyu Fu, Jinpeng Chen, Rui Liu, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: Proposes UI-KOBE, which boosts lightweight on-device mobile GUI agents using reusable app-specific graph knowledge built via autonomous exploration. Aims for cheaper, privacy-preserving on-device automation.

entry.title: From Blind Guess to Informed Judgment: Teaching LLMs to Evaluate Materials by Building Knowledge-Augmented Preference Signals

author.name: Yeyong Yu, Wenya Hu, Xing Wu, Quan Qian

entry.summary: Proposes MaterEval, a knowledge-augmented preference framework that pairs informed expert-rule-based judgments against rule-removed blind guesses to train LLMs to evaluate materials candidates reliably. Targets the evaluation bottleneck in materials discovery.

entry.title: DiffSpot: Can VLMs Spot Fine-Grained Visual Differences in Web Interfaces?

author.name: Linhao Zhang, Aiwei Liu, Yuan Liu, Xiao Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces DiffSpot, a code-driven spot-the-difference benchmark on web interfaces that mutates single CSS properties to create controlled image pairs, testing VLMs' fine-grained visual perception. Reveals limits in detecting subtle localized visual changes.

entry.title: Entity-Collision: A Stratified Protocol for Attributing Retrieval Lift in Agent Memory

author.name: Youwang Deng

entry.summary: Proposes entity-collision, a stratified protocol for attributing retrieval lift in agent memory by pinning the BM25 floor (distractors share answer entity tokens) and stratifying by tag, isolating embedder contributions. Reveals a two-axis pattern across embedders and collision degrees.

entry.title: PTCG-Bench: Can LLM Agents Master Pok\'emon Trading Card Game?

author.name: Dongdong Hua, Yifei Sun, Renhong Huang, Feng Gao, Chunping Wang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Presents PTCG-Bench, a benchmark on the Pokemon Trading Card Game evaluating LLM agents on single-environment decision-making and self-evolution through accumulated experience, with a modular harness ablation. Tests strategic and evolving decision-making in a complex board game.

entry.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Molecular Mixture Behavior Prediction

author.name: Roel J. Leenhouts, Nathan K. Morgan, William Green, Jan G. Rittig, Florence H. Vermeire

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation framework that decomposes molecular mixture-property prediction error into pure-compound and non-ideal interaction components, with leakage-aware splits and excess-property metrics, plus seven curated datasets. It exposes that absolute accuracy conflates ideal-mixing and interaction effects. Improves rigor in ML for chemistry.

entry.title: S2MDF: A Plug-And-Play Layer for Intersection-Free Multi-Object Signed Distance Fields

author.name: Deniz Sayin Mercadier, Federico Stella, Aurel Bizeau, Nicolas Talabot, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: S2MDF is a lightweight plug-and-play module enforcing a hard intersection-free constraint on multi-object compositional signed distance fields without architectural changes or soft penalty tuning. It guarantees physically plausible non-interpenetrating geometry. Relevant for 3D reconstruction and compositional scene modeling.

entry.title: Improving CLIP Adaptation by Breaking Tail Alignment for Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Shuai Yi, Yixiong Zou, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: Reports a counterintuitive finding that actively pushing low-similarity 'tail' image tokens away from their text embeddings improves CLIP adaptation in source-free cross-domain few-shot learning. It interprets this via the difficulty of aligning all tokens under domain shift and scarce data. Useful insight for VLM adaptation.

entry.title: Not All Inputs Are Valid: Towards Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval Using Language

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Daizong Liu, Xiaoye Qu, Jianfeng Dong, Pan Zhou, Renfu Li, Zichuan Xu, Lixing Chen, Panpan Zheng, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Not All Inputs Are Valid introduces Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval, where systems must reject out-of-distribution video-irrelevant queries instead of forcibly retrieving, addressing high-risk failure modes in applications like criminal activity detection. It moves VMR beyond the closed-set assumption. A useful new problem setting for video retrieval.

entry.title: Harnessing non-adversarial robustness in large language models

author.name: Qinghua Zhou, Ellina Aleshina, Andrey Lovyagin, Oleg Somov, Mikhail Seleznyov, Alexander Panchenko, Ivan Oseledets, Elena Tutubalina, Ivan Y. Tyukin
